Egnyte help

This guide holds Egnyte’s own help, gathered from helpdesk.egnyte.com on 15 November 2026. Egnyte is an online service that businesses use to store, share and work on files. Its help centre has about 1,500 articles, most written for the company administrators who set it up; this guide keeps the 421 written for a person who uses it: the web app, the desktop app, the iPhone and iPad app, the AI assistant, and Egnyte with Microsoft 365 and Google.

Left out on purpose: 607 announcements, release notes and known issues, which are a history of changes rather than help; the administrators’ pages, such as users and groups, governance, reporting, migration and the storage appliances; and the editions for architects and life sciences companies. If you run Egnyte for your company, Egnyte’s own help centre has those pages.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

The AI assistant

Agent Marketplace

Egnyte offers users the ability to configure and add agents using the Marketplace, making it easier to find agents that address specific business needs without having to build them from scratch.

This feature is available for Platform Plans with AI add-on and included in the New Generation Platform plans. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Access Agent Marketplace

  • Navigate to AI -> Agents
  • Click on Marketplace at the top or from the Create Your Own Agent tile.

Create an Agent from Marketplace

  • Click on any of the available agents from the Marketplace. Users can click on a specific category to see refined results or search for a specific agent using the search option at the top. Click on the desired agent.
  • Agent details, such as description, problem, suited for, capabilities, category, and a few sample questions will be displayed. Click on +Configure & add to configure and add the agent.
  • Agent details, such as description, problem, suited for, capabilities, category, and a few sample questions will be displayed. Click on +Configure & add to configure and add the agent.
  • The option to configure and add the agent will be disabled if the agent requires connectors that are not enabled for the organization. Admins shall enable access to continue adding such agents.
  • The details will be pre-filled for the selected agent for the users to review and edit. Users can modify the details as required, test the agent, and then create them for use. They can follow the steps to create the agent to complete agent creation.
  • The agent will then be created and will be available for use.

AI Connectors - Admin Guide

Egnyte’s AI Assistant can be easily utilised as a proactive agent capable of connecting to external data sources, automating cross-platform tasks, and performing deep agentic searches.

AI Connectors in Egnyte’s AI Assistant unlock the power of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, enabling the AI Assistant to connect with any compatible external service using supported authentication protocols. The catalog of available connectors is continually expanding.

Refer to Settings → Configuration → AI or visit the AI Assistant Tools panel for the latest list of the connectors.

Admins get the ability to add, configure, and manage these connectors for their domain. Admins can also configure the Egnyte Tools, such as file and folder tools from Settings -> AI Powered Features -> AI Connectors.

Manage Connectors from the Settings Page

Use a pre-loaded Connector

Egnyte provides two types of pre-loaded connectors:

  • By Egnyte : Connectors built and maintained by Egnyte (for example; Egnyte Outlook MCP, Egnyte Gmail MCP). These are built in-house. Currently, Egnyte offers the following connectors with the catalog continually expanding.
  • First-party connectors : Connectors built by the third-party vendor themselves (for example; Atlassian Rovo MCP is built by Atlassian, Notion MCP is built by Notion). Egnyte has added these to the catalog so admins can connect with one click. For both types, the server URL and metadata are pre-filled; the admin just needs to publish the connector for the end-users to be able to Add and Connect.
Back to Top…

Create a Custom Connector

Admins can create a custom connector to add a custom MCP server that isn’t in the catalog. They need to provide the server name, URL, and auth type manually. This is for internal tools, niche services, or any MCP-compatible server not already listed.

  • Click on Egnyte’s AI Assistant -> + icon -> Connectors.

  • Alternatively, click on the Settings icon at the top -> Connectors.

  • Click on Add connectors.

  • Click on Create new connector.

  • Alternatively, navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> AI Connectors and click on Add New MCP Server in MCP Client section.

  • Enter the details for the new connector

    • Server Name: Enter a short, descriptive name for the MCP Server
    • Server URL: Enter the full URL from where the MCP server can be accessed.
    • This is the MCP endpoint URL provided by the external service. Refer to the service’s developer documentation or MCP integration page to obtain the correct URL.
    • For Egnyte-provided connectors (available under the By Egnyte tab), the server URL is preconfigured. A URL needs to be entered only when creating a custom connector
    • Description (Optional): Provide any additional information, as needed
    • Authentication Type: Select the authentication type

  • Click on Test configuration.

  • Egnyte supports the following authentication types:

    • None: No authentication required
    • OAuth: The most common type for third-party services. When a user connects, they are redirected to the external service to grant permission (for example; Allow Egnyte to access your Jira data). Each user authenticates individually with their own credentials. Use this for services like project management tools, email, and collaboration platforms
    • OAuth Client ID: Used when the MCP server requires application-level authentication using a client ID and secret, rather than per-user authorization. The admin provides the credentials during setup and all users share the same application-level access. Appropriate for internal or organization-scoped services.Refer to Slack and Salesforce AI Connector guides for more details.
    • API Key: A static token-based authentication method. The admin enters an API key during configuration. Suited for services that use simple key-based access rather than OAuth flows
    • Select None only for MCP servers that are publicly accessible or hosted on an internal network without access controls, as this option may pose a risk of data exposure.

  • Provide the required authorization.

  • Admins can edit the logo for the connector by clicking on the Edit icon and selecting the desired logo. They can also choose to delete the logo by clicking on the Delete icon. Set the Server tools and permissions. For each of the listed tools, admin can select Allow unsupervised or Always ask permission. Egnyte’s AI Assistant will carry out the listed action as per the permissions set by the admin. Click on Continue after making the desired changes.

  • Review the summary, provide the acknowledgement by clicking on the checkbox, and click on Save and publish.

  • Click on Publish to confirm and the connector will be published.

  • When an admin publishes a custom MCP connector, their organization is responsible for configuring, managing, and maintaining that connector. Egnyte does not review, control, or guarantee the behavior of custom MCP connections. This is acknowledged via the checkbox on the Summary step.

  • Egnyte supports a growing library of MCP connectors with OAuth authentication.

Back to Top…

Understanding Tool Permissions

For each tool exposed by a connector, the admin must choose a permission level. This is the most important security decision in connector configuration as it controls whether the AI Assistant can act autonomously or must ask the user first.

The Allow all tools checkbox at the top applies the same permission level to every tool on the connector. For granular control, uncheck it and configure each tool individually.

  • Allow unsupervised - This means that AI can call this tool without user confirmation or permission
  • Always ask permission - The user will see a confirmation before each tool is called by the AI It is recommended from the security aspect to keep the setting as Always ask permission for the tools that can modify the data, such as send email, create ticket, delete an item, and similar actions.
Back to Top…

Manage Connectors

Edit Connector
  • Click on Egnyte’s AI Assistant -> + icon -> Connectors or click on the settings icon -> Connectors.
  • Click on the three-dots icon for a connector and click on Edit.
  • Click on Test configuration.
  • Make changes to the tools and permissions and click on Continue.
  • Review the summary and click on Save. The updated configuration will be saved for the connector.
Publish a Connector
  • For the connectors that have not been published yet, admins can click on the Publish option in the three-dots menu.
  • Click on Publish to confirm.
  • The connector will be published.
Unpublish a Connector
  • To unpublish a connector, click on the Unpublish option in the three-dots icon. Unpublishing removes the connector from users’ Connectors panel but does not delete the connector’s configuration. Users who previously connected will lose access until it is republished.
  • Click on Unpublish to confirm.
  • The connector will be unpublished.
Disconnect a Connector

To disconnect a connector, click on the three-dots icon -> Disconnect.

The connector will be disconnected.

Delete a Connector
  • To delete a connector, click on the three-dots icon -> Delete. Custom connectors need to be unpublished before they can be deleted. Pre-loaded connectors cannot be deleted.
  • Click on Remove to confirm.
  • The connector will be deleted successfully.

AI Connectors - User Guide

Users can leverage Egnyte’s AI Assistant to connect to external connectors such as Atlassian, Gmail, Procore, and others. This helps bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant supports AI Connectors via MCP servers. Egnyte admin manages which connectors are available on the domain. Once a connector is published, users can connect to it and start using it directly from the AI Assistant. The admin can also publish additional connectors beyond the Egnyte-provided catalog. Check the Connectors panel for the full list available on the domain.

Add and Connect a Connector

End users can Add and Connect the connectors that have been published for their domains by their admin. Users can also browse connectors from the Egnyte catalog using the By Egnyte filter. Under All Connectors, the ones published by the admins appear at the top (A–Z), followed by unpublished connectors (A–Z).

Each connector requires the users to authenticate with the external service using their own credentials as the admin cannot do this on their behalf.

  • Click on Egnyte’s AI Assistant -> + icon -> Connectors.
  • If the users have no connectors added, they will see no connectors configured. Click on Add Connector.
  • If one or more connectors are already configured, they will be displayed. Click on Add connector to add more connectors.
  • Select the desired connector and click on Add and Connect. Users can also filter the listed connectors using filters such as By Egnyte or Published. By default, all the connectors will show up.
  • Provide the required authorization and Continue.
  • Authenticate the connection by allowing the required permissions and Allow.
  • Authentication will be complete and the connector will be added.
  • Users can also add and manage their connectors using the settings icon at the top -> Connectors.

Use AI Connectors with Egnyte’s AI Assistant

Once users have connected one or more connectors, they can ask the AI Assistant questions that span the connected services. The AI Assistant automatically selects the right tools based on the question.

The availability of connectors and tools depends on what the admin has published and what users have connected.

Users can ask the AI Assistant to retrieve information, compose messages, or search content from AI connectors published by their admins.

In the example above, the AI Assistant will look through the user’s mail and provide the details of the workflow-related emails received on the date of query.

The AI Assistant will conduct iterative retrieval if the details are not immediately found. It will fire multiple search queries, analyze the information, and synthesize a comprehensive report.

Egnyte Tools

Users can also use Egnyte tools, such as file and folder tools while interacting with AI. Click on Connectors -> Enable File and Folder Tools.

Agentic Search

In addition to using external connectors, AI Connector also enhances the AI Assistant’s ability to search across the Egnyte content. The agentic search understands the context of the request and can reason through the custom metadata.

For instance, users can search for AEC projects in their organization. Egnyte’s AI Assistant will search through the project metadata to provide the results.

Managing Connectors - Enable or Disable, Disconnect, Edit Permissions

  • Navigate to AI Assistant and click on the + icon -> Connectors -> Manage Connectors or Click on the Settings icon -> Connectors.
  • Enable or disable the connector using the toggle or click on the disconnect icon to disconnect the connector.
  • Click on > of the desired connector to edit the tools and permissions.
  • Use the respective toggles to enable or disable a particular tool.
  • For instance, If the user disables certain tools from a connector, the AI Assistant will not be able to access those capabilities.

Permission Prompts and Admin-controlled Restrictions

For some tools, the AI Assistant will ask for confirmation before taking an action (for example; sending an email, creating a page). This is a security feature configured by the admin. When prompted, review what the AI Assistant is about to do and click Deny or Allow. Tools marked as unsupervised by the admin will execute automatically without a prompt.

If a tool has been disabled by the admin, users will not be able to enable it from their side, and the AI Assistant will let them know when a requested action is unavailable because the tool is restricted. For example, the admin may have disabled email-sending tools while keeping email-search tools available. In these cases, the AI Assistant will tell users what it can do and suggest alternatives as mentioned earlier.

AI Control Center - Overview

The AI Control Center gives administrators one place to find and fix Egnyte agents that interact with content in a less secure manner. It lists the agents in the domain, flags agents with a scope that is too broad or that can reach sensitive content, and recommends an action for each one.

  • This feature is available to customers on the Ultimate plan. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

  • Sensitive content detection requires Content Classification policies to be configured.

Benefits

  • See which agents need attention: Review every agent with an open issue in one list, instead of opening each agent’s settings.
  • Find agents that reach sensitive content: Agents are matched against the Content Classification policies that apply to the folders they use.
  • Prioritize by risk: Each flagged agent has a High, Medium, or Low risk level and a reason for the flag.
  • Fix issues in the same place: Re-scope an agent, create an AI Safeguard policy, or change tool permissions directly from the AI Control Center.
  • Support AI adoption: Give users access to agents while keeping visibility into what those agents can reach and do.

Common Use Cases

  • Unrestricted agent review: Find agents set to use all Egnyte files and folders, and re-scope them to specific folders.
  • Sensitive content exposure: Find agents scoped to folders that contain classified content, and either re-scope them or create an AI Safeguard policy.
  • Unsupervised actions: Find agents with Egnyte tools or third-party connector tools set to Always allow and change them to Ask each time.
  • Post-rollout check: Review newly created agents

Access the AI Control Center

  • Navigate to Settings → AI Powered Features → AI Control Center
  • Review the list of agents. By default, the list shows all agents with open issues. The following columns are available:
    • Agent: The agent name. Use the search box to find a specific agent.
    • Risk: The agent’s risk level, High, Medium, or Low. Use the filter to view specific levels.
    • Reason: The main reason the agent was flagged. If more than one reason applies, the number of additional reasons is shown. For example, Unrestricted access +1. Use the filter to view specific reasons. For agents with multiple reasons, the reasons can be viewed by clicking the “+1” or viewing the full agent details.
    • Created by: The user who created the agent. Use the filter to view agents created by specific users.
  • Each row also has a three-dot menu with the available actions.

How Risk Levels Are Determined

An agent’s risk level comes from two types of configurations:

  • Egnyte folder source: The content the agent can reach.
  • Connectors: The actions the agent can take, using Egnyte tools or third-party connector tools. The AI Control Center evaluates the agent’s configured scope, not what a specific user can reach when running the agent. Risk levels are shown as High, Medium, or Low. If an agent matches more than one rule, it appears once in the list with a combined risk level, and every reason is shown.

Rule

When it applies

Risk level on its own

Combined with other rules

Unrestricted access

The agent’s source is set to all Egnyte files and folders. The agent reaches everything the user who runs it can access.

High

Stays High.

Reaches sensitive content

The agent’s source is set to selected files and folders that contain content tagged by Content Classification policies.

Based on the sensitivity of the folders: Low, Medium, or High.

Raised by the two connector rules below.

Unsupervised Egnyte action

An Egnyte tool that changes content is set to Always allow. These tools copy, move, rename, or create files and folders, and update file metadata.

Medium

With Reaches sensitive content, raises the risk level by one step: Low to Medium, or Medium to High.

Unsupervised connector tool

A third-party connector tool, such as Gmail, Salesforce, or Procore, is set to Always allow.

Low

With Reaches sensitive content, raises Low to Medium only. It does not raise Medium to High.

  • If both connector rules apply to the same agent, the Egnyte action rule sets the increase, and both reasons are shown.

  • At this time, Egnyte cannot tell whether a third-party connector tool reads or changes content. Any third-party tool set to Always allow is flagged, including tools that only read content.

  • Agents that do not match any rule are not shown.

Review Agent Details

Select an agent in the list to open its details panel. The panel shows the following:

  • Risk level and agent name: The risk level badge and name appear at the top, with the available actions.
  • Issues: A description of each reason the agent was flagged. For example; Agent reaches content that matches 4 content classification policies or Agent can copy, move, or update Egnyte content without asking first.
  • General: Who created the agent and when.
  • What can Agent Reach: The agent’s Egnyte sources (for example; 2 folders), whether web sources are enabled, and the sensitive content tags that apply to its sources. Click View to see the sources.
  • Connectors & Tools: Each connector and tool the agent uses, and whether the tool is set to Always allow or Ask each time.

Resolve Flagged Agents

Each flagged agent has recommended actions. Actions are available from the three-dot menu on each row and from the details panel.

Action

Rescope an Agent

Use this action to limit the agent to specific folders.

  • Select the agent and click Rescope.
  • The Edit Agent window opens on the Sources tab. Review the agent’s current sources. Use the All, Egnyte, and Web filters to narrow the list. Remove sources the agent should no longer use or click Add sources to select specific folders.
  • Click Save in the top right of the window.
Create an AI Safeguard Policy

Use this action to block AI from processing the sensitive content an agent reaches. This action is available only for agents flagged with Reaches sensitive content.

  • Select the agent and click Create AI Safeguard policy.
  • The New AI Safeguard policy window opens with the matching Content Classification policies already selected.
    • Enter a Name for the policy.
    • Review the Criteria. To add more criteria, click Add criteria.
    • Review the Summary, which describes the content that AI processing will be restricted for.
  • Click Create. After the policy is created from the AI Control Center, the Reaches sensitive content reason is marked as resolved for the agent.

AI Safeguards do not apply to connector tool calls. A policy resolves only the Reaches sensitive content reason. To resolve the other reasons, change the tool permissions.

Set Tool Permissions to Always Ask

Use this action to require approval before an agent runs a tool. This action is available for agents flagged with Unsupervised Egnyte action or Unsupervised connector tool.

  • Click the three-dot menu on the agent’s row, or the three-dot menu in the details panel and select Set tool to always ask. The Update tool permissions window opens.
  • Review the agent’s recommended tools. By default, tools are set to Ask each time. To apply one setting to all tools in a group, use the All tools menu. To change a single tool, select Always allow, Ask each time, or Never allow for that tool. Click Save. Changes apply only to the selected agent. Other agents and domain-level connector settings are not changed. For more information on tool permissions, see AI Connectors - Admin Guide.

AI Models Supported in Egnyte

Egnyte integrates with leading AI language models to power intelligent features across the platform, giving users flexibility in selecting a model that aligns with their requirements and preferences. This article covers the supported models, the steps to select a preferred model, and how admins can enable or disable the model selector for end-users.

Supported Models

  • Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Default): Anthropic’s latest Sonnet model, designed for fast, efficient performance across everyday coding, document creation, and agentic workflows.
  • GPT-5.6 Terra: OpenAI’s flagship model built for reasoning-intensive and coding-heavy workloads, suited for complex professional tasks
  • GPT-6.1 Sol: OpenAI’s next-generation model delivering near-flagship performance in agentic coding, computer use, and professional work, suited for demanding tasks at scale.
  • Gemini 3.5 Flash: Google’s speed-optimized model designed for high-volume everyday tasks
  • Gemini 3.7 Flash: Google’s fast, efficient model designed for high-volume tasks and responsive everyday workflows.
  • Gemini 3.8 Flash: Google’s most capable Flash model, combining speed and efficiency with stronger software engineering, agentic, and multi-step reasoning performance.
  • Claude Sonnet 4.6: Anthropic’s model balancing performance and efficiency, with strong capabilities in coding, math, and agentic workflows.
  • Claude Sonnet 5: Anthropic’s advanced model designed for complex reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows, balancing strong performance with efficiency.

Model Selector

Users can also choose from multiple AI models directly within the chat input box in Egnyte.

  • Click on the models icon in the input box.
  • Click on the desired model to select.
  • The new model will be displayed as per the user’s selection.

Model Settings

Enable or Disable Model Selector

Admins have the option to choose if the users should be able to select their preferred Large Language Model.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • Use the Allow users to select their preferred Large Language Model toggle to enable or disable the model selector.
  • Click on Save changes. When the Model selector is disabled, GPT 5.6 will be used as the default model.

Manage AI Models Available for Use

Admins have the ability to select the specific AI models that will be available for use to the end users. They can enable or disable specific model(s) and also set the default model.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • Enable or disable the model by using the respective toggle.
  • Gemini-3.7 Flash is disabled by default. Admins can enable the model from the Allowed Models list to make it available for the end users.
  • Admins can also set the preferred default model by clicking on the respective check icon. There is a label added to the model recommended by Egnyte and it would be set as the default model.
  • Click on Set as default to confirm.
  • If the admins disable the default model, there would be an additional confirmation required. The next available model will then be automatically set as the default model.
  • It is required to keep at least one model enabled. Also, if there is only one model enabled then it will automatically be the default model.
  • The end-users will see the default model and the available AI model(s) as per the settings configured by the Admins. Some AI models have UI indicators that identify specific attributes. AI Safeguards - FAQ

For a full-featured overview of AI Safeguards, refer to the AI Safeguards - Overview, and for setup instructions and example use cases refer to the AI Safeguards - Admin Guide.

For Users

Who should be contacted if AI access is needed for a specific file or folder?

Contact your Egnyte domain administrator. Administrators can review which policies apply and determine whether access can be adjusted.

Why can’t my AI solution use a file I selected?

The file may be protected by an AI Safeguards policy that was configured by the domain administrator. The restriction applies to AI processing only. The file itself remains fully accessible and can be opened, edited, downloaded, and shared according to your access permissions.

Why can’t I see the AI Assistant or Agents in my account?

If AI functionality is available for other users but not for you, it likely means that a policy has been configured to remove AI access entirely for your account or the groups that you are in. When this type of restriction applies, all AI-related entry points are hidden. There is no visible indication that a restriction is in place.

If none of the users in your company have access to AI, it might mean that AI is not part of domain’s pricing plan or the AI functionality might be completely disabled by the domain Admin.

In both cases, contact your Egnyte administrator to find out whether AI access can be enabled.

Does restricting a file in AI Safeguards affect the ability to open or download it?

No. AI Safeguards restrict AI processing only. A user having correct file permissions can still open, download, edit, and share the file. The restriction applies only to AI features such as the AI Assistant and AI Agents

Why does an external AI tool such as Claude or ChatGPT give a different answer when connected to Egnyte?

External AI tools connected through the Egnyte MCP Server are subject to the same AI Safeguards policies as the Egnyte platform. Files restricted by an active policy are not returned to the external tool, so responses may differ from what would be expected without a restriction in place. These applications also utilize their own logic to generate responses, and the specific verbiage of the AI Safeguards response might differ between responses.

For Administrators

A user reports that a file is unexpectedly blocked from AI processing. How can the cause be identified?

Navigate to the Reports panel, then Audit, then AI Safeguards, then Blocked. Filter by the user and the date of the incident to find the relevant entry. The report shows the file name, the date, and which policy was matched.

Review the matching policy in Settings, then Configuration, then AI. Confirm whether the criteria are correctly scoped and adjust if needed.

What should be focused on when reviewing the Flagged report?

The Flagged report lists every request that matched a Report Only policy. The files in this report were processed by the AI without restriction. The report is most useful when preparing to switch a policy from Report Only to Active state.

When reviewing the Flagged report, look for the following:

  • Volume by folder or content type: a high volume of matches on a sensitive location or classification confirms that the policy scope is well-targeted before switching it to Active state.
  • Unexpected users: matches from users who should not be accessing sensitive information may indicate that group membership or folder permissions require review.
  • Missing activity: if expected high-risk activity does not appear in the report, the policy criteria may need to be broadened before enforcing.
How long does it take for a new or updated policy to take effect?

Changes to AI Safeguards policies may take a few hours to take effect across the domain.

Are changes to AI Safeguards policies recorded in audit logs?

Yes, these changes are recorded in audit logs and can be accessed from the Policy Settings Report. The report includes details when an AI Safeguards policy is created, modified, deleted, or reordered.

A user on a mobile device can still see AI entry points even though a Users or Groups-only policy applies to them. Is this expected?

Yes, but only on older app versions. Users on Egnyte for Android older than v.9.5 or Mobile App for iOS older than v.9.5 may still see AI entry points even when a Users/Groups-only policy applies to them. Upgrading the mobile app to v.9.5 or later resolves this situation. Despite having the entry points, they are still unable to execute any AI actions.

Can external AI tools connect to Egnyte on behalf of a user who has been fully excluded by a Users or Groups-only policy?

Yes. External tools connecting through the Egnyte MCP Server can still establish a connection on behalf of an excluded user. This is a known limitation of the MCP protocol and our target is to address it in future updates.

However, AI Safeguards policies apply to inbound requests to the Egnyte MCP Server, so the content returned to the external tool is sanitized according to the active policy set.

Are AI Safeguards available on all Egnyte plans?

AI Safeguards is available on the Essentials, Elite, and Ultimate plans, or for those who have purchased the AI Add-on. Contact your Egnyte account manager or Sales team for additional plan information.

The Content Classification criterion is not available when creating a policy. Why?

The Content Classification criterion requires Egnyte Content Classification capabilities, which are available on the Ultimate plan only. On the Elite plan, this criterion does not appear in the policy creation dialog.

A Users/Groups-only policy has been created but users can still see AI entry points. What could be the problem?

First check that the policy is in Active state and not Report Only or Inactive. Then verify that the affected users are members of the group referenced in the policy criteria or were selected individually. If the policy was recently created or updated, it might take a few hours for it to take effect.

If users are on a mobile app older than v.9.5, they will continue to see AI entry points regardless of the policy. Upgrading the app resolves this issue.

A policy with both Users or Groups criteria and other criteria type has been created, and users can still see AI entry points. Is that expected?

Yes, only policies configured to match just the Users or Groups criteria hide the AI entry points. In all other cases (from a user’s perspective), users will still see the AI entry points, and only certain files and folders they have access to will be covered by the policies.

AI Safeguards - Overview

What Are AI Safeguards?

AI Safeguards enable administrators to govern how AI operates within Egnyte. Policies control which files the AI can use to generate responses and which users can access AI-powered functionalities.

Two distinct governance needs are addressed:

  • Data Visibility: Policies control which files are excluded from AI visibility, preventing them from being used to generate responses. This applies within Egnyte Collaborate and requests processed through the Egnyte MCP Server.
  • Access Control: Policies restrict which users and groups have access to AI-powered functionalities. This supports phased rollouts and permanent exclusion of groups that do not need AI access. This feature is available on the Essentials, Elite, and Ultimate plans, or for those who have purchased the AI Add-on. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Benefits

  • Prevent information from sensitive files such as contracts, HR records, and classified documents from appearing in AI responses.
  • Roll out AI access to selected early adopters and expand coverage gradually over time.
  • Control AI access per user and/or group without changing underlying file permissions.
  • Sanitize content returned from the Egnyte MCP Server to external AI tools.
  • Monitor AI activity across the domain before enabling any restrictions, using Report Only policies.

Common Use Cases

The following use cases are covered step-by-step in AI Safeguards - Admin Guide.

  • Initial rollout: AI access is restricted to a single group during initial deployment. Access can be expanded to additional groups over time by extending the blocking policy.
  • Department-scoped access: Departments can use AI but only within their designated folder. Cross-department access and all other users are blocked.
  • Monitoring mode: Report Only policies are used to observe AI activity across the domain before any restrictions are applied.
  • Sensitive content protection: AI is prevented from processing files classified as Confidential or PII, with selected compliance teams retaining access.
  • Competitive confidentiality: Metadata tags are used to prevent AI from surfacing a client’s files to users working on a competing project.

Overview

AI Safeguards policies are managed in Settings -> Configuration -> AI -> AI Safeguards section. Administrators can create, edit, reorder, and change the state of policies from this page.

Policy Criteria Types

Each policy is built using one or more criteria. Four types are available:

  • Location: One or more folders. All subfolders are included by default when a parent folder is selected.
  • Content Classification policies: Classification tags applied by Secure & Govern Content Classification Policies. Exclusive to the Ultimate plan.
  • Metadata tags: Metadata applied to files in Egnyte Collaborate. Currently, single-select, multi-select, string, integer, and label metadata types are supported.
  • Users/Groups: Specific users and group identifiers.
    • Multiple criteria rows within a single policy are joined with AND. All rows must match for the policy to activate.
    • Multiple values within a single criterion use OR. Only one value needs to match.

Policy States

Each policy can be in one of three states. Administrators can choose whether a newly saved policy defaults to Active or Report Only.

  • Active: Restrictions are applied.
  • Mask: The content matched by the selected Content Classification policies is removed and replaced with a label, such as < SSN > or < ACCOUNT_NUMBER >, before the file is sent to AI. Users will still get answers from the rest of the document.
  • Report Only: Restrictions are tracked for reporting but not applied. Useful for monitoring activity before restrictions.
  • Inactive: Restrictions are not applied. Mask is available when the classification criterion in the AI Safeguard policy is set to “included in.”

Policy Priority and Evaluation

Policies are evaluated sequentially, starting from Policy 1. The priority number is shown on the left of each policy row. Evaluation behavior depends on the matching policy’s state:

  • Report Only: Evaluation continues to the next policy after a match. Multiple Report Only policies can match the same request, each adding a Flagged audit report entry.
  • Block or Mask: Evaluation stops immediately once a match is found. One Blocked report entry is created. No further policies are evaluated for that request. Report Only policies intended to monitor the same scope as an Block policy must be placed above it in the priority list. An Block policy stops evaluation. Report Only policies placed below Block policies will not be evaluated for requests that the Block policy already matched.

Priority order can be changed using the drag-and-drop handle on the left of each policy row.

Special Behavior: Users/Groups-Only Policies

A policy using only the Users/Groups criterion enters a special mode. In addition to restricting AI processing, it removes all AI-related entry points from the user interface for matched users. AI Assistant, Agents and all other AI surfaces are hidden entirely, with no visible indication that a restriction is in place.

External tools connecting through the Egnyte MCP Server can still connect on behalf of these users. AI Safeguards policies apply to all inbound requests and the content returned is sanitized accordingly.

This mode is recommended for hard blocks during initial rollout or for groups that should never have AI access.

Audit Reports

Audit reports are available in the Reports panel under Audit → AI Safeguards:

Users can navigate to either of the reports, click on New Report, fill in the details, and Submit to create a report.

  • Blocked: Files considered for use by the AI but blocked from generating responses. Files that matched a policy set to Mask also appear in this report.
  • Flagged (report-only): Files that would have been blocked, but were not, because the matching policy was set to Report Only. Useful for investigating activity without disrupting workflows.
  • Both Blocked and Flagged (report-only) reports include details such as Date, Policy Name, File, Requestor Name, and Requestor email.
  • Policy Settings: Logs when an AI Safeguards policy is created, modified, deleted, or reordered. The report includes Date, Performed by, IP Address, Action, Policy Name, Position, Policy Active, Match action, Old Criteria, and New Criteria.

User Experience

When a user interacts with a file protected by an Block policy (and they are not excluded entirely from using AI), the file is not processed and the user is informed that the item is protected by AI Safeguards. Files restricted through the MCP Server are not returned to the requesting application.

When a file matches a policy set to Mask, the file is processed with the matched content replaced by labels such as < SSN >. Users receive an answer based on the remaining content, and the masked values are not available to AI.

If user would like an excluded file to be available for AI processing:

  • Contact the Egnyte administrator to find out why the file is restricted.

  • Request policy configuration adjustments.

When at least one Block or Mask policy is in place on the domain, the “AI Safeguards active” indicator is shown in the AI Assistant panel.

Additional information is shown in the context menu, and when the user tries to interact with a restricted file.

Limitations

  • Users on Egnyte for Android older than v.9.5 or Mobile App for iOS older than v.9.5 may still see AI entry points even when a Users or Groups-only policy applies to them.
  • Changes to policies may take up to one hour to finish processing and take effect.
  • Because certain file formats, such as spreadsheets (XLSX, CSV), are inherently complex, they are blocked automatically whenever a Mask policy is triggered.
  • Since Mask policies redact sensitive information prior to analysis, generated outputs for heavily sanitized documents or PDFs might lack complete context or detail.

AI Safeguards – Admin Guide

This guide covers how to configure AI Safeguards policies. For a feature introduction and settings overview, refer to AI Safeguards - Overview.

This feature is available on the Essentials, Elite, and Ultimate plans, or for those who have purchased the AI Add-on. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Skip Ahead To…

Use Case 1: Monitoring Mode — Visibility Before Enforcement

Use Case 2: Initial Rollout — IT Group Only

Use Case 3: Continuous Governance — Department-Scoped Access

Use Case 4: Sensitive Content Protection

Use Case 5: Competitive Confidentiality — Metadata-Based File Hiding

Additional Resources

Getting Started

Navigate to Settings → Configuration → AI. The AI Safeguards section is at the bottom of the page.

Select New policy to open the policy creation modal. Each policy requires a name and at least one criterion. Use the Criteria section to select the criterion type, the matching direction (Included in or Not included in), and the specific values. Additional criteria rows can be added with the Add criteria button. Each additional row is joined with AND condition.

The Summary section at the bottom of the dialog shows a plain-language description of what the policy will do. Use the dropdown on the Create button to save the policy as Active by clicking Create or save as Report Only by clicking the dropdown and selecting the Create a ‘Report only’ policy.

  • It is recommended to begin with Report Only policies to observe what would be restricted before enforcing any restrictions.

  • Policies can be switched between Active and Report Only states at any time from the policy list.

  • Report Only policies that monitor the same scope as an Active policy must be placed above Active policy in the priority list.

  • An Active policy stops evaluation. Report Only policies placed after the Active policy will not execute for requests that the Active policy already matched.

Use Case 1: Monitoring Mode — Visibility Before Enforcement

Goal: Understand how AI is being used across the domain before applying any restrictions. All policies are set to Report Only. No requests are blocked. This phase is recommended to run for several weeks to build a report and understand user activity.

Policy set

Create the following four policies. Because all are Report Only, evaluation continues through all of them for every request and the order does not affect which entries are generated.

  • Create a policy named Sensitive folder access. Add one criterion: Location Included in [/Shared/Legal, /Shared/Finance, /Shared/HR]. Save the policy as Report Only.
  • Create a policy named Classified content access. Add one criterion: Content Classification Included in [Confidential, PII, Sensitive]. Save the policy as Report Only.
  • Create a policy named Metadata-tagged sensitive files. Click on the Tags field to define the metadata criteria.
  • In the metadata criteria selection, choose Policy Tags > Policy Tags in[restricted, internal-only]. Click on Confirm.
  • Click on the Create dropdown -> Create a ‘Report only’ policy.
  • Create a policy named All non-IT AI usage. Add one criterion: Users/Groups Not included in [IT]. Save the policy as Report Only.
Result

When switching any of these policies to Active, place any remaining Report Only policies covering the same or overlapping scope above the active policy. An Active policy stops evaluation. Therefore, Report Only policies placed after the Active policy will not execute for requests that the Active policy already matched.

In this example, the Classified content access policy was switched to Active and moved below all Report Only policies.

How Requests Are Evaluated
  • Because all policies are Report Only, evaluation continues through all four policies for every request. A single request can match multiple policies and generate a Flagged entry for each policy.
  • An IT user accessing an unclassified file outside the sensitive folders does not match any policy and produces no report entries at all.
  • No entries appear in the Blocked report throughout this phase due to not having any Active policies.
Report Entries
  • Flagged: every request matching any configured scope. A single request can generate multiple Flagged entries if it matches several policies.
  • Blocked: empty throughout this phase.
Transitioning to Enforcement

Once enough data has been gathered and reviewed, convert selected policies to Active accordingly to the business needs. Keep any Report Only policies covering the same or overlapping scope above the newly Active policy in the list to continue generating Flagged entries alongside the new Blocked entries.

Back to Top…

Use Case 2: Initial Rollout — IT Group Only

Goal: Restrict AI access to a named administrator group during initial deployment. All other users are blocked.

Policy set
  • Create a policy named Block all non-IT users. Add one criterion: Users/Groups - Not included in [IT]. This blocks every user who is not a member of the IT group. Save the policy.
  • Optionally, create a second policy named Track IT AI activity. It would generate a Flagged report entry for every AI request made by members of the IT group. One could use it to track IT Group’s activity but it’s not mandatory and can be omitted, if the user only wants to apply restrictions with the Block all non-IT users policy.
  • If user decide to still have this policy, add one criterion: Users/Groups - Included in [IT]. Place this policy above the blocking policy in the priority list. Save the policy as Report Only.
Result

To expand access over time, add groups and individual users to the values in the blocking policy. There is no need to create additional policies.

How Requests Are Evaluated
  • IT user making an AI request: the optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. Because it is Report Only, evaluation continues to the next policy. The blocking policy does not match because Not included in [IT] is false for IT members. The request is permitted.
  • Any other user making an AI request: the optional tracking policy does not match, no activity is logged and evaluation continues. The blocking policy matches and the request is blocked.
Report Entries
  • Flagged: IT user activity only. Populated only if the optional tracking policy is configured. Skipping the Report only policy leaves the Flagged report empty for this use case.
  • Blocked: All attempts from users that are not part of the IT group. Back to Top…

Use Case 3: Continuous Governance — Department-Scoped Access

Goal: Allow specific departments to use AI only within their designated folder. HR staff may use AI against files in /Shared/HR and Finance staff in /Shared/Finance. Cross-department access is blocked and all users outside of HR and Finance are blocked from access to AI entirely.

Policy set

  • Create a policy named Block HR outside /Shared/HR. Add two criteria: Users/Groups Included in [HR Group], and Location Not included in [/Shared/HR]. This policy executes when an HR Group member accesses any folder other than /Shared/HR. Save the policy.

  • Create a policy named Block Finance outside /Shared/Finance. Add two criteria: Users/Groups Included in [Finance Group], and Location Not included in [/Shared/Finance]. Save the policy.

  • Create a policy named Block all other users. Add one criterion: Users/Groups Not included in [HR Group, Finance Group]. This catch-all is required. Without it, users outside of both departments, pass through the first two policies without a match and have unrestricted AI access. With this policy, they will not have access to AI-powered capabilities anywhere in the platform. Save the policy.

  • Optionally, create a fourth policy named Track all HR and Finance activity. Add one criterion: Users/Groups Included in [HR Group, Finance Group] with no location filter. The absence of a location filter is deliberate to captures all HR and Finance requests, including permitted ones inside their own folders that would otherwise produce no report entries. Place this policy at the top of the list, above the three blocking policies. Save the policy as Report Only.

  • This policy set assumes each user belongs to at most one of the listed department groups.

  • A user who is a member of both HR Group and Finance Group will be blocked from /Shared/Finance by the HR policy.

Result

When adding a new department, with intention for it to follow the same access pattern, first create a new blocking policy following the same pattern:

Block Group_ABC outside /Shared/Group_ABC with two criteria: Users/Groups Included in [Group_ABC], and Location Not included in [/Shared/Group_ABC]. Save the policy and place it above the catch-all policy.

Then, update the catch-all policy to also include Group_ABC. Failing to update the catch-all means the new group is blocked across all folders by that policy, including /Shared/Group_ABC.

Then, if the user also created the Report Only policy for tracking activity and want to track Group_ABC’s activity too, extend it with Group_ABC.

How Requests Are Evaluated
  • HR member accessing /Shared/HR: The optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. The HR blocking policy does not match because the user is inside their permitted folder.
  • The Finance blocking policy does not match because the user is not in Finance Group and does not try to access /Shared/Finance either. The catch-all does not match because the user is in HR Group. The request is permitted.
  • Finance member accessing /Shared/Finance: The same logic as in point above applies. The request is permitted.
  • HR member accessing /Shared/Finance: The optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. The HR blocking policy matches because the user is in HR group and the location is not /Shared/HR. Evaluation stops. The request is blocked. The Finance blocking policy and catch-all are not evaluated for this request.
  • Finance member accessing /Shared/HR: The same logic as in point above applies. The request is blocked.
  • Any other user making a request: The optional tracking policy does not match. The HR and Finance blocking policies do not match. The catch-all matches and evaluation stops. User is not granted access to AI-powered capabilities.
Report Entries
  • Flagged: All HR and Finance requests, both permitted and blocked, if the optional tracking policy is configured.
  • Blocked: HR and Finance members accessing folders outside their designated folder. Back to Top…

Use Case 4: Sensitive Content Protection

Goal: Prevent AI from processing files classified as Confidential or PII for most users. A dedicated Compliance Group retains access. All classified-content activity can optionally be logged.

Policy set
  • Create a policy named Block non-Compliance access to classified content. Add two criteria: Users/Groups Not included in [Compliance Group], and Content Classification Included in [Confidential, PII]. This blocks any user outside the Compliance Group from using classified files in AI responses. Save the policy.
  • Create a policy named Block classified content in Legal folder. Add two criteria: Location Included in [/Shared/Legal], and Content Classification Included in [Confidential, PII]. The AND logic means this policy will execute when a file is within /Shared/Legal folder and carries a Confidential or PII classification. This blocks even the Compliance Group from using classified content in the Legal folder. Save the policy.
  • Optionally, create a third policy named Track all access to classified content. Add one criterion: Content Classification Included in [Confidential, PII]. Place this policy above both Active policies. This policy generates a Flagged entry for every classified-content AI request, including permitted Compliance Group activity that would otherwise produce no report entries. Save the policy as Report Only.
Result
How Requests Are Evaluated
  • Compliance Group member accessing a Confidential file outside /Shared/Legal: The optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. Evaluation continues. The first blocking policy does not match because the user is in the Compliance Group. The second blocking policy does not match because the file is not in /Shared/Legal. The request is permitted.
  • Regular user accessing a Confidential file: The optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. Evaluation continues. The first blocking policy matches because the user is not in the Compliance Group and the file is classified. Evaluation stops. The request is blocked. The second blocking policy is not evaluated for this request.
  • Compliance Group member accessing a Confidential file inside /Shared/Legal: The optional tracking policy matches and logs the activity. Evaluation continues. The first blocking policy does not match. Evaluation continues. The second blocking policy matches because the file is in /Shared/Legal and is classified. Evaluation stops. The request is blocked.
  • Any user accessing a non-classified file in any folder: No policy matches. The request is permitted and produces no report entries.
Report Entries
  • Flagged: Every classified-content access regardless of outcome, if the optional tracking policy is configured. Without it, Compliance Group access produces no report entries.
  • Blocked: Non-Compliance users accessing classified files, and Compliance users accessing classified files in /Shared/Legal. A Compliance user accessing a classified file in /Shared/Legal appears in both reports simultaneously. The optional tracking policy generates a Flagged entry and the Legal folder policy generates a Blocked entry for the same request.

Back to Top…

Use Case 5: Competitive Confidentiality — Metadata-Based File Hiding

Goal: Prevent AI from surfacing one client’s materials to users working on a competing account. An advertising agency manages files for competing clients. Files belonging to each client are tagged with a client-specific metadata value in Egnyte Collaborate. Policies use the Metadata tags criterion to ensure that users working on one account cannot use AI on files tagged as belonging to a competing client.

Policy set
  • Create a policy named Block Taz Industries team from Acme Corp files. Add two criteria: Users/Groups Included in [Taz Industries Account Group ], and Metadata tags in i[Client > Client Name: Acme Corp]. This blocks Taz Industries Group members from using AI on any file tagged with the Acme Corp client tag. Save the policy.
  • Create a policy named Block Acme Corp team from Taz Industries files. Add two criteria: Users/Groups Included in [Acme Corp Account Group ], and Metadata tags in [Client > Client Name: Taz Industries]. Save the policy.
Result

This pattern extends to any number of competing clients. Add one policy per combination of Group and competing client tag.

How Requests Are Evaluated
  • Taz Industries Group member accessing a file tagged client: Acme Corp: The first policy matches because the user is in Taz Industries Account Group and the file carries the Acme Corp tag. Evaluation stops. The request is blocked.
  • Acme Corp Group member accessing a file tagged client: Taz Industries: The first policy does not match. The second policy matches because the user is in Acme Corp Account Group and the file carries the Taz Industries tag. Evaluation stops. The request is blocked.
  • Taz Industries Group member accessing a file tagged client: Taz Industries: Neither policy matches because the user is working on their own client files. The request is permitted.
  • Acme Corp Group member accessing a file tagged client: Acme Corp: The same logic applies symmetrically. The request is permitted.
Report Entries
  • Flagged: No Flagged entries are generated for this use case. No Report Only policies are configured.
  • Blocked: Any Group member attempting to use AI on a competing client file. Back to Top…

  • AI Safeguards - Overview
  • AI Safeguards - FAQ

AI-Driven Metadata Tags – Trainable Classifiers

Egnyte provides powerful capabilities to create and manage metadata tags. The metadata tags can then be used to search, sort, and filter files and folders. Trainable classifiers provide a new way to apply metadata tags at scale by combining the power of AI-based classification and Egnyte’s robust metadata tagging framework.

This feature allows Power Users and Administrators to supply seed files that are used by the classifier to learn what the target files contain. Once trained, the classifier can then apply a user-defined tag to all matching files within the folder(s) specified by the user. Any Power User that has Full permissions on a folder can create a new classifier and apply it to any folders that they have full permissions on.

Once a classifier has been created and applied to a folder (or a set of folders), all matching files or folders will get the tag automatically applied to them. In addition, any new files or folders, that are added in the future, will be processed by the classifier and the tags will be automatically applied to any items that match. Multiple classifiers can be created and applied to the same folder if needed.

A user can also see the list of all classifiers already created (including ones created by other users), and can apply any existing classifier to their folders (provided they have full permission on those folders).

This feature is available for Platform Enterprise plans.

Skip Ahead To…

Creating A Classifier

Best Practices to Train the Classifier

Steps to Train The Classifier

Continue Training A Classifier

Activating Or Deactivating A Classifier

Edit Or Delete A Classifier

Tagged Files

Remove Applied Tags

Limitations

Creating A Classifier

A Power User or an admin can create a classifier.

  • Navigate to the Settings > Metadata Tags > Trainable Classifier Tags menu.
  • Click on Add new Classifier.
  • On the Classifier details screen, user can specify the following:
    • Name: Name of this classifier.
    • Smart tag: It is the metadata tag that will be applied to matching files.
    • Description (Optional): Description for the trainable classifier.
    • Folder(s): These are the associated folders in which, files will be processed and tagged by the classifier. In order to associate folders with the classifier, click on the Select Folder(s) button and choose the folders.
    • A user can only choose folders where they have full permissions or higher.
    • Seed content: It is a folder that contains all the files that will be used to train the classifier. In order to provide the seed content for training the classifier, click on the Select Folder button in the seed content section.
      • Minimum of 100 files are required in the selected folders for the classifier to be created.
      • In addition, at least 20 files must be provided as seed for training the classifier.
      • Egnyte recommends using at least 50 files for seed and 300 files in the scope folder(s).
      • OCR can be performed for trainable classifiers only when the OCR feature is enabled for the domain.
  • Once the folders and seed have been specified, click on Save Changes. The screen would change to indicate that the classifier is being created. The classifier status would say Creating, and Estimated Accuracy would show Unknown. At this point, the classifier is processing the seed files.

Once the processing is complete, the status will change to Inactive. It may take several minutes depending on the length and complexity of files. The user may close this screen and come back later to check the status.

Back to Top…

Best Practices to Train the Classifier

  • Include all document types in training: Make sure the documents being used for training include every kind of structure, format, quality, and wording that the real documents might have. If the actual documents are different from what the classifier is trained on, the classifier won’t work well.
  • Try to have about the same number of examples for each document category (Target and Non-Target). If one group is much bigger, the classifier may just learn to pick that one hurting accuracy for the smaller group.
  • Do not mix similar documents in different categories: Avoid putting nearly identical documents into both categories. This can confuse the system and hamper the reliability of the outcomes.
  • Only classify documents that are truly different in their structure or purpose, not small variations of the same form or template. The system needs obvious differences to learn from.
Back to Top…

Steps to Train The Classifier

Once the classifier status has changed to Inactive, the user can start interactively training the classifier to increase its accuracy.

  • Click on the Start training link.
  • It will start a training session. Each training session consists of manually providing feedback on five files.
  • It is highly recommended that the user completes at least 4 training sessions (20 files) to get a better measure of classifier accuracy. The reported estimated accuracy of the classifier fluctuates widely for the first few sessions.
  • After clicking on Start Training button, the classifier would show a file in the preview area and ask whether this file belongs to the class of documents the user is trying to train the classifier to recognize.
    • Click Yes or No as appropriate.
    • Users can also click on Stop Training to abandon this training session. They can start a new training session later as described in the following sections.
  • After responding to the Yes or No questions for five files, the user can choose to Complete the training session. Completing a session would save the changes and display an estimate of the classifier accuracy.
  • The user can choose to continue training by clicking Next training session, or finish training, or Activate the classifier which automatically finishes training and starts tagging all files that match within the folders they had selected.
Back to Top…

Continue Training A Classifier

The user can see the list of all AI trainable classifiers by navigating to:

  • Settings > Metadata Tags > Trainable Classifier Tags To further train a classifier created earlier:

  • Click on the classifier’s name to expand it, and then click on Continue Training next to the Estimated Accuracy. Continue training until the desired accuracy is reached. Egnyte recommends training every classifier for at least four sessions. Estimated accuracy measure may fluctuate widely during the first few training sessions.

Back to Top…

Activating Or Deactivating A Classifier

Activating a classifier will start applying tags to all files that match the classifier and are in the specified folders. An inactive classifier can be activated by clicking on the Activate link next to the status.

Once activated, the classifier will continue to examine any new files being added to those folders and apply tags as needed.

Similarly, an Active classifier can be deactivated by clicking on the Deactivate link.

Back to Top…

Edit Or Delete A Classifier

A classifier can be edited by the creator or by an admin.

To edit a classifier:

  • Navigate to Settings > Metadata Tags > Trainable Classifier Tags, and click on the Edit icon for the specific classifier to edit. Once the edit dialog opens, the user can modify the Name, Smart Tag, Description, and associated folders.

Changing the tag does not affect any of the files that are already labeled with the old tag. The new tag is applied only to the files tagged after the change is made.

If a folder is removed from the scope of this classifier, any files already tagged within that folder remain unaffected. However, no new files will be tagged on the folder that is now removed from the classifier scope.

Similarly, the user can also delete a classifier by clicking on the delete icon.

  • Editing a classifier does not affect any files that have already been tagged. Any changes made only take affect for new files.

  • If a classifier is deleted, any files that have already been tagged by the classifier retain their tags.

Back to Top…

Tagged Files

Users can view all tagged files by clicking on Show all Tagged Files

Click on Show tagged files and all the files tagged by the classifier along with the ones manually tagged with the same metadata tag will be listed.

The filters will be automatically applied and the files will be listed in the search results.

Once files are tagged, they can also be searched using the Egnyte’s search functionality.

Additionally, if a file is opened in the preview pane, the user can also see & edit all tags assigned to the file in the tags section.

Back to Top…

Remove Applied Tags

  • Click Remove applied tags to automatically remove tags from files that were tagged by the classifier.
  • Click on Remove to confirm.

Limitations

  • The maximum number of seed files that will be considered is 100. If the selected folders contain more than 100 files, the additional files will be ignored.
  • Estimated accuracy measurement may fluctuate widely until at least four training sessions are complete.
  • ​​​​Files containing only the image content are currently not supported for trainable classifiers. ​​​
Back to Top…

Bring Your Own AI Model - BYOM (Limited Availability)

Egnyte offers Bring Your Own Model (BYOM) capability to its users. Enabling customers to connect their own language models to use Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

This gives organizations more control over how their content is analyzed, summarized, or processed based on the models they trust and prefer to use. Currently, Egnyte supports OpenAI and Anthropic as the providers.

With BYOM, teams can take advantage of custom-tuned models that better understand their specific domain or compliance needs. It also gives companies more flexibility especially for those already investing in AI models.

For certain customers, BYOM provides a way to bring AI closer to their internal policies without giving up the benefits of Egnyte’s platform.

This feature is currently in Limited Availability for all customers having the Platform Plans and AI add-on. To request this feature, contact our Products team.

Connect a Model

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • Click on Connect model.
  • Enter the model details and click on Validate & Save.
    • Provider: Select the provider from the dropdown. Currently, Egnyte supports OpenAI and Anthropic as the providers.
    • Model: Select the model from the dropdown. All the models supported by OpenAI and Anthropic are listed here.
    • API-Key: Enter the API key for the model. The key will be encrypted and stored securely.
    • If an incorrect API key is entered, the user will see an error message.
    • Once a valid key is entered and saved, the model will be connected. When a customer is using their own AI model on Egnyte, it is essential to note that data handling and exposure are governed by the terms and policies of their model provider. Egnyte strongly recommends reviewing their terms and conditions to understand how their data may be used or stored.

Edit the Connected Model

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • Click on Edit.
  • Make changes to the model details and click on Validate & Save.
  • The edited model will then be connected.

Remove the Connected Model

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • Click on Remove.
  • Click on Remove to confirm.

Enable or Disable Model Selector

Admins have the option to choose if the users should be able to select their preferred Large Language Model from the chat input box.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> AI.
  • User the toggle under Models to enable or disable the setting.
  • Click on Save changes.

Configuration Agent

The Configuration Agent helps administrators assess an existing account configuration and suggest new configuration by translating natural language requests into action suggestions.

The agent always returns action suggestions that must be manually reviewed and approved by an administrator before they take effect. Every executed action is audited under the approving administrator’s identity, so the account’s audit trail remains complete and accurate.

The Configuration Agent currently supports:

  • Content Classification policies
  • Content Safeguards policies
  • AI Safeguards policies
  • Document Labelling policies
  • Content Lifecycle policies
  • S&G User Account configuration Functional coverage is being actively expanded. If you would like to participate in early access for the broadened capability scope, please contact the Egnyte Products team.

Accessing the Configuration Agent

Select Configuration Agent from the dropdown list in the sidebar.

Additionally, the agent can be invoked from Secure & Govern via the Create With AI action pill under settings for supported capabilities.

How It Works

The Configuration Agent follows the same principle across every request:

  • The administrator describes what they want in plain language.
  • The agent interprets the request and returns one or more action suggestions.
  • The administrator reviews the suggested actions and approves or rejects them.
  • Approved actions are executed and recorded in the audit trail under the approving administrator. Depending on the pricing plan, some capabilities may not be available. In those cases, the agent can suggest alternative approaches. For example, for domains on the Elite plan, AI Safeguards policies can instead use criteria such as location or metadata and not Sensitive Content tags, which are only available on the Ultimate plan.

Use Cases

The following list outlines examples of use cases the agent currently covers:

1. Configuring Policies (Find & Protect)

In a Find & Protect workflow, the agent assists with creating Content Classification policies to locate information, and then Content Safeguards and AI Safeguards policies to restrict access to it.

The agent can help build the following policy types:

  • Content Classification – Term Dictionary
  • Content Classification – Regex Dictionary
  • Content Classification – Custom Policy
  • Content Safeguards – Restriction Policy
2. Evaluating Domain’s Existing Configuration

This use case is especially relevant for accounts that have already configured Secure & Govern where:

  • Administrators do not have time to review those settings due to competing priorities
  • The IT team has evolved over time and newer administrators lack the original situational context
  • Administrators are not comfortable evaluating the settings on their own The agent reviews the current configuration and summarizes it in plain language, helping the team understand what is in place before making any changes.
3. Clarifying Questions and Fallback

If the agent does not have all the details required to prepare an action suggestion, it asks additional clarifying questions and refines its response based on the answers provided.

If an administrator asks the agent to configure a capability that is not yet supported, the agent responds with a link to the relevant help desk documentation.

4. Reverting an Action

After an administrator confirms the execution of an action, they can ask the agent to undo it. The agent returns a corresponding revert action for the administrator to confirm.

5. Shortcut to Egnyte Support

When the agent detects that an administrator is facing a problem, rather than simply requesting an action proposal or when human assistance is explicitly requested, it displays an additional message with a button to create a ticket for the Egnyte Support team.

6. Content Lifecycle and S&G User Account Configurations

The agent supports Content Lifecycle and S&G User Account configurations, expanding the functional coverage to those areas of the Product. Users can ask queries, such as:

  • Please verify which S&G notifications I am subscribed to
  • I would like to archive all files that were created more than 10 years ago
7. Alert, Issue, and Permission Review Configurations

The agent supports Alert, Issue and Permission Review configurations. Examples of prompts for these areas are:

  • Help me create an alert for public links with a High severity

Contract Analyst - Getting Started Guide (Limited Availability)

Contract Analyst can extract key terms, uncover risks, and reveal patterns, giving users a clear, comprehensive view of their contracts. To ensure the most effective and streamlined experience, following the testing steps listed below is highly recommended.

This feature is currently in Limited Availability for all customers having the AI add-on. To request this feature, contact our Products team.

Skip Ahead To…

Create a Dedicated Test Folder (All Testers)

Populate the Test Folder (All Testers)

Activate and Configure Contract Analyst (Egnyte Administrator Task)

Processing and Access

Explore the Dashboard

Review Excluded Files

Additional Resources

Create a Dedicated Test Folder (All Testers)

Start by creating a new, dedicated folder within the Egnyte domain for the initial setup (example: Contract Analyst Test Files). Avoid using a primary, large production contracts folder initially.

Why this dedicated folder approach?

  • Simplified Permissions: Administrator can more easily grant the required access (for example, Editor or Full) to all designated testers for this single folder.
  • Focused Testing: Using a curated set of contracts allows for targeted testing and validation of key features and contract types.
  • Safety & Support: A dedicated folder keeps testing separate from the production files reducing risks and simplifying troubleshooting without impacting live data.
Back to Top…

Populate the Test Folder (All Testers)

  • Gather a representative sample of contracts for analysis.
  • Ensure all contracts are in PDF format, as this is the only file type currently supported.
  • Upload the PDF contracts into the dedicated test folder created previously.
  • Optional: Users may create subfolders within the main test folder (for example, NDAs, Service Agreements, Expired Contracts) to keep their test files organized.
Back to Top…

Activate and Configure Contract Analyst (Egnyte Administrator Task)

Only a user with Egnyte Administrator privileges can perform this step.

  • Navigate to AI option in the left menu
  • Click on Create Agent -> Contract Analyst -> Use this Template
  • Alternatively, click Configure in the Contract Analyst tile.
  • A pre-filled template will appear. Enter the details and select the appropriate folder(s) as listed below. Click on Save.
    • The default name Contract Analyst in pre-filled but can be modified
    • Select an icon
    • Provide a description (optional)
    • Choose the folder(s) to include in the Contract Analyst and click on Save Note: If the Contract Analyst agent has already been created, navigate to Settings > AI Powered Features > Agents, locate the Contract Analyst agent, and click Edit.

Edit the Name, Icon, and/or Description. Ensure that no production files are included in the selected Folder(s). Users can view or add additional folders as needed. Click on Save.

Back to Top…

Processing and Access

After creating or editing the agent, the Contract Analyst agent will appear in AI-> Agents with a status as Preparing (displaying a progress percentage).

The Contract Analyst agent will be available for use once all the files have been processed.

Back to Top…

Explore the Dashboard

Once the status changes to Active, designated testers (with access to the test folder) can click the Contract Analyst tile in the AI -> Agents to open the dashboard and begin exploring.

In Contract Analyst, users can:

  • View the Key Metrics, Contracts by type, and upcoming contract expirations
  • Access the full list of contracts in the Contracts tab.
  • Review files that were not recognized as Contracts in the Excluded Files tab
Back to Top…

Review Excluded Files

Contract Analyst automatically identifies contracts, but some documents may not be recognized. The Review screen lists these files, allowing users to manually include them for analysis.

  • Access the Review Screen: From the Contract Analyzer dashboard, click the Excluded Files tab
  • Check for Excluded Files: Review the list of files from the folder that were not automatically processed. Use filters, such as Date Added and/or State or use the Search to locate the specific documents.
  • This list includes files the system did not recognize as contracts as well as files in unsupported formats.
  • Reprocess a File: To send a file for analysis, click the Reprocess button next to it. The system will process the document and add it to the Contract Analyst.
  • Unsupported documents cannot be reprocessed.
