Contract Analyst - Overview (Limited Availability)

Contract Analyst is a purpose-built AI agent designed to make contracts easy to understand, act on, and trust. It enables teams to ask questions, uncover key provisions, and identify potential risks while giving users a clear answer in plain language and a comprehensive view of their contracts.

Built to operate at scale across industries, Contract Analyst delivers the greatest impact in Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC), Financial Services, and Media and Entertainment.

This feature is currently in Limited Availability for all customers having the AI add-on. To request this feature, contact our Products team.

Benefits

  • Contract clarity for every role: Get clear, easy-to-understand answers on every single contract empowering teams to confidently understand key terms and act quickly. Responses can be presented in various formats, such as a table of deliverables or a summary of key dates, helping teams stay aligned and move work forward efficiently without overburdening legal teams
  • Automatic extraction saves time and reduces errors: Cut review time from days to minutes with an AI agent that automatically extracts key clauses and converts contract data into actionable insights. This reduces manual effort in reviews and metadata management, allowing teams to focus on higher-value work
  • All contract insights in one secure place: With Contract Analyst, there are no duplicate copies or the need to move contracts between systems. Teams get a single, secure location for contracts where anyone with access can obtain instant insights, without adding extra tools or complexity

Use Cases

Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC)

Contract scope and terms coordination: Surfaces key terms and details, identifies risks and notification obligations, and improves communication across project teams.

Media and Entertainment

Usage rights and licensing management: Extracts usage rights, deliverable terms, and expiration dates so creative agencies can understand renewals, licensing limits, or client obligations.

Financial Services

Financial agreement review: Analyzes policies, trusts, partnership terms, and promissory notes to quickly identify key terms, risks, and obligations, reducing manual review and improving productivity.

Key Capabilities

  • The Contract Analyst Dashboard displays key metrics based on selected folder(s) and related data. Metrics include Total contracts, Renewal clauses, Termination clauses, and Payment terms
  • Contracts are categorized by type and displayed in a pie chart divided into subcategories such as NDA, Employment, Sales, Licensing, and other contract types
  • Contracts are further organized by expiration date for easy tracking
  • Users can view all contracts and filter them by Folder(s), Contract Type, or Smart Tags. Options are available to export and edit the view
  • The Single Contract View allows users to see the content and details of individual contracts
    • Extracted fields appear as Smart Tags, with filtering options by selected tags. Users can click citations within each tag to view the source information
    • Users can interact with the Contracts Agent to get answers based on contract content and extracted smart tags. Users can also use prompts, such as Extract Risk Clause or others to get quicker responses.
  • The Files to Review tab lists documents that are not identified as contracts. Users can choose to reprocess files marked as Not a Contract, if needed
  • Users can configure the Contract Analyst agent to edit the name, icon, description, and folder(s). Insights are refreshed based on the folder(s) selected

File Support

  • Only PDF file formats are supported at this time

Deep Research Agent

Deep Research Agent in Egnyte helps users dive deeper into complex topics and understand detailed information. It gathers data from multiple sources, analyzes it, and presents clear insights.

Whether it’s understanding a complicated subject, reviewing detailed documents, or preparing for an important decision, the agent works in the background to bring together relevant details that might otherwise take hours to compile manually.

The agent can draw from Egnyte content and web sources to carry out in-depth research on a chosen subject. It is well-suited for creating research reports, summarizing market trends, or finding similar documents.

Egnyte Agents are available for Platform Plans with AI add-on, Elite and Ultimate Plans. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get access to this feature.

Access Deep Research Agent

Users can access the agent from the contextual entry point or from the AI -> Agents -> Deep Research Agent.

Deep Research Agent is preconfigured by Egnyte and cannot be edited or marked as inactive.

Use Deep Research Agent

  • Access the deep research agent and click on the Agent Name.
  • By default, all files and folders in Egnyte that the user has access to are selected as the source.
    • The user can select specific files and folders in Egnyte as the agent source(s). Click on the Add specific files and folders button, select up to 20 items, and click on Continue.
    • Users can also choose to enable Web search by turning the toggle on..
    • To select specific web sources, click on Add more websites. Type the URL and press enter. Click on Add more websites option again to add another web source. Click on x for any of the entered web sources to remove it.
    • The input box will display the selected source(s).
    • After selecting the source(s), enter the prompt or provide audio input for the agent. Users can choose to:
      • Improve the prompt
      • Use existing prompts from the Prompt Library
      • Include file(s) using the + icon
      • Once the user begins the interaction with the agent, the sources section will collapse. Users will not have the option to change their source(s) during a specific interaction. They can choose to start a new chat and re-select the source(s), if needed.
  • The agent will begin its research and the users will be able to view the progress in associated phases. The first is the planning phase.
  • Once the planning is complete, the agent offers options to either refine the plan or start the research. Users can click Edit plan to provide a prompt for improvements, or Start research to begin the process.
  • The agent will then move to the next phase, Research Sources. It will analyse and conduct research using the sources selected by the user. Depending on the number of sources, this process may take some time. Users can either stay on the page or continue with other activities, as the research will run in the background. A notification will be sent once the results are ready.
  • Once the research sources phase is complete, the agent moves to the next phase, which is Analyze Results.
  • The agent will create the research report after analyzing the results. The user can choose to view all the steps covered in the research under Response Progress. The users can continue to interact and ask follow-up questions as required. To initiate a fresh Research users should choose to start a new chat. Users can also access historical records as available for all the Egnyte Agents. They can share the chat with other users, as needed.

Egnyte Agents - Overview

Agents are AI tools that handle time-consuming, repetitive tasks, making life easier for users. These Agents take care of routine work like editing, writing, translating, or searching for information, so users do not have to do it manually every time.

Agents can handle specific jobs like fixing grammar or creating content. The agents are conversational, where a user can talk to the agent in natural language based on the associated file(s) input.

Users can create their agents from scratch or use the available templates. Egnyte also provides its users with the ability to configure, add, and use agents available on the Agent marketplace.

Agents can be personalized to use past chats and memories based on user preferences, and refer to them during interactions. Admins can also use Egnyte tools, such as file and folder tools, to organize files and folders through AI conversations.

  • This feature is available for Platform Plans with AI add-on and included in the New Generation Platform plans. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get this feature.

  • Currently, Egnyte tools are available to domain administrators only. Users who are not domain administrators will not see the File and Folder Tools connector and cannot use these tools in AI Assistant or in Agents.

For example, an Agent can review a document for language errors, generate content, translate a file, or get requested details from the web.

This feature is available for Platform Plans having AI add-on. It is included with the New Generation Platform plans (Elite and Ultimate).

Benefits of Egnyte Agents

There are numerous benefits to Egnyte Agents for the end-users.

  • Reduce the time users spend on manual tasks
  • Agents can easily execute repetitive work like reviewing documents, pulling information, or creating content, tasks that often take up hours each week. This means users can shift their focus on other activities requiring their input.
  • Improve consistency and accuracy in everyday work
  • Whether it’s editing text, gathering information, or responding to queries, Agents follow the defined logic every time. This leads to more consistent results and fewer mistakes compared to manual efforts that can vary from person to person or day to day.
  • Increase productivity by automating routine activities
  • By handling time-consuming tasks automatically, Agents help users accomplish more in less time. This boost in day-to-day efficiency, translates into quicker project turnarounds, and better use of working hours.
  • Help teams make faster decisions with easy access to relevant information
  • Instead of digging through documents or running multiple searches, users can rely on Agents to surface the exact information needed. This makes it easier to understand the context, compare options, and make informed decisions without delay.
  • Adapt to different roles and needs across departments
  • From HR to Legal to Operations, Agents can be configured for a wide range of tasks. They support the unique workflows of different teams working more efficiently with less effort.
  • Personalized Agents: Enable Agents to understand and retain relevant context about how tasks should be handled, so they can provide more consistent, context-aware results across interactions without requiring the same information to be provided repeatedly.
  • Egnyte tools in Agents: Admins can use Egnyte tools on Agents to complete tasks such as creating, moving, renaming, and organizing files and folders, making them more capable of handling end-to-end tasks with less manual intervention.

Egnyte MCP Server - Connecting Egnyte to ChatGPT

Egnyte is available as an app in ChatGPT enabling secure access to Egnyte files for natural language searches, summaries, and insights while respecting the organization’s permissions.

Egnyte app in ChatGPT offers several benefits:

  • Secured and governed AI usage: Use natural language to search and access authorized Egnyte files, while maintaining data security and compliance within the AI environment
  • Get fast answers from trusted files: Quickly surface insights from large content repositories, powered by the latest files stored in Egnyte
  • More streamlined experience: Speed up everyday work by reducing app switching and bringing Egnyte context together with information from other enabled applications
  • Generate smarter content: Produce summaries, documents, and analyses using own reliable, trusted business content
  • Binary File Upload and Download: Easily upload and download binary files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf) via signed URLs By bringing Egnyte context directly into ChatGPT, teams can eliminate the need to switch between systems and accelerate everyday workflows—while maintaining the governance, permissions, and security they rely on.

Egnyte MCP Server feature is available for all plans with the AI add-on enabled by default or purchased. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get access to this feature.

Setting Up the Egnyte Connector

Technical details of the Egnyte connector can be found in Egnyte’s MCP Server Documentation. Authentication is handled via OAuth 2.0, providing secure access to the Egnyte content.

Prerequisites

  • An active Egnyte account on Essential, Elite, or Ultimate plans, OR Platform Enterprise or Platform Enterprise Lite with the AI add-on

  • ChatGPT account

  • Egnyte domain name and credentials for authentication

  • To upload or download binary files such as .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, and .pdf files through the Egnyte MCP Server, the ChatGPT workspace execution environment must allow outbound network access to *.egnyte.com. Text-based operations such as search, summarization, and Q&A do not require this access and continue to work without the egress configuration

  • Workspace administrators must allow *.egnyte.com in the network egress settings for the execution environment. The exact location of this setting depends on the ChatGPT workspace configuration

  • Once the feature is enabled for a domain, all domain users can connect to and authenticate in ChatGPT. No admin controls are available to restrict access for specific users.

  • The applicable API request limits are 180 requests per minute per user and 250 requests per day per user.

Adding the Connector as an Organization Owner
  • Open ChatGPT.
  • Go to the bottom left and click on the profile icon.
  • Click on Settings.
  • Click on Apps.
  • The connected apps will be displayed. Click on Explore apps.
  • Search for Egnyte.
  • Click on the app and click on Connect.
  • Click on Continue to provide authorization.
  • Enter the domain and click on Continue to log into the Egnyte domain.
  • Click on Allow Access to provide access.
  • Egnyte will now be connected and users can Start chat.

Troubleshooting Guide

403 or Host-Blocked Error When Uploading or Downloading Files

This error occurs when the ChatGPT workspace execution environment does not allow outbound access to *.egnyte.com. Binary file transfers use Egnyte signed URLs and require this network access, while text-based operations such as search, summarization, and Q&A can continue to work.

To resolve the issue, ask the ChatGPT workspace administrator to allow outbound network access to *.egnyte.com in the workspace’s execution environment or network egress settings. After the domain is allowed, retry the file upload or download.

Egnyte MCP Server - Connecting Egnyte to Claude

Egnyte is available as a connector in Claude enabling the users to seamlessly access the Egnyte content directly within their Claude conversations.

Egnyte connector provides Claude with secure access to the organization’s content stored in Egnyte, enabling advanced document search, AI-powered analysis, and intelligent content management. Through the Egnyte MCP Server, Claude can search for files, retrieve document content, ask questions about specific documents, generate summaries, and upload or download binary files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf). It can interact with Egnyte AI capabilities like Egnyte’s AI Assistant and Agents.

Egnyte MCP Server feature is available for all plans with the AI add-on enabled by default or purchased. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get access to this feature.

Setting Up the Egnyte Connector

Technical details of the Egnyte connector can be found in Egnyte’s MCP Server Documentation. Authentication is handled via OAuth 2.0, providing secure access to the Egnyte content.

Prerequisites

  • An active Egnyte account on Essential, Elite, or Ultimate plans OR Platform Enterprise or Enterprise Lite plans with the AI add-on

  • Claude paid plans (Pro, Team, Enterprise)

  • Egnyte domain name and credentials for authentication

  • For binary file uploads and downloads: In the Claude organization settings, enable network egress for .egnyte.com. Go to Organization Settings > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation > Allow network egress, select Package managers plus specific domains, and add .egnyte.com. Without this, text-based operations (search, summarize, Q&A) will work, but file transfers will fail with a 403 host_not_allowed error

  • Once the feature is enabled for a domain, all domain users can connect to and authenticate in Claude. No admin controls are available to restrict access for specific users.

  • The applicable API request limits are 180 requests per minute per user and 250 requests per day per user.

Adding the Connector as an Claude Admin or Owner

Users can browse and add the connector directory from two different areas.

From a Chat

  • Click on the + icon on the lower left of the chat interface.

  • From the menu, select Add connectors.

  • Search for Egnyte and click on Egnyte in the search results.

  • Click on Add to your team and the connector will be added. From Settings

  • Navigate to Settings -> Connectors.

  • Click on Browse connectors.

  • Search for Egnyte and click on Egnyte from the search results.

  • Click on Add to your team and the connector will be added.

Troubleshooting Guide

403 Host_Not_Allowed Error When Uploading or Downloading Files

This error occurs when Claude’s code sandbox blocks outbound requests to *.egnyte.com.

To allow file transfers, add *.egnyte.com to the allowed domains under Organization Settings > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation > Allow network egress > Package managers plus specific domains.

Search, Summarize, and Q&A Work, File Upload or Download Fails

Text-based operations can work through the connector without network egress, but binary file transfers require direct access to Egnyte signed URLs. If egress is not configured, file transfers fail even though search and other text-based operations continue to work.

Add *.egnyte.com to the allowed domains under Organization Settings > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation > Allow network egress > Package managers plus specific domains.

Egnyte MCP Server - Connecting Egnyte to Microsoft Copilot Studio

The article provides IT Administrators with a comprehensive guide on configuring the Egnyte Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector within Microsoft Copilot Studio. It enables the Microsoft Copilot Studio to retrieve, search, summarize, upload, and download files while respecting the organization’s existing permissions and security policies.

By following these steps, admins will enable the Copilot agents to securely interact with Egnyte data using a standardized protocol.

Prerequisites

  • Licensing: An active license to access and build within Microsoft Copilot Studio
  • Permissions: Administrative privileges in both Microsoft Copilot Studio and the Egnyte domain
  • An active Egnyte account on either Gen 4: Essential, Elite, and Ultimate plans OR Gen 3: Platform Enterprise or Enterprise Lite, with the AI add-on
  • Binary file uploads and downloads through the Egnyte MCP Server require the Microsoft Copilot Studio environment and its connector configuration to allow outbound access to *.egnyte.com. This access is required because binary file transfers use Egnyte signed URLs. Text-based operations such as search, summarization, and Q&A do not require access to these signed URLs and continue to work without this configuration

Create Agent Connector

  • Sign in to Microsoft Copilot Studio.
  • Navigate to Agents -> Create Blank Agent.
  • Select Tools from the top bar menu and click on Add a tool.
  • Select Model Context Protocol (MCP) in the popup window.
  • Fill the form with the following details and click on Create:
    • Server name: for example; Egnyte MCP
    • Server description: for example; [Domain name] Egnyte MCP Server for Microsoft Copilot
    • Server URL: mcp-server.egnyte.com. Refer MCP server documentation for more details.
    • Authentication: Select Oauth 2.0
      • Type: Dynamic discovery
  • Click on Create new connection.
  • Click on Create to confirm connection creation.
  • Provide Egnyte domain name to connect and click on Continue.
  • Click on Allow Access to confirm consent. It is required to use an Egnyte Admin account.
  • Click on Add and configure to confirm.
  • The connection will be added successfully and the information can be viewed in the Details section.
  • Navigate to Tools and use the respective toggles to enable or disable a specific setting.

Test the Agent and Get the Response

Once the agent is provisioned, users can test the agent by typing their query for the agent.

The agent will provide the response based on the user’s query.

Troubleshooting Guide

File Upload or Download Fails With a Network or Host-Blocked Error

If file upload or download fails with a network, host-blocked, or similar error, the Microsoft Copilot Studio environment or connector may not have outbound access to *.egnyte.com. Binary file transfers use Egnyte signed URLs and require this access, while text-based operations such as search, summarization, and Q&A can continue to work.

To resolve the issue, verify the network configuration for the Power Platform environment and the connector used by the Copilot Studio agent. If network restrictions are enabled, allow outbound access to *.egnyte.com for the applicable Copilot Studio or connector traffic, and then retry the file transfer. For custom connectors or environments using network isolation, review the applicable Power Platform network configuration and connector settings.

Egnyte MCP Server - Overview

Egnyte MCP Server enables secure, controlled access to Egnyte content for AI-powered tools and assistants using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It acts as a bridge between Egnyte and supported AI clients, allowing them to retrieve, search, summarize, upload, and download files while fully respecting the organization’s existing permissions and security policies.

This capability allows users to work with Egnyte content using natural language within approved AI applications, without exposing data outside of Egnyte’s security framework. Access is governed through OAuth 2.0 authentication, ensuring enterprise-grade authorization and auditing.

Egnyte is available as an app in ChatGPT, enabling users to securely access Egnyte files for natural language searches, summaries, and insights. Similarly, Egnyte is available as a connector in Claude, allowing users to access Egnyte content directly within Claude conversations. In addition, any AI client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with OAuth 2.0 authentication can connect to the Egnyte MCP Server.

AI tools connected through Egnyte MCP Server, can also work with Agents. Users can see the Agents available to them and ask a specific Agent a question. The Agent answers using its own instructions and content sources. Agent responses can take up to two minutes, and the AI tool automatically checks for the response until it is ready.

  • This feature is available for customers having Essential, Elite, and Ultimate plans OR Platform Enterprise or Enterprise Lite plans with the AI Add-on purchased. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.
  • For Platform plans (Platform Team, Platform Business, Platform Enterprise Lite & Platform Enterprise, AFS (Advanced File System) and CFS (Cloud File System), the following tools are currently supported:
    • Browse the file system
    • Run advanced search across the content
    • Read and retrieve file content
    • Upload files to a folder path
    • Download files by path
    • Identify the connected Egnyte user and domain
  • The Agent list shows active Agents created by the user and shared with them. Egnyte’s built-in Agents are not included.
  • If an Agent needs the user to confirm an action or connect an external app during a run, it cannot finish through MCP. It is recommended to run that Agent in Egnyte UI instead.

Benefits

Using the Egnyte MCP Server provides the following benefits:

  • Enables AI-assisted access to Egnyte content without compromising security or compliance.
  • Ensures all access follows existing Egnyte permissions, roles, and folder-level controls.
  • Supports multiple AI clients through a standardized protocol, reducing the need for custom integrations.
  • Improves productivity by allowing users to search, summarize, and gain insights from files using natural language.
  • Keeps data within Egnyte’s control, with no direct database access or credential sharing.
  • Ability to upload and download binary files

Prerequisites

Before configuring the Egnyte MCP Server, ensure the following requirements are met:

  • An active Egnyte domain with appropriate administrative access.
  • OAuth 2.0 enabled for the Egnyte domain.
  • An AI client or platform that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
  • Network access that allows outbound HTTPS communication to the Egnyte MCP endpoint.
  • Users must have valid Egnyte accounts and permissions for the content they intend to access. Learn more about the configuration steps, authentication, available tools, data privacy, and security here.

Option to Allow External LLM Access via MCP

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> MCP Server
  • Admins can enable or disable the toggle for Allow external LLM clients to connect to Egnyte via MCP.
  • Choose the allowed apps. ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini Enterprise and Local AI Apps are checked by default.
  • Admins can also define custom allowed apps by clicking the Add button and following the instructions.
  • Other web-based AI Apps (unverified) option is disabled by default. Enabling it allows any web-based MCP client without a registered redirect URI to connect; this is highly permissive and should be used with caution.
  • Click on Save changes.
  • If any of the default allowed apps are unchecked, an additional confirmation to revoke app access will appear. Click on Revoke & Save to confirm.
  • To add a custom app, click Add. Enter the client name (required), description (optional), and redirect URLs (required).. Redirect URLs differ depending on the application and must be taken from that app’s documentation. Click on Save.
  • The custom app will then be present on the list. Click on Edit or Delete icons to make changes or remove the app.
  • On clicking the delete icon, the confirmation popup shows up. Click on Delete App to confirm and the custom app will be removed from the list. For binary file transfers (upload/download of .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf), the AI client’s sandbox or execution environment must allow outbound network access to *.egnyte.com. Text-based operations (search, summarize, Q&A) are not affected.

MCP Server Reports

Admins can access MCP Server Reports and analyze the MCP session activity across their domain.

Limitations

  • The following capabilities are currently not supported in Platform Plans (Platform Team, Platform Business, Platform Enterprise Lite & Platform Enterprise, AFS (Advanced File System) and CFS (Cloud File System)) :
    • AI-powered Q&A and summarisation on documents
    • Link sharing and project folder tools
    • Agents
  • Agent responses are asynchronous. After submitting a request to an Agent, users must check the request status to view the response.
  • Binary file upload and download requires the AI client’s execution environment to allow outbound access to *.egnyte.com. If the organization’s client sandbox restricts network egress, an admin must allowlist this domain.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

How to Verify Whether MCP Server is Available for a Domain?

Domains that do not have the feature enabled will receive an error message as “MCP Server Access Unavailable: MCP Server connectivity is not enabled for your domain. Contact your account executive or Egnyte Support to enable this feature.”

An Egnyte administrator can verify whether MCP Server is available by navigating to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> MCP Server.

  • If the MCP Server page is visible, MCP Server is available for the domain.
  • If the MCP Server page is not visible, MCP Server is not available for the domain. If MCP Server is enabled but AI Safeguards block access for a supported MCP client, the client displays an error indicating that access is restricted. In this case, the administrator must update the AI Safeguards configuration to allow the client.
How Can a Customer Request for MCP Enablement?

Customers can sign up for a trial on an eligible plan. The eligible plans include Essential, Elite, Ultimate, or Platform Enterprise / Enterprise Lite with AI add-on.

What is the Difference Between MCP Server and MCP Client?

MCP Server enables external AI tools, such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot Studio, to securely access and search content stored in Egnyte.

AI Connectors (MCP Client) enable Egnyte AI Assistant and Agents to connect to external applications and services, such as Slack, Jira, and Salesforce, to retrieve information and perform supported actions.

These are separate features with different purposes and are configured independently by the admins.

How Can Users Collect Diagnostic Information When an MCP Tool is Not Working as Expected?

If an Egnyte MCP tool is not working as expected, run the following prompt in the AI client to collect diagnostic information before contacting Egnyte Support:

I am experiencing a technical issue with the Egnyte MCP integration. Please provide a diagnostic report including: (1) the name and parameters of the Egnyte tool that failed, (2) the full verbatim response from the Egnyte MCP server, (3) the Egnyte Request ID and MCP Session ID from the response metadata, and (4) the exact timestamp of the failure, including your timezone. Format this as a structured summary that can be pasted into a support ticket.

Providing this diagnostic report with the support request can help Egnyte Support investigate and troubleshoot the issue more efficiently.

What are the steps the users shall follow if they get a 403 host_not_allowed error when trying to upload or download files through an AI client?

This error occurs when the AI client’s code sandbox or network configuration blocks outbound requests to Egnyte’s signed URLs. Binary file transfers (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf) require the client’s sandbox to allow *.egnyte.com. This is configured differently per client:

  • Claude: Organization Settings > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation > Allow network egress > select Package managers plus specific domains > add *.egnyte.com
  • ChatGPT: Check the workspace’s network/connector egress settings
  • Microsoft Copilot: Check Copilot Studio connector network policies Text-based operations (search, summarize, Q&A) are not affected by this setting.

Egnyte MCP Server - Tool Access Controls

AI apps such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot connect to Egnyte through the Egnyte MCP Server. The MCP Server offers these apps a set of tools, for example searching for files, reading a file, creating a folder, or creating a share link.

With Tool access, administrators choose which of those tools each user or group can use. A tool that’s switched off disappears from that user’s AI app interface, and Egnyte refuses any request that tries to use it anyway.

  • Tool access controls which tools are available. It does not change Egnyte permissions. Every tool continues to respect the user’s folder permissions and domain’s link sharing settings.

  • Only administrators can view and change Tool access settings.

  • Administrators always have access to every tool irrespective of the settings.

  • Tool access control is available on New Gen Essential, Elite, and Ultimate plans and legacy Platform Plans with AI Add on. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

How Tool Access Works

General access sets the default MCP Server access for all users:

  • Public: All users with MCP Server access can use all tools by default. Users and groups added to the list are limited to the tools assigned to them.
  • Restricted: Only the users and groups added to the list can use MCP Server tools. All other users have no access to the tools. Each tool is classified as Read or Write. Read tools retrieve content, while Write tools create or modify content, such as Create Folder, Upload File, and Create Link. Read and Write tools can be controlled separately, so users can be given read access without allowing their AI applications to make changes.

Ask AI Assistant and Ask Agent are added as Write tools, because they can generate documents and take actions. An admin who disables write tools to make a group read-only will lose those two as well.

If a user belongs to multiple groups in the access list, the user can use all tools allowed for any of those groups. Switching a tool off for one group doesn’t remove it from a member of another group that allows it. To block a specific person, switch the tool off on that user’s entry, which is prioritized over their groups.

Navigate and Configure Tool Access

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> MCP Server
  • Configure Tool access with General access by clicking on Public (default) or Restricted.
  • Click on Switch to confirm. Switching between Public and Restricted does not remove access for every user and group already added in the settings. Switching to Restricted with no users or groups in the list removes MCP Server tools from every non-admin user right away.
Add Users and Groups
  • Select Add, next to Restricted users and groups (Public) or Users and groups with access (Restricted).
  • In User or group, type at least two characters and select a user or a group. Built-in groups such as All Power Users are available too.
  • Use respective toggles to configure a specific tool or click on the Bulk actions dropdown to enable or disable tools in bulk. Admins can also search for the specific tool to configure. Click on Save.
  • Tool access list displays the list of user(s) and group(s) with their tool access. Each row shows the tools assigned to that entry. A user’s actual access combines every entry that applies to them and their groups.
Edit Tool Access
  • Hover over on any user or group and click on the edit icon. Alternatively, click on the three-dots icon -> Edit.
  • Make the desired edits and click on Save.
Delete Tool Access
  • Hover over any user or group and click on the delete icon. Alternatively, click on the three-dots icon -> Delete.
  • Click on Remove access to confirm. With Public access, removing a restriction gives that user or group every tool again right away, if no other entry, such as one of their groups still applies. For restricted, removing an entry takes those tools access right away.
Notification for New Tools

When a new tool becomes available on the MCP Server, Tool access shows a notification for it. Admins can review the users and groups in their list and configure the tool access for them, as needed.

Tools Accessible to End-Users

  • Tools that are switched off do not appear in the AI app’s list of Egnyte tools. In the example below, Read-only tools are displayed when write tools are disabled.
  • If the user asks the AI app to do something that needs a tool that’s switched off, it cannot perform the associated action.
  • If an app calls a switched-off tool anyway, Egnyte refuses the request with this message:
  • Tool ‘<tool name>’ is not available under your organization’s access policy. Contact your Egnyte admin.
  • If the admin makes any changes to the tool access, these changes apply to the next request; users don’t need to sign in again. Some AI apps keep a copy of the tool list, so users may need to refresh it to see the change. In Claude, open the Egnyte connector and select the Refresh tools list.
  • Any changes to Egnyte group membership can take up to an hour to apply on the Tools access. For example, a user added to a restricted group will have access to their tools for up to an hour.

Egnyte Tools in AI Conversations

Admins can enable or disable Egnyte tools in AI conversations and control when each tool can run. They can set a tool to Custom, Always Allow, Always Ask, or Deny to organize files and folders as per the configured setting.

For example, file and folder tools help users organize content by creating files and folders, copying and renaming files, moving files, and updating file metadata. Users can also use Egnyte tools to check the status of asynchronous jobs.

Currently, Egnyte tools are available to domain administrators only. Users who are not domain administrators will not see the File and Folder Tools connector and cannot use these tools in AI Assistant or in Agents.

Configure File and Folder Tools

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> AI Connectors
  • Click on Egnyte Tools tab.
  • Admins can click on the dropdown at the tool level and select the desired option (Always allow, Always ask, or Deny). Admins can also select Custom.
  • Under Custom, Admins can configure the setting for each tool by using the respective icons to Always allow, Always ask, or Deny.
  • Click on Save changes.

Use File and Folder Tools

Admins can choose to enable or disable file and folder tools using the toggle from Connectors.

Admins can ask AI to organize files and folders. AI Assistant and Agents may ask for clarification before taking an action and will execute it according to the configured setting. For example, in the scenario below, AI asks for clarification about the rename action. Because the rename tool is set to Always Ask, it also requests the user’s confirmation before renaming the files.

Known Limitations

File and Folder Tools are designed for straightforward folder organization and for renaming a small number of files within a conversation. File and folder actions work reliably for up to about 60-75 files in a single request. Larger requests often succeed, but not always: when the file service is busy the AI Assistant or Agent completes part of the work, stops, and tells you how many files it finished. They are not intended for bulk operations. Organizing large folders, or renaming files in bulk, is not supported in AI Assistant or in Agents.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant - User Guide

Egnyte incorporates innovative strategies to harness Generative AI’s full potential while safeguarding its customer’s proprietary data and aligning with specific business processes and goals.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant is an AI-powered conversational interface grounded in the company’s data.

Users can choose any of the prompts or recommended questions, use audio input or type in their question in the input bar on Egnyte’s AI Assistant. They can regenerate responses, verify answers, provide feedback, and view the chat history.

Users can leverage Egnyte’s AI Assistant to connect to external connectors such as Atlassian, Gmail, Procore, and others. The Admins can configure the required AI connectors for their users.

Use Egnyte’s AI Assistant

From Any Page on Egnyte Web UI
  • Navigate to Files or any specific folder.
  • Click on the Egnyte’s AI Assistant icon.
  • When the user opens Egnyte’s AI Assistant from the side panel while browsing a folder, that folder is automatically selected as the source context. This means their queries will prioritize content from files within that folder. Back to Top ↑
Accessing Egnyte’s AI Assistant from Left Hand Menu

The auto-scoping is applicable only on launching Egnyte’s AI Assistant from within a folder view. When accessing Egnyte’s AI Assistant from the AI option in the left menu or other entry points, the default All Sources behavior applies.

  • Navigate to Collaborate -> AI
  • Egnyte’s AI Assistant will be available for the users to interact with it. Back to Top ↑
Document Preview

The auto-scoping is also applicable when opening a document in preview. The scope is automatically set to the document that the user opens in preview. The user can continue their interaction on the document in Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Back to Top ↑

Q&A on Egnyte’s AI Assistant

Users can ask questions on Egnyte’s AI Assistant and get a response based on their queries. Users can use audio input/type the question to get a response.

They can click on any of the suggested chips to expand a set of ready-to-use prompts. For instance, they can click on Create -> Document and the corresponding prompt will be available in the input box. Users can edit the prompt as needed to create a new document.

Asking brief and specific questions generates the best answers. Multipart questions, when asked separately, generate better answers.

Users can also find specific files or folders within Egnyte’s AI Assistant. Responses to their queries may include relevant files or folders, depending on the nature of the question.

Users can choose from multiple AI models directly within the chat input box in Egnyte.

AI Assistant asks for clarification before proceeding if the query entered by the user is not clear or too broad. This eliminates the need for excessive re-prompting for the users and provides them with clearer and accurate response.

Users can always choose to skip the questions, if asked or provide their response and submit.

Select Scope and Web Search

Users can enable or disable the sources using the + icon or by clicking on the source(s) in the input box.

  • Click on the + icon
  • Use the toggle for Egnyte (enabled by default) and Web (disabled by default) to enable or disable.
  • As soon as the user enables Egnyte and web search, the sources will show up in the scope. Users can choose to add specific Egnyte and Web source(s).
  • Click on the Egnyte source or + icon -> Egnyte -> to set the scope for Egnyte sources
  • Click on Add files & folders
  • Select the desired file(s), folder(s), and click on Continue.
  • The selected source(s) will appear. Users can continue to modify by adding or removing the required items for the scope.
  • Users can currently select and add up to 20 items as the source for Egnyte’s AI Assistant.
  • If web search is enabled, click on All sources or click on the + icon -> Web
  • Enter the web address and click on + Add to add the web source(s)
  • Users can hover over a web source added and click on x to remove the sources. They can also click on Clear all to remove all the added web sources.
  • Users can also click on the Settings icon and click on Egnyte files and/or Web Search and manage the scope. The Web Search preference selected by users is remembered across new chats, so users do not need to enable Web Search each time a new chat is started. However, when the users sign in from a new browser session or device, Web Search remains disabled by default, ensuring that the preference is explicitly selected for the new session.

Back to Top ↑

Users can select up to 20 files and/or folders and interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant based on their selections.

The users can also select the desired items and click on Open AI Assistant from the context menu to begin their interaction based on the selected items.

If a user is already interacting with Egnyte’s AI Assistant and selects specific file(s) or folder(s) during the conversation, they will see the new source(s) displayed in the input box.

Back to Top ↑

Multi-File Ask on Search Results

The users can interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant on the selected files based on their search results. This enables faster access to relevant content and enhances productivity by allowing users to extract insights, summarize, or take actions on multiple files simultaneously.

Click on Upload files and select the file(s) to upload. Users can also drag, drop or paste the files.

The selected files will be saved in the user’s private folder at /Private/<username>/AI Uploads. These files are automatically tagged with the Content Source: AI Upload tag under ai content section.

Users can upload a maximum of 20 files in a single prompt.

  • Modified Date (for example, updates from last week, modified in the last month)

The agent will be tagged and can be used while interacting with AI Assistant.

Currently, Egnyte tools are available to domain administrators only. Users who are not domain administrators will not see the File and Folder Tools connector and cannot use these tools in AI Assistant or in Agents.

Scheduled Tasks

Users can write a prompt once and schedule the task for the AI Assistant to run it automatically.

  • Navigate to AI -> Scheduled Tasks

  • Click on New Task

  • Enter the Task details

    • Provide the Instruction. Users can select the source(s), tag agents, connectors, files and folders, and select the preferred model.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant does not consider password protected files and files protected using Microsoft Purview Solution (having restricted, confidential, or other protected labels) to generate responses.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant - Overview

Egnyte’s AI Assistant (formerly known as Egnyte Copilot) is an AI-powered conversational interface designed to enhance productivity and collaboration across an organization.

The users get access to Egnyte’s AI Assistant to interact with it by asking questions and receiving a response. They can use the suggested questions or prompts, use audio input or type in their own questions. Admins can also configure AI connectors for the users to connect to the external connectors, such as Atlassian, Gmail, Procore, and others.

AI Assistant can be personalized to use past chats and memories based on user preferences, and refer to them during interactions. Admins can also use Egnyte tools, such as file and folder tools, to organize files and folders through AI conversations.

In addition, users can also verify sources, regenerate responses, provide feedback, manage chat history, and use suggested questions/prompts within Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Users can create new or use existing prompts, and ask questions based on selected file(s).

Users can choose from multiple AI models directly within the chat input box in Egnyte.

Suggestions are displayed as prompt chips that users can select to ask questions or explore related topics.

  • Egnyte’s AI Assistant is available only through the AI Add-on plan. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started.

  • Egnyte uses closed models with no cross-training. Refer to the Egnyte Generative Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) Policy for more details.

Benefits & Capabilities

  • Interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant: The users get access to Egnyte’s AI Assistant that enables seamless interaction with content across the entire domain for enhanced productivity.
  • Efficient Query Resolution: Egnyte’s AI Assistant enable the user to ask questions and receive accurate, AI-generated responses in real-time, reducing the time spent searching for answers.
  • Source Verification: Users can verify the sources of information provided, ensuring reliability and transparency in the responses they receive.
  • Tailored Suggestions: Benefit from customized question suggestions that streamline the search process, helping users quickly find relevant information.
  • Response Regeneration: Users can easily regenerate responses to refine the answers to their queries, ensuring that they get the most relevant and up-to-date information.
  • Feedback Mechanism: The option enables providing feedback on responses to help improve the AI Assistant and address any queries, ensuring continuous improvement and user satisfaction.
  • Advanced Spreadsheet Analysis: This feature enables users to analyze complex spreadsheets and extract insights using natural language queries, without writing a single formula or line of code. Users can tag multiple spreadsheets, and the AI Assistant processes them in parallel to extract the exact data needed from each simultaneously.
  • Document Generation: Users can ask AI Assistant to create fully formatted documents from scratch. They can also convert between formats as well. For instance, users can convert a Word document into a polished PowerPoint presentation.
  • Personalized AI Assistant: Get responses that become more relevant to individual needs by allowing AI Assistant to use past chats, saved memories, and user preferences as context during interactions. This helps users spend less time repeating information or providing the same context across conversations.
  • Egnyte tools in AI Assistant: Admins can easily organize files and folders, update metadata, and perform other supported actions directly through AI Assistant, reducing repetitive manual work.

Prerequisites

  • The customer must have the AI add-on enabled.

Use Case

  • Construction:
    • Utilize Egnyte’s AI Assistant to quickly identify contracts and other relevant documentation specific to a project by asking questions.
  • Financial Services:
    • Retrieve and analyze financial reports, compliance documents, and investment portfolios for informed decision-making.
  • Investment Diligence:
    • Specific financial statements, legal documents, and contracts can be obtained.
  • Project Management:
    • Project managers and teams can summarize the meetings, obtain best practices and checklists, and access project plans using the feature.
  • Employee Services:
    • Employees can easily know about company policies and benefits by asking questions.
  • Public Sector:
    • Easily access policy documents and regulatory frameworks by querying the AI Assistant.
  • Marketing:
    • Identification of the market trends and patterns using the campaign performance reports, customer research studies, and market reports.
  • Life Sciences:
    • Get access to relevant case studies and research papers for a specific research project.

Known Limitations

  • This product offering works only on textual data
  • AI Assistant will not be able to provide satisfactory answers in the following scenarios:
    • Questions where aggregation or other mathematical operations are required to be executed to find the answer, eg:
      • What are the total sales for the year 2024?
    • Questions where inference needs to be drawn by considering multiple information source
      • What is the largest proposal?
      • Which district has the highest population density?
      • What was the most expensive project
    • Question related to file counts
      • How many files are present in this folder?
      • For January, how many receipts exist?
  • The following limitations are applicable on the advanced spreadsheet analysis:
    • Supported File Types : .xlsx .xlsm .xls .xlsb .csv .tsv,gsheet
    • File Size Limit: It supports files up to 64MB to ensure fast, responsive answers
    • Focuses on Data, Not Design (.xls, .xlsb): For legacy Excel files, it is laser-focused on the text and numbers. It cannot interpret visual cues like cell colors or formatting (for example, asking it to sum up the highlighted rows will not work)
    • Analysis of macro-enabled workbooks (.xlsm): AI Assistant analyzes content stored in the workbook’s last-saved state, including cell values and saved formula results. It doesn’t run embedded VBA macros. Values, sheets, or tables created by a macro may be blank or unavailable until the user runs the macro in Microsoft Excel, saves the populated workbook, and uploads it again.
    • Latest File Versions: It analyzes the data exactly as it appeared the last time the file was saved
    • Integration with AI Agents is still pending and will be available soon.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant - Summarize and Ask Questions on a Single Document

Document Summarization

Egnyte’s AI Assistant synthesizes the content using industry-leading large language models (LLMs). These models will recognize and generate the summary based on the information within the document.

To retrieve the document summary, open any of the supported files for preview and click on the Generate Summary prompt in Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

The instruction will be visible in the chat input. Users can make changes, if required.

The AI Assistant will begin processing as per the instructions provided by the user and will provide the summary of the document.

Users can Copy the instructions or Edit them to refine and generate the response.

The new response will be generated as per the new prompt.

Users can copy the response, generate answer, and provide feedback on the summary by using the thumbs-up or thumbs-down icons at the bottom of the response.

  • This feature is available on all Platform plans.

  • In domains with the AI add-on enabled, users will be able to interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant as per the source(s) selected rather than just the document in preview.

Q&A on the Document

Egnyte’s AI Assistant can be used on a single document and it allows the users to ask questions about a document using a chatbot-style interface. Users can also ask questions on complex spreadsheets and extract insights using natural language queries, without writing a single formula or line of code.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant opens by default when a user opens a document in full preview. If the user has opened any other available options, they can click on the Egnyte’s AI Assistant icon in the sidebar to utilize the feature.

At this point, users can click on the prompt to generate a summary of the document, or select other prompts. User can also provide audio input or type their questions in the chat box at the bottom.

They can click on the + icon -> Prompts to access the prompt library and insert prompts from there. Users can also click on the History icon at the top-right to access historical records.

Users can access chat history and click on any of the past conversations. They can click on the three-dots icon to Rename, Pin, or Delete a record.

Click on the New chat icon at the top-right to start a new chat.

The users can also click on Modify at the top to select another class of the document or add more tags.

Select the desired tag(s).

Click on Save.

Use Egnyte’s AI Assistant on Images

The users can also use Egnyte’s AI Assistant to ask questions on the supported images based on the textual and visual elements in the files. They can use generate summary or other prompts to get a response.

The users can also ask various other questions on the image files to get a response or use the suggested prompts once the conversation begins.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Data Confidentiality Assured While Egnyte’s AI Assistant Generates Summaries?

Egnyte remains committed to the confidentiality of the user’s data. The inputs, summaries, and

data:

  • Are not available to other customers,
  • Are not used to improve third-party models, or any third-party products or services,
  • Are not stored by third-party models
  • Are not accessible by or visible to Egnyte employees In addition, all generated summaries can only be accessed by users on the domain that have permission to view the original documents.

For more details on Egnyte’s Privacy policy, click here.

Is it possible to opt out of these AI features?

Yes. An admin user can turn off these features by navigating to the Settings -> Configuration-> AI page and then setting the AI Assistant toggle to Disabled.

Turning the toggle off will turn off both the Document Summarization as well as the Document Q&A features (if available in the plan and on the domain). It is not possible to enable/disable individual features.

Can Some Documents Be Excluded from Being Summarized?

No. The summarization feature will summarize all files when enabled. Individual files can not be excluded from summarization.

What Types of Files Can Be Summarized and Can Be Used for the Q&A Feature?

Any file where text can be extracted can be summarized, and can also be used for Q&A. This includes text documents, presentations, spreadsheets and PDF files.

Can a user Provide Feedback on these Features?

Yes, the user can provide feedback on the summary and all the responses generated by clicking on the thumbs-up or thumbs-down icons that appear below every response generated by Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

If the users provide negative feedback on a response, a pop-up appears explaining that Egnyte may review logs to investigate the issue. Users can choose to give consent or opt out. Egnyte will only use logs to address the user issue.

Do the Users Have Any Control Over the Length/Type/Format of the Summary that is Created?

Not at this time. Egnyte is looking at adding additional configuration tools for the users.

Are there any document size limitations for creating summaries?

The first 90,000 characters of a document are used to generate a summary.

Will the Summary always generate the same responses?

Responses are cached and reused. However, the cache can expire and there is a possibility that the generated responses have some variation

Are the generated summaries always accurate?

Like any AI feature, the AI-driven summary is not perfect. It can sometimes generate responses that are incorrect, or misleading. It’s important to fact-check information and not rely solely on the responses for critical decisions.

How are the Summaries and Answers Stored, And Who Has Access To Them?

Summaries are cached in memory for performance and are only visible to users who have permission to view the underlying file.

Are there any limitations associated with advanced spreadsheet analysis?

The following limitations are applicable on the advanced spreadsheet analysis:

  • Supported File Types : .xlsx .xlsm .xls .xlsb .csv .tsv
  • File Size Limit: It supports files up to 64MB to ensure fast, responsive answers.
  • Focuses on Data, Not Design (.xls, .xlsb): For legacy Excel files, it is laser-focused on the text and numbers. It cannot interpret visual cues like cell colors or formatting (for example; asking it to sum up the highlighted rows will not work).
  • Safe Analysis of Macros (.xlsm): While it seamlessly reads data from macro-enabled workbooks, it strictly analyzes the content and will not run or execute any embedded scripts or macros.
  • Latest File Versions: It analyzes the data exactly as it appeared the last time the file was saved.

Images Search and Readability for Agents and AI Assistant

Photos, scans and screenshots often hold information that never makes it into a file name. AI Image Captioning closes that gap. Egnyte automatically generates a detailed description of every newly uploaded image and saves it on the file, so image content can be found through search and used by the AI Assistant and Agents in the same way as text in a document.

Image captioning is part of Egnyte’s Context Layer, which automatically prepares content for AI by classifying, enriching and connecting files as they arrive. Captions require no setup and no manual tagging.

  • The feature is available to all the customers with the AI add-on enabled. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

  • The supported file types are PNG, JPG / JPEG, TIF / TIFF, BMP, JPX, GIF, WEBP, and HEIC with the maximum file size as 64 MB per image.

Use Cases

  • Construction and Engineering: Find job site photos by condition, equipment or progress stage, and gather visual evidence for RFIs, inspections and daily reports
  • Marketing and Creative Teams: Locate brand assets, product shots and event photos by what they show
  • Facilities and Real Estate: Search for property and maintenance photos showing a specific room, fixture or issue
  • Insurance and Claims: Locate damage photos by type of damage or affected item
  • Scanned Notes and Signage: Find whiteboard photos, labels and signs by the text written on them

How Captions are Generated

When an image is uploaded to Egnyte through any channel, such as the Web UI, the Desktop App or an integration, Egnyte sends it to an AI vision model for processing. The model examines the image and writes a description covering:

  • Objects and Equipment: for example, a yellow bulldozer, a fire extinguisher or a laptop
  • Scene and Setting: such as, a dirt construction site, an office lobby or a warehouse aisle
  • Materials and Conditions: for example, exposed rebar, standing water, mud on equipment or a cracked surface
  • Visible Text: words on signs, labels, banners, whiteboards and equipment markings
  • Notable Absences: where relevant, the caption notes what is not present, for example, no workers or safety equipment are visible The caption is saved on the file as an Egnyte Document Tag named Caption and is added to the search index. Users can open the image and open the Tags panel to view the caption.

Captions are generated shortly after upload. During periods of high upload volume, some images can take longer to be captioned, but every supported image is processed.

Captions describe people in general terms, for example, a person in a high-visibility vest. They do not identify individuals by their face, and Egnyte does not perform facial recognition on images.

Generating a Caption for an Existing Image

Images that were already in Egnyte before the feature was enabled are not captioned automatically. Users can generate a caption for an existing image on demand:

  • Open the image in the file preview and open the Tags panel. Select Auto tag. Users can also select multiple files and add captions using Egnyte’s multi-document tagging.
  • The multi-document tagging feature is available for customers on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Essentials, Elite and Ultimate plans. To request access, contact the Egnyte Products team.
  • Select Egnyte Document Tags and the caption will automatically be generated. Click on Save.
  • The caption is added to the Tags panel and to the search index within a few moments.

How Captions are Used

Search

Captions make image content searchable alongside documents. Users can find an image by describing what it shows instead of remembering its file name or folder. For example, a search for bulldozer on a dirt site or whiteboard with a sprint plan returns matching images even when the files are named IMG_4821.jpg.

In the example below, a search for photos with steel rebar bundles in a site photos folder returns the matching image. The AI Overview describes what the photo shows, using the image caption.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant

The AI Assistant uses captions to find relevant images and to answer questions about them. Users can ask questions such as:

  • Find photos in the Riverside project folder that show water damage.
  • Which site photos from last week show the crane?
  • List the event photos that show the company banner. The AI Assistant can also read the image itself when a file is selected, so captions and image content work together. Users can view the source image(s) in the answers.

In the example below, a user asks the AI Assistant which site photos show steel rebar or heavy equipment. The AI Assistant lists the matching photos with a short description of each, and notes the photo it excluded.

Agents

Agents use captions to search and reason over images within the content they have access to. This lets an agent include photos in its response such as checking site photos against a punch list, gathering inspection photos for a report, or finding product images that match a description.

In the example below, a site photo inspection agent, with a site photos folder as its source, is asked to check the photos for safety issues. The agent reviews every image and returns a table with what each photo shows and any visible safety or housekeeping concerns, then recommends which issues to check on site first.

Limitations

  • Captions are generated automatically only for images uploaded after the feature is enabled on the domain. Images that were already in Egnyte can be captioned with Auto tag, as described above. Bulk Tagging can only be done using Multi-document tagging available on eligible plans.
  • Images larger than 64 MB are not captioned.
  • Captions are generated by AI and can occasionally miss details or describe an image imperfectly. Users should verify important details by opening the image.
  • Captions do not identify people by their face.
  • Image captioning in the Egnyte Mobile Apps is a separate, on-device feature. Refer AI Image Labelling on Mobile.

Include Forms in Agents

Forms provide a structured way for users to interact with Egnyte Agents. Instead of typing free-form instructions, users fill out a predefined form, and the Agent uses those inputs to carry out a task automatically. These tasks may include submitting a feature request, filing a bug report, or drafting a product specification, and similar tasks.

This combination is useful when an organization wants to standardize how users trigger Agent workflows, ensuring the Agent always receives the right information to act on.

This feature is available for Platform Plans with AI add-on and included in the New Generation Platform plans. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

How It Works

When a user submits a form, the Agent receives the structured inputs and begins executing the associated workflow. The Agent can perform actions such as routing the submission to the right team, searching for duplicate or related records, enriching the request with additional context, and notifying stakeholders , all without manual intervention.

For example, a salesperson fills out a feature request form with the customer name, problem description, and business impact. The Agent then checks for similar existing requests, creates or updates a tracking ticket, assigns it to the right product manager, and confirms the submission back to the user.

Benefits of Using Forms with Egnyte Agents

  • Ensure Agents receive complete and consistent inputs
  • Forms guide users to provide all the information an Agent needs to act. This reduces back-and-forth and prevents incomplete submissions that would otherwise require follow-up.
  • Standardize how workflows are triggered across teams
  • Instead of each user prompting an Agent differently, forms create a uniform entry point. This makes Agent behavior more predictable and easier to manage at scale.
  • Reduce errors and missed steps
  • Required fields and structured input types, such as dropdowns, checkboxes, and date pickers prevent common mistakes that occur when users submit requests in free text.
  • Enable non-technical users to interact with Agents confidently
  • Users do not need to know how to prompt an Agent. The form handles the structure, so anyone in the organization can trigger an Agent workflow without prior training.
  • Support a wide range of business workflows
  • Forms can be configured for different use cases across departments each with its own fields, required inputs, and associated Agent actions.

Creating a Form for an Agent

Admins and Agent creators can attach a form to an Agent from within the Agent configuration interface.

  • Navigate to AI in the left sidebar and select Agents. Open the Agent to add a form to, or create a new Agent.
  • In the Agent configuration panel, select Add Form in Prompts tab.
  • Define the title of the form-based prompt which will be shown to the end user in the Agent interaction interface. It is mandatory to provide instructions to the agent, as these instructions enable the agent to understand what the form information is for. Click on Click to create form.
  • Define the form fields. For each field, specify:
    • Label: the question or prompt shown to the user
    • Field Type: Radio Button Group, Checkboxes, Dropdown, Single-Line Input (Default), Long Text, Multiple Textboxes, File Selection or Folder Selection.
    • For Single-Line Input fields, select the type
    • Required: whether the field must be completed before submission which will be highlighted if selected
  • Optionally, add a Form Title and description that is shown to users when the form opens.
  • Click on Duplicate to duplicate the question added. Click on Delete to delete the respective question.
  • Click on Add Question and continue adding the question(s). Users can click on Preview to view the form preview. They can also click on the JSON Editor to view and edit the form in JSON. Click on Apply once the form has been designed.
  • Click on Apply.
  • The form added will be available as a prompt.
  • Save the Agent. The form is now active and will appear whenever a user selects that Agent.

Interacting With a Form as a User

  • Open the Agent. The form created will be available as a prompt. Click on the prompt to fill the form.
  • The form will open. Fill in each field as prompted. Fields may include:
    • Text or paragraph inputs
    • Single or multi-select options
    • Date fields
    • File upload fields, which open the Egnyte file picker
  • For file fields, click Select File to open the Egnyte file browser. Navigate to the file to attach, select it, and click Done.
  • Once all required fields are complete, click Submit.
  • The Agent processes the inputs and responds directly in the conversation thread. Users can review the Agent’s output, ask follow-up questions, or start a new request.

Common Use Cases

  • RFI Submission: Project teams at Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) firms can submit Requests for Information (RFIs) through forms, attaching relevant drawings or specifications using the file selection field. The Agent can search the project folders for related documents and prior RFIs, and use the configured AI Connectors, such as Jira, to log and track the request through to resolution.
  • Employee Onboarding Requests: HR teams can use forms to initiate onboarding for new hires by providing details such as role, department, and start date. The Agent can generate the required onboarding documents from approved templates, organize them in the appropriate folders, and notify the relevant stakeholders, such as IT and the hiring manager using Slack or Gmail connectors, so each team can complete its onboarding tasks.
  • Feature Request: Team members from Sales or Customer Success can submit feature requests received from customers through forms, capturing details such as the customer name, problem description, and business impact. The Agent can check for duplicate or similar requests and use the configured AI Connectors, such as Jira, to create a tracking ticket for the Product Managers.
  • Bug Report: Team members can submit bug reports through forms with relevant issue details, such as steps to reproduce, expected behavior, and severity. The Agent can enrich the report with available logs and environment information, and use AI Connectors, such as Jira, to create or update the issue and assign it to the appropriate engineering team.
  • Product Requirements Document (PRD) Intake: Product Managers can use forms to provide the key inputs for a product requirements document, such as the problem statement, target users, and success metrics. The Agent can retrieve related tickets and usage data through the configured AI Connectors and use this information to draft a structured PRD for the Product Manager to review and refine.
  • Contract Review Request: Legal or Operations teams can submit contract review requests through forms, attaching the contract using the file selection field along with details such as the counterparty and review priority. The Agent can route the request to a Contract Analyst Agent and track the review status as the request moves through the workflow.
  • Document Comparison: Team members can select two files through a form, such as two versions of a contract or policy document, for comparison. The Agent can analyze the selected files and return a structured comparison directly in the conversation, highlighting the differences for review.
