Migration of Knowledge Bases to Agents

Egnyte Knowledge Bases are being retired and replaced by Agents. This is an upgrade and not a loss of capability. Existing Knowledge Bases are being automatically converted to Agents with the same file sources, behavior, and settings preserved.

For most users, nothing changes in day-to-day work. Agents answer questions the same way Knowledge Bases did. The only visible difference is their location as they now appear under the Agents section of the AI Assistant page, not a separate Knowledge Bases section.

Teams that have built integrations against the Knowledge Base API or use the Egnyte MCP Server will need to update those integrations. This article explains the associated changes.

Timeline at a Glance

Date

What happens?

July 16, 2026

In-product banner on the Knowledge Bases page announcing the migration. Helpdesk article was published.

August 5, 2026

Release notes announced that creating a new Knowledge Base now opens the Create Agent flow with a Knowledge Base template pre-selected.

By October 22nd, 2026

Existing Knowledge Bases automatically converted to Agents, domain by domain. The Knowledge Bases section in the UI is removed.

Knowledge Base API endpoints stop accepting requests on the domain. MCP tools ask_knowledge_base and list_knowledge_bases stop working on the domain.

Changes for End Users

Location of Migrated Knowledge Bases

After migration, Knowledge Bases appear in the Agents section of the AI Assistant page, under agents whose names match the former Knowledge Bases. The behavior is the same as users can ask a question and receive an answer grounded in their Egnyte content.

Required Actions for Users

None. Knowledge Bases are migrated automatically. Users do not need to recreate them, reconfigure them, or re-upload content. The files and folder paths previously connected remain connected.

Creating a New Knowledge Base Going Forward

Use Create New Agent and select the Knowledge Base template. This template is pre-configured with the same behavior Knowledge Bases had. It searches the selected Egnyte content and cites its sources. The instructions can be customized further if needed.

Shared Knowledge Base Links

Shared links for Knowledge Bases are updated to point to the corresponding Agent during migration. Old links should redirect correctly. If a link is broken after the domain migrates, users should create a new share link from the Agent.

Answer Behavior After Migration

The core behavior is the same - the agent searches the configured Egnyte content and answers based on what it finds.

Agents use a more capable reasoning engine, so answers may be slightly more detailed or better-sourced. The agent only answers from the sources configured into it.

For API and Integration Developers

The KB API endpoints are deprecated and will stop working after the domain is migrated. The integration code needs to be updated. Refer here for more details.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will Existing Knowledge Base Content be Preserved?

Yes. The file sources and folder paths configured in a Knowledge Base are carried over to the Agent automatically. No content is lost and no re-indexing is needed.

What if a Domain has Agents Turned Off?

If Agents are not enabled on a domain, migrated Knowledge Bases will not be visible in the AI Assistant interface after migration. Admins should contact the Egnyte Customer Success Manager or Egnyte Support to coordinate enabling Agents before the domain migrates.

Can the Knowledge Base API still be Used after Migration if the Code has not been Updated Yet?

No. After a domain migrates, calls to the deprecated KB API endpoints will fail. The deprecation warning headers currently in API responses indicate the endpoint is going away; those responses serve as a signal.

Does the Agent behave Exactly like the Knowledge Base?

The core behavior is preserved: the Agent searches the connected Egnyte content and answers questions based on what it finds. It will not answer questions outside the scope of that content. The Agent uses an updated instruction set that matches the Knowledge Base behavior by design.

If a Knowledge Base was set up to Transcribe Audio and Video files, does that Still Work after Migration?

Yes. Audio and video transcription is tied to the files configured as sources in the Knowledge Base (now Agent), not to the domain as a whole. After migration, files in the Agent’s source folders continue to be transcribed, exactly as they were when it was a Knowledge Base.

A few points worth knowing:

  • Transcription applies to files within the Agent’s configured sources. Files outside those folders are not transcribed, regardless of the migration.
  • Transcription happens for files in Agent sources even if the Agent is never queried. This matches the previous Knowledge Base behavior.
  • This is not a domain-level capability. Enabling Agents on a domain does not enable transcription for all files across the domain.
What Should be Done With a Power Automate Flow or Custom Connector that Uses the KB APIs?

Update the flow to call the Agent endpoints instead. The agentId is the same UUID as the kb-id. The main code change is adopting the async pattern: call the Agent ask endpoint, save the executionId, and poll for the result rather than reading it from the initial response.

Are there API Reference Docs for the New Agent Endpoints?

Yes. The Egnyte Developer Portal contains the Agent API reference, including the ask and status endpoints. Those docs can be used alongside this guide.

What Happens to the Shared Link for a Knowledge Base after Migration?

Shared links for Knowledge Bases are updated to Agent links during migration. Egnyte recommends testing shared links on the domain after migration and recreating any that do not resolve correctly.

Will there be Any Further Deprecations of AI APIs?

The ask_ai_assistant MCP tool and its corresponding API are being updated to use an async model (returning an executionId and requiring a status poll), consistent with the Agent pattern. The tool itself is not being removed - only the underlying call mechanism is being modernized. Updated documentation will be published separately.

Outlook AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Outlook as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can now search and read emails, access recent communications, retrieve calendar events, and look up contacts directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Prerequisites

  • Microsoft 365 Tenant with Entra/Azure AD Global Admin access
  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher)
  • Outlook connector already visible in the Egnyte connectors library as a pre-loaded connector

Tenant Admin Consent (Pre-Step for Outlook Connector)

Before publishing the connector for end users, a Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant tenant-wide consent to the Outlook MCP by Egnyte app through Microsoft Graph.

The app requests scopes that individual non-admin users cannot consent to on their own. Without tenant-wide consent, every non-admin user will see Microsoft’s Need admin approval screen and will be blocked from authenticating.

Refer to these steps to use a pre-loaded connector, publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other admin actions.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the Outlook connector for configuration:

  • outlook_get_calendar_event - Retrieves complete details of a specific calendar event using its ID, including description, attendees, and meeting notes
  • outlook_list_calendar_events - Lists calendar events within a specified date range, including key details such as title, time, location, organizer, and meeting links
  • outlook_get_email - Retrieves the full content of a specific email using its ID, including the complete message body
  • outlook_get_recent_emails - Fetches the most recent emails from the user’s inbox, sorted by received date for quick access to recent communications
  • outlook_search_emails - Searches emails in the user’s mailbox using filters such as keywords, sender, date range, or folders, and returns matching results with metadata
  • outlook_search_contacts - Searches the user’s address book by name, email, or company, and returns contact details such as email addresses, phone numbers, and organization information Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised or Always ask permission.

All Outlook tools are read-only (list, get, and search operations). It is safe to set them to Allow unsupervised since they only retrieve data from Outlook and do not create, update, or delete any content.

Additional Information

Consideration

Users Previously Granted Individual Consent

Some users may have already granted individual consent to the application prior to tenant-wide approval. Egnyte’s authentication flow supports this scenario. Once tenant admin consent is granted, users can proceed without any additional action.

Troubleshooting

Need Admin Approval Error

If users see a Need admin approval message during authentication, it means tenant-wide admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions has not yet been granted. A Microsoft 365 tenant admin must approve access by visiting their admin portal

OAuth Authentication Fails

Authentication may fail if admin consent is incomplete or still propagating. After granting consent, allow a few minutes for changes to take effect and retry. Also ensure the required Microsoft Graph permissions are correctly configured.

Tools Return Empty Results or No Access Errors

If tools return no results, it may be due to Outlook or Microsoft Graph permission constraints. The connector only returns data that the user has access to in Outlook. Verify that the user has access to the relevant emails, calendar events, or contacts, and retry if needed.

Personalization in AI Assistant and Agents

Egnyte offers AI personalization enabling the users to choose if AI can personalize responses using the data and memories. AI Assistant and Agents can remember information shared during chats and learn from the user’s role, folders, and previous conversations, helping deliver more relevant and context-aware responses.

Skip Ahead To…

Personalization Settings

Edit AI Profile
Add a Memory
Edit or Delete a Memory

Corporate Glossary

Manage AI Personalization

Personalization Settings

  • Navigate to Settings in AI Assistant or Agents.
  • Click on Personalization.
Edit AI Profile
  • Click on Edit to add work context. AI will set context as per the user’s profile and preferences.
  • The user will be redirected to My Profile -> My Preferences in a new tab and they can edit the fields: Time zone, Job Title, Job Role, etc. Save the changes and the work context will be set accordingly.
Add a Memory

AI tools can automatically learn and add memories over time as users interact with them. Users can also manually Add and Save specific memories.

  • Click on Add under Personalization.
  • Enter the memory and click on Save. The memory will be saved.

These memories will be referred to when the user interacts with the AI tools.

Similarly, the past chats will be referred to as applicable.

Users can also provide their prompts to the AI tools to refer to a saved memory or a past chat.

The memories are individual to each user. Each person can View, Add, Edit, or Delete their own memories at any time from Personalization Settings.

Edit or Delete a Memory
  • Click on the three-dots icon of a saved memory and click on Edit.
  • Make the desired changes and click on Save.
  • To delete a memory, click on the three-dots icon and click on Delete.
  • Click on Delete memory to confirm deletion.

Corporate Glossary

Admins can choose to disable or enable corporate glossary (enabled by default) for AI Assistant and Agents to refer to the company-specific terminology and definitions.

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Personalization
  • Click on Add term
  • Enter the Term, Description, and Synonyms. Click on Save.
  • Admins can also click on Import taxonomy and upload the CSV file to quickly add or update the glossary in bulk. The sample of the CSV file is as shown below. The header must be exactly term, description, synonyms. Synonyms are separated by | in the CSV as opposed to commas in the UI.

The terms added in the corporate glossary will be listed. Admins can use the search functionality to search for a specific term. They can hover over or click on the three-dots icon to Edit or Delete a particular term. They can also edit the columns displayed and set the view to a list or condensed view.

Manage AI Personalization

Admins can enable or disable the AI personalization options.

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Personalization
  • Enable or disable the toggles for:
    • Allow AI to personalize responses using your data and memories
    • Allow AI to reference past chats
    • Allow AI to reference the corporate glossary
    • Click on Save changes.

Prompt Wizard for Agent Builder

Egnyte’s Prompt Wizard feature helps the users write better AI prompts with a single click when using the Agent Builder.

This feature automatically refines the initial prompt input into a clearer, more structured, and effective prompt. This helps the users get more accurate instructions for their agents.

Steps to Improve a Prompt

  • Navigate to AI -> Agents -> + Create Agent.
  • Create a Custom Agent or use an existing template to create an agent.
  • Provide an instruction in the Details section of the Agent Builder. Alternatively, Instructions will be auto-populated based on the description provided.
  • Click on the icon to regenerate the instructions using the Prompt Wizard.
  • An improved prompt is autogenerated and displayed based on the original input. Users can click Insert to use the suggested prompt or continue refining their original input. By clicking Improve again, new variations can be generated until the desired prompt is achieved.
  • After clicking Insert, the improved prompt will appear in the instructions field. The users can use these instructions to build their agent.

Additional Resources

Prompts Management in Egnyte’s AI Assistant

Egnyte provides the users with the ability to view and manage prompts. Users can interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant using prompts and they can also view them using the icon in the input box.

With the Prompt Library, users can choose from the Egnyte prompts or create custom prompts for specific tasks. These prompts guide Egnyte’s AI Assistant with clear instructions by saving time, reducing repetitive work, and making everyday tasks a lot easier for the end-users.

Skip Ahead To…

View and Insert Prompts

Prompt Library ​​

Actions on Egnyte Prompts

Actions on Custom and My Prompts

Role-Based Prompt Management

Create New Prompt

Edit a Prompt

Duplicate a Prompt

Delete a Custom Prompt

View and Insert Prompts

When a user clicks on the Prompts option, they will be presented with the prompt library to select a prompt and use it in the conversation.

​​​The users can refine the ​​​list ​​by searching for a specific prompt or applying the filters at the top.​​

There are three filter options available as:

  • ​​​Task categories: Prompts are classified in four task categories as Understand, Create, Ask, and Analyze. ​​

  • Job Types: There are different options available, such as, Engineering, Customer Success, Finance, Marketing, etc. ​

  • Document Types: Narrow down the prompts by specific document type, such as financial statement, travel policy, Balance sheet, meeting minutes, etc. ​​ Prompts are classified into different categories:

  • All (Default selection)

  • By Egnyte : By Egnyte prompts are the Egnyte seeded prompts available to the domain

  • Custom Prompts : Custom Prompts are the ones created by admin or power users within the domain

  • My Prompts : My Prompts are the ones which are created by the user themselves

  • Favorites : The ones marked as a favorite show up under Favorites

  • Trending Now : Trending Now includes the prompts which have been used 10 or more times recently. Based on the recent usage, top 5 prompts can be included under the Trending Now category By default, all prompts are displayed to the user, sorted with new prompts first, followed by trending prompts, and then the remaining prompts in alphabetical order. All the new prompts can be identified by the New badge added to the prompts.

​​​​Users can hover over on a particular prompt to view its details. ​​

​​​To use a prompt, select the prompt and click on Insert. ​​

​​​The instructions associated with the selected prompt will populate in the input b​ox​. The user can modify these instructions, if required, and provide the input to get a response. ​​

For instance, the prompt selected in the example below enables the user to select two files for comparison. The instructions are populated in the input box as soon as the user inserts the prompt. They simply need to select the two files and provide the input for comparison.

Prompt Library ​​

To access prompt library:

  • Click on Prompts option and the prompt library will open in the pop-up.​​​Alternatively, navigate to Settings-> AI Powered Features -> Prompt Library.
  • ​​ Prompts will be classified in six categories as All (default Selection), By Egnyte, Custom Prompts, My Prompts, Favorites, and Trending Now.

The users will have the search functionality and filter options as mentioned earlier.

Actions on Egnyte Prompts

For Egnyte prompts, the user can add a prompt as their favorite by clicking on the three dots menu -> Add to Favorites.

If a prompt is already marked as favorite, click on the three dots menu -> Remove from Favorites for the desired prompt again to remove it from favorites.

Users can also duplicate an Egnyte prompt.

Actions on Custom and My Prompts

For Custom or My prompts, users can click on the three dots menu and choose to add to/remove from favorites. The user can also click on three-dots menu to edit, duplicate, and delete a prompt.

All the prompts marked as favorites appear in the Favorites tab. Actions available for favorite or trending prompts depend on the prompt being an Egnyte or Custom prompt.

Role-Based Prompt Management

There are specific controls for managing prompts based on the user roles.

Admins:

  • For Egnyte prompts, Admins can Duplicate the prompts to create their own custom versions

  • Admins have full control over Custom Prompts. They can Edit, Duplicate, Delete, and Add to Favorites directly from the library Power Users & Non-Admins:

  • Can create new custom prompts and add prompts to Favorites

  • Have Edit, Duplicate, and Delete permissions for prompts created by themselves

  • For prompts created by others in the Custom Prompts tab, they can easily Duplicate them to use as a template for their own needs Standard Users :

  • Can only add prompts to their Favorites.

Create New Prompt

Admin and Power users have the ability to create new prompts. Prompts created or edited by a user are visible to the other admins and power users.

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Prompt Library.
  • Click on Create New Prompt.
  • Alternatively, users can click on the View Prompts icon and click on Create new prompt.
  • Provide the details and click Next:
    • Name: A unique name to the prompt
    • Description: A brief description about the prompt
    • Icon: Select the icon for the prompt
    • Instruction: Type the instruction for the prompt or click on Generate Instruction to automatically generate instruction
      • Add a file: The users can create file placeholders in the instructions. For instance, users can provide instructions to compare two documents. While using this prompt, the user will be able to select and provide actual files for comparison as shown in the example below.
      • Refine Instructions: Users can provide instructions to the prompt and request the system to refine the instructions for them by clicking on the wand icon. Refined instructions based on the details given by the user will be generated.
      • The user can continue to refine the instructions and click on Insert when they have the desired instructions generated.
      • The refined instructions will be available for use.
  • Provide the appropriate Prompt Categorization (optional) to the prompt
    • Agents: The prompt will appear in the tagged agent(s)
    • Document tags: The prompt will appear in Egnyte’s AI Assistant for the tagged documents
    • Task categories: The label will help categorize the prompt based on the task type
    • Job types: The label will help categorize the prompt based on the job functions
  • Users can test their prompt on the right and keep on modifying the details and categorization until they get the intended response. Click on Save.
  • Users can also manage the scope of prompts during testing while creating the prompt using the prompt library. For instance, if a user wishes to test a prompt on a specific folder, they can click the ‘+’ icon in the input box on the testing side and select the desired folder. If no folder is selected, the default scope remains the Shared folder.
  • Users can continue to change the scope until they get the desired results.
  • If the user creates a prompt from their interaction on a specific knowledge base, the scope remains in the respective Knowledge Base folder. The scope cannot be modified in this case.
  • If there are file placeholders in a prompt, the option to manage the scope does not appear in this case.
  • The prompt will be created and it will appear under the My Prompts and Custom Prompts tab in the Prompt Library.

Edit a Prompt

Users can edit a prompt from the Prompt Library.

  • Click on the three-dots menu -> Edit for Custom or My prompt.
  • Make the required changes in the prompt details and/or tags and save the changes. The user will be notified of the prompt being updated.

Duplicate a Prompt

  • Click on the three dots menu -> Duplicate for By Egnyte, Custom, or My Prompts.
  • When creating a new prompt by duplication, the details from the original prompt will be pre-filled. The new prompt will be named Duplicate of <original prompt> by default. Make the desired changes, if any, and save the prompt. The new prompt will be created under custom and my prompts.

Delete a Custom Prompt

Users can delete a custom prompt from the Prompt Library.

  • Click on the three-dots menu -> Delete for Custom or My prompt.
  • Click on Delete to confirm deletion.
  • The user will be notified about the deletion.

Prompts Management in Egnyte’s AI Assistant on a Single Document

Users can use prompts while interacting on a specific document through Egnyte’s AI Assistant. ​​By using the clear instructions in the prompt, users can get quicker, more focused responses based on the document content.

  • Prompts for Egnyte’s AI assistant are available only in the Web UI and not in the Desktop App.

  • In domains with the AI add-on enabled, users will be able to interact with Egnyte’s AI Assistant as per the source(s) selected rather than just the document in preview.

Users can interact ​on a document using prompts from the prompt library by clicking on + icon -> Prompts.

Setting up OneDrive AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting OneDrive as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can now search and read documents directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Prerequisites

  • Microsoft 365 Tenant with Entra/Azure AD Global Admin access
  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher)
  • OneDrive connector already visible in the Egnyte connectors library as a pre-loaded connector

Tenant Admin Consent (Pre-Step for OneDrive Connector)

Before the connector can be published to end users, a Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant tenant-wide consent to the OneDrive MCP by Egnyte app. This lets the app access the Microsoft Graph permissions it needs on behalf of the whole organization.

  • Open the consent link: Grant admin consent and sign in as a Global Administrator.
  • Review the list of permissions in the dialog.
  • Select Accept to confirm. This gives the app access to your organization’s data through the listed permissions. The app requests scopes that individual non-admin users cannot consent to on their own. Without tenant-wide consent, every non-admin user will see Microsoft’s Need admin approval screen and will be blocked from authenticating.

Refer to these steps to use a pre-loaded connector, publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other admin actions.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the OneDrive connector for configuration:

  • onedrive_get_onedrive: Retrieves information regarding the owner, storage quotas, and associated metadata for the OneDrive account.
  • onedrive_find_file_or_folder: Utilizes free-form text to locate specific items within the personal drive, proving effective when the path is unknown.
  • onedrive_get_folder_children: Provides a paginated list of internal contents, defaults to the root directory if no specific identifier is provided.
  • onedrive_get_file_or_folder_metadata: Accesses detailed properties including file size, direct links, creation dates, and authorship details.
  • onedrive_get_file_or_folder_metadata_by_url: Obtains metadata through a provided share link, contingent upon the user possessing existing access rights.
  • onedrive_read_text_file: Extracts content from text-based files under 5MB, such as Markdown, CSV, or various configuration and source formats.
  • onedrive_read_binary_file_as_base64: Parses binary documents like PDFs, images, or Word files under 5MB into a base64 encoded string format. Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised (checkmark icon)or Always ask permission (info icon).

All OneDrive tools are read-only (list, get, and search operations). It is safe to set them to Allow unsupervised since they only retrieve data from OneDrive and do not create, update, or delete any content.

Additional Information And Resources

Consideration

Users Previously Granted Individual Consent

Some users may have already granted individual consent to the application prior to tenant-wide approval. Egnyte’s authentication flow supports this scenario. Once tenant admin consent is granted, users can proceed without any additional action.

Troubleshooting

Need Admin Approval Error

If users see a Need admin approval message during authentication, it means tenant-wide admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions has not yet been granted. A Microsoft 365 tenant admin must approve access by visiting their admin portal

OAuth Authentication Fails

Authentication may fail if admin consent is incomplete or still propagating. After granting consent, allow a few minutes for changes to take effect and retry. Also ensure the required Microsoft Graph permissions are correctly configured.

Tools Return Empty Results or No Access Errors

If tools return no results, it may be due to OneDrive or Microsoft Graph permission constraints. The connector only returns data that the user has access to in OneDrive. Verify that the user has access to the relevant content and retry if needed.

Setting Up Procore AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Procore as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can query Procore project data, RFIs, submittals, meetings, incidents, and more directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Prerequisites

  • An active Procore account with Company Admin access
  • Egnyte admin account
  • Agent Mode enabled in Egnyte’s AI Assistant
  • Egnyte MCP App Version ID for Procore: 7c7c8b15-ef27-492a-b879-9b8e59a3d0fc If the App Version ID is not available contact the Egnyte account Manager or Egnyte Sales team.

Install the Egnyte MCP App in Procore

The first step is to install the Egnyte MCP application in the Procore company account. This allows Procore to communicate with Egnyte’s AI Assistant through the MCP protocol.

  • Log in to the Procore account at app.procore.com. Enter the email address and click on Continue.
  • Click on the profile icon in the top-right corner and select Account & Admin Settings. Alternatively, navigate to Company Tools -> Admin
  • Click on App Management in the sidebar.
  • Click on Install App -> Install Custom App option in the top-right corner of the App Management page.
  • Enter the App Version ID as 7c7c8b15-ef27-492a-b879-9b8e59a3d0fc and click on Install.
  • A confirmation message will appear. Click on Install to confirm.
  • Egnyte MCP app will appear in the Installed Apps list. If Egnyte MCP is already available in the Installed Apps list, skip installing Egnyte MCP App in Procore and proceed directly to publishing the Procore connector in Egnyte.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the Procore connector for configuration:

Read Tools
  • List companies — Lists Procore companies the user can access.
  • List projects — Lists projects for a selected Procore company, with optional status or name filters.
  • Get project — Retrieves detailed information for one project.
  • List documents — Lists files and folders in a project’s Procore Documents tool.
  • List RFIs — Lists Requests for Information for a project, with status and assignment filters.
  • Get RFI — Retrieves the full details, question, response, and attachments for one RFI.
  • List submittals — Lists project submittals with filters for title, status, reviewer, or specification section.
  • Get submittal — Retrieves a submittal’s workflow, approvers, current status, and ball-in-court details.
  • List submittal responses — Lists the configured response options, such as Approved or Revise and Resubmit.
  • List safety incidents — Lists recorded site safety incidents, with filters for dates, type, hazards, and status.
  • Get safety incident — Retrieves the full narrative, witness details, corrective actions, and attachments for an incident.
  • List meetings — Lists project meetings, including dates, attendees, and meeting type.
  • Get meeting — Retrieves a meeting’s agenda, minutes, attendees, and action items.
  • Get daily log summary — Returns aggregated daily-log counts by type, such as manpower, weather, notes, and equipment.
  • List punch items — Lists project punch items, including descriptions, assignees, status, and due dates.
  • Get punch item — Retrieves complete details for one punch item before it is changed.
  • List punch item types — Lists configured punch-item types available for a project.
  • List punch-list assignee options — Lists people eligible to be assigned to project punch items.
  • List observations — Lists project observations for safety or quality findings, with status, priority, and assignee filters.
  • Get observation — Retrieves full details for one observation.
  • List observation types — Lists valid observation types and their categories for a project.
  • List project users — Lists project members with their names, emails, roles, and permission templates.
  • List vendors — Lists vendor companies in the company directory, optionally filtered by name, trade, country, or active status.
  • Get current user — Retrieves the identity of the user associated with the current Procore connection.
Write Tools
  • Create RFI — Creates a draft or open RFI with a subject, question, assignees, and optional due date.
  • Update RFI — Updates selected RFI fields such as status, subject, due date, assignee, or question.
  • Update submittal status — Records the current user’s approval response on a submittal and advances its workflow when applicable.
  • Create punch item — Creates a new punch item with optional assignee, priority, due date, and location.
  • Update punch item — Updates an existing punch item’s fields, assignment, due date, priority, or workflow status.
  • Create observation — Creates a new project observation with a required type and optional assignment, priority, and due date.
  • Update observation — Updates an observation’s title, description, status, assignee, date, priority, or type. Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised or Always ask permission.

All Procore tools are read-only (list, get, search operations). It is safe to set them to Allow unsupervised since they only retrieve data and do not modify anything in Procore.

Refer the steps to publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other admin actions.

Troubleshooting

OAuth Authentication Fails

Confirm that the Egnyte MCP app is installed in Procore. Check that the Procore account has Company Admin permissions. If the app was recently installed, wait a few minutes and try again.

Connector is Published but Users Cannot See It

Users must have Agent Mode enabled in their AI Assistant Tools panel. They may need to refresh their browser or start a new AI Assistant conversation to see newly published connectors.

Tools Return Empty Results

The user’s Procore account must have access to the projects and data being queried. Procore tools respect the user’s existing Procore permissions - if they cannot see a project in Procore, the AI Assistant cannot access it either.

Setting Up Revizto AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Revizto as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can query Revizto projects, issues, clashes, sheets and project members directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant based on what the admin allowed for creating and updating the issues.

Prerequisites

  • A Revizto account with access to Manage account info and the Developer portal (Revizto Account admin)
  • The Revizto MCP Server app enabled for the organization’s account
  • An Egnyte admin account
  • The Revizto region that hosts the organization’s Revizto account. The region is shown in the Revizto Workspace header, for example Region: North America (USA).

Choose the Revizto Connector for the Region

Revizto hosts its data in separate regions, so the Egnyte connector catalog lists one Revizto connector per region. If Revizto is used in multiple regions, the admin will need to add each region they access Revizto in. Configure the connector that matches the region of the Revizto account:

  • Revizto North America
  • Revizto Canada
  • Revizto Europe
  • Revizto United Kingdom
  • Revizto UAE
  • Revizto South America
  • Revizto Southeast Asia
  • Revizto ANZ
  • Revizto Japan
  • Revizto KSA
  • Revizto Switzerland A connector for a different region cannot reach the organization’s Revizto data. Any sign-in or tool calls will fail as a result.

Create a Custom App in Revizto

The Revizto connector signs in with an OAuth client that the Revizto admin creates in the Revizto Developer portal.

  • Sign in to Revizto. Click Tools -> Manage account info -> Developer portal. Before proceeding, confirm that the Revizto MCP Server app is Active. Click on Add custom app.
  • Enter the following details and click on Add.
    • App name: a recognizable name, for example Egnyte AI Assistant
    • Redirect URIs: a temporary placeholder such as example.com. The field requires a valid URL; it is replaced with the Egnyte redirect URL in a later step.
    • API notification contacts: the email address of the Revizto admin who maintains the app
  • The App credentials dialog shows the Client ID and Client secret. Copy both values and store them securely. Revizto shows the client secret only once and cannot display it again. If the client secret is lost, open the app credentials in the Developer portal and click Regenerate secret, then enter the new secret in Egnyte.

Configure the Connector in Egnyte

  • Navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> AI Connectors
  • Open the External MCPs tab. Find the Revizto connector for the region, click the three-dot menu and select Edit.
  • Make sure the Authentication Type is set to OAuth Client ID. Paste the Client ID from Revizto into OAuth Client ID and the Client secret from Revizto into OAuth Client Secret, then click Generate Redirect URL. Copy the Redirect URL using the copy icon next to the field. Keep this window open. Generating a new Redirect URL overwrites the existing configuration immediately, even without saving. If the Redirect URL is generated again, update it in the Revizto app as well.

Add the Redirect URL and Activate the App in Revizto

  • Return to the Revizto Developer portal. Under Custom apps, click the app name to edit. Replace the placeholder in Redirect URIs with the Egnyte Redirect URL and click Update.
  • Turn on the Active toggle for the app and click Activate to confirm.

Test the Connection in Egnyte

  • Click on Test configuration.
  • A new browser tab opens the Revizto sign-in page. Sign in with the Revizto account. When Authentication Complete appears, close the tab and return to Egnyte.
  • The Tools step will show Successfully connected to the server, followed by the list of Revizto tools. Set permissions for the tools and click Continue.
  • Review the server configuration on the Summary step and click Save. Refer to the admin guide on AI Connectors for understanding tool permissions.

Manage Connector

Admins have the ability to edit, publish, unpublish, disconnect, and delete the connector. Refer here for more details.

Connect Revizto as an End User

Users can add and use Revizto by following the steps as mentioned here.

Revizto tools act with the permissions of the signed-in user. If a user cannot see a project in Revizto, AI Assistant cannot access it either.

Troubleshooting

Redirect URIs Field Shows an Invalid Format Error

Revizto accepts only complete URLs that start with https://. Enter a placeholder such as example.com when creating the app, then replace it with the Egnyte Redirect URL.

OAuth Authentication Fails

Confirm that the Revizto app is Active, that its Redirect URIs field contains the exact Redirect URL Egnyte generated most recently, and that the Egnyte connector matches the region of the Revizto account. Start the sign-in from Egnyte (Test configuration for admins, Connect for users).

Client Secret is No Longer Available

Regenerate the secret in the Revizto Developer portal and enter the new value in OAuth Client Secret in Egnyte.

Connector is Published but Users Cannot See It

Confirm the connector shows Published in the External MCPs list. Users may need to refresh the browser or start a new AI Assistant conversation.

Tools Return Empty Results

Check that the user’s Revizto account has access to the projects being queried and that the user connected the connector for the correct region.

Setting Up Salesforce AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Salesforce as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can query, read, create, and update Salesforce records directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Skip Ahead To…

Prerequisites

Create the External Client App in Salesforce

Activate the MCP Server in Salesforce

Create the Salesforce Connector in Egnyte

Configure Tool Permissions

Troubleshooting

Prerequisites

  • A Salesforce org with System Administrator access (required to create External Client Apps and activate MCP Servers).

  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher).

  • Access to the Salesforce Setup interface and permission to receive verification emails on the administrator’s email address.

  • Salesforce’s MCP feature requires a dedicated External Client App and an activated MCP Server in your Salesforce org. The Salesforce connector is added as a custom connector in Egnyte until it becomes available as a pre-loaded connector in the Egnyte catalog.

  • If Egnyte MCP is already available in the Installed Apps list, skip creating the external client app in Salesforce and proceed directly to publishing the Salesforce connector in Egnyte.

Create the External Client App in Salesforce

The first step is to create a new External Client App in Salesforce. This app generates the Consumer Key (Client ID) and Consumer Secret (Client Secret) that Egnyte will use to authenticate, and it holds the OAuth scopes that authorize access to the Salesforce-hosted MCP server.

  • Log in to the Salesforce org, click on the gear icon -> Setup
  • Search for External Client App Manager in the side panel on the left.
  • Click on New External Client App.
  • Fill the basic information:
    • External Client App Name: Egnyte MCP (or any other name of choice). API name will be auto-populated based on the external client app name entered
    • Contact Email: The Salesforce administrator’s email address
    • Distribution State: Local (unless the org requires another value)
  • Expand API (Enable OAuth Settings) and click the checkbox for Enable OAuth.
  • Configure the OAuth settings:
    • Callback URL: Enter a temporary placeholder. This will be replaced with the real Egnyte redirect URL while publishing the connector
    • OAuth Scopes: Select the following scopes:
      • Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access)
      • Access Salesforce hosted MCP servers (mcp_api)
      • Security: Check Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) and Issue JSON Web Token (JWT)-based access tokens for named users
  • Click on Create to save the External Client App.
  • The app will be created. Navigate to Settings and click on Consumer Key and Secret under OAuth Settings.
  • The verification code will be sent to the email address. Enter the code and click on Verify. Copy the Consumer Key (Client ID) and Consumer Secret (Client Secret) and store them securely.

Activate the MCP Server in Salesforce

Salesforce exposes multiple MCP servers, each scoped to a different set of objects and operations. Admins must activate the server they want to connect to in order to generate its public URL.

  • In Salesforce Setup, use the Quick Find box to search for MCP Servers and open the page.
  • Click on the server to open the details.
  • Click on Activate
  • Once the server is activated, copy the server details The exact URL may differ by region or org. Always copy the URL shown on the MCP Server’s page rather than typing it manually. If the Admin activates a different server, the URL path will reflect that server’s name.

Create the Salesforce Connector in Egnyte

If Egnyte MCP is already available in the Installed Apps list, skip creating the external client app in Salesforce and proceed directly to publishing the Salesforce connector in Egnyte.

For Salesforce AI Connector, select the authentication type as OAuth Client ID. The Client ID and Client Secret generated earlier will be used. Click on Generate Redirect URL and copy the Redirect URL.

Return to Salesforce. Open External Client App Manager, open the app created earlier. Navigate to Settings > OAuth Settings, click Edit, and replace the Callback URL with the Egnyte redirect URL. Click Save.

Salesforce requires approximately 6-7 minutes for Redirect URL changes to propagate after they are saved on the External Client App. If the admins run Test configuration in Egnyte immediately after updating the Redirect URL in Salesforce, authentication will fail with a redirect_uri_mismatch error.

Navigate back to Egnyte and click on Test Configuration. Complete the Salesforce OAuth authorization. Admins will be redirected to Salesforce to log in and verify their identity. Approve the access request.

Configure Tool Permissions

The exact tools shown depend on the Salesforce MCP server activated earlier. Activating the subject-all server exposes a broad set of tools covering standard Salesforce record operations, including:

  • Query Salesforce objects (accounts, contacts, opportunities, leads, cases, and other standard and custom objects)
  • Read individual records by ID
  • Create new records
  • Update existing records Other Salesforce MCP servers expose narrower toolsets scoped to specific objects. Review the tool list shown in Egnyte and confirm it matches the expectations from the activated server.

Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised or Always ask permission.

The subject-all server exposes write tools (create and update record operations). It is strongly recommended to set write tools to Always ask permission so users can confirm before the AI modifies Salesforce data. Read-only tools (query and read operations) are safe to set to Allow unsupervised.

Refer the steps to publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other Admin actions.

Troubleshooting

Redirect_uri_mismatch Error During Test Configuration

Salesforce takes approximately 6-7 minutes to propagate Callback URL changes on an External Client App. Wait at least 7 minutes after saving the updated Callback URL in Salesforce before clicking Test configuration in Egnyte. If the error persists past 10 minutes, verify the Callback URL in Salesforce matches the Egnyte-generated redirect URL exactly, including the trailing path and no extra spaces.

Cannot Find the MCP Servers Page in Salesforce

MCP Servers is a Salesforce platform feature that may not be available in every Salesforce edition. Confirm that the edition supports Salesforce-hosted MCP servers and that the feature is enabled for the org. Contact Salesforce support if the page is missing.

Insufficient_scope Errors when Tools are Invoked

The External Client App may be missing the mcp_api scope or the refresh_token scope. Return to External Client App Manager, open the app, and verify both scopes as mentioned earlier are selected. After updating scopes, users may need to disconnect and reconnect the Salesforce connector for the new scopes to take effect.

Verification Code Email not Received

When viewing OAuth Settings on a newly created External Client App, Salesforce sends a verification code to the administrator’s email. Check spam folders, confirm the Contact Email on the app is correct, and request the code again if needed.

Tools Return Empty Results or No Access Errors

Salesforce tools respect the connected user’s object and field-level security. If the user cannot see an object or record in Salesforce directly, the AI Assistant cannot access it either. Confirm the user’s profile and permission sets in Salesforce.

Setting up SharePoint AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting SharePoint as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can now search and read SharePoint content directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Prerequisites

  • Microsoft 365 Tenant with Entra/Azure AD Global Admin access
  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher)
  • SharePoint connector already visible in the Egnyte connectors library as a pre-loaded connector

Tenant Admin Consent (Pre-Step for SharePoint Connector)

Before the connector can be published to end users, a Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant tenant-wide consent to the SharePoint MCP by Egnyte app. This lets the app access the Microsoft Graph permissions it needs on behalf of the whole organization.

  • Open the consent link: Grant admin consent and sign in as a Global Administrator.
  • Review the list of permissions in the dialog.
  • Select Accept to confirm. This gives the app access to your organization’s data through the listed permissions. The app requests scopes that individual non-admin users cannot consent to on their own. Without tenant-wide consent, every non-admin user will see Microsoft’s Need admin approval screen and will be blocked from authenticating.

Refer to these steps to use a pre-loaded connector, publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other admin actions.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the SharePoint connector for configuration:

  • sharepoint_find_site: Perform a keyword search to locate accessible sites and retrieve the required site_id as a preliminary step.
  • sharepoint_get_site_by_path: Identify a site via its specific hostname and relative path. This is applicable only when the complete URL structure is known.
  • sharepoint_list_subsites: Enumerate child sites under a specific parent site, with pagination support available.
  • sharepoint_list_document_libraries: View all document libraries contained within a site, including paginated results.
  • sharepoint_get_default_document_library: Directly retrieve the primary document library (often labeled Documents) without scanning all libraries.
  • sharepoint_get_folder_children: List items within a specific document library folder. The library root is shown if no folder ID is provided.
  • sharepoint_find_file_or_folder: Search for files and folders across all reachable SharePoint locations. It is recommended to use specific queries as only the initial page is returned.
  • sharepoint_get_file_or_folder_metadata: Fetch detailed information, such as file size, source URLs, timestamps, and ownership, for a given item.
  • sharepoint_get_file_or_folder_metadata_by_url: Extract metadata using a SharePoint sharing link, provided the user possesses existing access rights.
  • sharepoint_read_text_file: Open and retrieve the content of text files smaller than 5MB in plain text format.
  • sharepoint_list_lists: Enumerate all SharePoint Lists available on a site with optional pagination.
  • sharepoint_list_list_items: Access rows and associated column data from a list, supporting paginated views.
  • sharepoint_get_list_item: Fetch a particular list item and its column values using a specific ID.
  • sharepoint_list_columns: Review the schema and column definitions of a list to better understand the returned item results. Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised (checkmark icon)or Always ask permission (info icon).

All SharePoint tools are read-only (list, get, and search operations). It is safe to set them to Allow unsupervised since they only retrieve data from SharePoint and do not create, update, or delete any content.

Additional Information and Resources

Consideration

Users Previously Granted Individual Consent

Some users may have already granted individual consent to the application prior to tenant-wide approval. Egnyte’s authentication flow supports this scenario. Once tenant admin consent is granted, users can proceed without any additional action.

Troubleshooting

Need Admin Approval Error

If users see a Need admin approval message during authentication, it means tenant-wide admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions has not yet been granted. A Microsoft 365 tenant admin must approve access by visiting their admin portal.

OAuth Authentication Fails

Authentication may fail if admin consent is incomplete or still propagating. After granting consent, allow a few minutes for changes to take effect and retry. Also ensure the required Microsoft Graph permissions are correctly configured.

Tools Return Empty Results or No Access Errors

If tools return no results, it may be due to SharePoint or Microsoft Graph permission constraints. The connector only returns data that the user has access to in SharePoint. Verify that the user has access to the relevant content, and retry if needed.

Setting Up Slack AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Slack as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can search channels, read threads and canvases, send and schedule messages, and look up profiles directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Skip Ahead To…

Prerequisites

Install the Egnyte MCP App in Slack

Create the Slack Connector in Egnyte

Configure Tool Permissions

Troubleshooting

Prerequisites

  • A Slack workspace with permission to create and install apps (Workspace Owner or Admin, or a workspace that allows members to install apps).

  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher)

  • Access to api.slack.com to create a new Slack app.

  • Slack’s MCP feature requires a dedicated Slack app in the workspace. The Slack connector is added as a custom connector in Egnyte until it becomes available as a pre-loaded connector in the Egnyte catalog.

  • If Egnyte MCP is already available in the Installed Apps list, skip installing Egnyte MCP App in Slack and proceed directly to publishing the Slack connector in Egnyte.

Install the Egnyte MCP App in Slack

The first step is to create a new Slack app and configure it to expose Slack’s Model Context Protocol endpoint. This app generates the Client ID and Client Secret that Egnyte will use to authenticate.

  • Navigate to api.slack.com/apps and click Create an App.
  • Select From scratch. Enter an App Name and select the Slack workspace. Click Create App.
  • In the left sidebar, navigate to Agents & AI Apps and enable Model Context Protocol.
  • In the left sidebar, navigate to OAuth & Permissions and configure the following:
    • Click on Opt In for Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE). Provide confirmation by clicking on Opt In.
    • Click on Add New Redirect URL and add a temporary Redirect URL (for example, egnyte.com) and click Add.
    • Users can edit or delete the URL(s) using the Edit or Delete icon. Click on Save URLs. This placeholder is required before Token Rotation can be enabled.
    • Click on Opt In to turn on Token Rotation. Provide confirmation by clicking on Opt In.
    • On the same OAuth & Permissions page, scroll to Scopes and click on Add an OAuth Scope to add the following scopes:
      • Bot Token Scopes (at least one is required):
        • channels:read
        • Select the desired User Token Scope, such as:
          • channels:history
          • search:read.public
          • search:read.users
          • users:read
          • users:read.email
          • User Token Scopes drive what the Egnyte’s AI Assistant can search and read on behalf of the connected user. It is recommended to add only the scopes that the organization is comfortable exposing.
          • In the left sidebar, navigate to Basic Information and copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Store these values securely as these will be required later.

Create the Slack Connector in Egnyte

If Egnyte MCP is already available in the Installed Apps list, skip installing Egnyte MCP App in Slack and proceed directly to publishing the Slack connector in Egnyte.

  • For Slack AI Connector, select the authentication type as OAuth Client ID. The Client ID and Client Secret generated earlier will be used. Click on Generate Redirect URL and copy the Redirect URL. Navigate to api.slack.com > OAuth & Permissions. Under Redirect URLs, add the generated Egnyte redirect URL, click Add and click on Save URLs. Click on Test Configuration to test the configuration.
  • Click on Allow to grant Egnyte access.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the Slack connector for configuration:

  • slack_create_canvas - Create a new Slack canvas
  • slack_read_canvas - Read the contents of a Slack canvas
  • slack_read_channel - Read messages from a Slack channel
  • slack_read_thread - Read messages in a thread
  • slack_read_user_profile - Look up a Slack user profile
  • slack_schedule_message - Schedule a message to be sent later
  • slack_search_channels - Search for channels by name
  • slack_search_public_messages - Search messages in public channels
  • slack_search_public_and_private_messages - Search messages across public and private channels the user has access to
  • slack_send_message - Send a message to a channel or user
  • slack_update_message - Update a previously sent message Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised or Always ask permission.

Slack exposes write tools (slack_send_message, slack_schedule_message, slack_update_message, slack_create_canvas). It is strongly recommended to set these to Always ask permission so users can confirm before the AI posts on their behalf. For Read-only tools, (slack_read_, slack_search_) it is safe to set these to Allow unsupervised.

Refer the steps to publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other Admin actions.

Troubleshooting

Issues in Token Rotation on the Slack App

Slack requires at least one Redirect URL to be configured before Token Rotation can be turned on. Add the temporary URL first, save, and then enable Token Rotation. Admins can replace the URL with the real Egnyte redirect URL while adding the Slack AI Connector on Egnyte.

OAuth Authorization Fails with Invalid Redirect URL Error

Verify that the redirect URL generated by Egnyte has been added exactly as copied to the Slack app’s OAuth & Permissions page. Also, ensure that the Save URLs button was clicked. The URL is case-sensitive and must not have trailing spaces.

Missing Scope Error when Tools are Invoked

The Slack app may be missing a required Bot or User scope. Return to OAuth & Permissions in the Slack app and confirm that all scopes listed earlier are present. After adding scopes, the user may need to reconnect the connector for the new scopes to take effect.

Search or Read Tools Return Empty Results

Slack tools respect the connected user’s existing Slack permissions and channel memberships. If the user is not a member of a private channel, the AI Assistant cannot read it either. Confirm the user has access in Slack directly.

Setting up Teams AI Connector on Egnyte

Egnyte offers its users the ability to connect to external AI connectors in order to bridge the gap between Egnyte and widely used productivity tools.

This guide walks Egnyte admins through connecting Teams as an AI Connector using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once configured, users can now search and read Teams content directly from Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Prerequisites

  • Microsoft 365 Tenant with Entra/Azure AD Global Admin access
  • Egnyte admin privileges (Power User role or higher)
  • Teams connector already visible in the Egnyte connectors library as a pre-loaded connector

Tenant Admin Consent (Pre-Step for Teams Connector)

Before the connector can be published to end users, a Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant tenant-wide consent to the Teams MCP by Egnyte app. This lets the app access the Microsoft Graph permissions it needs on behalf of the whole organization.

  • Open the consent link: Grant admin consent and sign in as a Global Administrator.
  • Review the list of permissions in the dialog.
  • Select Accept to confirm. This gives the app access to your organization’s data through the listed permissions. The app requests scopes that individual non-admin users cannot consent to on their own. Without tenant-wide consent, every non-admin user will see Microsoft’s Need admin approval screen and will be blocked from authenticating.

Refer to these steps to use a pre-loaded connector, publish the connector, editing the connector, along with the other admin actions.

Configure Tool Permissions

The following tools are available in the Teams connector for configuration:

  • teams_list_teams: Retrieves a list of workspaces where the user is active, including the ID, name, details, and URL. This should be performed prior to channel tasks.
  • teams_list_chats: Fetches current chat metadata such as ID, subject, and latest message snippet. Useful for identifying IDs before message retrieval.
  • teams_list_channels: Provides all channels within a specific team. This operation necessitates a team ID obtained from the teams_list_teams tool.
  • teams_list_chat_messages: Lists chat history in reverse chronological order and includes pagination support.
  • teams_list_channel_messages: Shows primary messages in a channel, excluding replies, sorted by recent activity. Supports pagination.
  • teams_list_channel_message_replies: Retrieves threaded replies for a specific channel message. Use this following list_channel_messages.
  • teams_get_chat_message: Fetches the full content and sender info for a designated chat message via its ID.
  • teams_search_messages: Uses keywords or KQL to find messages. Note that search results provide snippets rather than complete bodies and are eventually consistent.
  • teams_list_channel_files: Displays all documents shared within a channel and allows for paginated results.
  • teams_list_team_members: Lists everyone in a team, showing their name, email address, and assigned role.
  • teams_list_chat_members: Provides details on chat participants, including their IDs and roles.
  • teams_list_channel_members: Enumerates members of a channel with display names and user identifiers.
  • teams_get_user_presence: Returns real-time availability status. If no user is specified, it defaults to the current user’s status.
  • teams_send_message_to_chat: Delivers a message to an active chat. These actions are immediate and permanent.
  • teams_send_message_to_channel: Initiates a new discussion thread in a channel. These posts cannot be retracted once sent.
  • teams_reply_to_channel_message: Posts a response in an existing thread. Changes are visible instantly and are irreversible.
  • teams_send_message_to_user: Sends a direct message. A 1:1 chat is located or initiated automatically without requiring a chat ID. Admins can set permissions for each tool by selecting either Allow unsupervised (checkmark icon)or Always ask permission (info icon).

Most Teams tools are read-only and safe to Allow unsupervised. The send/reply tools post messages to Teams, and these actions cannot be undone. These tools should only be enabled if write access is required. They can be deselected to limit users to the read-only tools only.

Additional Information and Resources

Consideration

Users Previously Granted Individual Consent

Some users may have already granted individual consent to the application prior to tenant-wide approval. Egnyte’s authentication flow supports this scenario. Once tenant admin consent is granted, users can proceed without any additional action.

Troubleshooting

Need Admin Approval Error

If users see a Need admin approval message during authentication, it means tenant-wide admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions has not yet been granted. A Microsoft 365 tenant admin must approve access by visiting their Admin portal.

OAuth Authentication Fails

Authentication may fail if admin consent is incomplete or still propagating. After granting consent, allow a few minutes for changes to take effect and retry. Also ensure the required Microsoft Graph permissions are correctly configured.

Tools Return Empty Results or No Access Errors

If tools return no results, it may be due to Teams or Microsoft Graph permission constraints. The connector only returns data that the user has access to in Teams. Verify that the user has access to the relevant Teams content, and retry if needed.

Working with Egnyte Agents

Agents automate repetitive, time-consuming daily tasks enabling the users to focus on other essential activities requiring their time and effort.

This article covers the details on working with these agents in a stepwise manner.

This feature is available for Platform Plans with AI add-on and included in the New Generation AI plans. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get this feature.

Skip Ahead To…

Agent Builder - Create an Agent

Create a Custom Agent

Create Agent from a Template

Import Agent

Use an Agent

AI Personalization

Use Egnyte Tools

Edit a Prompt

Copy Text

Share Chat

Save Response

Download

Regenerate Response

Provide Feedback

New Chat

Recents

Search Chats

Edit an Agent

Mark Agent as Inactive

Enable or Disable Power Users to Create Agents

Model Settings

Limitations

Agent Builder - Create an Agent

Users can create their own custom agent as per their requirements or use an existing template to create an agent. They can also use the Agent marketplace to configure and add agents.

Create a Custom Agent
  • Navigate to the AI option in the left menu. Click on Agents.
  • Click on +Create Agents button at the top-right or in the tile.
  • Users can also navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Agents and click on Create New Agent.
  • Custom Agent is selected as the default choice in the left menu. Click on Create a Custom Agent.
  • This will open the Describe tab in the Agent builder.
  • Describe
  • Enter the details on what the agent would do. Users can also click on the + icon and select up to 20 files in their description.
  • The Agent Builder will start analyzing the description provided by the user.
  • Agent Builder will provide the updated description and also suggest the next steps for the user. Some of the details can also be auto-populated based on the description provided and a Blue dot will be displayed in these tabs. Users can keep the auto-populated information or continue to edit as per their choice. They can provide feedback to the description provided by the Agent Builder and continue to make the changes to the new agent by typing the query in the input box.
  • Details
  • The details will be auto-populated as per the description provided. Users can choose to update the detail(s) as per their preference.
    • Icon: Select the icon for the agent
    • Name: A descriptive name
    • Description: Provide a brief description
    • Instruction: A custom instruction will be auto-populated. Click on the Magic wand icon to regenerate and improve their instruction
  • Prompts
  • Some of the Starter prompts may be auto-populated. Users can click on the Delete icon to delete any of the prompt(s).
  • They can click on Add Prompt to add new prompts. They can either choose to add from the prompt library or enter manually.
  • For entering the prompt(s) manually, the user can type the prompt, click on Add more to add more prompts, and click on the Delete icon to delete a specific prompt. Click on Save.
  • Users can also add form by clicking on Add Form.
  • They can provide a Title and Instructions for the form and create a new form by clicking on Click to create form.
  • Sources
  • Based on the description, some of the source(s) may be auto-populated. Click on Add sources to add more sources.
  • Users can choose to add All or Selected Egnyte files and folders and All or Selected web sources.
    • All Egnyte files and folders: Click to select all the Egnyte files and folders. If there are specific files and folders already selected as the agent source, the user will be asked to confirm their choice. Click on Switch to all sources to confirm
    • All web sources: Click to select all the web sources. If there are specific web sources already selected as the agent source, the user will be asked to confirm their choice. Click on Switch to all sources to confirm
    • Selected files and folders: Users can select up to 20 items. Click on Continue
    • Selected web sources: Users can type specific web source(s) and save. Click on Add more to continue adding sources and Delete icon to delete a specific source.
    • If there are All Egnyte or web sources selected, the user will be asked to re-confirm if they choose to add specific Egnyte or web sources.
  • Users can filter the source(s) as All (default), Egnyte, and Web. They can also click on the three-dots icon -> Delete or select the source(s) and click on Delete to delete the source(s).
  • Tagging criteria can also be added for the source(s). Click on Set tagging criteria and select the source(s) or select the source(s) and then click on the three-dots icon -> Set tagging criteria.
  • Choose the metadata criteria by selecting the Select property, Relative, and Value for each condition.
  • Users can continue to add criteria by clicking on Add another criteria. They can click on the Delete icon to delete a specific criteria. Click on Save.
  • Source(s) with tag(s) specified will have the Tag indicator visible.
  • Egnyte ensures that data privacy and security are protected at all times when Egnyte and/or Web Search is selected as the source. Learn more about Egnyte’s Generative AI policy.
  • Connectors
  • With Agent Builder, users can also add connectors for their agent. Click on Add connector and the available AI connectors can be added.
  • Admins can also add Egnyte tools as connectors.
  • Select File and Folder Tools and click on Add.
  • Set each tool Permissions as always allow, always ask, deny or Custom and click on Save.
  • Egnyte tool will be added to the agent as a Connector.
  • Access
  • Access to the agent can also be defined while creating the agent. By default, Public is selected.
  • Users can select the following options:
    • Public: Any user in the domain can view and interact with the agent
    • Private: Only the creator and admin users can view and interact with the agent
    • Restricted: Access is granted to specific users and groups
  • If the user selects Restricted as the option, they can enter the user or group details, select the permission as Viewer (default) or Owner. Owners get the ability to edit the agent whereas Viewers can only interact with the agent.
  • Click on Add to continue adding more users or groups.
  • Egnyte does not store the edit or modification history for agents. It is recommended to grant Owner access only to users who require it.
  • Advanced
  • Users can select the model for the agent. Click on the dropdown to select the available model. Users can also select the response mode:
    • Fast (default): Preferable for everyday tasks
    • Thinking: Select this mode when calculations or advanced mathematical reasoning is needed
  • Test Your Agent
  • Users can test their agent before creating it. They can enter a prompt to test or select from the prompt added by the user. Testing the agent also offers the following:
    • Improve the prompt
    • Use existing prompts for testing
    • Include file(s) using the + icon
  • Click on Save and Open to create the agent.
  • The agent will be created successfully and it will be available for the user to start using it.
  • The newly created agent will be available under AI -> Agents section and under the Agents listing in the contextual entry point.
Back to Top…
Create Agent from a Template
  • Navigate to the AI option in the left menu. Click on Agents -> +Create Agents button at the top-right or in the tile.
  • Users can also navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Agents and click on Create New Agent.
  • Select the desired template from the left menu and click on Use this template.
  • Egnyte offers five templates to provide the users with Agents ideas. Additional Templates cannot be created at this time.
  • Agent details will be pre-filled based on the template selected. Users can modify the details, if required, and test the agent using the steps as mentioned earlier. Click on Save and Open to create.
  • The agent will be created successfully and it will open for the user to start using it.
Back to Top…
Import Agent
  • Navigate to the AI option in the left menu. Click on Agents -> +Create Agents button at the top-right or in the tile.
  • Users can also navigate to Settings -> AI Powered Features -> Agents and click on Create New Agent.
  • Click on Import Agent.
  • Click on Select file(s) and select the desired file(s) or drag-drop the file(s) to continue.
  • The details will populate as per the file(s) uploaded. Users can click on the Re-upload skills file and select different file(s), if needed.
  • Users can modify the details, if required, and test the agent using the steps as mentioned earlier. Click on Save and Open to create.
Back to Top…

Use an Agent

  • Users can navigate to AI and click on any agent available under Agents.
  • Users can search for a specific agent or use the following quick filters:
    • All: This is the default selection displaying all the agents
    • By Egnyte: The agents created by the system are displayed
    • My Agents: The agents created by the user are displayed
    • Trending Now: The most frequently used agents are displayed
  • Alternatively, users can also utilize the contextual entry point from any of the Egnyte pages. They can select the desired agent from the dropdown.
  • As soon as the users open the agent, they will get an option to provide their input and start interacting with the agent. They can click on the icon at the top-left to collapse the side panel. Users can hover over the i icon to read the agent description.
  • Provide the input to the agent and get the response. They can type the prompt or click on the + icon -> Prompts to select any of the prompts from the Prompt library. Users can also type @<filename or folder name> to direct their query to specific file(s) and folder(s). Users can tag up to 20 items directly within a prompt using @<filename/foldername>.
  • Users can also click on the + icon -> Upload files and select the files to directly use them in their prompt to the agent. Users can also drag and drop the files or paste the files.
  • The selected files will be saved in the user’s private folder at /Private/<username>/AI Uploads. These files are automatically tagged with the Content Source: AI Upload tag under ai content section.
  • If the user adds more than 20 items using @<filename/foldername>, further selection will be disabled and they will see a message to deselect some items to select the new ones.
  • Similarly, the users will be informed about the maximum limit if they try to upload files after 20 items are already selected and/or uploaded.
  • Click on the source(s) to view the agent source(s). Alternatively, click on the + icon and click on > for Egnyte and Web sources to view the specific source(s). Click on the arrow to send the query to the agent.
  • The agent begins processing the input to provide a response. The user can monitor the status.
  • The response is generated based on the user’s input.
  • Based on the user’s query, the agent may take a while before generating the response. In such scenarios, there is a notification made available in the Notifications Icon at the top. The notification appears when the user moves out from the Agents screen and the response is generated.

AI Personalization

Agents can personalize responses using data and memories based on configured settings.

Admins can also set up a corporate glossary for AI to refer to the company-specific terminology and definitions.

Agents can automatically learn and add memories from user interactions, refer to past chats, and allow users to add, view, and manage memories.

Use Egnyte Tools

Egnyte tools can be added as connectors while creating an agent. These tools, such as file and folder tools can then be utilised while interacting with the agent. For instance, required files in a particular folder can be renamed by the agent. The agent will ask for the user’s confirmation based on the configured setting as Always allow, Always ask, or Deny.

Currently, Egnyte tools are available to domain administrators only. Users who are not domain administrators will not see the File and Folder Tools connector and cannot use these tools in AI Assistant or in Agents.

Edit a Prompt

Users can edit the most recent prompt given to the agent to refine the response.

  • Click on the Edit icon.
  • Edit the prompt and click on Send.
  • The agent will generate the response as per the edited prompt.
Copy Text

Click on the Copy text icon and the response generated by the agent will be copied to Clipboard.

Back to Top…
Share Chat

Chats can be shared with any existing users or users that have been selected.

  • Click on the Share icon -> Share from any of the responses or from the Share icon at the top. The option at the top is disabled unless the user starts interacting with the agent.
  • Alternatively, users can navigate to the Recents, click on the three-dots icon -> Share.
  • Select Existing Users (default) or Users you choose and enter the user(s). Click on Get share link.
  • The link to the conversation will be copied and the user can share it with the intended recipients
  • Source files are referenced but not shared while sharing a conversation. The recipients will see the conversation content only, even if they don’t have access to the files.
  • The chosen users will receive an email informing them about the shared conversation.
  • When the users click on the link they receive, the same conversation will open up for them to continue interacting with the AI Agent.

  • Click on Save to Egnyte and provide the name to the file. Click on Select Folder.
  • Select the desired folder location and click on Select.
  • Click on Change to reselect the folder location. Click on Save. The response will be saved to the selected folder location.
Download

Users can download the response by clicking on Share icon -> Download. The response will be downloaded to the user’s system as a word document.

Back to Top…
Regenerate Response

The user can regenerate the response by clicking on the Regenerate icon.

Provide Feedback

Users can provide feedback on the responses generated by the agent. They can click on the thumbs up icon if the response was useful.

Click on the thumbs down icon if not satisfied with the response. Enter additional details and click on Submit to improve the response. They can also choose to either provide consent (checked by default) or opt out of allowing Egnyte access to the logs.

Click on any of the historical records to access the agent history of up to 180 days.

Users can access any of the historical records by clicking on it. They can also hover over on the three-dots icon and choose to Share, Rename, Pin or Unpin, and Delete it.

Conversations are automatically generated and assigned meaningful titles, making it easier for users to quickly locate them.

Edit an Agent

This article explains the process of identifying the billing experience and steps to manage any billing settings based on what users see in the product.

Customers Paying by Card
