Creating a Document Room from Portal

The document room owner can create a blank document room from the Document Room Portal by following these steps:

  • Navigate to the Document Room Portal. It provides two options to create a document room as shown in the screenshot.
  • Select the +New Document Room button from the top right corner OR click on the +New Document room tile to expand the Create Document Room menu.
  • Select the Custom Document Room option to create a blank document room. To create a document room from a template, select one of the available templates from the menu. Selecting either will open the Create Document Room Wizard.
  • When creating Document room from templates, the orange box as shown below will indicate the name of the template from which the structure will be copied.
  • On the General page of the wizard, enter the Document Room Name and optionally populate the other document room metadata including Document Room ID and Description. There is also an option to upload a logo (optional) and enable watermarking for files previewed and downloaded by viewer and viewer-only permission (recommended).
  • Click on the Next button after entering the required details.
  • If the user groups and permissions are defined within the document room template, the Document Room ID becomes mandatory metadata.
  • On the Timeline page, choose a Document Room Status and optionally select Document Room Duration. Click Next.
  • On the Folder page, select the location for the document room to be created. The user can select the folders where they have the permission to create the document room. All other folders will remain disabled with tooltip information as shown in the screenshot.
  • Select the Create Document Room button after choosing the folder.
  • On selecting the option to create from the template with dynamic groups configured, the user will be presented with the Document Room Permissions screen. The dynamic user groups will be created for the document room with an option to manage them.
  • Users can select the Manage group for each of the user groups to add appropriate users to the group. Once done with all the user groups, click Close to close the wizard.
  • A new tile corresponding to the created document room will be added to the Document Room Portal.
  • Refer to Document Room Templates for a detailed article on the document room template and how it can be created in Egnyte.
Back to Top…

Filter and Search Options on Document Room Portal

The document room portal displays the document rooms the user has access to. Each tile represents one document room and includes the name of the document room, the duration, and the custom logo.

The user can filter the document rooms by type as All, Active (default), or Inactive (Archived).

They can also filter the document rooms by Status as All (default), Pending, In-Progress, Done, On-hold, or Cancelled.

Clicking on Reset All resets the home page to the default view.

The user can also search for a specific document room using the search functionality at the top right corner.

Creating a Document Room from Collaborate

The document room owners will also have the option to create and manage document rooms from the Collaborate app as well:

  • Navigate to the Collaborate App from the app drawer to access Egnyte Web UI.
  • Navigate to the folder where you want to create the document room.
  • Users need Owner permission to the parent folder where they want to create the document rooms.
  • Click on the +Create dropdown and select the Document Room option. In order to create a document room from a template, click on the +Create dropdown, select the Document Room>From Template option from the dropdown menu, and then select one of the available templates.
  • Enter the Document Room Name and choose a Document Room Status. You can optionally populate the other document room metadata including Document Room ID, Description, and Duration. If the user groups and permissions are defined within the document room template, the Document Room ID becomes mandatory metadata.
  • The user can also upload a logo to be associated with the document room (optional) and enable watermarking for files previewed by users with viewer-only permission (recommended).
  • Select Save to create the document room.
  • On selecting the option to create document room from template with dynamic groups configured, the user will be presented with Document Room Permissions screen. The dynamic user groups will be created for the document room with an option to manage them.
  • The user can select the Manage group for each of the user groups to add appropriate users to the group. Once done with all the user groups, select Close to close the wizard.

Create and Manage Workspaces

The Document Portal organizes content into Workspaces. Each external user such as client, vendor, or partner organization will have their own Workspace that acts as a secure portal for both internal and external access. Each Workspace is associated with a single folder in the Egnyte filesystem.

Create an Empty Workspace

Create a Workspace From an Existing Folder

Create a Workspace From a Template

Editing Workspace Settings

Manage External Users

Delete Workspace

Create Folders and Manage Users

Audit Reporting

Users can create a Workspace in three different ways:

  • Create an Empty Workspace
  • Create a Workspace from an Existing Folder
  • Create a Workspace from a Template Workspaces are included in the Document Portal Add-on and available to all Platform plans. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to learn more on how to get access to this feature.

Create an Empty Workspace

To create an empty Workspace, perform the following steps:

  • Open the Document Portal app.
  • Click on the New Workspace button in the top right corner, and then select Empty Workspace from the displayed options.
  • In the New Workspace dialog, choose the Workspace Type, enter the Workspace Name, select the Workspace Status, and then click Next.
  • Optionally add key Contacts and Links within the Resources tab, and then click Next. These static resources will be available to the external users on their home tab of a Workspace.
  • Select the Workspace folder location by choosing an existing folder or creating a new one in the shared space by clicking on the Create new folder option and click Create Workspace.
  • The system will create a new Workspace folder under the selected destination with the Workspace Name entered on the General step.
  • The workspace folder will inherit the permissions from a selected folder.
  • The newly created Workspace will be displayed on the Document Portal’s Workspaces list. Navigate to the Workspace by selecting the Workspace name, and begin creating a folder structure according to specific requirements. User permissions can be managed using the Manage Folder Permissions option available in the Share menu.
  • Refer to the Create Folders and Manage Users section for more information.

Create a Workspace From an Existing Folder

To create a Workspace from an existing folder, perform the following steps:

  • Navigate to the folder in the Collaborate Web UI.
  • From the three-dots menu, choose Mark as Document Portal Workspace.
  • Fill in the fields in the dialog, choosing the Type, optionally changing the Name (defaults to the existing folder name), and choosing the status, and then click Next.
  • Optionally, the users can also add key Contacts and Links for the external users in the Resources tab.
  • Click Mark as workspace to create the Workspace from the selected folder. The Workspace will be displayed on the Document Portal’s Workspaces list. Upon navigating to the Workspace by selecting the Workspace name, the existing folders and files will be displayed. New folders can be created, and user permissions can be managed through the Manage Folder Permissions option under the Share menu.
  • Refer to the Create Folders and Manage Users section for more information.

Create a Workspace From a Template

To create a workspace from an existing template, perform the following steps:

  • Open the Document Portal app.
  • Click on the New Workspace button in the top right corner, and select a template to create a Workspace from.
  • A new Workspace dialog will open. Choose the Workspace Type, enter the Workspace Name, select the Workspace Status, and then click Next.
  • Optionally, the users can also add key Contacts and Links for the external users in the Resources tab, and then click Next.
  • Select the Workspace folder location by choosing an existing folder or creating a new one in the shared space by clicking on the Create new folder option and click Next.
  • The system will create a new Workspace folder under the selected destination with the Workspace Name entered on the General step.
  • Within the Access tab, a list of dynamic roles is displayed. Users can be added to one or multiple roles, all roles, or left unassigned if permissions are not being set up at this time. These dynamic roles are created in the template settings, where folder paths can be defined, and specific permission types can be assigned to each role individually.
  • The dynamic roles are available during workspace creation only.
  • Once the workspace is created, users can manage the permissions using the Manage Folder Permissions option available in the Share menu. Refer to the Create Folders and Manage Users section for more information.

Editing Workspace Settings

Users can modify the Workspace Type, name, status, and the Resources by navigating to the Workspace and then clicking on Workspace Settings on the top right corner. They can also manage external users from these settings.

Manage External Users

Admins and Workspace creators can remove external users from Workspace. Once removed, the system will automatically revoke the folder permissions associated with Workspace.

  • If the external users had access to only or the last accessible Workspace, they will be automatically redirected to Egnyte Collaborate and can access the folder(s) with permissions.
  • If the external users have access to other Workspaces, they will no longer see the Workspace they are removed from but will continue to access other Workspace(s) in their Document Portal. To remove an external user, Navigate to the Workspace -> Workspace Settings -> External Users. Hover over on the user to delete and click on the delete icon.

Delete Workspace

Admins and Owners can now delete a Workspace that is no longer needed. Once deleted, the associated folder in Collaborate will have a Workspace icon removed and converted into a regular folder.

All user permissions will be retained, and all the users can access the folder in Collaborate.

  • If the Standard users have access to only deleted or the last accessible Workspace, they will be automatically redirected to Egnyte Collaborate and can access the folder(s) with permissions.
  • If the Standard users have access to other Workspaces, they will no longer see the deleted one but will continue to access other Workspace(s) in their Document Portal. To delete a workspace, Navigate to the Workspace -> Workspace Settings -> General. Click on the Delete Workspace button at the bottom left.

Create Folders and Manage Users

Once a Workspace is created, files and folders can be added and access can be given to external parties. This can be done either within the Workspace itself, or through any other mechanism like the Collaborate Web UI or Mobile App.

To add content and invite users in the Workspace:

  • Navigate to the Workspace in the Document Portal App.
  • New folder(s) and subfolder(s) can be created within the Workspace folder as per your needs. Users can be added or removed from specific folders and folder permissions can be set for each user.
  • Power and Admin users (internal users) with permissions to any folder(s) within the Workspace can access the Workspace folder from both the Document Portal and from any other Egnyte endpoint.
  • Standard Users (external users) with access to any folder(s) within the Workspace will only be able to access Egnyte via the Document Portal. They will not have access to the Collaborate app or any other Egnyte functionality.

All actions performed by users related to Workspace are tracked in the File Reports under Audit Reports. The report tracks the following activities under the Action Info column and can be filtered by using Workspace Activity in the Actions field.

Document Portal For External Users

The Egnyte Document Portal provides a streamlined interface for external users (Standard Users) to access content in Egnyte and complete assigned tasks. External users with access to a Workspace will only have access to Egnyte via the Document Portal. They will not be able to access the Collaborate app or any other Egnyte functionality.

Accessing External User Specific Portal

The external users have access to three tabs in the portal:

  • The Home tab with a consolidated list of pending tasks including upload requests, signature requests, and workflows, along with resources featuring key Contacts and Links.
  • The Tasks tab with a comprehensive list of all tasks assigned to the user. This list includes all the pending, completed and canceled tasks
  • The Files tab which provides access to the files and folders the user has been given access to On logging into Egnyte Document Portal, external users see a list of pending tasks and essential Resources with key Contacts and Links. They can open and complete their pending tasks directly from the list.

When an external user has access to multiple Workspaces, then they will see a list of Workspaces along with the number of pending tasks for each Workspace. Once users click on a specific workspace, they are navigated to the Workspace’s Home tab. From here, the user can navigate to the Tasks and Files tabs of the specific workspace.

Limitations

  • Each external user consumes an Egnyte Standard User license
  • It may take up to 60 minutes for an existing Standard User to gain access to the Document Portal after being assigned to a Workspace. Newly created Standard Users will immediately have access.

Document Portal Overview and using Document Portal

Document Portal Overview

Egnyte’s Document Portal provides a secure platform that allows customers to collaborate, communicate and share files with their external users easily. It offers a user-friendly portal for external users where they can participate in document-centric workflows and tasks. Document Portal decreases turnaround time on external user tasks.

Following are some of the key capabilities included in Egnyte’s Document Portal:

  • Create dedicated Workspaces for working with external users (Standard Users)
  • Workspaces provide external users a streamlined, task-centric experience for upload requests, eSignature requests, and workflows
  • Internal users (Power Users) can see the list of Workspaces and search or filter to access them without needing to know their location in the file system
  • Create Workspaces from a template, from an existing folder, or from scratch
  • Set up Workspace Types to manage different types of external parties (Example: clients, partners, vendors) Document Portal and Upload Requests are included in the Document Portal Add-on and available to all Platform plans. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to learn more on how to get access to this feature.

Accessing The Document Portal Application

To access the Document Portal application:

  • Click on the App Picker icon in the top-left corner of the screen.
  • Choose Document Portal from the list. All Administrators and Power Users will see this application.

Workspaces

Document Portal organizes content in “Workspaces”. Each external user such as client, vendor, or partner organization will have their own Workspace that acts as a secure portal for both internal and external access. Each Workspace is associated with a single folder in the Egnyte filesystem.

External users are limited to accessing the Workspace folder from within the portal, while internal users can access it through the portal or directly through the Egnyte folder. This means that if external parties are already being invited to Egnyte as Standard Users, their folders can be marked as Workspaces to provide a richer external user experience.

Upon opening the Document Portal application, a list of the Workspaces will be displayed.

All Power and Admin users can view the entire list of workspaces but only those with permissions to the underlying Workspace folder can open it. Users can search for a specific Workspace, Workspace type, Workspace creator and status by clicking on the Filters button.

Access Collaborate from Workspaces

Users can access Collaborate folders from Workspaces.

  • Navigate to Workspaces and hover over any of the Workspace. Click on the three-dots menu -> Open in Collaborate
  • If the user is already within a workspace, they can navigate to the Files tab within the workspace and click on the Collaborate icon.
  • In either case, Files will open in Collaborate. Ready to create a Workspace. Check this Create and Manage Workspaces article to learn more.

Document Room Collaboration Portal

Document Room Portal is the main homepage that users will navigate to when they login into the Document Room.

The document room portal displays all document rooms accessible to the user. Each tile represents one document room and includes the name of the document room, the duration of the document room, and the custom logo.

Users can filter the document rooms by type:

  • All

  • Active (default)

  • Inactive (Archived) Users can also filter the document rooms by Status:

  • All (default)

  • Pending

  • In-Progress

  • Done

  • On-hold

  • Cancelled They can also search for a specific document room using the search functionality at the top right corner.

User Access Levels

  • Document room owner will have to switch to the Collaborate app for performing some of the collaboration activities such as
    • Reporting
    • Creating a document room
    • Managing document room templates
    • Managing users and groups
    • Managing settings, configurations, and preferences
  • The internal collaborators (power users) will also have an option to switch to Collaborate although they can perform most of the collaboration from the document room portal.
  • The external stakeholders (standard users) will not have access to collaborate and the only portal to collaborate for standard users will be the document room portal. When the user clicks on the Document Room tile, it will navigate the user to that Document Room with the overview page loaded by default. The overview will be as shown below.

The contextual left menu bar helps the user to browse through different aspects of the document room in which they want to collaborate.

If the user wants to navigate to another document room, they can select the home icon available on the top left menu bar and select the desired document room from the home dashboard.

Recent Files

All the recent files accessed by the user within the context of the document room are visible here.

File and Folder Listing

The file and folder listing of the document room based on the user’s permissions are visible here. The user can upload documents, preview documents, download documents, share links, and share upload links.

The files and folders within the document room are auto-indexed so that each document or folder within the doc room can be referenced with its unique index number. At this time, auto-indexing is currently supported up to 5 levels deep. Files and folders beyond that will not be auto-indexed.

Users have the option to export the index report (document room contents along with indexes) in csv format.

Standard users will have limited collaboration abilities within the document room. They will not be able to access the following:

  • Document comments
  • Document workflows
  • Document version history
  • Sharing folder and file links
  • Folder activity stream
  • File and folder details like modified by or last modified. Depending upon the permissions assigned, standard users will get access to folders and documents. Additionally, document previews and/or downloads within the document room will be watermarked according to the watermarking settings configured at the domain and document room level.

Bookmarks

All the folders bookmarked by the user within the context of the document room they are in, are visible here. Refer to Bookmark Folders in the Web UI – Egnyte for a detailed article on how bookmarks work in Egnyte.

Refer helpdesk pages for guidance on how to collaborate in Egnyte.

Trash

Files and folders that were deleted from the document room are visible here based on the user’s permissions. User with restore privileges can restore the files and folders from the trash as needed.

Searching within a Document Room

The search bar in the top right corner enables the user to search for any documents within that document room. Refer to Search for Files and Folders in the WebUI for a detailed article on how search works in Egnyte.

Document Room capabilities are available only through dedicated Document Room Plans - Document Room and Document Room Enterprise.

Document Room Lifecycle Management

Updating Document Room Status

To update the document room timelines, including lifecycle phase and start and end date, click on More > Document Room Settings. If you would like to convert the document room back to a standard folder, click on Don’t treat as Document Room anymore.

Initiating Document Room Clean Up

Document Room lifecycle management also makes it quick and convenient to remove external access to the document room and apply pre-defined retention, archival, or deletion policies on the document room after completion of the document room.

To initiate the clean-up, the document room owner must first open to the Document Room Settings page. This can be found by navigating inside the Document Room either from Document Room Portal or Collaborate and then selecting More > Document Room Settings (as shown in screenshot below).

On the Document Room Settings page, updating the Status to Done will initiate the document room clean-up process.

There are 2 major components to the document room clean-up process.

  • A notification that the document room might be under Content Archiving Policy will be displayed. If any Content Lifecycle policies have already been created and are applicable to this document room, the policies will begin upon selecting Save.

  • There will be an option to Clean up Document Room after saving status as “Done”. Selecting this checkbox and then Save will open a new document room clean-up window where links & standard user access can be revoked. When “Clean up Document Room” has been selected a new window will appear with three sections, each with its own options.

  • Section 1: Links associated with this Document Room – a user has the option to delete links or leave them in place.

  • Section 2: Standard User Accounts associated with this Document Room – a user has the option to Select or view users, Delete all users, Deactivate all users, or Don’t do anything. When they click on Select or view users, they can delete or deactivate users on a case-by-case basis.

  • Section 3: Standard User Accounts associated with this and other document rooms - Selecting View users, lists out all the standard users that have access to this document room and the other document rooms within your domain; however, standard users cannot be deleted or disabled from this interface. When Clean-up is selected a final confirmation screen will be shown. This screen requires the user to type a confirmation message and then select Clean up Users and links to complete the process.

Document Room capabilities are available only through dedicated Document Room Plans - Document Room and Document Room Enterprise.

Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started with the new document room plan.

Document Room Templates

Document Room Templates make it easy to create new document rooms using a predefined folder structure and permission set.

In addition to assigning permissions for pre-existing groups or users, document room-specific groups can be created and assigned permissions on the folder structure at the time of document room creation. The document room-specific groups can then be populated with individual users giving them access to the respective document room.

The user can set up different templates for different document room types and choose who has access to use templates.

Creating a Document Room Template

Document Room Templates are stored in /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Document Room Templates. Follow these steps to create a Document Room Template:

  • Create a folder under /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Document Room Templates. The name of the folder will be the template name.

  • Add subfolders and files to the template as needed.

  • (Optionally) Set any folder options (e.g. descriptions, link sharing controls, etc.) on the folders within the template.

  • (Optionally) Use Document Room Template Settings from the three-dots menu to set a template description and configure the groups and permissions for the template. The Document Room Template Settings dialog has two tabs General and Template Permissions. The user can enter the template name and description in the General tab. The Template Permissions tab allows users to define Document Room Template Permissions with a User Interface. Click on Manage Permissions to open the permissions page.

  • In the Permissions template a list of folders appears in the left pane. Select a folder to assign permissions to groups.

  • Additionally there is a toggle to control whether or not the folder should inherit permissions from its parent folder.

  • To assign users or groups with the permissions, click on the Add user group menu and select Existing user or group option.

  • This will open a pop-up window, where the user will be prompted to enter an existing user or an existing group name and specify a permission.

  • After the permission is entered it becomes visible on the template permission page. To control who can create new document rooms from your Document Room Template, set permissions on the template folder using the Permissions icon from the top menu. Any user with at least Viewer permissions on the template will be able to use it to create new document rooms.

Create Dynamic Groups

Users can also create dynamic groups, for example, “{Document Room Name} - Finance”, which will be created upon project setup.

  • Click on the Add user or group menu and then select Create new group.
  • If the Use a prefix is checked, then either the Document Room Name or Document Room ID will be used as a prefix in the dynamic group.
  • Enter the required details and click on Create.

Creating a Document Room from a Template

Use the following steps to create a new document room from a template:

  • Navigate to a folder with Owner permissions.
  • From the +Create menu, choose Document Room > From Template.
  • Enter details about the document room. The Document Room name will be used as the folder name for the new document room. Depending on the template selected, the Document Room ID may be required. Click Next after entering the details about the document room.
  • The new document room is created. If the template created document room-specific groups, the user will see a list of those groups with an option to manage each group. Clicking the Manage Group button will open the group details page in a separate browser tab. Here, it is possible to add users to groups so that they get access to the new document room. Document Room capabilities are available only through dedicated Document Room Plans - Document Room and Document Room Enterprise.

Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started with the new document room plan.

Egnyte Document Room Overview

Egnyte Document Room is a single, secure repository for sensitive data that employs AI-powered capabilities to easily manage, find, and utilize unstructured content and information within an organization’s content while preserving data confidentiality.

Following are some of the key value propositions that Egnyte Document Room has to offer to our customers:

Improved Security Posture

A standalone and separate domain to collaborate on your sensitive and confidential information to improve the security posture.

Purpose-Built User Experience

Provides a simple, straightforward portal for external user access, including anonymity controls. This ensures that external stakeholders can collaborate on document rooms with ease without exposing their identity to other external stakeholders.

Enhanced Content Management

Includes content indexing, permission change alerts, permission templates and deal closure. This improves the overall experience of collaborating on document rooms and makes it a more efficient and effective process.

Enhanced Sharing Controls

The means to restrict who can access, download, comment and re-share content on a fine-grained basis. This gives better control to the owners of the document rooms to ensure that the stakeholders have appropriate access to the necessary content.

Enhanced Analytics

Provides visibility into who and how often content is accessed on a per-room basis as well as being able to make document owners based on informed decisions while performing due diligence on their document room.

In addition, Egnyte Document Room is commonly used for the following:

  • Mergers and Acquisitions
  • Investment Fundraising
  • Board Reporting
  • Asset Sales
  • Private Equity Diligence and IPO Preparation
  • Investor Services
  • Bid Management
  • IP Protection Egnyte Document Rooms can be configured to provide enhanced sharing controls, with full anonymity across various counterparties. With these Document Rooms, your teams can also access self-service reporting to understand who’s been viewing and interacting with shared documents.

Document Room works seamlessly with your existing Egnyte solution, so there is no need to replicate data or learn new tools.

Egnyte Document Room – FAQs

Q. Why does a user need a document room?

Companies looking to manage and share very sensitive files with partners require additional security and controls beyond what a traditional file-sharing service can provide.

Egnyte Document Room is a single, secure repository for sensitive data that employs AI-powered capabilities to easily manage, find, and utilize unstructured content and information within an organization’s content while preserving data confidentiality. It provides

  • Enhanced sharing controls
  • Enhanced analytics
  • A purpose-built user experience
  • Enhanced content management
  • AI-powered content insight

Q. How is the Egnyte Document Room different from the traditional Egnyte?

Egnyte Document Rooms provides additional features not available in traditional Egnyte. They are summarised in the following table.

Traditional Egnyte

Egnyte Document Room

Access and Activity Reports

Reports are available at domain level

Self-service, predesigned reports for file audits, user permissions, and provisioning available to document room owners

Folder Tree

Users can view all folders they have permissions for in the entire domain

Users can only view the folders they have permission to within a specific document room

Restricted access for SU

Not available

Disabled comments, workflows, version history, activity stream, sensitive metadata like last modified and modified by

Watermarking

Files shared via links can be watermarked (higher tier plans only)

Files in preview and downloaded files display dynamic watermarks

Content Indexing

Not available

Automatically adds a unique number to each file and folder

User Portal

Not available

Users have their own portal displaying the document rooms they can access

Project Lifecycle

Available on AEC Package - Close a project and sever links and permissions

Close a project, sever links and permissions, and apply RAD policies

Viewer-Only Permission

Available to only Platform Enterprise plan (On demand based on technical eligibility)

Available with both the Egnyte Document Room plans.

Q. Can a user deploy Egnyte Document Room within their existing Egnyte domain?

No. Egnyte Document Room is a dedicated and separate domain to ensure you can securely collaborate on sensitive content in a controlled environment.

Q. Can a user have Egnyte Document Room as one of their MEM domains?

Yes. However, Multiple Entity Management (MEM) only lets users switch between domains from a single login and it does not link data, permissions, or features. Document Room folders and content remain isolated to the Document Room domain and will not be visible or accessible from any other MEM-linked (non–Document Room) domain.

Q. What different billing plans are available for Egnyte Document Room?

There are two billing plans – Document Room and Document Room Enterprise. Reach out to your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more details on these plans.

Q. How can one get started with Egnyte Document Room?

Please contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started with a new document room plan.

Q. How can a user configure Egnyte Document Room?

Please refer to Configure Document Room Domain – Egnyte for more details on how to configure your Egnyte Document Room.

Q. What kind of custom branding is supported by Egnyte Document Room?

The same custom branding capabilities supported by traditional Egnyte are also applicable to Egnyte Document Room. For more details, you can refer to Custom Branding Egnyte – Egnyte.

Q. Can a user migrate my data from my existing Egnyte domain/external data sources to the Egnyte Document Room domain? What options are available?

Yes. There are multiple options available to migrate the data from an existing Egnyte domain/third-party apps into Egnyte Document Room domain:

  • Use the Egnyte to Egnyte Connector feature (existing domain needs to have Secure & Govern enabled) to sync the data from an existing domain into the new Egnyte Document Room domain.
  • For more complex migration or to migrate data from external data sources, use the Migration Tool provided by Egnyte.
  • It is also possible to use Egnyte Professional Services to migrate data from external data sources into Egnyte Document Room domain. Please discuss specific requirements with the account manager or Egnyte Sales team to choose the right option.

Q. Is there any limit on the number of document rooms that can be created?

No, there is no limit.

Q. Does Egnyte Document Room support templates?

Yes. The user can create document rooms based on pre-defined templates but first need to configure the document room templates . For more details, please refer to Document Room Templates – Egnyte.

The user can also engage with Egnyte Professional Services to set up the document room templates.

Q. If a user is unable to create document rooms do they need any special privileges for creating document rooms?

Yes, only Admins and Power Users with administrative privileges of managing document rooms are allowed to create document rooms. Please refer to Create and Manage Document Rooms – Egnyte for more details on how to create and manage document rooms.

Q. How can one customise document rooms so that the stakeholders can identify them quickly?

Each document room can be given a specific name, description and logo.

Q. Can a user invite multiple stakeholders to collaborate in their document room?

Yes. For more details, please refer to Inviting Multiple Users in Document Room – Egnyte.

Q. What is the Document Room Portal in the Egnyte Document Room?

Document Room Portal is the default landing page where stakeholders can access all the document rooms that they have permissions for. For more details, please refer to Document Room Collaboration Portal – Egnyte

Q. How can a user enable content indexed in the file and folder listing?

In Egnyte Document Room files and folders are auto-indexed with a unique number when a new folder is created or a new file is uploaded. However, the index is only displayed when the user accesses the Document Room from the Document Room Portal. If they access the Document Room via Collaborate app they will not see the indexing numbers.

Q.How can a user export the file and folder listing of their document room along with the index?

The user can export the index report which will have all the files and folders contained within the document room along with respective indexes by going to More > Download Index (CSV) from the file and folder listing of the root folder within any document room.

Q. Are there any restrictions for Admins and Power Users in the Egnyte Document Room?

No.

Q. Are there any restrictions for Standard Users in the Egnyte Document Room?

Yes, Standard Users are the external stakeholders collaborating on sensitive content and hence there are some restrictions on what they can do.

Standard users will have limited collaboration abilities within the document room. They will not be able to access the following:

  • Document comments
  • Document workflows
  • Document version history
  • Sharing folder and file links
  • Folder activity stream
  • File and folder details like modified by, last modified, etc.

Q. What kind of reporting and analytics capabilities are available with Egnyte Document Room?

Document Room owners and privileged internal collaborators have access to specific reports to track file usage and governance within their document rooms. For more details, please refer to Utilizing Document Room Specific Reports – Egnyte.

Q. What is the maximum time duration available for the reports?

The past 180 days.

Q. What is the default time duration selected for running the reports?

The Last 7 days.

Q. Can a user selectively enable watermarking for specific document rooms?

Yes, but only if the domain admin has configured the Egnyte Document Room to allow Document Room owners to override the domain-level watermarking configuration for document rooms. Then the Document Room Owners can decide whether they want to watermark files previewed and downloaded within specific document rooms or not.

Q. If watermarking is enabled, which permission levels will see watermarks?

When the watermarking is enabled for the document room, the files previewed by viewer and viewer-only permission will be watermarked. In addition, the files downloaded with viewer permission will also be watermarked.

Q. Why can’t a user download a folder in the Egnyte Document Room?

Currently, Egnyte does not support watermarking the files when the entire folder is downloaded. In order to reduce unauthorized dissemination, when watermarking on download for viewer permission is enabled, downloading the entire folder is prevented.

Q. Why can’t a user download some files in the Egnyte Document Room?

Currently, Egnyte does not support watermarking files above 50 MB size (for txt files it is 1 MB). In order to reduce unauthorized dissemination, downloading of files larger than 50 MB in size is prevented.

Q. What kind of lifecycle management capabilities are available in the Egnyte Document Room?

Document room lifecycle management allows a user to remove external access to a document room and initiate previously created retention, archival, or deletion policies on a document room after completion. For more details, please refer to Document Room Lifecycle Management – Egnyte.

Q. What integrations are available with Egnyte Document Room?

Technically all the integrations supported by Egnyte are also available with Egnyte Document Room. However, only MS and Google co-editing integrations, Power User-initiated DocuSign, and Adobe Sign integrations are fully supported and hence can be safely enabled and used.

Q. Can one use SSO to access Egnyte Document Room?

Yes, the Egnyte Document Room supports integration with several SSO service providers exactly the same as traditional Egnyte. Please note that only Admins and Power Users can be externally authenticated via SSO. For more details on how to configure SSO, you can refer to Single Sign-On (SSO) Configuration – Egnyte.

Q. Can one use the Desktop and Mobile App to collaborate on Egnyte Document Room?

The Desktop App, Desktop Sync and Mobile App are not fully optimized for document rooms and we recommend they not be enabled.

Q. Can one use Public APIs to integrate third-party applications with Egnyte Document Room?

Although Public APIs are not fully optimized for Document Room, they are available to be used for any third-party integrations. However, it is strongly recommended not to have any third-party integrations with Egnyte Document Room to ensure content security and confidentiality.

Q. Does renaming the Document Room automatically rename the associated parent folder?

No, the names of the Document room and the associated parent folder are not in sync. Renaming the document room does not automatically rename its associated parent folder.

Note: Document Room capabilities are available only through dedicated Document Room Plans - Document Room and Document Room Enterprise.

Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started with the new document room plan.

Inviting Multiple Users in Document Room

Egnyte provides the capability to invite multiple new users to collaborate in a document room. At this time the document room owner can also associate them with appropriate user groups so that once they register, they will automatically get access to the document room and permissioned content.

Inviting New Users to Document Room

Document room owners who have been assigned the admin privilege of adding users within the domain will be able to invite new users to collaborate within their document room from the permission management display as shown below.

When the user selects the option to invite new users, it will open a dialogue box where the details of each user can be added. When the users are not associated with any groups, specific permissions can be added as shown below.

As a best practice, new users should be assigned to existing user groups to ensure the proper permissions are conveyed.

The user can also add a custom welcome message to the invitation email sent.

Once the user adds all the required user details and selects “Invite Users”, all the users will be sent the invitation email to register and will be added to the user groups as configured. New users who aren’t associated with a group will inherit the permission of the folder they are assigned to.

The admin capability to add users, user groups, and add users to the groups from Collaborate will continue to be supported. To invite existing users to collaborate within the document room, they will need to be added to the user groups from the Collaborate user group settings or their permissions added from permission management

Tasks Management in Document Portal

Tasks Assignments in Document Portal

Internal users (Power Users) can assign the following three types of tasks to either internal or external users (Standard Users).

  • Upload Request Workflows

  • Review and Approval workflows

  • Egnyte Signature requests (Requires the PDF File Handler Add-On) Perform the following step to assign a task from the Document Portal.

  • Navigate to the Document Portal.

  • Open a Workspace and navigate to the Files tab.

  • To assign Upload Requests:

    1. Navigate to the desired folder where the files need to be uploaded, then click on the three-dots icon.

  • b. Navigate to Create Upload Request Workflow option and select one of the available templates. Refer to Creating an Upload Request to learn more about it.

  • To send a Signature request, select the file first and refer to Sending Signature Requests for information on how to create a Signature request.

  • To create a Review and Approval Workflow, select the file to assign a task on and refer to the Creating a Workflow section for detailed instructions on creating workflow tasks.

Tasks Management For Internal Users

Internal users (Power Users) can easily track and manage their tasks using the Home and Tasks tabs in a Workspace.

The Home provides a list of in-progress tasks within the current Workspace. This includes the following list of tasks.

  • Assigned to me: A list of all in-progress tasks assigned to the logged-in user.
  • Created by me: A list of all in-progress tasks created by the logged-in user. Users can access a comprehensive list of tasks, by navigating to the Tasks tab of a Workspace. In the Tasks tab, users can view and manage tasks with all statuses, including canceled and completed tasks. Users can access the list of tasks assigned to them by navigating to Tasks -> Assigned to them. Users can access the list of tasks created by them by navigating to Tasks -> Created By Me.

Additionally, the tasks can be viewed and managed by navigating to Workflows & Signatures in Collaborate.

To manage Upload Requests, navigate to Upload Requests Workflows > Upload Requests created by me. For more details, refer to Managing Upload Requests.

Navigate to Signatures > Sent Requests to manage Egnyte Sign requests you have created. Refer to Manage Signature Requests for more information.

Navigate to Document Workflows > Workflows I Created to manage Review and Approval Workflow tasks. Refer to Workflows I Created for more information on how to manage the workflows and Editing A Workflow for how to edit a workflow.

Completing Tasks

All assignees receive email notifications for their assigned tasks. They can open and complete these tasks directly from their email.

Assignees with access to the Collaborate Web UI can access their assigned tasks by navigating to the Workflows & Signatures in Collaborate.

  • Upload Request Workflows > Upload Requests assigned to me provides access to upload requests.
  • Signatures > My Requests provides access to assigned Egnyte Sign requests.
  • Workflows > Tasks Assigned to me provides access to Review and Approval workflow tasks Assignees with access to a Workspace can access their assigned tasks from the Pending tasks list on the home tab of the Document Portal.

Once the assignee opens the specific task to complete, refer to the following articles to complete designated tasks.

  • Uploading the Documents to complete Upload Request
  • Signing the Document to complete Egnyte Sign task
  • Completing Workflow Tasks for completing Review and Approval tasks

Terms of Access in Document Room

Egnyte enables admins and Document Room Owners to create Terms of Access for Document Rooms to help facilitate compliance when collaborating on sensitive information. Admins and Document Room Owners can enable, disable, and update those terms as needed. Users must review and accept the Terms of Access before they can access the Document Room, ensuring that access is granted only after the required terms have been acknowledged.

Enable and Create Terms of Access

Disable Terms of Access

Acceptance of Terms of Access

Terms of Access Audit Report

Additional Information

Enable and Create Terms of Access

Admins and Document Room Owners have the capability to enable and create the Terms of Access for other users. By default, the terms acceptance to access the document room is disabled.

  • Navigate to the Document Room and click on the Document Room Settings.
  • Click on Terms of Access.
  • Enable Terms acceptance to access the Document Room.
  • Enter the Terms title (mandatory) and define the Terms content (optional).
  • Egnyte supports RTF Editor but with certain restrictions implemented to enhance security. For example, email addresses and URLs cannot be added.
  • Click on Save
  • The document room settings will be successfully saved.

Disable Terms of Access

Navigate to the Document Room -> Document Room Settings -> Terms of Access. Disable the toggle and click on Save.

Acceptance of Terms of Access

Users will be able to access the document room’s content only when they accept the newly created or updated terms of access.

They will see the document room but the content will not be accessible.

To view and accept the Terms of Access
  • Click on the Document Room and read through the terms of access.
  • Accept the terms and click on Accept and continue.
  • The user will then be able to access the Document Room contents. Also, the document room owners will receive a similar notification.
  • A copy of the Terms of Access accepted by the users is attached as a PDF to the email notification. Similarly, the user who accepts the terms of access will also receive the email notification with the attached PDF in the email.
  • If the users cancel and do not accept the terms, they will receive a notification and will not be able to access the contents of the Document Room.

Terms of Access Audit Report

Admins and Document Room Owners will be able to access the terms of access audit report.

  • Navigate to Reports -> Governance reports -> Terms of Access audit.
  • Terms of Access audit report will be displayed. The report comprises of Date, User name, User company, User group(s), Action, Action info, IP Address, and Old Value. Users can apply filters, such as Timeframe, User type, Specific group, Specific user, Specific company, and Action. They can also click on the Export report to CSV to export the report to their system.

Upload Request Workflows

Upload Request Workflows allow internal users to request a specified list of documents from both external or internal users. This feature provides a streamlined experience for the uploaders and includes an optional built-in document review process to improve the quality of collected documents while minimizing the need for back-and-forth communication between internal and external stakeholders.

Upload Request Workflows are included as part of the Document Portal Add-On. Contact your Account Manager or Egnyte Sales team to add this feature.

Upload Request Templates

Users can create Upload Request templates with a predefined list of required documents, along with an option to enable a review process, set customizable instructions for both uploaders and reviewers, define file size and file type limitations, and configure other details for each document.

Accessing Upload Request Templates

Upload Request templates are available in the Workflow section of the Configuration Settings. The Templates tab allows users to create new templates and manage existing templates.

The Templates tab is available to:

  • Administrators
  • Power Users with a role that grants the can manage Workflow Templates capability. Refer to the Role-Based Administration article to learn more about creating and assigning a role to a Power User By default, the list of templates includes both File Workflow and Upload Request Templates with both Active and Inactive statuses. Users can filter the templates by using Status and Type filters. Active templates are available to end users for creating Upload Request workflows, while Inactive templates are not available to users to create Upload Request workflows.

Creating An Upload Request Template

Perform the following steps to create a new Upload Request template:

  • Navigate to Configuration > Workflows > Templates page
  • Click the Add Template button and select Upload Request Template
  • A New Upload Request Template page will be opened allowing the configuration of the template in the following three sections:
    • Template General Setup
    • Request Setup
    • Template Document Setup General setup section:

This section allows users to define the template’s name and description.

  • Enter a unique Template name with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 50 characters.
  • Optionally, enter Template description with up to 128 characters.
  • Optionally, choose to Allow Document Customization. This is disabled by default. Once enabled, users can add new document(s), edit existing document properties, and exclude existing documents for new requests as well as any of the existing requests in-progress.
  • Choose if anyone (default) or specific group can use the template.
  • Choose if the template can be applied to any folder (default) or existing folder. Request Setup section:

This section enables users to add overall request instructions and provides the option to enable an optional review process.

  • Optionally, enter overall request instructions for assignees in the Request instructions for assignee(s) text field, with a maximum of 500 characters.
  • Users can choose to enable the review option by using the Document review required toggle switch. If enabled, the built-in workflow allows the requester to manually accept or reject the documents. If disabled, uploaded documents are submitted without going through any manual review process.
  • Users can define the due date using the Request expiration period is _ days. When an Upload Request workflow is created, the due date is calculated automatically based on the date request is created and number of days entered in this field. Document Setup section:

Users can add documents and provide instructions and limitations for each document in this section.

Follow these steps to add the documents to be requested by clicking Add document. Users can add up to 50 documents per template.

  • In the Add Document dialog, enter a document name with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 50 characters in the Requested document name field.
  • Select the toggle to keep the document optional or mandatory. By default, it is enabled to make the document mandatory. Disable the toggle to make the document optional.
  • There should at least be one mandatory document in a template.
  • Select Document Type from the options available in the dropdown.
  • In the Instructions for assignee(s) field, users can optionally provide document-specific instructions for assignees with a limit of 500 characters
  • Choose one of the following two options to define the number of files requested from the assignees. The user can request up to 150 files per document.
    • Specific number: Specify the exact number of files required and the assignees will be required to upload a specified number of files
    • Range: Define the minimum and maximum number of files required and the assignees will be required to upload files within a specified range
  • If the document review option is enabled in the Request Setup section, then users will have an option to enter the Instructions for reviewer with a limit of 500 characters
  • Users can choose to enable the Limit the file size and format for the requested files option to further apply the restrictions to the requested files. They can define the maximum file size and allowed file type(s), and the system will enforce these limits during the upload process
  • Click Save to add the document and repeat the steps from this section to add more documents. Once the required document(s) are added , select the checkbox to Activate the template and click the Create template button in the top right corner to make it available to all users.

To restrict the users from using the template, do not select the Activate checkbox. The template can be activated later.

Back to Top

Editing An Upload Request Template

To edit any of the existing templates, select the template name. Then, the Edit option will show up. Click on Edit to update the template configuration. When an edited template is successfully saved, it is stored with an incremented version. The system automatically keeps templates in version control.

Any new changes made to the templates will not affect existing in progress Upload Requests created based on the previous version of the templates.

Back to Top

Duplicating An Upload Request Template

Users can easily create a new template by duplicating an existing one by selecting the duplicate icon when hovering over to a specific template. When duplicating, all parameters except the template name are copied from the new template. Users can then modify any of the parameters and assign a unique template name to create the new template.

Back to Top

Creating An Upload Request From A Template

Once the template is defined, power users and administrators can create Upload Request workflows from the template by using the following steps:

  • Navigate to the folder where the Upload Request should be created and click on the three-dots icon.
  • Navigate to Create Upload Request Workflow option and select one of the available templates.
  • A Create Upload Request Workflow dialog with the pre-populated parameters opens. Any of the pre-populated parameters can be modified if needed
  • Enter users in the Assignee(s) field. Users with an Egnyte account or non-Egnyte users can be added by using their email addresses. If multiple users are added as the assignees, all of them will be able to contribute to the same request.
  • Click on Documents In The Request tab to view the list of documents, number of files required for each document and if the document is optional or mandatory.
  • If the template has the option to allow document customization, the request creator will be able to make modifications.
    • The request creator can add document(s), modify the requirement of the existing documents to Mandatory or Optional, and remove an existing document. At least one document in the request must be marked as mandatory.
  • Click the Submit button
  • The system will automatically create a folder with the same name as the Upload Request name, and within that folder, it will also create subfolders named the same as each individual document included in the request. Once the assignee uploads the documents, they are stored within the designated folder created for the request. Refer to Uploading and Reviewing Documents for an Upload Request article to learn more about how to upload and review the documents.
Back to Top

Managing Upload Requests

Requesters can view and manage the Upload Requests they created by navigating to Upload Request Workflows > Upload Requests created by me under the Workflows & Signatures tab in Egnyte Collaborate.

Requesters can open the upload request by clicking on the specific Upload Request name.They can also edit or cancel an in progress request by hovering over the request and clicking on the Edit option or Cancel icon.

Back to Top

Edit an Existing In-progress Request

  • Hover over a request with pending review or pending upload status and click on Edit.
  • Make changes to the Assignee(s) or Due date under General Settings as needed.
  • Click on Add Document to add another document to the request following the steps as mentioned here.
  • Hover over any of the documents, click on the Edit icon, and select the document type as Mandatory or Optional.
  • Click on the Delete icon to remove any of the documents from the request.
  • Click on Save after making the edits.
  • The upload request workflow will be updated and saved.
Back to Top

Cancel an Existing Pending Request

  • Hover over any of the pending requests and click on the Cancel icon.
  • Click on Cancel request to confirm.

Uploading and Reviewing Documents for an Upload Request

Skip Ahead To…

Uploading the Documents

Document Review

Upload Request Workflows are included as part of the Document Portal Add-On. Contact your Account Manager or Egnyte Sales team to add this feature.

Uploading the Documents

When the new Upload Request is assigned, the assignee receives an email notification including the link to the request, the due date, and the requester’s name. Recipients can open the request directly from the email.

Assignees with access to a Workspace can open the assigned Upload Request from Pending tasks list on the home tab of Document Portal.

Assignees with access to the Collaborate Web UI can access their assigned Upload Request by navigating to Upload Request Workflows > Upload Requests Assigned to Me under the Workflows & Signature tab in Collaborate, as shown in the screenshot below.

The Upload Request will open in a separate tab of the browser. After opening the request, assignees will see the General Request Details section that includes overall request instructions, due date, and the requester’s information.

Assignees can see the list of requested documents in the navigation panel on the left side and select a specific document to upload the file(s) for that document.

Upon selecting a document, assignees can view the document specific instructions and limitations such as number of files, file type and file size, if set by the requester. They can upload files either by clicking the Choose file(s) button or by dragging and dropping from their computer. The system will reject the uploaded file if it does not meet any predefined requirements.

Once the required file(s) for a document are uploaded, assignees can click the Submit and Continue button to submit the uploaded document(s). Alternatively, users can click on Continue without Submission to continue working on the upload request without submission.

Assignees can choose to upload all documents at once or just upload one or more files, and return to complete the rest later. The system will automatically save their progress, allowing them to resume from where they left off.

Users can submit the request without uploading the optional documents.

They can click on Submit document and confirm the submission by clicking on Yes, submit.

The submission will be successful and the user will be notified about the request completion.

If there are multiple assignees added in a single Upload Request, they all will be able to contribute to the same request.

Document Review

If the review option is not selected, submitted documents will be accepted without going through any review process. Once all of the documents are submitted, the requester will be notified via email with a link to the request folder. They can view the uploaded documents by clicking the Open Request Folder link from the email.

If the document review option is selected for the upload request, the document status will be changed to Pending Review.

Once all the documents are submitted, the requester is notified that all the documents are submitted for the request and that the Upload Request is now in Pending Review status.

The requester can access the Upload Request link directly from the email notification or by navigating to Upload Request Workflows > Upload Requests created by me under the Workflows & Signature tab in Egnyte Collaborate.

They can open the upload request by hovering over the specific Upload Request name and clicking on the Open option from the three-dot menu.

The selected Upload Request will open in a separate tab. The requesters can select the document with Pending Review state and preview the uploaded files by hovering over to the specific file and clicking the Preview button. On the document preview page, they can view the predefined instructions provided for both the reviewer and the assignee.

File type is automatically detected and displayed against the specific document uploaded by the user. If the uploaded file(s) meets the requested document type(s), the indicator appears in green with the respective count.

If all uploaded file(s) meet the requirements, the requester can accept the document and its files by using the Accept button in the top right corner.

If an incorrect document has been uploaded, the file type is not detected and None is displayed in the detected file type column. The indicator appears in red with the count as 0.

The reviewer can open the document and view its details, such as upload timeframe, uploader’s email address, expected and detected file type, and extracted attributes.

AI-assisted metadata extraction on the uploaded documents displays the set of extracted attributes.

If any file(s) of the document needs to be re-uploaded, the requester can reject the document by clicking the Reject button in the top right corner. A dialog box will appear where they can enter the Reason for rejection. Upon rejection, the document status will change back to Pending.

The assignee will receive an email notification about the rejected document along with the rejection reason. The assignee can open up the request directly from the email to re-upload the required file(s). The assignee can remove existing file(s) by clicking the delete icon and then reupload the correct file(s).

Once all required file(s) are successfully uploaded and submitted, the document status will be changed to Pending Review.

The requester will be notified again about Upload Request in the pending review status and can review the document to either accept or reject it. This accept or reject process will continue until the document is successfully accepted. Once all the documents are reviewed and accepted, the Upload Request will be marked as completed and assignees will be notified about acceptance of all the documents.

Utilizing Document Room Specific Reports

Document Room owners and privileged internal collaborators have access to specific reports to track file usage and governance within their document rooms.

Accessing and Running the Reports

Users with permission (assigned via role-based administration) will see a tab called Reports when they enter the document room.

When they access the tab, the users will see a dashboard with 3 usage reports and 3 governance reports.

The reports can be accessed from either the dashboard or from the report navigation bar. The table below describes the reports available in the document room.

See File Audit Report Description of Actions for details.

Report Name

Description

Additional Details

User Visits

Provides visibility into the login and log-out activities for the stakeholders collaborating within the document room.

The report duration can be customized; the default is the past 7 days.

File Views

Provides visibility into read-only activities like preview, download, etc. by any of the stakeholders collaborating within the document room.

The report duration can be customized; the default is the past 7 days.

File Modifications

Provides visibility into any changes to files and folders (such as upload, add metadata, etc.) in the document room.

The report duration can be customized; the default is the past 7 days.

User Permissions

Provides granular visibility into the folder-level permissions assigned to different stakeholders collaborating within the document room.

Point-in-time snapshot of the permissions across different folders within the document room.

Full Audit

Provides visibility into all the activities (full content audit) by different stakeholders collaborating within the document room.

The report duration can be customized; the default is the past 7 days.

User Provisioning

Provides visibility into all the user provisioning activities (user provisioning audit) for the stakeholders collaborating within the document room.

The report duration can be customized; the default is the past 7 days.

Note: The maximum duration available for activity-based reports is 180 days.

Filtering the Reports

Each of the reports can be filtered based on the following criteria.

  • User Type
  • Specific User Group
  • Specific User
  • Specific Company Note that the “Company” column in the report will show the domain name from the email address used to register the user.

For filter-based report, additional options can be selected to filter the report by specific activity type.

Also, for the user provisioning report, an additional option is available to filter the report by specific actions.

Exporting the Reports

Full report can be exported into a .csv format by clicking the export button.

Document Room capabilities are available only through dedicated Document Room Plans - Document Room and Document Room Enterprise.

Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get started with the new document room plan.

Workspace Templates

Workspace templates make it easy to create new Workspaces using a predefined folder structure and permission set. Different Workspace templates can be set up based on the specific business needs.

Creating a Workspace Template

Users can create Workspace templates in the Egnyte Collaborate Web UI. They are stored in /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Workspace Templates. Perform the following steps to create a Workspace template:

  • Create a folder under /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Workspace Templates. The name of your folder will be the template name.
  • Add subfolders and files to the template
  • Optionally define template permissions by using Workspace Template Settings from the context menu.
  • The Workspace Template Settings dialog will open. The Workspace Template Permissions section allows users to configure which users will have access to Workspaces created from this template. In addition to predefined users and groups, users can configure dynamic roles which will be mapped to users when a Workspace is created from this template. Users can download a sample JSON file from the Workspace Template Settings dialog, which provides examples for reference. In the example JSON below, there are four dynamic roles defined:

  1. Account Manager

  2. Account Team

  3. Account Verification Team

  4. Client.

The Account Manager and Account Team are granted access to the entire workspace, but with different permission levels. The Account Verification Team is given Editor access and the user Bill Smith (username - bsmith) is given Full access to the Onboarding folder. The user group Legal Team is given Owner access to the Contracts folder and permission inheritance is turned off for Contracts folder.

The Client is granted Viewer access to the Client Access subfolder.

Note: The dynamic roles are only available during workspace creation and will not be accessible afterwards.

A sample permissions JSON is listed below:

{

    "folders": [

        {

            "path": "/",

            "permissions": {

                "userPerms": {

                    "{{Account Manager}}": "Owner",

                    "{{Account Team}}": "Full"

                }

            }

        },

        {

            "path": "/Onboarding",

            "permissions": {

                "groupPerms": {

                    "Account Verification Team": "Editor"

                },

                "userPerms": {

                    "bsmith": "Full"

                }

            }

        },

        {

            "path": "/Contracts",

            "permissions": {

                "groupPerms": {

                    "Legal Team": "Full"

                },

                "inheritsPermissions": false

            }

        },

        {

            "path": "/Client Access",

            "permissions": {

                "userPerms": {

                    "{{Client}}": "Viewer"

                }

            }

        }

    ]

}

The following table describes the fields of the Permissions JSON object.

Field

Description

Required

Possible Values

folders

Top-level key that contains the definition of folders and their permissions

Yes

Array of folder definition objects

folder.path

The folder for which you want to set permissions

Yes

Path, relative to the root of the project, e.g.:

/

/Onboarding

/Client Access

folder.permissions

Object with details about the permissions

Yes

See fields below. The structure is the same as is used in the Set Folder Permissions Public API

folder.permissions.groupPerms

Object with details on groups and their permissions.

No

An object where the keys represent group names and the values the permissions those groups should have. Groups can be existing groups, e.g., “Finance” or can be created upon creating a workspace.

Valid folder permissions include: None, Viewer, Editor, Full, Owner

folder.permissions.userPerms

Object with details on users and their permissions.

No

An object where the keys represent configurable dynamic roles or usernames and the values represent permissions those users should have.

To give permissions to a specific user, list their username, e.g., bsmith.

To define a dynamic role, enter a role name enclosed in double curly braces, e.g., {{Account Manager}}

Valid folder permissions include: None, Viewer, Editor, Full, Owner

folder.permissions.inheritsPermissions

Whether or not the folder should inherit permissions from its parent folder.

No

true or false

Defaults to true

Managing Workspace Templates Access

Users can control who can create new workspaces from a specific template, set permissions on the template folder using the Share > Manage Folder Permissions dialog. Any user with Viewer permissions on the template will be able to create a new Workspace from the template.

By giving Editor permissions to the template folder, users will be able to create a Workspace from a template as well as modify the Workspace template.

Creating A Workspace from a Workspace Template

You can create a workspace from available template(s). Refer to Create a Workspace From a Template for more information.
