Egnyte for Google Workspace Integration - Troubleshooting Guide for Known Issues

The article provides troubleshooting for some of the known issues associated with the latest Egnyte for Google Workspace Integration.

Refer to the Configuration or Migration guide for the integration and the recommended practices.

Checklist to Follow

The following is a checklist to follow before troubleshooting any of the issues associated with the integration:

  • Ensure that the Google Workspace plan is Business Standard or above (Shared Drives required)
  • A dedicated Google Workspace account has been created for integration (for example; egnyte-integration@domain.com)
    • Account is not an existing Egnyte user
    • Account is a licensed Google Workspace member (not a no-license service account)
    • Account is active (not suspended or deactivated)
  • Prevent users from creating Shared Drives policy is disabled in Google Admin Console
  • Allow users to create files in Drive setting is enabled in Google Admin Console
  • Latest Egnyte for Google Workspace integration is authorized in Egnyte App Control Center (all wizard steps are completed, including Allow Access)
  • Test the integration by creating a new Google Doc and confirming co-edit access. The file will display a blue Egnyte tag next to the file name.

Known Issues and Resolution

Google Workspace Plan Limitation (Business Starter)

Users receive upgrade notifications for the latest Google integration but are on the Google Workspace Business Starter plan. Upgrade attempts fail or result in errors related to Shared Drive creation. Users may also inquire about continuing with the older integration or using an alternative setup.

Root Cause

  • The latest Google integration depends on Google Shared Drives

  • Google Workspace Business Starter does not support Shared Drives Resolution Options

  • Upgrade the Google Workspace plan to Business Standard or higher to enable Shared Drives and support the integration.

  • Alternatively, use a separate Google Workspace tenant with a supported plan for the integration, ensuring that Egnyte user email addresses match those in the Google tenant.

Error Creating Permissions

In case there are permissions issues for shared drives, a message is shown stating Your account lacks sufficient permissions to create or manage shared drives.

Root Causes

  • Integration account does not have permission to create or manage Shared Drives in the Google Workspace tenant

  • A Google Workspace admin policy is enabled that prevents users from creating Shared Drives Resolution Steps

  • Ensure the integration account has access to create and manage Shared Drives in the Google Workspace Admin Console

  • Check the Shared Drive creation policy under Apps -> Google Workspace -> Drive and Docs -> Sharing settings. Confirm that the setting preventing users from creating Shared Drives is turned off

  • Use a licensed Google Workspace user account for the integration instead of a service account without a license

  • Verify that the target user is allowed within the Google tenant and not restricted by admin policies.

  • Re-authenticate the integration in Egnyte after correcting permissions A Super Admin role is not required. A standard Google Workspace user with Shared Drive creation access is sufficient.

Drive ID Required Error

Users encountering an error Drive ID is required when attempting to open or create Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides in Egnyte’s Web UI. Previously created Google files continue to open correctly, but newly created files are impacted. Re-disabling and re-enabling the integration may lead to another error indicating the account is already registered. The user observes this issue consistently across browsers.

Root Causes

  • The integration account was not fully or correctly authorized during setup, often due to an incomplete or failed earlier configuration attempt

  • The target user for whom permissions are being created is restricted or blocked in the Google tenant Resolution Steps

  • Use a new, dedicated Google Workspace account if the existing account was part of an incomplete setup and re-authenticate the integration

  • If the account shows as already registered, please reach out to Egnyte Support to clear the registration before retrying

  • Ensure all steps of the latest Google integration setup are completed, including the final access authorization step

504 Gateway Timeout when Opening Files

After upgrading to the latest Google integration, newly created Egnyte files fail to open in Google’s editor. The browser displays a 504 Gateway Timeout error. This issue occurs specifically when the setting to allow users to create files in Google Drive is disabled in the Google Admin Console.

Root Cause

  • The latest Google integration requires the ability to create and access files in Google Shared Drives.

  • When the setting to allow users to create files in Drive is disabled, the integration cannot complete backend file creation and access operations, resulting in a timeout. Resolution Steps

  • Enable the setting in Google Admin Console under Apps -> Google Workspace -> Drive and Docs to allow users to create files in Drive

  • If compliance requirements block this change, contact Egnyte Products team for assistance.

Access Denied on @mention Email Notification Links

Users receive email notifications when they are mentioned in comments within Google Workspace documents. Clicking the link in the email results in an Access Denied error, even though the user has appropriate permissions in Egnyte.

Root Cause

  • The user’s Google session for the file is either expired or not initialized through Egnyte Access tokens required by Google are only established when the file is opened via Egnyte.

Resolution Steps

  • Open the file first through the Egnyte web interface to establish the Google session
  • Once the session is initialized, access through email links should work correctly
  • Alternatively, continue accessing files directly from Egnyte to avoid the issue

Google Native File Format Limitations

When a user imports Google files, such as Google Docs, Google Sheets, or Google Slides, into Egnyte, the files get converted to standard OOXML or Office formats during import. This is because Google uses its own file formats such as .gdoc, .gsheet, and .gslide that cannot be used directly on external platforms.

During the conversion, most of the standard content and formatting will be preserved, but certain Google-specific features may be changed, removed, or may work differently after the file is imported into Egnyte. For example, in Google Sheets, features such as custom dropdowns, certain interactive elements, or advanced formatting may not be preserved.

We recommend reviewing important files after the import to ensure that the content and formatting meets expectations.

Google Previewer for Google Workspace Files

Overview

The Google Previewer enables a native, in-browser preview of Google Workspace files (.gdoc, .gsheet, .gslides) directly within the Egnyte interface. Instead of converting these files to PDF for display, Egnyte renders them using Google’s viewer, preserving formatting, layouts, and other Google-specific elements as they appear in Google Workspace.

Using Google Previewer

There is nothing to configure as a user or administrator. Simply click to preview a Google Workspace file in Egnyte, and the Google native previewer will load automatically inside the Egnyte preview panel.

  • The preview is read-only. To edit the file, use the standard Edit in Google option.

  • Users and administrators must use the same email address for their Google account and Egnyte account to use the Previewer properly.

Eligible Users

The user must be logged into their Google account to use the Google Previewer. The previewer requires the user’s identity to verify permissions on the underlying Google file.

User Type

Preview Available

Authenticated (logged-in) Egnyte user

Yes

External share link

No, falls back to native previewer

Supported File Types

The Google Previewer works with the following file types stored in Egnyte:

  • Google Docs (.gdoc)
  • Google Sheets (.gsheet)
  • Google Slides (.gslides)

Troubleshooting

Preview is Stuck Loading or Shows a Login Prompt

Ensure that the user is logged into their Google account in the same browser session and third-party cookies or cross-site tracking are not blocked.

Fallback to PDF or Standard Previewer Occurs

Verify that the file is viewed by an authenticated Egnyte user and not through an external public share link.

Preview Displays a “You need access” Message

Verify that the user are logged in to Google with the same email address that is used in the Egnyte account.

Import Files from Google Drive

Egnyte enables its users to bring their Google Drive files into Egnyte’s platform through the upload option in the Web UI. This feature provides an easy way to the users to consolidate their files, ensuring everything is in one place for seamless collaboration across teams.

Prerequisites

  • The latest Google Workspace Integration should be enabled on the domain.
  • Supported plans:
    • Google Workspace Editions: Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise, Enterprise for Education, and Nonprofits Legacy
    • G Suite Editions: Business, Education, and Enterprise

Enablement Process for Admins

Admins must enable the integration for the users from the Apps & Integrations page.

  • Navigate to the Apps & Integrations page and search for Google Drive Import integration.
  • Click on Enable Integration button within the Google Drive Import app tile.
  • If the integration is already enabled, the admin can change the settings. To do this, click on the Settings icon of the Google Drive Import integration.
  • Choose the desired option from the Status dropdown and click Save:
    • Not enabled for domain: Google Drive Import integration will not be enabled for the domain users
    • Added for Groups: Makes it available to a specific group of users
    • Allowed for users: Makes it available to all users, but the users need to add the integration if they want to use it
    • Added for all users: Makes it available to all users
  • The integration will be enabled as per the selected option.

Initial Configuration for Users

Non-admin users will be required to configure Google Drive Import and grant access to import files from their Google Drive account. This is a one-time process that must be completed before the first attempt to import files from Google Drive.

  • Navigate to the Apps & Integrations page and search for Google Drive Import integration.
  • Click on the Settings icon.
  • Click on Continue to configure Google Drive Import.
  • Alternatively, when the user clicks on the Upload icon -> Import from Google Drive option in the Web UI for the first time, they can allow access to continue uploading the files from their Google Drive.
  • Click on Allow Access.
  • Login to the Google account and click on Allow to authorize access to the files. A message will appear after successful authentication. Close the pop-up.

Import Files from Google Drive

  • Click on the Upload icon in the Web UI.
  • Click on Import from Google Drive. The user will be required to configure and grant access during the first-time use of this option, if not already done.
  • Select the file(s) from the Google Drive to upload. The selected files will be uploaded and the progress will be visible on the Web UI. The files will appear in the selected folder after completion.

Limitations

  • Users can import up to 10 files at a time, with a combined size not exceeding 1 GB. For Google files, an additional limit applies where each file must not exceed 10 MB.
  • When Google files such as Google Docs, Google Sheets, or Google Slides are imported into Egnyte, they are converted to standard OOXML or Office formats. This is because Google’s native file formats (.gdoc, .gsheet, .gslide) are not supported on external platforms.
  • Most standard content and formatting is preserved during conversion, but certain Google-specific features may be changed, removed, or behave differently in Egnyte. For example, custom dropdowns, interactive elements, or advanced formatting in Google Sheets may not carry over.
  • We recommend reviewing important files after import to confirm the content and formatting meet your expectations.

Admin Guidelines and Action Items

Prerequisite

  • The upgrade should be scheduled at non-business hours. This is to avoid data inconsistency issues

  • The admin should create and use a separate Google Workspace account, solely created to authenticate this integration rather than relying on personal accounts. It is equally crucial to ensure these credentials are kept secure to prevent any unauthorized access It is required to create a new Workspace User Account with a generic name and use that email to authorize the Google integration of the domain. Additionally, please make sure that this email address is not affiliated with a corresponding Egnyte user.

  • To allow organizational users to create shared drives, administrators must uncheck the Prevent users in selected organizational units from creating new shared drives option. Administrators can also choose to restrict shared drive creation for specific organizational units or groups by checking this option

  • Supported plans:

Steps for Editing Existing Configuration

  • Log in to the Egnyte domain and navigate to Apps & Integrations.

  • Click Google Workspace -> Settings.

  • Click Edit Configuration.

  • Provide consent and click Authorize.

  • Click here for more details regarding Google shared drives.

  • Click Allow Access.

  • Sign in with the email address associated with a service account. Click Next in the Google Authorization pop-up.

  • Enter the password and click Next.

  • Click Continue.

  • Click Allow.

  • An Authorization Successful message will be displayed on setup completion.

  • The above configuration is a one-time setup and does not need to be repeated.

  • Once the authorization is complete, a service account named googlev4integration@domainname is automatically created. This account is visible only to administrators. It is strongly recommended not to delete or deactivate this account, as it is required to perform backend data synchronization.

  • The google workspace account used to authorize the integration must remain active. If this account is deactivated or needs to be changed, contact Egnyte Support as this cannot be done as self-service action.

Next Generation Egnyte for Google Workspace Integration - Overview

Egnyte for Google Workspace enables customers to collaborate on files stored in Egnyte using Workspace applications. The integration offers a wide range of capabilities and features, such as creating and editing Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and saving them directly on Egnyte. Google Workspace supports real-time collaboration, enabling multiple users to work together simultaneously. It also allows editing and co-authoring of Microsoft Office files.

Egnyte is now proactively adapting to Google’s strategic shifts, prioritizing uninterrupted functionality and an enriched user experience for our customers. In response to Google’s plans to sunset the Decoupled Docs API in 2026, we’re upgrading our existing Workspace integration.

Skip Ahead To…

Reasons for Upgrading

Who is Impacted?

User-Centric Benefits and Key Impacts

Reasons for Upgrading

  • Egnyte is required to adopt the new APIs for integrating with Google Workspace, aligning with the latest changes in Google’s infrastructure
  • Upgrading the current Workspace integration ensures a seamless and consistent user experience
  • The new version comes with an additional set of capabilities above what we currently offer. Some of these include:
    • Suite of capabilities under smart canvas, making task assignments, progress tracking, and collaboration more intuitive
    • The integration of Gemini, including the side panel in Workspace and other AI tools which operates behind the scenes in refining existing work or starting new projects, with specific features tailored for various Google Workspace applications.
Back to Top…

Who is Impacted?

All Egnyte customers utilizing the Workspace integration are impacted by this transition.

Egnyte customers using the latest integration will notice a blue Egnyte label next to the file name as shown below. The absence of this blue label indicates the previous integration is being used. To upgrade, refer to the Configuration and Migration Guide.

Back to Top…

User-Centric Benefits and Key Impacts

Create a New File with Workspace in Egnyte

In the legacy version, users can create new files in Workspace through the Create menu, with files stored directly in Egnyte. The functionality remains intact in the upgraded version, but with an enhancement - these files are now stored in Egnyte, accompanied by a copy in Google Drive for Google files. All users apart from authorized users, will see all the files in Shared with me with an Egnyte label.

Collaborate in Real-Time on Files in Google Workspace

The collaborative experience for Google files remains supported in both versions. However, in the upgraded version, Google files are opened directly in Google’s editor. Users can also leverage Google’s Smart Canvas feature now.

Collaborate in Real-Time on Microsoft Files

The collaboration and co-editing support for Microsoft files remain consistent across both versions.

File Management: Rename, Move, Copy, Delete

File management capabilities such as renaming, moving, copying, and deleting are supported in both versions.

In the upgraded version,

  • The renaming process works bidirectionally between Google Drive and Egnyte.
  • Copying a file creates a duplicate in Google Drive to retain advanced Google smart canvas features.
  • Deleting a file sends it to the Trash in Egnyte and revokes user permission in Drive. Deleting it from the Trash removes the file from Google Drive as well, ensuring data integrity.
File Preview

Previewing the file is available in the upgraded version as currently offered.

File Sharing

Sharing file capabilities as offered currently undergo positive changes in the upgraded version. Users can share files directly from the Workspace editor using the Egnyte add-on, making the process faster and more convenient.

‘New File’ Or ‘Make a Copy’ Via Google Editor

The options to create a New File or Make a Copy via the Google Editor are consistent between the two versions.

Additional Features

The upgraded version includes smart canvas for intuitive task management and collaboration, along with Workspace advanced AI features for enhanced workflow efficiency.

For any issues or assistance with migration, contact Egnyte Support.

Recommended Practices for Next Generation Egnyte for Google Workspace Integration

Requirement for Authorization Account

Limitations for Users with Lifetime (Personal) Workspace Accounts

File Sync

Shared Drive Creation Permissions

Administrative Control of Shared Drive Settings

Grant Access to Shared Drive

Requirement for Authorization Account

The admin should create and use a separate Workspace account, solely created to authenticate the latest Egnyte for Google Workspace integration.

This approach helps safeguard access to stored content in case the owner of a personal account leaves the company or if credentials are lost, reducing the risk of permanent data loss.

Limitations for Users with Lifetime (Personal) Workspace Accounts

Users with personal, independent, or free Workspace accounts cannot use the latest version of Google integration. This is expected due to limitations associated with individual accounts. Personal accounts do not have access to the shared drive creation feature, which is exclusive to certain Google Workspace editions.

Shared drive creation feature is supported only in following Google Workspace editions:

  • Workspace Editions: Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise, Enterprise for Education, and Nonprofits
  • Legacy G Suite Editions: Business, Education, and Enterprise

File Sync

  • The existing files from Egnyte are synced to the Shared Drive when opened.
  • After switching to the new version, all existing user sessions will expire due to token expiration. Since Google Workspace may take up to 5 minutes to invoke the API calls, users could lose any unsaved changes made during this period. ​​​​To minimize disruption, it is recommended to perform the migration during a time of low or no user activity. Users will receive a warning message prompting them to reload the page, which will then open in the upgraded version.

Shared Drive Creation Permissions

Not all users within the eligible editions can create shared drives. This ability depends on permissions managed by the Workspace administrator within the organization. By default, organizational users have shared drive creation rights, though administrators can restrict this to certain organizational units or groups as needed.

For individual users with personal Workspace accounts (e.g., @gmail.com) or those on Google Workspace Basic, Business Starter, or Free editions, shared drives cannot be created, but these users can be invited to collaborate on files created by supported users.

Administrative Control of Shared Drive Settings

The management of shared drive settings and permissions is exclusively available to Google Workspace administrators. Administrators have the authority to set policies governing shared drive access and creation within the organization. For further details, refer to the Workspace support article here.

For files migrated from the legacy Google Integration to the upgraded version, the version history is not available in the Shared Drive. The files are re-created in Google Drive after reauthorization, and the file creator will appear as the Google account used to authorize the integration. Users can continue to view the file version history in Egnyte.

Grant Access to Shared Drive

Egnyte’s Google integration successfully creates the required Google Shared Drive; however, Google does not automatically grant access to other users in the same organization.

Access to a Shared Drive must be explicitly granted, and Google allows this only for individual users or Google Groups. Other email domains cannot be added directly as members. If a domain is neither a user nor a group, Google shows an error stating that it’s not a valid user or group.

This may lead to error in Google co-edit as well as display an Error creating permissions message. This is because the users opening the files are not yet members of the Google Shared Drive.

Follow the steps listed below to resolve the error:

  • Sign into Google Admin Console (admin.google.com) with the admin account
  • Go to Directory → Groups
  • Create a new group (e.g., all-users@domainname or egnyte-access@domainname)
  • Add all users who need access to the Egnyte Google integration to this group. Alternatively, admins can configure the group to automatically include all users in the domain (under Group settings → Access type → All users in the domain can join)
  • Go back to Google Drive and sign in as powerview_egnyte@domainname
  • Navigate to Shared drives → select the Egnyte shared drive
  • Click Manage members
  • Add the Google Group (e.g., all-users@domainname) as a member with Contributor access
  • Click Done

Using Egnyte with Google Chat

Egnyte for Google Chat is a bot that allows users to share and collaborate on Egnyte documents instantly, without leaving the chat window. This article will cover how to install and use the bot on your Chat conversations.

Google Chat

Google Chat is Google Workspaces’s powerful text and video messaging app, helping users communicate with each other through 1:1 and group conversations.

With a few commands, users can easily access and share their Egnyte documents within the flow of conversation. Just add the bot to any room, and use the command “@Egnyte share” to start.

Please note the following restrictions:

  • Bots can only be added to rooms, not individual conversations
  • Google Chat does not offer the ability to add bots for every room - bots must be added to each room individually

Adding the Egnyte Bot to Chat

  • First, open up your Chat app. Choose “Add People & Bots” from the top left menu to add the bot to your Chat account
  • After clicking, a menu will appear. Search for “Egnyte” and it will appear in your results. Click “Egnyte” to add it.
  • Now the Bot is added to your list

Adding the Egnyte Bot to Rooms

  • To add the Bot to your room, first, navigate to a room. Just above the text box at the bottom of the screen, click “Add People & Bots”
  • A window will appear. Search for “Egnyte” and select the bot from the results. Click “Send” to add the bot to the room.
  • You’ve now added the Egnyte bot to your room!

Sharing File Links with the Egnyte Bot

  • To share a document using the Egnyte bot, go to a conversation and type “@Egnyte share” and click “Select Items to Share”
  • To authorize your Egnyte account, click “Authorize” (this is a one-time step).
  • Sign in to your Egnyte account and click “Next”
  • Select “Allow Access” on the authorization screen
  • Now you can navigate your Egnyte account and select the file you want to share
  • Select the link visibility permissions for your file. You can select “Anyone”, File Server Users, or “Domain Users with Permission”
  • Press “Send” , and your file will appear in the chat conversation

Help Command

To easily navigate to this page, type in “@Egnyte help” to get a link to this helpdesk article directly from the bot.

    • Click Next.
  • As an optional step, Egnyte can be added as a Trusted Place. Click ‘Learn more’ link in the pop-up for additional details. Click Next.
  • Ensure the requirements for individual device setup are met. Reference to the Mass Deployment – Egnyte Co-Edit Configuration guide can be accessed from the pop-up. Click on the Finish and Enable Integration button. Back to Top ↑

Update App Configuration

  • Navigate to Apps & Integrations -> Microsoft 365 co-editing for Desktop and Mobile tile under the Featured section. The user can also search for this integration using the filters search bar. Click on Settings.
  • Make changes to the app enablement settings, if needed and click on Save.
    • Not enabled for domain: Microsoft 365 co-editing for Desktop and Mobile will not be enabled for the domain users
    • Added for Groups: Makes it available to a specific group of users (who have Microsoft Licenses)

  • Click Save to complete the configuration.
  • Admins also can set the default option for one-click coediting under the App Control Center tab on the Apps & Integrations page: This is a prioritized list of available co-editing applications whose order can be changed via drag-and-drop. The ranking order sets the one-click default coediting application for users on the Web UI and Egnyte Desktop Apps. Back to Top ↑
Changing Co-Editing Defaults for Existing Desktop App Users

When Allow users to overwrite these defaults is enabled, the Egnyte Desktop App treats the co-editing preference stored on the device as user-owned. Because of this, changing the co-editing default in the Admin Console (App defaults or App Control Center) is not pushed down to devices that already have a cached preference.

Expected Behavior

  • Double-clicking an Office file in File Explorer or Finder opens it normally (or shows the previously configured behavior), ignoring the new admin default.
  • Right-click → Co-edit continues to work correctly — only the default double-click action is affected.
  • Restarting the Desktop App does not apply the new setting, because the cached value is intentionally preserved. The Desktop App cannot distinguish a preference the user deliberately chose from one that was simply cached during an earlier configuration sync, so it keeps the local value in both cases. This is expected behavior of the current design, not a sync failure.

How to Apply the New Default

Choose either option:

  • Per user (recommended for individual devices): In the Egnyte Desktop App, open Preferences → Collaboration and set the Co-editing preference for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. This writes a fresh local value that takes effect immediately.
  • Domain-wide (admin): In Apps & Integrations → Microsoft 365 co-editing for Desktop and Mobile → Settings → App defaults, clear the Allow users to overwrite these defaults checkbox and click Save, then re-select it and Save again. Changing this flag forces Desktop Apps to resync the underlying co-editing policy from the cloud on their next configuration refresh. If Allow users to overwrite these defaults is left disabled, admin co-editing defaults always apply and no extra step is needed.

Notifications for Co-Edit Session Availability

Desktop App will display specific alerts when co-editing sessions cannot be started.

  • No Microsoft 365 apps installed
  • Storage not added or not authenticated
  • No permissions to edit
  • Extension not supported (old Office files)
  • File locked (self-lock and locked by other users)
  • No internet connection
  • File removed
  • File too large to co-edit
  • File in upload
  • Unknown error - ‘retry later’ Back to Top ↑

Limitations

File Size Limits for Microsoft 365 for the web Co-Editing:

  • Excel 100 MB

  • Word 100 MB

  • PowerPoint 2 GB File Size Limits for Microsoft 365 Desktop Co-Editing:

  • Excel 300 MB

  • Word 300 MB

  • PowerPoint 2 GB

Other Limitations
  • File Types supported are docx, pptx, xlsx, and xlsm.
  • Co-Authoring performance is targeted at group less than 15 users.
  • Starting a co-editing session from the Egnyte Desktop Apps is limited to Power Users & Admins in Egnyte.
  • Starting a co-editing session from the Egnyte Desktop App is not supported on Egnyte Gov environments.
  • @mentions feature is not available with this integration on the Microsoft document.
  • Local file paths for files opened in co-editing are converted to HTTP links, which may affect links, references, or macros (file operations and path manipulation do not work).
  • Linking is only supported from Excel to Excel; cross-application linking (for example, PowerPoint to Word, Word to Word, etc.) is not supported.
  • Excel linked sheets will only be available to be linked to files from the same Egnyte domain.
  • Excel linked cells will only be opened correctly for cells that are created in co-edit mode.
  • For PowerPoint files, there is a limit of 5000 elements on a single PowerPoint file, which will cause the file to not open via co-edit. An element is any object (Text field, graphic, etc.).
  • Zero-byte files are not supported for co-edit.
  • Files can’t be saved back to Egnyte as PDF files.
  • Microsoft Purview Labels are not enabled for files opened in co-editing mode.
  • Password encryption is not available on the document for co-editing.
  • Co-editing defaults changed in the Admin Console are not re-applied to Desktop Apps that already have a locally cached preference while Allow users to overwrite these defaults is enabled. See Changing Co-Editing Defaults for Existing Desktop App Users for how to apply the new default. Back to Top ↑

Edit and Create Egnyte Files Using Microsoft 365 for the Web

The powerful integration of Egnyte and Microsoft 365 for the web enables a seamless user collaboration experience. This article covers how to use the Microsoft 365 for the web integration, but users can also use Egnyte for Microsoft 365 from their mobile device (iOS, Android, and Windows).

In addition, Egnyte’s support for Microsoft 365 for the web’s co-authoring capability enables multiple users to edit the same document simultaneously while viewing changes made by others in real-time.

Microsoft 365 Licensing Requirements

Users must have a valid Microsoft 365 Account to edit files.

Additional Information

Create a New Microsoft 365 File

User can create a new Microsoft 365 File (Word, Excel, or PowerPoint) directly from Egnyte Web UI in just a few easy steps.

  • Navigate to Egnyte WebUI
  • Click on the + Create drop-down
  • Select the type of file to create – for example Word Online Document
  • Alternatively, if the user intends to create the document from the template
    • Navigate to the sub-menu by hovering on > and Select From Template from the dropdown
    • Select the specific template from the subsequent dropdown. Creating Documents from the Home Dashboard:

The option to create documents will not be available if MS 365 integration is not enabled for the domain/user.

When creating a new Microsoft 365 file from the WebUI, users will see a pop-up. The pop-up offers options to rename the document, modify the file’s Location, and enable Draft mode.

After clicking Save, the user will be taken to a new tab to start working on the new file. All changes are automatically saved within Egnyte.

The default location for the documents created from the home dashboard will be Private/User’s Private Folder Name/Quick Created Files/YYYY, where YYYY is the year in which the document is created.

For example, if the document is created on 15th December 2022 and the user’s private folder name is myprivatefolder, then the default location will be Private/myprivatefolder/Quick Created Files/2022.

This will help the user structure the documents created from the home dashboard for easy management.

This folder will get created in the user’s private folder when the user clicks on the Create menu from the home dashboard.

Creating Documents from a Template

While creating the document from the template, users will be prompted to enter the name for the new document to be created and then the document created will be opened in the new tab for editing and collaboration. All changes are automatically saved within Egnyte.

If the document is in a format which is not supported for co-editing, the document created from the template will not open for editing. In such a case, if the user is creating the document from the home dashboard, the user will get an option to either preview the file or navigate to the folder where the document is created as shown below.

Open and Edit an Microsoft 365 File

To open a file in Microsoft 365 for the web for this example, right-click on the file (or click the checkbox next to a file), click on Edit -> Word for the Web.

Users will need to log in using their Microsoft 365 account periodically to verify their subscription is active. Once they have done that, they should see their file is ready for editing.

To edit the file, simply make the desired changes to the file. Any changes are automatically saved to Egnyte as they are made.

Additional Information

Supported File Types

The user may notice some Microsoft 365 files have an Edit option while others may only have a View option. This is because Microsoft 365 for the web only supports their newer file formats (e.g., docx, pptx, xlsx) for editing in Microsoft 365 for the web. Others are supported in a view-only mode. A list of supported extensions is available here.

Other Notes
  • Microsoft 365 for the web has a more limited feature set than the installed version. Many special features like forms, advanced document elements, and such can result in an error message prompting the users to use read-only mode.
  • Microsoft imposes API size limits for Microsoft 365 for the web files. API limitations are imposed equally on all of Microsoft’s partners. Egnyte’s own API is not limited by these constraints; it will automatically allow larger files to work with Microsoft applications when Microsoft removes or reduces their limitations. Refer to this helpdesk article for the specific limits for the Microsoft 365 for the web application.

Limitations

Overview

Egnyte agent for MS Copilot can be used in MS Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot Web interface, Outlook and productivity apps (Office). Users can seamlessly generate concise summaries and accurate answers from Egnyte-stored files directly within the MS Teams environment by simply writing a prompt in the Copilot tab. The prompt also displays the source files where the summaries were generated from for quick file actions such as preview and share, simplifying information retrieval and enhancing productivity.

The data stays within Egnyte’s security controls and won’t be retained outside of it during AI interactions. Additionally, the integration adheres to Egnyte’s permission model, such that a user’s AI will never have access to more data than that user is entitled to.

The Egnyte agent runs on the Egnyte MCP server. It is published as part of the certified EgnyteM365 app. This enables the admins to install and approve one app rather than a custom built or side loaded agent.

There are three separate ways to work with Egnyte content in Microsoft 365 Copilot, all built on Egnyte MCP:

  • Egnyte agent
  • Egnyte added as a source in Copilot Chat and the Researcher agent (through the Egnyte federated connector)
  • Egnyte Cowork plugin. Adding Egnyte as a source is independent of the agent; users do not need to go through the agent to do it.

Benefits

  • Ask questions against shared content stored in Egnyte directly within the Copilot tab.
  • Get Egnyte-stored file summaries in the Copilot tab with links to relevant documents and quick access to the source files via the Open in Egnyte action.
  • Maintain organizational security with Egnyte permission-based controls to the documents.
  • Displayed content and documents remain secure and protected within Egnyte.

Use Cases

  • Identifying key information and takeaways from complex documents like contracts, reports, or meeting notes.
  • Surfacing insights by querying across related files, ideal for finding repeated themes, inconsistencies, or dependencies.

Security and Compliance

  • Copilot interactions only return content the user is authorized to access, based on Egnyte’s granular subfolder permissions
  • All Copilot usage adheres to existing Egnyte policies, including lifecycle management, retention schedules, classification labels, and legal holds.

Prerequisites

  • Enabled Egnyte for M365 in the Microsoft Admin center
  • Users need to be logged in to the Egnyte domain in MS Teams
  • Users need to select the Egnyte agent on the right side panel with listed agents
  • Active licenses for MS Teams and MS Copilot
    • To check Microsoft plan, Admin can navigate to the Microsoft Admin center and can look at all the licences per user on the main screen.
    • Microsoft plans with available products are listed here.
  • Admins who have enabled Search Egnyte App in their tenant are recommended to disable it (optional). Refer to the section How to Disable Search Egnyte for more information.
  • An eligible Microsoft 365 plan with Copilot Chat (basic) for the Egnyte Agent in Copilot Chat. There is no additional Microsoft cost applicable for the agent itself.
  • A paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license (Premium seat) and enrollment in the Microsoft Frontier program for Egnyte in Cowork. Cowork tasks are metered in Copilot Credits.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence per user for Egnyte as a data source in Copilot Chat and Researcher.
  • The users must have Essential, Elite or Ultimate, or Platform Enterprise and Enterprise Lite plan with the AI add-on. Essential, Elite and Ultimate plans include the full MCP toolset; Platform plans support a reduced toolset (browse, advanced search, read and retrieve)
  • An active Egnyte MCP server for the domain, with Microsoft Copilot allowed as an MCP client (Egnyte Settings > AI Powered Features > MCP Server)

Using the Egnyte Agent with MCP

As the agent runs on the Egnyte MCP server, it can do a lot more than answer questions and write summaries.

The MCP server exposes a set of tools that the agent utilises on the user’s behalf, always within the Egnyte permissions, with classification and audit logging enforced.

What can be done
  • Browse and navigate Egnyte folder structure
  • Run advanced search across content, including by metadata
  • Open and retrieve specific files and read their content
  • Ask questions and get answers and summaries grounded in Egnyte documents
  • Ask questions to Egnyte Agents, including Agents converted from Knowledge Bases
  • Create and share secure links to files, and work with project folders The exact set of tools depends on the Egnyte plan (as listed below).
Egnyte plan and MCP scope (Platform and New Generation Plans)

The Egnyte MCP server is available on New Generation plans (Essential, Elite, Ultimate), and on Platform plans (Platform Team, Platform Business, Platform Enterprise Lite, Platform Enterprise, AFS, CFS) with the AI add-on. The MCP tools available depend on the plan generation.

New Generation Plans (Essential, Elite, Ultimate) - Full Toolset

  • Browse the file system, run advanced search, and read and retrieve file content

  • AI-powered Q&A and summarisation on documents

  • Agent Questions

  • Link sharing and project folder tools Platform plans with the AI add-on - Core Toolset

  • Browse the file system

  • Run advanced search across the content

  • Read and retrieve file content. AI-powered Q&A and summarisation on documents, agent questions, link sharing and project folder tools are not available on Platform plans.

Egnyte admin must allow Microsoft Copilot as an MCP client in Egnyte (Settings > AI Powered Features > MCP Server). Without this, Copilot cannot connect to the Egnyte MCP server.

Admin Setup

Getting Started

Activation needs to be done in both the Microsoft Teams Admin Center and the Microsoft Admin Center. This ensures the Egnyte Copilot agent is enabled for all domain users or for specific groups across Teams, Outlook, M365, and Office apps, maintaining a consistent experience across the Microsoft environment.

Configure Egnyte agent for M365 in Microsoft Teams Admin Center
  • To install Egnyte for M365, navigate to Microsoft Teams Admin Center. Unfold the Teams apps on the sidebar and click on Manage apps.
  • Search for Egnyte app and check if the status is Unblocked.
  • Click on the app name to confirm the app is available to everyone or selected groups. Click on Edit availability to make changes in the availability.
  • Click on Grant admin consent in the Permissions tab.
  • Provide consent in the pop-up. Click Allow access.
  • The changes will then be visible.

Configure Egnyte Agent for M365 in Microsoft Admin Center
  • To configure Egnyte agent for M365, navigate to Microsoft Admin Center. Unfold Copilot on the sidebar and click on Agents.
  • Search for Egnyte agent and check if the status is available for all users.
  • Select Users and adjust agent availability, if needed. Click on Deploy.
  • Click on Next.
  • Assign users and click on Next. The admin can choose to select:
    • Just me: The agent will be deployed only for the admin
    • Entire organization: The agent will be deployed to all the users in the organization
    • Specific user/groups: Search and select specific users/groups and the agent will be deployed only to the selected user(s)/group(s).
  • Click on Accept Permissions to accept permission requests.
  • Click on Accept after reviewing permissions.
  • Click Next to continue.
  • Review the details and click on Finish Deployment.
  • Click on Done to finish the deployment.
  • The Deployed to in the Users tab will show the user(s) for which the deployment has been completed.

For End User

  • Navigate to MS Copilot in MS Teams, Outlook, M365 or Office app.

  • Select Egnyte on the right side panel.

  • The user can begin interacting with the Egnyte agent.

  • With the first attempt to use the Egnyte agent, the user will be asked to authenticate and provide consent for the access to Egnyte content.

  • Click on Sign in to Egnyte.

  • Provide the credentials and sign in to Microsoft account.

  • Provide the Egnyte domain name.

  • Click Next and confirm consent.

  • The user will get the responses to their queries based on Egnyte-stored files along with the direct file references. It is possible that the user gets logged out due to inactivity and would be required to sign in again after searching for the Egnyte app. In such a scenario,

  • Search for the Egnyte App.

  • If the user is already logged in and they wish to log-in using a different account, they can click on Sign out, search for the app again and follow the steps mentioned ahead.

  • Click on Sign in.

  • Provide the new user credentials and repeat the login steps mentioned above.

Egnyte in Copilot Cowork (plugin)

The Egnyte Cowork plugin lets Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork use Egnyte content for long running, multi-step tasks, while keeping Egnyte permissions and governance. Like the agent, it runs on the Egnyte MCP server.

Prerequisites
  • A paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence (Premium seat) for each user
  • The organisation enrolled in the Microsoft Frontier program
  • Cowork enabled in the Microsoft 365 Copilot environment (Anthropic turned on in the tenant)
  • Copilot Credits capacity, because Cowork tasks are metered on top of the seat
  • An admin role of AI Admin, Security Admin or Office Apps Admin to manage Frontier settings
Admin setup (Microsoft side)
  • Turn on the Frontier program. In the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, go to Copilot > Settings, search for Frontier, and select Copilot Frontier.
  • Turn on ‎Frontier‎ features for the entire organization or selected groups/users. Click on Save.
  • Verify if Egnyte plugin is enabled in Agents > Tools.
  • Check details, and edit availability if needed.
For End User
  • Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and start a Cowork task.
  • Select Customise > add or select Egnyte as a source.
  • Users will be prompted to authenticate to the Egnyte domain on first use. Enter the Egnyte domain.
  • Enter the credentials and give consent for Egnyte in the last step. The Egnyte plugin will then be enabled and users can run the task. Cowork uses Egnyte content within the user’s permissions and shows source references.

Cowork plugins and connectors are in Microsoft public preview through the Frontier program. Availability rolls out gradually and the Microsoft Admin Center steps may change.

Egnyte as a data source in Copilot Chat and Researcher

Egnyte surfaces as a content source in Copilot Chat and the Researcher agent through the Egnyte federated connector. Federated connectors use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to query Egnyte in real time with the user’s identity and permissions.

No Egnyte content is indexed into Microsoft 365, and in Researcher the connector is read only. This is separate from the Egnyte agent: users add Egnyte as a source in Copilot settings, not through the agent.

Licensing

Each user who queries Egnyte needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7). It is not available with a Copilot Studio license or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

Connect Egnyte in Copilot Chat
  • Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Select the ellipsis (…)menu -> Settings.
  • Select Sources in the left panel. Search for Egnyte and click on Connect.
  • Provide the consent for the connection and complete the sign-in to Egnyte.
  • Enter the prompt. Copilot fetches answers from Egnyte in real time and shows source references. Users can turn the source off again in Copilot Chat settings, as needed.
Connect Egnyte in Researcher
  • Open the Researcher agent. If Egnyte as a source is already added in Copilot Chat, Egnyte connector is also enabled for Researcher.
  • In the Sources menu toggle Egnyte on or off, depending on the needs.
  • Run the research prompt. Researcher reads Egnyte content within the associated permissions.
Back to Top…

Best Practices

  • ​​Focus on What, Not Where:
  • Users should frame questions around the information they need rather than the file or folder location.
    • Less effective: What’s in the “Marketing Q4” folder?
    • More effective: Summarize the key marketing strategies for Q4 based on recent reports.
  • Be Specific for More Accurate Responses:
  • Queries that clearly describe the required information return more relevant and precise results.
    • Example: What were the final budget numbers in “Q4_Financials_Final.xlsx”?
  • Use the UI for Core Actions:
  • Actions such as signing in, signing out, or sharing files should be completed using the dedicated Web UI options to ensure expected behavior.

How to Disable the Search Egnyte Integration

Technical Requirements to uninstall Search Egnyte integration:

  • Must be Global Admin in Microsoft tenant
Disable Search Egnyte in MS Teams
  • To disable Search Egnyte integration in MS Teams, navigate to the Microsoft Teams Admin Center. Unfold the Teams apps on the sidebar and go to Manage apps.
  • This action affects all domain users or all users in a selected group using Microsoft Teams and blocked apps can be reversed at any time.
  • Search and select the Search Egnyte (legacy) app. Block the app from the details view by clicking on the Block app option.
  • A confirmation will appear saying that the app is blocked.
Back to Top…
Disable Search Egnyte in MS Copilot
  • To Block Search Egnyte integration in MS Copilot, navigate to the Microsoft Admin Center. Unfold Copilot on the sidebar and go to the Agents section.
  • This action affects all domain users or all users in a selected group using Microsoft Copilot and blocked apps can be reversed at any time.
  • Search and select the Search Egnyte (legacy) app and click on Block.
  • Check Block agent and click on Save.
  • A Confirmation will appear on the agent being blocked.
  • The status Blocked will also be visible on the Agents listing.
Back to Top…

Limitations

  • Limited Source Set: Responses are typically derived from a focused set of documents (around five), ensuring relevance.
  • Independent Query Processing: Each request is processed individually, without retaining conversational context across queries.
  • Copilot-Driven Output: Egnyte supplies the raw data, while Microsoft Copilot determines how this data is interpreted and displayed to the user, as required.

Egnyte for Dynamics 365 Sales CRM in Beta

The Egnyte for Dynamics integration enables users to embed an Egnyte window within a Dynamics object and Map the Dynamics record to an Egnyte folder, establishing a 1:1 relationship between a Dynamics record and an Egnyte Folder. This document covers the steps to install the integration.

Create a Dynamics Service Account

Register an Egnyte App

Configure API Permissions

Configure Certificates and Secrets

3. Setup Dynamics Resources

4. Entity Configuration

5. Final Admin Configuration

6 Permission Settings

Setup for an Admin

Setup for Individual User or Teams

Limitations

Installation Steps

1. Setup Microsoft Entra ID
Create a Dynamics Service Account

Create a Dynamics Service Account via Microsoft Entra ID by performing the following steps.

  • Log in to the Azure dashboard using the Dynamics CRM credentials (no additional Azure subscription required).
  • Navigate to Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory or Azure AD) in the side menu or click here.
Register an Egnyte App
  • Open App registrations and Click on New registration.
  • Complete the provided form, including a display name, and click Register.
  • From the pop-up screen, copy the Application ID and Directory ID (or Tenant ID). We recommend securely storing this information for a later step in this guide.
  • (Optional)Click on Add Application ID URI.
  • Again, click on Add - this will open a popup. Customize the Application ID URI or use the one that is automatically generated. Copy URI value for later and save your changes.
Configure API Permissions
  • Click API Permissions in the side menu.
  • Click Add a Permission.
  • Choose Dynamics CRM.
  • Ensure that user_impersonation is checked, and then click Add permissions.
  • Results should be similar to the following example.
Configure Certificates and Secrets.
  • Choose the Certificates & secrets option from the menu in the sidebar.
  • Click New client secret and set an expiration date.
  • Save the Client Secret for later use as it is only visible on this screen and cannot be obtained later.
2. Setup Dynamics 365 CRM Dashboard:
  • Log into the Dynamics CRM dashboard. Here is an example of the URL to log in - https://<Egnyte Domain>.crm.dynamics.com
  • Navigate to Settings by clicking the gear icon on the top right corner.
  • Select Advanced Settings.
  • Select Security.
  • Click Users.
  • Click the New button in the top left corner and click on Application Users dropdown.
  • Fill out new User Information or assign an already existing user.
  • If adding a new user, paste the Application ID and Application ID URI with the same value (this is the Application ID value from the Azure AD that was created earlier and the user was asked to keep handy). The Azure AD Object ID can be left blank as it will be filled automatically upon saving.
  • For User Name and Primary Email, note that this user must be of TYPE ‘admin’ in the Egnyte Domain to which the user is connecting, and should have the same email ID. It doesn’t have to be a Microsoft organizational email ID, as shown in the example below.
  • Save the changes.
  • Now, the application user should be able to make API requests (ensure that all required permissions are provided). A System Administrator role will grant the ability to make API requests. Make sure to click on ‘Assign Roles’ and assign this user ‘System Administrator’ permissions in the dialog. This completes the admin setup.
3. Setup Dynamics Resources

This will create the resources needed to add the Egnyte integration in Dynamics. Once these resources are added, the user will be able to add them to their Dynamics Entities.

  • Download HTML
  • Log in as a Dynamics Admin.
  • Navigate to Settings -> Customization -> Customize the System.
  • Once the new page opens, Click Web resources in the side menu and Click New.
  • Fill out Web Resource Form for HTML
    • set a name e.g. (“new_”) “PintWebresource”.
    • set a display name e.g.”#Egnyte HTML” (“#” is to make search easier).
    • Set Type as “webpage(HTML)”.
    • Click on the Choose File button next to upload file and upload Egnyte html web resource downloaded in the first step.
    • Click save and then publish.
4. Entity Configuration

The admin can add the Egnyte iframe window to any entity associated with the integration. A folder will be created and mapped in the Egnyte file system by the selected entity. See the following steps to create a service account in the Microsoft Azure AD environment.

  • Log in as a Dynamics Admin.
  • Navigate to Settings > Customization > Customize the System.
  • In the side menu, click Entities.
  • Click on the specific entity to place the Egnyte iframe. We will use Account as an example.
  • Expand the dropdown menu of the selected entity and Click on Forms.
  • Chose Specific form where the add-on should be placed.
  • Select the Insert tab.
  • Select Web Resource (It may require expanding the screen to find Web Resource in menu)
  • Click on the search icon and search for the form created in the previous step (“new_PintWebResource” in our example).
  • Fill out the form and click OK.
  • Move position to desired locations in Account Object where the user will need Egnyte files or folder.
  • Save and publish.
  • Once completed, “#Egnyte” should be visible in the forms.
5. Final Admin Configuration

Admin will connect Dynamics CRM to their specific Egnyte Domain in the step. Admin will also be able to configure the integration to the specific root folder in Egnyte

  • Create a new Account entry.
  • When the user opens the Egnyte Addon in edit mode, it will prompt them to map it with the Egnyte account.
  • The user will see an authorization button for the first time. Click the button and go through the Auth process. Make sure to map it to the Egnyte Admin. Enter Egnyte domain – e.g. DOMAIN.egnye.com.
    • The account used here is XX@microsoft.com to sign in to Entra ID, and in Dynamics, it should be the same User and Email ID in Egnyte as the admin.
    • Additionally, the Application user (pint@egnyte.com in the example used) – Should be the same user and email ID used in the Egnyte domain and it must be in an active state.
  • The user will be asked to fill out a form and input Tenant ID, Application ID and client secret gathered from previous steps(this knowledge should be familiar to Dynamics admins). Additionally, the resource URL is https://<user’s dynamics subdomain>.crm.dynamics.com.
  • Enter the resource URL without a slash (/) at the end (known issue).
  • The user also needs to input the Egnyte folder path – enter this path: ’/Shared/CRM/Dynamics.’
  • Submit the form.
  • On completion, the user will see the Egnyte embedded UI to access the files.
  • To change the configuration and the default folder, click on the Settings on the bottom left corner.
  • The user can also reset the configuration, and by doing so, they will be redirected to the Configuration form.
  • If there is a failed status on uploading files, check the browser and cookies flags. Make sure that the flag ‘chrome://flags/#same-site-by-default-cookies’ is disabled for the Chrome browser.
6. Permission Settings

Depending on the permissions allowed by the Dynamics account, the user may need to set up the following permissions for Egnyte admins and users.

Setup for an Admin
  • Log in as a Dynamics Admin.
  • Navigate to Settings > Security.
  • Select Users.
  • Select the Admin user from the user dropdown and edit the admin user by clicking on Manage Roles.
  • Add the Egnyte - Service User role by checking the box. If this role is not visible, try the System Administrator profile.
Setup for Individual User or Teams
  • Log in as a Dynamics Admin.
  • Navigate to Settings > Security.
  • Select Users.
  • Select the individual user or team from the user dropdown and edit the user by clicking on Manage Roles.
  • Add Egnyte - Authorized User role. If this role is not visible, try the System Administrator profile.
  • Make sure the admin is not part of the team that is being edited as their role will be reduced from ‘Service User’ to ‘Authorized User’.

Limitations

  • The add-on has to be visited once before the corresponding folder in Egnyte is created.
  • If an object of the same name is added, a numerical folder will be created on Egnyte (for example, a folder will be added with ‘~2’).
  • Renaming a folder in Egnyte will not replicate in Dynamics.
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Sales (on-Premises) is not supported.
  • The user’s (non-admin) Dynamics Email must match the email on their Egnyte account.
  • Downloads initiated from the Egnyte iframe may be blocked due to browser limitations. If there are still any issues, contact the CSM or reach out to support@egnyte.com.

Egnyte for M365 (MS Teams, MS Copilot, and Outlook) Overview

With Egnyte’s universal integration across Microsoft 365 (including MS Teams, MS Copilot, and Outlook) users can access and interact with Egnyte-stored content directly within their daily M365 workflows.

Egnyte for Microsoft 365 – Key Features

Microsoft Teams
  • View and edit Egnyte files shared in Teams channels
  • Share Egnyte files directly in Teams conversations
  • Quickly access recently added or edited content and insert secure links
  • Egnyte Tab: manage files from Teams chats and associated Egnyte folders
  • Personal Tab: For quick access to Egnyte Bookmarks, shared links, and domain content
Egnyte Agent for Copilot (Teams, Outlook, M365 Web)
  • Generate summaries and get accurate answers from Egnyte files via Copilot prompts
  • Responses include source file references for quick preview and sharing
  • All actions happen within Microsoft apps—no need to switch platforms
Egnyte in Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork
  • Use Egnyte content in Copilot Cowork for multi-step, long running tasks
  • Egnyte Cowork plugin connects the Egnyte domain as a content source via Egnyte MCP inside the native Copilot experience
  • Egnyte permissions, classification and retention are respected at all times
Egnyte as a content source in Copilot
  • Egnyte content can surface in the native Copilot experience through the Egnyte connector (Copilot Chat and Researcher) using the Egnyte MCP layer and keep Egnyte permissions; no Egnyte content is copied into Microsoft 365
Microsoft Outlook
  • Access Egnyte files while composing emails
  • Insert secure links and reference document content directly
  • Seamless, secure collaboration without leaving Outlook
  • Personal Tab: Centralized access point for Egnyte bookmarks, shared links, and domain content

Security & Permissions

  • Integration respects Microsoft’s native interface
  • AI interactions remain within Egnyte’s security framework
  • No content stored outside Egnyte
  • Strict permission controls ensure users access only what they’re entitled to This comprehensive M365 integration simplifies information retrieval, enhances collaboration, and keeps data secure, whether the user is working in Teams, writing an email in Outlook, or engaging with Copilot across the suite.

Egnyte for Microsoft 365 App can be found under the Apps & Integrations.

Prerequisites and Initial Steps

For Admins
  • Individual M365 License including at least Teams, Outlook or MS Copilot, licences are listed on Microsoft page.
  • Egnyte Admin permissions
  • Global Admin in Microsoft tenant
For End User
  • Admin must complete configuration steps for both Microsoft and Egnyte integration for 365 (Activation affects all domain users or all users in selected Microsoft Entra groups using Microsoft Teams)
  • Individual M365 License (including at least Teams, Outlook or MS Copilot)
  • Co-Editable links are only supported for Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files. In addition, Microsoft 365 for the web must be enabled for the domain. Shared Files can be co-edited once a sharing link was posted on the channel or file is in the shared/target/default folder.
  • Enabled Egnyte for M365 integration by the admin
  • An eligible Microsoft 365 plan with Copilot Chat (basic) for the Egnyte Agent in Copilot Chat. There is no additional Microsoft cost applicable for the agent itself
  • A paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence (Premium seat) and enrolment in the Microsoft Frontier program for Egnyte in Cowork. Cowork tasks are metered in Copilot Credits
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence per user for Egnyte as a data source in Copilot Chat and Researcher
  • The users must have Essential, Elite or Ultimate, or Platform Enterprise, or Enterprise Lite with the AI add-on. Essential, Elite and Ultimate plans include the full MCP toolset; Platform plans support a reduced toolset (browse, advanced search, read and retrieve)
  • An active Egnyte MCP server for the domain, with Microsoft Copilot allowed as an MCP client (Egnyte Settings > AI Powered Features > MCP Server)

Egnyte for M365 - Outlook Configuration Guide

Egnyte integration brings Egnyte content directly into Outlook installed on desktop (Windows and Mac) or Outlook on the web. With this integration, Egnyte users will be able to share links to files or folders with others securely and will be able to store emails, as well as email attachments directly into Egnyte. Since users are sending shared links in their email messages – not actual files – they preserve any security restrictions and keep Egnyte as a source of truth.

This integration is located under Apps & Integrations as Egnyte for M365.

Prerequisites

The following is needed for the setup:

  • Microsoft Office 365 Global Admin Account to deploy integration Enterprise Integrated Apps
  • An Egnyte account
  • Users need to have an active Outlook client (Windows and Mac) installed or access to the web version

Supported Client (Outlook) Configurations by Microsoft

The Microsoft Outlook client must be one of the supported applications. For supported Outlook Clients, Please check Microsoft documentation here.

-The integration is currently not supported on mobile (iOS and Android) due to a Microsoft limitation.

-Due to another Microsoft limitation, the client must be connected to an Exchange server or Microsoft 365 using a direct connection. When configuring the client, the user must choose an Exchange, Office, or Outlook.com account type. If the client is configured to connect with POP3 or IMAP, add-ins will NOT load.

Supported Licenses by Microsoft

Currently supported Outlook licences versions are listed in Microsoft documentation

To check Microsoft plan, Admin can navigate to the Microsoft Admin center and can look at all the licences per user on the main screen.

Microsoft plans with available products are listed here.

Egnyte’s Product and Support Policy includes supporting the last three active versions of the client software.

Configuring Egnyte for M365 in Outlook as an Admin

This integration requires configuration in the Microsoft environment. Please see the section below, which will provide a guide on how to install this add-in within the Microsoft Environment and provide options as a best practice guide.

Deploy Egnyte for Outlook as an Admin

  • Egnyte for M365 in Outlook add-in is certified and can be installed from the Microsoft 365 AppSource here. Click Get it now and follow the wizard to get this deployed to the organization
  • The user will be redirected to Microsoft Admin Center where the deployment will be guided through the deployment wizard
  • Select Egnyte and click Next. In the next step select target users to deploy the app. Select the whole org or selected users or groups.
  • In the Users section, choose from the following options:
    • Just me
    • The entire organization (recommended)
    • Specific users/groups
  • Verify and click Next.
  • In the next step confirm consent for the app permissions.
  • Clicking Accept permissions opens new window where admins can review and accept permissions.
  • Once Permissions accepted is confirmed, select Next.
  • Review app deployment and confirm the final stage of deployment. Click on Finish deployment
  • The deployment status will be updated. Once the deployment process is completed, click Done. It may take between 6 to 24 hours for the add-in to appear in the Outlook Mail client. See Microsoft’s documentation for more details
  • According to Microsoft, process app propagation may take up to 48 hours but usually it takes few minutes for users to see the app in the Outlook
  • An alternative way to enable integration is to go to the Microsoft Admin Center Settings -> Integrated apps. Add Egnyte via Get apps
  • Search for Egnyte in the new Window that opens up.
  • Select Egnyte and click Get it now. A confirmation window will appear.
  • Follow the deployment wizard as described in previous steps
  • According to Microsoft, process app propagation may take up to 48 hours but usually it takes few minutes for users to see the app in the Outlook
  • The Egnyte add-in button displays for everyone the admin has added. All users using this add-in for the first time must complete a one-time authentication when the system prompts them to log in to Egnyte and grant access. This is only needed once per client and is explained in the user guide. Any further changes will be auto-deployed to organization users.

Manage or Remove Egnyte for Outlook

  • Go to the Microsoft Admin Center -> Settings -> Integrated Apps. Click Egnyte App
  • A pop-up screen will appear on the side.
  • In the Configuration tab, the admin can remove the Egnyte app
  • The admin can also add or edit users in the Users tab as mentioned in previous steps.
  • Any changes will take effect in 6 to 24 hours per Microsoft documentation to show up in Outlook clients.

Known Limitations

  • The integration cannot detect when the users are dragging and dropping a file from their local device into an email. To attach a file, double-click to select it.
  • Egnyte for Outlook integration will not be supported on on-premises implementations of Exchange.
  • The current integration does not support Shared Office 365 mailboxes.
  • Egnyte app is not supported on mobile devices (iOS and Android) due to a Microsoft limitation

Saving Email Messages and Attachments to Egnyte

Note: All saved emails and attachments now have unified naming conventions to make it easier to find the saved content.

When saving emails (.eml) to Egnyte, they are named in the following format:

Timestamp YYYY-MM-DD_hourminutessecond [time when email was received in UTC]/ sanitize(title)[140characters}internalMessageid [10characters].eml.

For example: 2026-01-28_141245 Acme Proposal be0e50390d.eml

Similarly, when saving attachments to Egnyte, they are named using the format below:

Timestamp YYYY-MM-DD_hourminutessecond [time when email was received in UTC]/ sanitize(title)[140characters}[sanitize(Attachement name)[60characters]]internalMessageid + attachmentId)[10characters].file type.

For example: 2026-01-28_141245 Acme Proposal prop_RFP_Design_Town_Hall_and_Facilities_Remodel a63353a0d8.docx

  • Open an email or select multiple e-mails in Outlook. If the Egnyte for Outlook icon is pinned, it will appear to the right of the message header. Otherwise, access it from the (…) menu, as shown below
  • Multiple e-mails selected
  • Click Egnyte - a separate pane opens, displaying the email with the subject name as an .eml file and listing the attachments with checkboxes. By default, selecting Select All chooses all attachments. To exclude certain attachments from being saved to Egnyte, clear the checkboxes next to the unwanted files
  • In the next step the user needs to click on Select location and select a folder location for saving content to Egnyte.
    • User can use All Tab to select folder from the file structure
    • It is not permitted to save an email directly to the /Shared or /Private folders. Users will need to select the subfolders.
    • User can use Bookmarks tab to select a folder from the bookmarked folders (these are the same bookmarked folders available in the Web UI)
    • Users can also use search to find the folder
  • Click on Save to Egnyte button after making the selection.
  • A progress bar will appear next to each file during the saving process. Once all files are saved, a summary screen will be displayed. If any attachments fail to upload, a retry option will be available next to the file with the corresponding status
  • Once all attachments are saved, the user can preview the attachments by clicking the View in Egnyte link. This opens the file in Web UI in a new browser tab.
How to Open uploaded e-mails and attachments

To open the uploaded email message in Outlook or any installed mail client, use the Egnyte Desktop App and double-click the saved email file. This will redirect the email with attachments to the appropriate e-mail client application, allowing further actions.

Auto-added e-mail metadata tags

Depending on selected settings, metadata tags will be added to all saved emails and attachments to make it easier to find saved content. Auto-added email tags are visible in the file Details > Metadata > Custom Tags under the namespace Outlook 365

File metadata tags in the WebUI for uploaded e-mails and attachments

Users can enable or disable the setting to auto-add metadata. It is available under Settings in the Outlook add-in hamburger menu.

Enable or disable the toggle as needed.

Additionally, the following settings are available:

  • View Metadata Namespace: Users can click on the option and they will be redirected to the Egnyte Domain settings and can look for Outlook 365 namespace in the listing.
  • Remove Metadata Namespace: Selecting this option will delete the metadata namespace. Please note that this action is retroactive and will also remove metadata from files already saved to Egnyte via the Outlook add-in.

Sending Shared Links to the Egnyte Files or Folders via Email

The user can use Outlook to send any Egnyte files to external users safely and securely. Current folder permissions and privacy settings are applicable ensuring unauthorized access is prevented. The user cannot send a shared link of a file they do not have permission to share.

  • Open Outlook and click Compose.
  • In the third-party application bar at the top of the new message window, click Egnyte in a Pinned bar or click on the office ribbon. Select Share files
  • An Egnyte dialog box opens, displaying the Egnyte folders in a long list. Scroll down until the required folder is visible, then click to open it and select the desired file. For ease of access, the last ten recent files and bookmarked folders are also displayed. User can also search for file names.
  • Multiple files selected
  • Select files or folders to share.
  • By default, the shared link permissions are set to the default settings in the Web UI. Users can adjust the permissions on the shared link. To do this, click Select to choose files or folders, and choose the available options on the Sharing Parameters screen
    • Anyone
    • Anyone with password
    • Egnyte File Server Users
    • Domain users with permission
    • Specific Recipients
  • The message redisplays, and Egnyte links are displayed within the email body
  • Click Send when done. The recipient receives this email with Egnyte’s shared link(s). The recipient will need permission to view files shared in the Egnyte Collaborate platform. The link is displayed as an icon that can be moved within the body of the email message, for instance, to place between paragraphs or just above the signature. The location of the Egnyte (Add-In) icon varies depending on the Microsoft platform in use, such as Web Outlook Client, Desktop on Windows, or Mac. If the user uses the new Outlook Web app, the Egnyte icon is displayed within a drop-down menu in the lower toolbar (when creating a new message) or in the top-right toolbar (when opening a message) if pinned, or via a bar with an overflow menu (…).

Requesting Files from Others

Upload links provide an easy way for individuals outside of an Egnyte domain to contribute content directly to a specific Shared folder, ensuring they cannot view the folder’s existing contents. More information about Requesting files from others can be found here.

  • Open Outlook and click New email
  • In the third-party application bar at the top of the new message window, click Egnyte in the pinned bar or select it from the apps on the office ribbon. With this an Egnyte dialog box opens, displaying the list of available actions while creating a new email. Select Request files from others
  • Select a folder for upload (only one folder at a time can be selected) from the Egnyte folder listing. Scroll down until the required folder is visible, then click to select the folder. Users can also search for folder names. Click on continue with the selected folder.
  • In the next step, define sharing parameters
    • By default, the link permissions are set to Anyone
    • If links need to be active for a certain amount of time, set an expiration time, which will prevent uploads after the designated time frame. The drop-down menu offers various time options such as 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, etc.
    • The Create separate folder for files received from each person option will store each recipient’s files in a unique subfolder. For example, if 100 people uploaded files via an upload link, then 100 subfolders will be created with each recipient’s name, email address, and their respective files.
  • Click Share link when done and the Egnyte upload link is displayed within the Email body. Once the email is sent, the recipient receives this email with Egnyte’s upload link.
