Egnyte for M365 in MS Teams - User Guide

Overview

The Egnyte for MS Teams Integration effectively merges Egnyte’s file sync and sharing capabilities with Microsoft Teams, available on both its web and desktop versions. Users can safely share links and collaborate on files like Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint within Teams without switching platforms with changes being automatically saved to Egnyte storage. It also allows the sharing of files from local machines, which are securely uploaded to Egnyte instead of native content stores like OneDrive and SharePoint.

In general, Egnyte is limited by the restrictions placed by Microsoft on the Teams Messenger Extension and Tab integrations frameworks.

Prerequisites

  • Individual Microsoft Teams License
  • Microsoft 365 subscription to provide real-time collaboration of MS Office files
  • Microsoft 365 for the web integration must be enabled for the domain. Co-Editable links are only supported for Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files. Shared Files can be co-edited once a sharing link was posted on the channel or file is in the shared/target/default folder.
  • Egnyte for MS Teams integration needs to be enabled by the admin for MS Teams users.

Getting Started

  • Users can see the Egnyte app on the bottom bar post-creation.
  • Egnyte Files Tab is added to the channels, making it easier for users to access and share files.

Features and Capabilities

The detailed MS Teams - User Guide lists down the initial steps along with the various features and capabilities provided to the end-users with the Egnyte - MS Teams integration.

Egnyte for M365 - MS Teams – User Guide

The user guide covers the step-by-step guidelines for the following features:

  • Upload File(s) to Egnyte Folder
    • Change Target Folder
  • Share Egnyte File(s) Link
  • Using Egnyte File(s) Tab
    • Create a New File/Folder
    • Upload a File or Folder
    • Open the File or Folder in Egnyte
  • Preview the Shared File
  • Opening a File/Folder in Egnyte
  • Co-Edit a Shared File
    • Co-editing a Shared MS 365 File
    • Co-editing a File using Egnyte tab
  • Remove a File or Folder The users can also access the detailed user guide to learn about the known issues and limitations and to refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

Egnyte for M365 in MS Teams FAQ

I store sensitive data in Egnyte. Will shared files be stored in MS Teams?

No, Teams has access only to shared links and file metadata (such as thumbnail, file name, author, version, and uploaded timestamp).

Is it possible to designate Egnyte as the default file storage system for MS Teams?

Yes, it is possible. To configure Egnyte as the default storage for your Teams environment, the administrator needs to follow the steps outlined in the MS Teams Admin Guide.

However, note that Private Channels do not currently support the Egnyte for Teams integration. If your administrator hides the OneDrive / SharePoint (ODSP) entry points, users won’t be able to share files through either Egnyte or SharePoint within Private Channels.

What happens to the content in the default Egnyte folder if a Team or Channel is deleted?

The content in the default Egnyte folder will not be visible within Teams if the team or channel is deleted. However, to ensure content accessibility, it will always be available and accessible through Egnyte’s WebUI.

What happens to SharePoint content once the Egnyte integration is enabled?

Egnyte integration will not delete or move any SharePoint content. If you wish to migrate these files to Egnyte, you need to move them manually.

What do I do if I deleted the Egnyte Files tab?

If you’ve accidentally removed the Egnyte Files tab, you can easily re-add it.

Just navigate to the top of your Teams application, click the “+” button, search for the Egnyte app, and then follow the instructions provided.

Can I search through my Egnyte content from the Teams interface?

Indeed, you can utilize the Egnyte Files Tab to search for Egnyte content. However, note that the search functionality is confined to the content within the default folder.

Do I have to uninstall the earlier version of the integration before I can install this updated version?

No, but utilizing both simultaneously may lead to issues. We advise uninstalling the previous integration before installing and utilizing the latest version 4.0.0.

When I remove a channel member from Channel, is that member also removed from the Egnyte collaborators of that mapped folder?

If you use the automatically created folder, Egnyte automatically removes that member from the mapped folder when they are removed from the Channel.

Can I use an existing folder with a Teams Channel instead of the automatically created folder?

Yes, you can manually map the Egnyte folder of your choice (excluding the root “Shared” folder) to a Teams Channel.

Who can assign a Default Egnyte Folder to a Teams Channel?

You must be a Team owner to establish a custom default Channel folder.

What happens if I change the default folder?

You have the flexibility to modify the default Egnyte folders, even for Channels that have already been linked to the default Egnyte folders. In such cases, any content that was previously present in the original Egnyte folder will remain there. To transfer this pre-existing content to the newly specified folder, you need to use the Egnyte Web UI and perform the relocation manually. Alternatively, you can choose to archive or delete the content. Once the transfer is complete, you have the option to delete the original folder.

Egnyte for OneNote

The Egnyte for OneNote Integration allows users to effectively integrate Egnyte’s powerful file sync and sharing capabilities within Microsoft OneNote Online. This article covers how to use Egnyte for Microsoft OneNote Online. This integration currently is available in Microsoft OneNote online products.

With this Add-In you can do the following from Microsoft OneNote online

  1. Put a link to a file that is stored in your Egnyte File system

  2. Put a link to an image file with a Preview Mode, for you to view the image in the OneNote page along with the link. You also have the option to disable the preview mode of the image file.

  3. Control who can access the link while you share your OneNote online page with others to collaborate

  4. Set File link expiry based on the number of days/weeks/months or number or clicks

  5. Notify the user when their file links are clicked

  6. Add filename to the link

  7. Search files in Egnyte from within OneNote to share the link for.

Installation and System Requirements

This capability is provided through the OneNote online Add-In. In order to add the Add-In, the user needs to click on the Insert tab and click on the Office Add-ins.

If you are an enterprise User this Add-In will be enabled at your Organization level by your Microsoft Office Admin. You just need to click on the My Organization and see the Egnyte for OneNote Add-in already added by your Admin.

If you are the Enterprise Admin, you need to make the Add-In available to all the Microsoft Enterprise users in your Organization. You can search the “Egnyte for OneNote” app in the Office Add-ins store and add it for your Organization.

Once the Add-In is added to your OneNote App, it will be available under your Insert tab. On clicking on the Insert tab you should see the Egnyte Logo that says “File from Egnyte Connect”.

Click on the tab “File from Egnyte Connect” and you will see that in your left-hand panel of your OneNote online as shown below.

Click on the Connect Egnyte account and it takes you to a new tab where you Authenticate and Authorize

Once the authorization is done the tab autocloses and you again land in your OneNote online tab with the Egnyte Connect File Picker available for you to share links to files from Egnyte in your OneNote pages

Now you can search, navigate to files for which you want to put the links into your OneNote online document.

For Browser Support the below Browsers are supported

Chrome (latest)

Firefox (latest)

Internet Explorer 11

Microsoft Edge

Safari 10.0 (11602.1.50.0.10)

Settings

We have s separate Settings section in OneNote Add-in from which you can control various link properties, re-configure your Egnyte domain to be used with your OneNote, toggle the Image preview settings.

To navigate to the Settings section click on the settings icon as shown below.

The settings tab has various link options described earlier. Also, you can re-configure your domain by clicking log out and providing you new domain details again. You can also use the General Settings checkbox to Embed file preview for pictures.

Egnyte for Outlook Add-In - User Guide

Egnyte for Outlook brings Egnyte content directly into Outlook installed on PC or Outlook on the Web. With this integration, users can:

  • Select files from Egnyte and send them as links anywhere within the body of the email
  • Save attachments directly from the email message into an Egnyte folder
  • Save the body of the email message into an Egnyte folder The Egnyte for Outlook integration is located under the Apps and Integrations page.

Prerequisites

Admin has to complete the setup before the user can use Microsoft Outlook Add-in.

The following is essential for the user:

  • Egnyte Account
  • A supported Microsoft 365/Office 365 Business or Enterprise subscription is required. Standalone Outlook client installations are not supported
  • The add-in can only be deployed in a licensed and administrator-managed Microsoft 365 environment. Deployment using personal email accounts (for example, @gmail.com) or company email accounts that are not managed through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center with the required licenses is not supported
  • The integration can be used from both Outlook Web and Outlook Client

Supported Client (Outlook) Configurations by Microsoft

The Microsoft Outlook client must be one of the supported applications which supports Outlook add-ins. For supported Outlook Clients, check Microsoft documentation here.

Egnyte for Outlook add-in is not supported in the new Outlook for Mac (Microsoft’s redesigned client). This is a Microsoft-side compatibility limitation and affected users on the new client will see a blank sign-in panel.

The following are the workarounds:

  1. Switch to the Egnyte for M365 add-in that is supported in the new Outlook client (Mac or Windows)

  2. If the first option is not possible then switch to the legacy Outlook for Mac (available via the Switch to Legacy Outlook option in the app) or use the Egnyte Outlook add-in via Outlook on the web (outlook.office.com).

Supported Office Licenses by Microsoft

Tip: If a user has a valid Microsoft 365 subscription but does not have access to the Outlook Client, they can download and install the latest version of Office.

  • In the third-party application bar at the top of the new message window, click Egnyte for Outlook in the pinned bar or select Egnyte from the apps on the office ribbon. With this an Egnyte dialog box opens, displaying the list of available actions while creating a new email.
  • Select Request files from others, as shown below.
  • Select a folder for upload (only one folder at a time can be selected) from the Egnyte folder listing. Scroll down until the required folder is visible, then click to select the folder. Users can also search for folder names. Click on Continue with the selected folder.
  • In the next step, define sharing parameters:
    • By default, the link permissions are set to Anyone
    • If links need to be active for a certain amount of time, set an expiration time, which will prevent uploads after the designated time frame. The drop-down menu offers various time options such as 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, etc.
    • The Create separate folder for files received from each person option will store each recipient’s files in a unique subfolder. For example, if 100 people uploaded files via an upload link, then 100 subfolders will be created with each recipient’s name, email address, and their respective files.
  • Click Share link when done.
  • The Egnyte upload link will be displayed within the body of the email. Once the email is sent, the recipient receives this email with Egnyte’s upload link.

Additional Features within Egnyte for Outlook Add-in.

  • Outlook Version Information is provided in the About screen in settings. Settings will show more admin options. Help will let users submit bugs /defects regarding outlook add-in with Egnyte support.
  • Users can also change domains by first logging out and then logging in again.
Known Limitations
  • Egnyte for Outlook integration works only for Office365 customers.
  • Egnyte Standard users can upload attachments, and upload files to Egnyte., but they can share Direct links.
  • Outlook add-ins are different from COM or VSTO add-ins, which are older integrations specific to Outlook running on Windows. Unlike COM add-ins, Outlook add-ins don’t have any code physically installed on the user’s device or Outlook and are supported via Office Store and add-in program. So if the user has installed Outlook.COM Add-in on windows, we recommend disabling it.
  • Egnyte for Outlook integration is NOT supported with on-premises implementations of Exchange.
  • The current integration does not support Shared Office365 mailboxes. Microsoft Limitation: The client must be connected to an Exchange server or Microsoft 365 using a direct connection. When configuring the client, the user must choose an Exchange, Office, or Outlook.com account type. If the client is configured to connect with POP3 or IMAP, add-ins will NOT load.

Egnyte for Outlook Add-in: Metadata for Saved Emails

MS Outlook v 1.2.0. April, 2022.

Egnyte for Outlook brings Egnyte content directly into Outlook installed on your PC, Mac or Outlook on the web. With this integration, Egnyte Users will be able to share links to files or folders with others securely and now will be able to store emails with metadata in Egnyte.

Since users are saving emails with metadata in Egnyte, they can use the Collaborate platform and advanced search functionality to locate emails using supported fields easily and quickly. Egnyte users will also be able to open saved email (.EML file) using the Egnyte Desktop product, which will open it in the installed Outlook client to take further actions.

This integration is located under Apps & Integrations and is named Egnyte for Outlook. Currently, this Add-in is available to all under all plans.

Prerequisites

Add-in is configured and added by Admin per Egnyte for Outlook Admin Guide

Enabling Metadata for Email in the Outlook Add-in as an Admin

  1. Open the web client or the installed Outlook on a Windows or Mac machine.

  2. Log in to Egnyte for Outlook Add-in, navigate to the side panel and click on Settings.

  3. Admin can click on Enable and ensure to click the box. Click Save.

End User Experience with the Added Metadata to Saved Emails

Once users save emails to Egnyte, they will now automatically see metadata with saved emails in Egnyte, if it’s enabled by an admin. This will light up advanced search functions in the platform.

If user does not see the metadata with the saved email (.EML) file, please check first with IT /Admin to ensure that it was Enabled, by going to the Egnyte for Outlook Add-in -> Settings.

Known Limitations

  • None

Egnyte for Outlook Add-In: Upload a Local File

Egnyte for Outlook Add-In brings Egnyte content directly into Outlook installed on your PC, Mac or Outlook on the web. It is now capable of uploading a file from the user’s device to Egnyte within itself so there is no need to navigate away from the Outlook.

To start, users have to select the folder to which file will be uploaded. Button with “file icon” as shown opens the OS file picker. If a file is selected and confirmed the upload will start. While the process is running, users can cancel it. In case of an error or when the process was interrupted, there is an option to restart upload.

Upload is not allowed to root folders, “Shared” and “Private”, and the size limit is set to 100MB /file.

This integration is located under Apps & Integrations and is named Egnyte for Outlook. Currently, this Add-in is available to all under all plans.

Egnyte for Outlook Classic Add-In - Configuration Guide

Egnyte for Outlook brings Egnyte content directly into Outlook Classic installed on your PC, Mac or Outlook on the web. With this integration, Egnyte Users will be able to share links to files or folders to others securely and will be able to store emails, as well as email attachments directly into the Egnyte. Since users are sending shared links in their email messages – not actual files – they preserve any security restrictions and keep Egnyte as a source of truth for your enterprise content.

This integration is located under Apps & Integrations and is named “Egnyte for Outlook”.

Prerequisites

The following is needed for the setup:

  • Microsoft Office 365 Global Admin Account to Deploy Add-in via Enterprise Integrated Apps
  • An Egnyte account
  • Users have an active Outlook Email client installed or on the web.

Supported Outlook Client Configurations by Microsoft

The Microsoft Outlook client must be one of the supported applications which supports Outlook add-ins. For supported Outlook Clients, Please check Microsoft documentation here.

  • Microsoft Limitation - The client must be connected to an Exchange server or Microsoft 365 using a direct connection. When configuring the client, the user must choose an Exchange, Office, or Outlook.com account type. If the client is configured to connect with POP3 or IMAP, add-ins will NOT load.

  • Egnyte for Outlook add-in is not supported in the new Outlook for Mac (Microsoft’s redesigned client). This is a Microsoft-side compatibility limitation and affected users on the new client will see a blank sign-in panel.

The following are the workarounds:

  1. Switch to the Egnyte for M365 add-in that is supported in the new Outlook client (Mac or Windows)

  2. If the first option is not possible then switch to the legacy Outlook for Mac (available via the Switch to Legacy Outlook option in the app) or use the Egnyte Outlook add-in via Outlook on the web (outlook.office.com).

Supported Office Licenses by Microsoft

Microsoft Side - If you have a valid Microsoft 365 subscription and you do not have access to the Outlook Client, you can download and install the latest version of Office.

  • Microsoft 365 Business licenses (Business Basic, Business Standard, Business Premium), Office 365 Enterprise licenses, or Microsoft 365 Enterprise licenses (E3/E5/F3).
  • Version 1808 or later of Office Professional Plus 2019 or Office Standard 2019.
Third-Party Contact Disclaimer

Egnyte provides third-party contact information to help find technical support within the external product. This contact information may change without notice. Egnyte does not guarantee the accuracy of this third-party contact information.

Egnyte’ Product and Support Policy includes supporting the last three active versions of the client software.

Configuring Outlook Add-in as an Admin

  • In Egnyte, as an Admin, navigate to Apps & Integrations
  • Scroll down to the Individual Tiles and look for the Egnyte for Outlook App.
  • This integration requires external configuration in the Microsoft environment. See below section, which will provide a guide on how to install this add-in within Microsoft Environment during and provide options as a best practice guide.

Deploy Egnyte for Outlook as an Admin.

For O365 Admins:

  1. Outlook add-in is certified and can be installed from the Microsoft 365 AppSource here. Click Get it now and follow the wizard to get this deployed to the organization.

  2. The system displays a screen describing the Egnyte Add-in. Click Next.

  3. In the Users section, choose from the following options:

  • Just me
  • The entire organization (recommended)
  • Specific users/groups
  • Verify and click Next.

  1. Review permissions and select Next.

  2. Agree to the App permissions and select Accept.

Administrator consent for Microsoft Outlook Integration - Microsoft graph explained here.

Permission

Details

Why does the app need this?

Read user and shared mail

Allows the app to read mail a user can access, including their own and shared mail.

Required to read mail subject, content and attachments to perform upload to Egnyte

Maintain access to data you have given it access to

Allows the app to see and update the data you gave it access to, even when users are not currently using the app. This does not give the app any additional permissions

Required to reliably perform the transfer operation in a backend service rather than on a device

Sign in and read user profile

Allows users to sign-in to the app, and allows the app to read the profile of signed-in users. It also allows the app to read basic company information of signed-in users

Required to authenticate the user

  1. Review the settings. Click the Finish deployment at bottom of the screen.

  2. Once the deployment process is completed, click Done. It may take up to 6 hours for the add-in to appear in the Outlook Mail client or even up to 24 hours. See Microsoft’s documentation for more details.

The Egnyte add-in button displays for everyone the user has added. Everyone using this add-in for the first time must complete a one-time authentication when the system prompts them to log in to Egnyte and grant access. This is only needed once per client and is explained in the user guide.

Manage or Remove Egnyte for Outlook

For O365 Admins

  1. Go to the Office 365 admin center and navigate to Settings > Services and Add-ins.

  2. Click Egnyte for Outlook App. Click Edit Users or Edit Configuration options.

  3. It would pop up on the screen on the side. Admin can also add/edit users from here.

Any changes will take effect in 6-24 hours per Microsoft documentation to show up in Outlook clients.

Known Limitations

  • Egnyte for Outlook integration works only for Office365 customers.
  • The integration cannot detect when the user is dragging and dropping a file from their local device into an email. To attach a file, double-click to select it.
  • Egnyte for Outlook integration will not be supported on on-premises implementations of Exchange.
  • Admins who deployed “Egnyte for Outlook” in Beta should remove the app from the Integrated store per this article, and re-deploy it from the Microsoft 365 AppSource per Step 1. It is only required once, and only if the user is enrolled in Beta previously. All subsequent changes can be auto-deployed to organization users, as this is recommended option by Microsoft for certified applications.
  • The current integration does not support Shared Office365 mailboxes.

  • Real-time Sync: Embed Egnyte folder structures directly in SharePoint to keep information up-to-date.
  • Full Web UI Access: Access the full Egnyte Web UI or specific Web Parts to perform actions like editing files via Microsoft 365 for the web.

Prerequisites

Before starting the installation, ensure that the following administrative privileges are granted:

  • Egnyte Admin permissions
  • Microsoft Tenant: Global Admin rights with Microsoft Admin permissions enabled for SharePoint.
Back to Top…

Installation

  • Download the Egnyte for SharePoint App manifest file.
  • Navigate to Sharepoint Admin Center.
  • Select More features and click Open under the Apps section.
  • On the Manage Apps page, click the Upload button and select the downloaded manifest file.
  • Once the file is uploaded, an Enable app panel will appear. Select the preferred App availability (for example, Enable this app and add it to all sites) and click Enable app.
  • Confirm that Egnyte for SharePoint v2 appears as Enabled in the app list.
  • Confirm app consent - click the authorization link and confirm consent.
  • Complete the Egnyte redirection process.
Back to Top…

Adding the Egnyte Web Part to a Site

Once the Egnyte app is added to the catalog, the Egnyte component can be added to a Sharepoint site, and users can then use Egnyte inside the Sharepoint site.

  • Navigate to the SharePoint site (for example, yourtenantname.sharepoint.com).
  • Go to the specific page where the Egnyte Web view needs to be added and click Edit.
  • Hover over the section to add the view and click the gray + (plus) button.
  • Search for and select the Egnyte for SharePoint v2 app from the dialog.
  • Authenticate the Egnyte domain and approve the requested app permissions when prompted.
Back to Top…

Configuration & Customization

By default, the app displays the Shared root folder. To customize this:

  • Select the Edit properties (sliders icon) on the top of Egnyte Web Part.
  • In the right-hand panel, enter the specific Default directory path to be displayed. Click Apply to save the changes.
  • (Optional) Use standard SharePoint settings to adjust the Web Part’s layout or size to fit the page design.

Troubleshooting Consent Required Error:

If there is an error stating that the user or administrator has not consented to use the application, it would be required to manually grant tenant-wide consent.

  • Click the authorization link and confirm consent.
  • Complete the Egnyte redirection process.
  • Return to the SharePoint site and refresh the page to clear the error.
Back to Top…

Troubleshooting Invalid User Token

The add-in shows a We’re sorry, but something went wrong message.

This is usually caused by an authentication problem. Most often, it is observed when the user has recently changed their password, or hasn’t used the add-in for a while and their session has expired.

To resolve this issue:

  • Click the add-in settings button.
  • Select Logout on the add-in settings panel.
  • A confirmation screen will appear to reload. Click on Reload.
  • Log in with the Egnyte credentials.
  • Once re-authenticated, the add-in will automatically reload. If the issue persists after logging in again, please contact Egnyte Support.

Troubleshooting SharePoint integration Sign-In Loop

There might be an issue where SharePoint keeps prompting the user sign-in in a loop.

This is usually caused by the browser blocking third-party cookies, which the SharePoint integration requires to load correctly. Users can confirm this by checking for a crossed-out eye icon on the right side of the browser’s address bar.

Solution (Chrome)
  • Allow third-party cookies for this site, follow instructions on Chrome official documentation
  • Reload the page.
Solution (Safari)
  • Allow third-party cookies for this site, follow instructions on Safari official documentation
  • Reload the page.
Solution (Firefox)
  • Allow third-party cookies for this site, follow instructions on Firefox official documentation
  • Reload the page.
Solution (Microsoft Edge)
  • Allow third-party cookies for this site, follow instructions on Microsoft Edge official documentation
  • Reload the page.

Uninstalling integration

  • To disable and remove the integration navigate to the SharePoint Admin Center.
  • Select More features and click Open under the Apps section.
  • On the Manage Apps page, locate the Egnyte for SharePoint V2 app. Select it and click on Delete.
  • Confirm the deletion when prompted. This will remove the integration component from all sites in the tenant.

Egnyte Sharing Options within Microsoft 365 for the Web

The article covers details on the sharing options within Egnyte’s Microsoft 365 co-editing for the Web integration. The users can also co-edit their files with other users in real-time without leaving the Microsoft 365 Apps.

For Admins, all domain settings and sharing settings that they have set up in the Collaborate Product will be applicable, offering a consistent experience across Egnyte.

Enable Microsoft 365 Co-editing for the Web:

For new domains, if Microsoft 365 co-editing for the Integration is not enabled by the Egnyte Admins for the users, they can:

  • Navigate to Egnyte Domain -> Apps & Integrations -> Microsoft 365 co-editing for the Web, and enable it for the users.
  • Click on Enable Integration.
  • Choose Added for all users from the dropdown and click Save. For Egnyte domains where this is enabled or added, there is no action needed.

Egnyte Sharing within Microsoft 365 Co-Editing for the Web:

Egnyte users with edit permissions can open and co-edit a file in Microsoft 365 for the web.

  • Right-click on the file (or click the checkbox next to a file), choose Microsoft Word for the Web in Edit options.
  • Alternatively, hover over the three-dots menu of a file, click on edit icon -> Microsoft Word for the Web. The user may need to log in using their Microsoft 365 Business account periodically to verify their Microsoft subscription is active as they will be working with Third party Software.

To edit the file, make the desired changes to the file. All changes are automatically saved to Egnyte instantly and the user can co-edit by inviting other Egnyte users to join them in the document.

Share Options in MS 365 for the Web

When the user opens a Microsoft 365[Word], [PowerPoint], or [Excel] file on the web, they will see the Microsoft Share UI on the top-right side of the window depending on the 365 Client version they have.

Click on Share and any of the following options:

  • Share: The user can share the file by choosing the access and setting the link properties.
  • Copy Link: The user can set the link access and properties to get the share link and copy the link to share with other user(s).
  • Manage Access: The option enables the user to manage access to the file’s link to share it with anyone/anyone with password/existing user(s)/specific recipients. There are some additional options when the user as a sender, clicks Share. All three options will lead to opening a new browser Tab with the Egnyte Sharing options.

User can click on Get share link to copy the link and share it with the intended users. Alternatively, Click Email Link, choose the recipient(s), fill in the short message, and click on Send email.

Learn more about link sharing here.

After clicking on send email, the sender will get a confirmation dialog. Sender needs to close this browser tab after sharing is done, and they can resume working on the Microsoft 365 document.

The recipient (s) will get an email with the link to join the sender in the document to co-edit if they have an Egnyte account and required permissions.

  • Standard Users can not share links.

  • Any changes in the default settings or permissions can be done in Collaborate -> Settings. The same settings will be applicable in Microsoft 365 for the web applications.

Egnyte’s Microsoft Power Automate Integration

Overview

Power Automate (Formerly known as Microsoft Flow), is a cloud-based software that allows users to create and automate workflows and tasks across over 220 applications and services without help from developers. Automated workflows are called flows. To create a flow, the user specifies what action should take place when a specific event occurs. Once a flow is built, it can be managed on the desktop or through an app on a mobile device. With Egnyte, users can create workflows with files stored in Egnyte when they are copied, created, deleted, or moved allowing do automate these processes.

To learn more about Microsoft Power Automate, watch our democast

Connector

The Egnyte Connector can be found in the Connectors section within the Power Automate website.

Triggers

The Egnyte Connector has 10 triggers to which to start the workflow within Power Automate. These are standard triggers to watch certain folders for a certain event to kick off the workflow. These triggers can start workflows within Egnyte or with one of the many other connectors in Power Automate. Build an Automated Flow with an Egnyte Trigger.

Actions

The Egnyte Connector has 67 different actions. The actions allows user to move, lock, or share a file within Egnyte. Use these actions in the different workflows within Power Automate.

The field Namespace name in the context of the metadata refers to the metadata section. Click here to know more about using Metadata in Egnyte.

Prerequisite: Add Exchange as a Source

To add Exchange Online as a source, follow the steps below:

  • In Egnyte Secure & Govern, navigate to Settings > Content Sources. In case Microsoft or Office 365 has not yet been added as a source, go to step 2. Otherwise, go to step 3.
  • Click on Add Cloud Source and select the Microsoft option.
  • In the next step select To migrate data to Egnyte
  • The option to add Exchange Online appears as an additional step during the setup process. During this step, Exchange Admin privileges are requested for the application to access email content across all users. Now, Microsoft or Office 365 with Exchange Online has been successfully added as a source, but Exchange needs to be configured in the next step.
  • Open the source details for the existing Microsoft source. Cancel or adjust settings for SharePoint. The option to Configure Exchange Online appears as a sub-source in addition to OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Click on it.
  • Follow wizard and once all settings are in place, source status will change into Monitoring

Prerequisite: Grant End Users Access to Secure & Govern

Before end users can create mappings between Outlook folders and Egnyte Project Folders, they need access to Secure & Govern.

  • In Secure & Govern, navigate to Settings -> User Management -> Users & Groups
  • Go to the Auto-provision for Egnyte Collaborate Admins & Power Users section. Toggle on Allow any power user in linked Egnyte domains to get access to Secure & Govern.

Enable Email Capture Features

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General
  • Scroll down to the Email Capture section.
Enabling Manual Email Capture
  • Turn on the Manual Email capture toggle. This allows end users to create mappings between Outlook folders and Egnyte Project Folders, and enables advanced features such as email thread filing, saving emails directly to a Project Folder, and automatically applying a dedicated metadata set to all saved emails.
  • Prerequisite: Ensure that the Egnyte for M365 in Outlook is enabled separately in the Microsoft Admin Center. For detailed setup instructions, see the Admin Guide
Enable Automated Capture

  • Select the toggle for Automated Email capture and turn it on

  • Define the target location of the Emails folder (that is automatically created by integration). By default folder is created under main project folder, but it is possible to define a custom path that applies to all synced Project folders by clicking Change with a pencil icon

  • Enter the desired path, example: Correspondence. The integration will create a custom folder structure

  • Click on Proceed to confirm.

  • Select Email Server: Exchange servers that have been added as content sources from Egnyte Secure & Govern (S&G) will show up here.

    • To add a content source from S&G see instructions in the Prerequisite section. Click on Configure new to start configuration

  • Select Projects: In the Select Egnyte projects for email syncs pop-up, check the boxes for the projects to sync. Click Next.

  • Map Shared Mailboxes and Folders: On the Configure Email Syncs screen:

  • Under Egnyte folder, verify the target project folder

  • Under Mailbox account, select the relevant user email address from the dropdown

  • Under Mail folder, choose the specific Outlook folder to monitor (For example: Inbox, Sent, Archive, or Conversation History)

  • Click the Configure button to activate the sync rules.

  • Enable or disable sync for all existing emails with a toggle Sync previous emails - with this option integration will save not only all upcoming emails, but also the historical ones.

  • Please note that syncing historical emails may take up to 48 hours, depending on the emails volume.

  • Manage Existing Syncs: To edit or delete active rules, click Manage in the Email Capture section of Settings.

  • Click Save after making any changes.

  • When Automated Email Capture is fully configured, any email placed in a synced Outlook folder is automatically copied to the corresponding mapped Egnyte folder. This process is fully automated and triggers whether the email is moved via manual drag-and-drop, user-defined Outlook rules, or administrator-defined Exchange routing rules.

  • Admins can configure syncs for Shared Mailboxes only. Personal mailboxes can be synced by end users. Admin has view-only of user mailboxes connections, with option to delete connection, but editing is restricted to end users only.

  • Folder Connection option in the Egnyte for M365 add-in only appears when Automated Email capture toggle is turned on

Email Capture - Overview

Email Capture lets users save emails and their attachments from Microsoft Outlook directly into Egnyte Project folders either manually on demand, or automatically via rules configured by the administrator.

Filed emails are stored as .eml files inside a structured folder hierarchy within the relevant Egnyte Project. Once filed, emails are discoverable via Egnyte search and can be previewed in the Egnyte Web UI, giving teams a single, searchable record of all project correspondence alongside the rest of the project files.

Benefits and Capabilities

Project decisions, approvals, and key communications often live only in individual inboxes making them invisible to the broader team and difficult to retrieve later. Email Capture solves this by bringing correspondence into Egnyte so that:

  • Project teams have full context on decisions, regardless of when they joined
  • Filed emails are searchable alongside documents, drawings, and other Project files
  • Records are preserved for legal, compliance, and audit purposes
  • Teams moving from tools like Newforma have a familiar, structured filing workflow
  • Email Capture requires Egnyte for M365 in Outlook, Microsoft Exchange/365, and is available in all Next Gen Plans (Essentials, Elite & Ultimate) with Egnyte Secure & Govern. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Requirements and Prerequisites

Before Email Capture feature can be used, ensure the following configurations are in place by Egnyte Admin:

  • Outlook version: New Outlook for Mac or Windows (classic Outlook is not supported)
  • Egnyte for M365 in Outlook : Must be installed from the Microsoft AppSource
  • Folder mappings : Requires an Exchange server connection configured in Egnyte Settings by a domain administrator
  • Email Capture: Feature must be enabled by administrator
  • Permissions: User must have at least Editor permission to the Egnyte project folder to capture emails to
  • Supported mail provider: Microsoft Exchange or Microsoft 365. Other email providers are currently not supported Email Capture feature is not supported on Egnyte for Outlook Classic Add-In Integration.

Limitations and Known Issues

  • Outlook Compatibility: The Egnyte Outlook Add-in and all Email Capture features require New Outlook. Classic Outlook is not fully supported. Users who are restricted to Classic Outlook by their IT policy will not be able to use all manual email capture features.
  • 50,000 Files Per Folder Limit: Egnyte enforces a limit of 50,000 files per folder. For high-volume projects, when this limit is reached within a monthly folder, a new sub-folder is automatically created using the naming convention: YYYY-MM (Month Name) [From MMM DD]
  • Example: 2026-01 (January) [From Jan 20]
  • The folder split is handled automatically. No action is required from the user, be aware that emails for a single month may span more than one folder on very active projects.
  • Thread Filing via Add-In: Thread filing via the manual Outlook Add-in is not yet available.
  • Multi-Domain Support: Automated Email Capture currently supports the following multi-domain configurations
    • One S&G tenant with one Exchange server + multiple Egnyte domains
    • Multiple S&G tenants, each with the same Exchange server + one Egnyte domain per tenant
    • The following configuration is not supported:
      • A master Egnyte domain (with its own S&G tenant) plus sub-domains under different S&G tenants, where all email capture configurations need to be visible from the master domain.
      • Users on unsupported MEM setups who wish to file to multiple domains must sign out and sign back into the add-in for each domain. Full MEM support is planned for a future phase.
      • Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for assistance if clarification is required regarding your domain setup.
  • Automated Capture (Configuration Is Folder-to-Folder Mapping): The Automated Capture flow relies on admin-configured mailbox-to-Egnyte folder mappings. Rules must be set up manually per project. There is no out-of-the-box auto-detection of which project an email belongs to. AI-assisted automatic routing is under consideration for a future phase.
  • Timestamp Discrepancy (Known Issue): In some cases, the message date metadata on a filed email and the date shown in the filename may differ by one day. This is caused by time zone differences between the sender and recipient.

  • Email Capture - User Guide

Email Capture - User Guide

Email Capture enables users to save project emails and their attachments directly from Microsoft Outlook using Egnyte for M365 in Outlook, keeping important correspondence accessible alongside other project files. This guide covers the end-user configuration steps.

Refer here for the Admin Guide.

  • Email Capture requires Egnyte for M365 in Outlook, Microsoft Exchange/365, and is available in all Next Gen Plans (Essentials, Elite & Ultimate) with Egnyte Secure & Govern. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

  • For complete list of prerequisites and configuration steps refer to this article.

  • Email Capture feature is not supported on Egnyte for Outlook Classic Add-In Integration.

Configuration Steps

Use the Egnyte M365 app in Outlook to create folder mappings and sync Outlook folders with Egnyte Project Folders.

  • Open Outlook Add-in and go to the Folder connections
  • To create a mapping, users can also use the link in the notification they receive when an Admin enables Email Capture on their domain.
  • In the Folder Connections panel, review recommended connections and click on Approve connections to approve them and create mappings.
  • Users can also create new mappings. Select Not connected from the dropdown, choose the Outlook folder to map, and click the Pencil icon on the right to edit it.
  • Select the Egnyte Project Folder to map to the selected Outlook folder.
  • Project Folders marked as Bookmarks will appear on the top of the list.
  • Click on Change to confirm
  • Egnyte Project Folder will be connected to the Outlook folder. Any email moved to this Outlook folder will be automatically saved to the corresponding Egnyte Project Folder. Users can just drag and drop them. The new mapping will appear in the All and Connected tabs.
Remove Connection
  • To remove a mapping, click the bin icon.
  • Confirm the deletion in the dialog that appears.
Edit Connection
  • Use the pencil icon to change connected folders
  • Select target Project folder from the list
  • Click on Change to Confirm

Manually Save an Email to Egnyte

Use the Egnyte M365 in Outlook to file a specific email and its attachments at any time. Refer here for details.

  • Open the Egnyte Add-in: In Outlook, select the email to save. Click the Egnyte icon in the top ribbon to open the side panel.
  • Select content to save: In the Egnyte side panel, check the box for Select all to file the email and all attachments, or check individual items to file selectively. By default, toggle to save all emails in the thread is on but users can turn off this setting. Choose a destination by clicking on the Select location button at the bottom of the panel.
  • Navigate to folder: Browse Egnyte folders using the Projects, All, or Bookmarks tabs. Select the specific project folder where the email should be stored. Click the Save to Egnyte button.
  • Search within the folder picker searches across all folders, regardless of which tab is currently selected. Tab-specific search filtering is not yet available.
  • Verify: Once the upload is complete, a View in Egnyte link will appear. Click it to open the Egnyte Web UI and confirm the file’s location.

Preview for Saved Emails and Attachments

In the Egnyte web interface, users can preview saved emails and attachments.

  • Click any file to open the preview. To see all emails and attachments in a thread, click the thread icon on the left.
  • The thread panel shows all emails and attachments in a thread. Click any file to open it in preview and quickly review the whole thread.

Expected Behavior

File Storage and Folder Structure

Filed emails are saved as .eml files and stored within the following folder structure inside the target project:

Emails / YYYY / YYYY-MM (Month Name)

Example: Emails / 2026 / 2026-03 (March)

  • Monthly folders are used, there are no day-level subfolders
  • Folder names display the year first for chronological ordering across multiple years
  • Email attachments are stored separately in the same monthly folder alongside the .eml file
Visual Indicators in Outlook

Once an email has been automatically filed to Egnyte, it will be labelled with the Egnyte category in Outlook. This provides a visual indicator that the email has been successfully filed, reducing the likelihood of duplicate filings. Visual indicators are visible only for emails filed with automated configuration.

Email Metadata

Each filed .eml file is tagged with the following metadata in Egnyte:

Metadata Field

Description

From

Sender email address

Date sent

Date the email was sent by the sender

Date received

Date the email was received

Email subject

Subject line of the email

Email ID

Unique ID of the email in the recipient’s inbox

Internet Message ID

Universal message ID (same across all recipients’ inboxes)

Conversation ID

Unique thread identifier

CC

Comma-separated list of CC recipients

Number of attachments

Total count of attachments on the email

Attachment name

Empty for .eml files; file name for each attachment

Bcc metadata is only captured in the Automated Capture flow. It is not available when filing manually via the add-in.

Emails With No Subject

Emails without a subject line are saved with the naming convention: YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS (No subject) <hash>.eml

Attachments in Filed Emails

When an email is filed, its attachments are extracted and saved as separate files in the same monthly folder. The .eml file itself will contain a text notice indicating that the attachment was removed and filed separately. This notice is visible in standard desktop email clients (For example: Outlook, Thunderbird).

The Egnyte file preview may not render this attachment-removed notice. Open the .eml in a desktop email client to see the full message with the notice.

How to Report Microsoft Co-Editing Issues

The Egnyte Microsoft co-editing feature allows Egnyte users to collaborate on Microsoft 365 files with other users through Egnyte’s Microsoft 365 integrations. As the feature continues to improve, users may encounter some issues with the co-editing feature. This guide provided instructions for end users to effectively report issues to Egnyte and Microsoft Support.

Send Feedback to Microsoft

How to Get the Direct URL with File ID

Contact Egnyte Support

Send Debug Logs from Egnyte Desktop App

When an issue occurs during a co-editing session, users must send feedback to Microsoft within 3 to 4 days since the occurrence. It is important to report the issue from the same Microsoft co-editing session immediately when the issue occurred. If the session was closed, we recommend opening a new session for the affected file and immediately send feedback to Microsoft.

For example, if a co-editing issue occurred during a session via Microsoft 365 for the web, the Microsoft feedback should be submitted from the same Microsoft 365 for the web session. Follow the steps below on how to send the necessary information to properly report the issue.

Send Feedback to Microsoft

For better success in efficiently addressing an issue, it is recommended to send feedback to Microsoft within 3 to 4 days of when the issue occurred. Follow the steps below to send feedback:

  • During the co-edit session, click Help
  • Select Feedback
  • Click on Report a problem
  • In the What did you dislike? box, copy and paste the provided template, and fill in the necessary information:
    • ‘#EgnyteM365Integration’
    • Egnyte domain name:
    • A brief description of the issue:
    • Approximate timestamp and date of the issue:
    • (for example, 5/3/26 approximately 12pm PST):
    • Direct URL from Egnyte with file ID (see section below):
  • Add any error message screenshots
  • Select the option Yes, you may contact me
  • Click Submit and take a screenshot of the submission. If an Egnyte Support ticket was already submitted for the same issue, update the respective ticket after the feedback was sent to Microsoft, and include a screenshot of the submission to Egnyte Support.

How to Get the Direct URL with File ID

To find the Direct URL for the respective application, perform the following steps:

For Microsoft 365 for the web Co-editing:
  • In the Web UI, navigate to the folder where the file is hosted in,
  • Right-click the affected file
  • Select Copy direct URL
  • Paste the link in the What did you dislike? Box (section above)
For Desktop Co-Editing on Windows:
  • Open File Explorer
  • Navigate the folder where the file is hosted in via the associated mapped drive
  • Right-click the affected file
  • Click Share
  • Pick Copy direct link and save it for next step.
  • Paste the link in the What did you dislike? Box (section above)
For Desktop Co-Editing on Mac:
  • Open Finder
  • Navigate the folder where the file is hosted in via the associated mapped drive
  • Right-click the affected file
  • Click on Share: Copy Direct Link and save it for next step.
  • Paste the link in the What did you dislike? Box (section above)

Contact Egnyte Support

In addition to reporting this issue to Microsoft Support, also submit a case with Egnyte Support or send an email to support@egnyte.com. Include the following information in the ticket submission:

  • Egnyte Domain:
  • A brief description of the issue:
  • Approximate timestamp and date of the issue (for example, 5/3/26 approximately 12pm PST):
  • Direct URL from Egnyte and File ID (see section above):
  • Full file path(s) where the issue occurred (.pptx):
  • Affected username(s) or email addresses of the users:
  • Any additional resources and information such as screenshots or recordings related to the issue
  • Screenshot of the feedback submission to Microsoft If an Egnyte Support ticket was already submitted, provide the same information to the existing ticket.

Send Debug Logs from Egnyte Desktop App

In addition to submitting feedback and an Egnyte Support ticket, users can also submit logs for co-editing issues that occur when using the Desktop App using instructions from How-to-Contact-Egnyte-Support-from-Egnyte-Products.

Importing Credentials from Desktop App for Microsoft Co-Editing

Overview

Egnyte has made it easier to connect Microsoft Office Applications to an Egnyte domain. In order to use our Microsoft Desktop Co-Editing feature, connect Microsoft Office Apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) to an Egnyte domain. With this new feature, it is possible to import the domains that are connected to Egnyte Desktop App to Microsoft. This is also available for multiple domains. Once connected, a co-editing session can be launched from Egnyte’s WebUI, Egnyte’s Desktop App, or the Microsoft Office Application.

Requirements

Office Subscription
  • Users require a Microsoft 365 Business Standard license or above
  • OR
  • Enterprise Office 365 E3 subscription or above
  • Microsoft license must allow for Office Desktop Apps and they should be downloaded onto a user’s machine
  • Perpetual licenses are not supported (Office 2016, Office 2019, etc.)
  • Microsoft GCC licenses are not supported
Egnyte Desktop App
  • Egnyte Desktop App for Windows v3.15.4 or newer
  • Egnyte Desktop App for Mac Core v0.10.3 or newer

Enablement

  • Click on Open in any Microsoft Office application.
  • Select Add a Place.
  • Choose Egnyte.
  • This will launch a screen that will allow to either manually add a domain or Import the credentials from Desktop App.
  • Click Allow Access to provide the Microsoft Application access to Egnyte
  • This will complete the task and import all the credentials from the Egnyte Desktop App to Microsoft

Troubleshooting

  • Install or upgrade to ensure that Desktop App has this capability based on the requirements
  • Egnyte Desktop App for Mac is not supported
  • Make sure that at least one domain is connected to Desktop App in order to import credentials

Microsoft 365 FAQs

Does Microsoft 365 Integration Work with Egnyte Desktop Applications?

Yes, Microsoft 365 integration works with the Egnyte Desktop App.

When Does a File Lock in Microsoft 365 for the Web Integration?

When a file is opened through Microsoft 365 for the Web integration, it is locked to other applications and shows a collaboration icon in the Web UI that represents an active coediting session. If other users open the same file through the Microsoft 365 for the web integration, they will still be able to open the file so they can collaborate and co-author it together.

What Happens if a User is Editing in Microsoft 365 for the Web and Then Another User Tries to Update in Desktop App?

When a user edits using Microsoft 365 for the Web, the file will be locked, and no other application (besides another Microsoft 365 for the web session) will be able to save as long as that file is open.

Are Microsoft 365 for the Web Files Cached by Microsoft?

Yes. Files opened through the Microsoft 365 for the web integration are cached by Microsoft. Users are typically routed to the Microsoft 365 for the web data center closest to their current geographic location. However, this routing is not guaranteed, and users may be routed to any global data center for a variety of reasons.

What are Some of the Ways to Report Microsoft Co-Editing Issues?

Users may encounter some issues with the co-editing feature as it continues to improve. Refer here to report issues to Egnyte and Microsoft Support.

Microsoft Co-Editing Sharepoint Embedded (SPE) Integration

Egnyte’s SharePoint Embedded (SPE) Co-Editing integration addresses key limitations in the current Cloud Storage Partner Program (CSPP+) solution by providing support for critical Microsoft features like @mentions and Sensitivity Labeling.

It has been designed to meet growing customer demands and ensure a consistent and secure co-editing experience across Office Online and Office Desktop, while maintaining essential functionality such as Excel sheet linking.

The feature is accessible through Egnyte’s Web UI, Desktop App, and Mobile.

Please fill this form to request the enablement of the integration on the domain.

Initial Setup on a New Egnyte Domain

  • Navigate to Apps & Integrations and search for Microsoft Office Desktop and Online integration. This integration is not compatible with previous versions of Microsoft Office.
  • In order for the Microsoft Office Desktop and Online tile to appear, users must make sure both Microsoft Office Online tile and Microsoft Office Desktop and Mobile tile are set to Not enabled for domain.
  • Hover over on the app tile and click on Enable Integration.
  • Click on Start Configuration to begin the configuration.
  • Click on Continue to Egnyte Sign in in the setup wizard.
  • Continue to login as an Admin User on Egnyte and Allow Access.
  • Log in as Microsoft Admin to configure Microsoft tenant which will be used by this integration. Click on Continue to Microsoft Sign In.
  • Click on Grant permissions to confirm app level permission required by Microsoft in order to finish tenant configuration.
  • Accept Microsoft permissions for Egnyte access to SharePoint container.
  • On the Container Creation step, review the Container location. By default, the container is created in the Microsoft tenant’s default location, which is shown on screen (for example, United States (NAM)). If the tenant has Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo enabled and a container in a different region if needed, select Use a different location than the tenant’s default and choose a location from the dropdown. Only locations enabled on the tenant are listed. Then click Create Sharepoint Container
  • Container Creation Step with the Default Location
  • Choosing a Different Location from the Tenant’s Enabled Geos
  • The container location cannot be changed after the container is created. To use a different location the admin must choose Reset Configuration and run the setup again, which creates a new container; files already in the previous container are not moved and links to them stop working. Each Egnyte domain has exactly one container, so organizations that need content in more than one region must configure the integration on a separate Egnyte domain per region. If the Container location section is not visible, the Microsoft tenant does not have Multi-Geo enabled and the container is created in the tenant’s default location. Admins can verify a container’s location in the SharePoint Admin Center under SharePoint Embedded → Active containers → General.
  • Choose the Security Preferences. Files that are in the SharePoint container are controlled by settings on SharePoint and not by Egnyte permissions. The user can update the settings by clicking Go to SharePoint Button, otherwise users can go with the standard settings that they have already configured in SharePoint.
  • If the user chooses to Go to SharePoint and update their settings it can be found under Polices->Sharing
  • Review the summary and click on Enable Integration to complete the setup. To make changes, click on Reset Configuration and restart the configuration process.
  • If the user chooses Reset Configuration, they need to confirm by clicking on Reset Configuration in the confirmation pop-up.
  • If the configuration is reset, the users need to redo the configuration from step 2 onwards.
  • Select the group of users for whom the integration needs to be enabled and click on Save.

  • Click on Edit Configuration and repeat the steps as mentioned in the initial setup process.
Re-Running the Setup
  • Changing the Microsoft admin account that authenticates the integration is safe and keeps the existing container, as long as the new account is also a Global Admin. It can be done during business hours, though off-hours is recommended.
  • Use a dedicated service account. The Microsoft account used during setup is the owner of files in the container and receives comment and @mention notifications for every file. Re-running setup with a service account directs those notifications away from a personal mailbox.

Co-Edit a Document

To co-edit a document, select the document and click on Open with -> Select the appropriate co-editing Microsoft Office Desktop or Co-editing Microsoft Office Online app from the Context menu. Alternatively, hover over the file and select the co-editing app.

The document will then open in the corresponding Office Desktop or Online app (in the example above - Word Online or Word Desktop).

A File is ready for editing confirmation page is shown while the file is prepared in the SharePoint container; the document then opens in the corresponding Office Desktop or Online app. Opening a file for the first time can take longer than subsequent opens.

When other user(s) open the same document, they will be able to co-edit in real-time. Even if a file is locked via co-editing, other users opening the file in Office Online or Desktop will be able to join the ongoing co-authoring session. There is no option to remove a participant from an active co-authoring session from Egnyte.

Back to Top…

Sharing and Permissions from Microsoft Office Apps

When a file is opened for co-editing, it is copied into the SharePoint Embedded container in the Microsoft tenant, and it remains in the container after the session ends, so that @mention links and comments continue to work. While a file is in the container, it follows SharePoint’s rules:

  • Sharing from within Office apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) uses the tenant’s SharePoint sharing settings and does not apply Egnyte permissions. Permissions granted this way are not reflected in Egnyte. The Share button in Office cannot be hidden for container files only.
  • Permission changes made in Egnyte are synchronized to the container, but a user already in an active session keeps access until the session ends. Share files using Egnyte share links rather than the Share button in Office, and review the SharePoint tenant sharing policy (Policies → Sharing) before enabling the integration for a wide user group.
Back to Top…

Migrating from CSPP+ to SPE Co-Editing

  • CSPP+ and SPE Co-Editing cannot interact with each other. A file must not be in a CSPP+ co-editing session before it is launched with SPE Co-editing.
  • It is recommended that all users remove Egnyte Add-a-Place from all their Microsoft Office Applications before starting with SPE co-editing.
Back to Top…

Migrating from Microsoft Office (Legacy) to SPE Co-editing

  • Schedule the switch during non-business hours to avoid any disruption to active users.
  • Data & Comments: All files, document versions, and existing comments remain stored securely in Egnyte and will persist through the transition.
  • Legacy Links & Notifications: Once the switch is made, any SharePoint links shared via the old legacy integration (including links in old email notifications) will no longer be valid. Users will need to generate new links via the SPE integration.
  • Disable Legacy Tile: Navigate to the Apps & Integrations page in your admin settings and turn off the Microsoft Office (Legacy) tile.
  • Enable New Tile: On the same page, turn on the Microsoft Office Online and Desktop tile and file through the steps.
Back to Top…

Limitations and Best Practices

File Size
  • Max file size for Word or Excel Online is 100 MB
  • Max file size for Word or Excel on Desktop is 300 MB
  • Max file size for PowerPoint Online and Desktop is 2 GB
File Names (Office Desktop on Windows)
  • Office Desktop on Windows is subject to the Windows 260-character path limit. The container path consumes a fixed portion, leaving approximately 105–116 characters for the file name including extension (exact value = 260 − 125 − length of the tenant.sharepoint.com host name). Files with longer names will not open in Office Desktop but can be co-edited in Office Online. The Egnyte folder path does not count towards this limit, files are stored flat in the container. Enabling long paths in Windows does not remove this limit.
Synchronization and Sessions
  • Files are synced with Egnyte every 3 minutes; during this time, the preview may be outdated and downloading a file will download the older version.
  • A user cannot be removed from an active co-authoring session from Egnyte; an Egnyte lock does not end the SharePoint session.
  • Files remain in the SharePoint Embedded container after co-editing and are not automatically removed.
Data Location
  • The container location is fixed when the container is created; choosing a non-default location requires Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo on the tenant.
  • Only one container is created per Egnyte domain. Content cannot be moved between containers.
Notifications and Sharing
  • The Microsoft account used for setup receives comment or @mention notifications for files in the container. Use a service account to avoid this on a personal mailbox.
  • Sharing from Office applications follows SharePoint settings, not Egnyte permissions.
Renaming
  • Rename files from Egnyte, not from within Office Desktop. Renaming a file from Office Desktop (for example, File → Rename in Excel) while it is open for co-editing breaks the link between the file in Egnyte and its copy in the container which can cause lost updates. If this happens:
    • Open the file with Co-editing Microsoft Office Online, choose Editing → Open in Desktop
    • Rename it back to its previous name
    • Rename from Egnyte if a new name is needed
  • Microsoft is updating Office Desktop to block rename during co-editing.
Back to Top…

Microsoft Co-Editing with External Users

Egnyte simplifies teamwork by allowing co-editing Microsoft 365 files with users outside of the organization. This article describes Egnyte’s file sharing with co-editing and collaboration features with external users and partners. Refer to the Sharing Co-Editable Links Quick-Tip Video for details.

Share Co-Editable Links with External Users using Egnyte WebUI

Often, Egnyte users need to collaborate with people outside of their organization who don’t have Egnyte accounts. Sharing co-editable links with them makes it easy for such users to quickly access and co-edit files using Microsoft 365 for the Web. Accessing the co-editable links does not require any licensing as it opens via this integration.

Prerequisites
  • Co-Editable links are only supported for Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files.
  • Microsoft 365 for the Web integration must be enabled for the user sharing the links.
Create and Share Co-Editable Links
  • Hover over on the three-dots menu on the file name or click the checkbox before the file name and click Share.
  • Click on People you choose to choose specific recipients of the link.
  • Click on Co-editing to allow co-editing. Additionally, the users can choose to allow downloads, notify when the link is clicked, include file name in links, and show the most recent version of the file to the recipients. Click on Email link.
  • Enter the email addresses of the recipient(s). Users can also type in an optional message and choose to receive a copy of the email to themselves.
  • Click Send.
  • The external user(s) will receive an email notification on the given email address with a link to co-edit the file. Administrators can configure the type of co-editable links allowed for sharing. Click here to know more about these settings.

Creating a co-editable link that can be accessed by ‘Anyone’ will allow anonymous users to edit the file. Consider using ‘Specific recipients’ option to share the co-editable links. Click here to learn more about sharing links with specific recipients.

Co-Edit using Microsoft 365 Desktop

In certain instances, specific Microsoft features are exclusively available in the desktop versions of Microsoft 365 apps. For example, Microsoft Word Desktop allows users to insert a cover page, create bibliographies, and manage citations, among other functionalities not offered in the web version. In such cases, it is advisable to enable users to co-edit the file using Microsoft 365 Desktop Apps.

MS Desktop Licensing Requirements
  • A business or enterprise license is required to open a file in Microsoft 365 Desktop.
    • Users require a Microsoft 365 Business Standard license or above.
    • OR
    • Enterprise 365 E3 subscription or above.
    • Microsoft license must allow for Microsoft 365 Desktop Apps and they should be downloaded onto a user’s machine. -Perpetual licenses are not supported such as Office 2016 and Office 2019.

-Microsoft GCC licenses are not supported.

The following steps will allow the Standard Users that have the correct MS licenses to co-edit files on Microsoft 365 Desktop applications.

  • Create a Standard User account for an external user.
  • Manage file/folder permissions for the Standard User ensuring they can edit the shared file.
  • To ensure co-editing works seamlessly on the Microsoft 365 App, the Standard User will need to setup Egnyte on the Microsoft 365 App only once by following these steps:
    • Click Open in the Microsoft App.
    • Select Add a Place.
    • Choose Egnyte and click Add Manually.
    • Enter the domain name and click Next.
    • Enter the credentials and click Continue.
    • Click Allow Access to authenticate and provide access to the Egnyte domain.
    • Once connected to the Microsoft Apps, Click Open and select the file to open. Click here to learn more about co-edit using the Microsoft 365 Desktop.

Limitations

  • Opening a co-editable link will open the file in Microsoft 365 for the web for external users. Microsoft 365 for the web has fewer features than Microsoft 365 for Desktop, and some formatting may not show up correctly when users are collaborating using different versions of Microsoft 365. Egnyte and our integration with Microsoft 365 do not cause such formatting changes, and they occur natively in Microsoft when users utilize different versions of Microsoft 365. If such changes are undesirable, we recommend that all users co-edit using either Microsoft 365 for the web or Desktop, but not both. translate well between the file versions. These are issues as a result of Microsoft limitations.
  • When an Egnyte user shares a co-editable link, any edits by the external user are recorded in the audit logs as changes made by the original Egnyte user. This behavior also occurs when users initiate a co-editing session directly from Microsoft products (such as when initiating an external co-editing session from Sharepoint), and it is not a function of the Egnyte integration.

Configure Co-Editing for Microsoft 365 Desktop

Step-By-Step Guide

Creating Enterprise Applications For Provisioning
  • Log in to the Azure Portal.
  • Go to Enterprise Applications in the Microsoft Entra ID section.
  • Find Egnyte in Search Application input.
  • If the user configured an application before June 2025, the previous guidance directed them to create a custom application. While those existing custom applications will continue to function, we now recommend using an official Egnyte app for all new configurations.
  • (Optional) Choose the name of the App so it can be easily identified.
  • Click on the newly created app, select Provisioning Section, and click the Get started button.
  • Set provisioning mode to Automatic.
  • Provide the tenant URL by changing <domain> to the Egnyte domain:
    • https://<domain>.egnyte.com/pubapi/scim/v2/azure-connector
    • https://<domain>.egnytegov.com/pubapi/scim/v2/azure-connector (for EgnyteGov domains)
    • This URL can not be used with other identity providers
  • Go to scim-20.egnyte.com or scim-20.egnytegov.com (for EgnyteGov customers) to generate a Secret Token for the domain. It is essential to log in with the domain admin credentials (a service account is recommended).
  • Disclaimer: Even though this portal was initially created for the Okta identity provider, it can be used to generate a token for Azure.
  • Test the connection, and hit the Save button (users can also add email for notifications).
Mapping Attributes

Here we set up mappings between Microsoft Entra ID object attributes and Egnyte object attributes. Please note that it would be possible to edit the mappings only when the connection is successfully tested and the user has saved the basic configuration.

Group Mappings

Go to the application in Azure -> Provisioning -> Edit provisioning. Click on Mappings and then Provision Azure Active Directory Groups.

Set Mappings in the Following Way:

  • Group provisioning may require a different Azure plan.

  • objectID attribute is optional.

displayName allowed characters:

  • Alphanumeric characters: Letters (A-Z, a-z) and numbers (0-9)

  • Hyphen: -

  • Underscore: _

  • Period: .

  • Spaces: Group names can contain spaces in between words.

User Mappings

Go to the application in Azure -> Provisioning -> Edit provisioning. Click on Mappings and then Provision Azure Active Directory Users.

Additional Comments to Mappings

There are many ways to customize those mappings (depending on the setup). Azure allows for a:

  • direct mapping (Azure attribute is sent to Egnyte as is)
  • constant mapping (there is an arbitrary constant value set, independent from Entra ID attributes)
  • expression mapping. The last one allows for the most flexibility. Find more about expressions in this Microsoft article Keep in mind that Admins get to choose when those attributes should get updated while editing those mappings. Always, Upon Object Creation, or Only when there are multiple values for one attribute. This is important for attributes that should not change after being created once.

Provisioning

Adding Users and Groups to the Scope

Once the mapping is configured and saved, add users and groups to the scope by going to the application in Azure and then to Users and groups. Keep in mind that only explicitly added groups will be created in Egnyte. Nested groups will be ignored. Users in nested groups will also be ignored.

Narrowing the Scope

The scope can be narrowed down. For example, there are groups created in Egnyte but certain users like admins need to be excluded from being provisioned.

To narrow down the scope, follow these steps:

  • Go back to user attribute mappings
  • Open Source Object Scope
  • Here one can create filters based on attributes to include/exclude certain users or user sets. For example, One does not want to manage the primary admin user via SCIM, but it should stay in the provisioned group in Azure. Create a filter like this: userPrincipalName NOT EQUALS <UPN for the admin account>
Test or Troubleshoot Provisioning

Go to the Application -> Provisioning -> Provisioning on demand. Try to provision some users. Check in Egnyte if every attribute maps correctly. Unfortunately, provisioning on demand is not available for groups.

Enabling Provisioning

If tests passed, users can enable provisioning by going to the Application -> Provisioning -> Edit provisioning and enable provisioning:

Provisioning is an automated process from Azure’s side, which runs every 40 minutes, and there is no control over this period. Depending on the number of users, the initial sync should take only a few minutes, but it can take several hours sometimes.

Deactivating and Deleting Users

Users will be deactivated in Egnyte when:

  • They are removed from the application scope

  • They are soft deleted in Microsoft Entra ID Users will be deleted in Egnyte when:

  • They are permanently deleted in Microsoft Entra ID (by default 30 days after soft delete) The change will take effect after the first successful provision. We can manually trigger the change by running provisioning on-demand.

Deleting Groups and Impact on Users

Groups will be deleted in Egnyte when:

  • They are removed from the application scope

  • They are deleted in Microsoft Entra ID Impact on Users when a Group is Deleted

  • There is no impact on the users if a group is deleted and the user is part of another group OR has been separately provisioned individually. They will be deactivated if the only provisioning source was the deleted group; however, they won’t be deleted.

Limitations

  • Currently usage of any custom attributes is not possible upon user creation. However it is possible to send custom attributes with PATCH.
  • There are user account changes that should be performed manually, though. The user type is one of them. However, using dynamic groups in Azure or applying a custom attribute to users may allow for easy user type control.
  • Keep in mind that groups do not get owners. There are ways to use expressions or Microsoft Entra ID custom attributes, but that requires a deep dive.
  • Keep in mind that Microsoft ID and on-prem AD allow using custom attributes. Those can be mapped to Egnyte just as easily. For example, user type cannot be obtained by group affiliation but can be added as a custom attribute via PowerShell script. Then, such an attribute can be mapped to Egnyte as userType, allowing the option to control user type from within AD and without the need to log into Egnyte at all.
  • Service accounts are recommended for the token generation, as deactivating or deleting the account may render the SCIM integration incapacitated.
  • The sync is one way. No changes to Egnyte will be reflected in Azure.
  • Microsoft Entra ID SCIM provisioning does not support setting newly created users into a custom role.

Microsoft Power BI Data Connector

Microsoft Power BI helps organizations empower everyone to make every decision based on data. Egnyte for Power BI Data Connector enables power users to connect and get easy access to Egnyte data. They can query, shape, and select data from multiple files to create dashboards and reports in Power BI Desktop.

As the user publishes these reports to Power BI Service, they will be able to auto-refresh data through Microsoft Gateway and can collaborate with the other users so they can access the latest data.
