Additional factors and Power BI Knowledgebase

Initial Setup

Prerequisites
  • Microsoft Power BI Pro or Premium license for both admins and users to access the content of the report
  • Standard on-premises gateway is recommended to collaborate with other users. Refreshing doesn’t work if the computer installed with the standard gateway is offline.

Computer Setup

  • If using Personal gateway - Create a “[My Documents]BI DesktopConnectors” directory AND/OR
  • For Standard gateway - Create a “BI DesktopConnectors” directory.
  • Get EgnyteConnectorProduction.pqx file here and place it in the “Custom Connectors” directory above.
  • Add the thumbprint: 9272CAFD79BD0D84DEF40D0003B17C2A41C4387D. Refer MSFT Documentation for additional information.
  • Close all instances of Power BI and restart Power BI Desktop. If Egnyte connector in the Power BI is not visible, try putting the connector file in both locations mentioned above in step 1 and step 2, and try again.

Power BI Gateway Setup (For refreshing data)

An on-premises data gateway (standard gateway) is a software that the user installs in an on-premises network. The gateway facilitates access to data in that network. The user can install a gateway either in personal mode, which applies to Power BI only, or in standard mode. Recommended mode is the standard mode.

  • Install On-premise (Standard) and Personal gateway and follow the process and Microsoft wizard.
  • Login using the admin credentials and Configure and name the Gateway Connection (The user installing the gateway must be the admin of the gateway)
  • Add gateway admins who can also manage and administer other network requirements.
  • Use the gateway to refresh an on-premises data source.
  • Troubleshoot the gateway in case of errors, and make sure it is online. On a single computer, the user can run a single instance of the personal and standard gateway.

Power BI Desktop (For Creating reports)

  • Install Power BI Desktop if not installed already.
  • Login with the same Microsoft credentials as Power BI Pro or Premium license.
  • Enable “(Not Recommended) Allow any extension to load without validation or warning” under File -> Options -> Settings -> Data Extension and Click Get Data.
  • Select the Egnyte connector from the list.
  • Clicking Connect will open a dialog and ask the user to enter their Egnyte domain. Use Domain in the form here - “https://<YOURDOMAIN>.egnyte.com” and click OK.
  • Follow the Sign-in process and use the Egnyte credentials to complete the sign-in process.
  • Once signed in, the user will see the navigator table with their Egnyte files as below. They can select 1 or more files (supported formats are XLS, XLSX, CSV, and Text files).
  • Creating visualizations is not part of the integration currently, integrate the data as per the needs of the organization and create reports.
  • Save the report or dashboard and create publish.

Power BI Service (for Collaboration)

  • Open Power BI Service in the browser as shown in the step above. Alternatively, access this report via browser, using the same account login (as used in the desktop app) to access the published data.
  • Ensure the Gateway is running and is online and connected.
  • On the machine where the gateway is running, enter the gateway in Windows search.
  • Select the On-premises data gateway app
  • Log in with Microsoft credentials as used above.
  • Go to Connectors - and Ensure Egnyte is therein the dropdown list.
  • Select Egnyte from the list
  • Ensure that in the folder settings, you have EgnyteConnectorProduction.pqx file if using Personal Gateway OR, if using Standard Gateway.
  • Go to the dataset on the left-hand side, and click on scheduled refresh. The example uses “Life Expectancy” report, which is on the left-hand side, and “scheduled refresh” for illustration.
  • Configure. If using a Personal gateway, select that checkbox and Apply.
  • If using Standard Gateway - ensure selecting “data sources” and select the dataset to refresh for the report or dashboards. See the next 3 screens.
    • Configure data source setting, ensure the user has valid credentials, and “connection is successful”.
    • Ensure the above dataset is connected to the standard gateway in use as below.
    • Ensure there is no error in the data source credentials section.
  • Configure to initiate auto-refresh. Note. Auto-refresh frequency depends on the type of Power BI license from Microsoft - Pro or Premium.
  • User can select Refresh History from the top of the screen.
  • Refresh will not succeed if the computer with the personal gateway is offline. Additionally, when using a standard gateway, refresh will fail if the server is offline. Hence if a refresh fails, check the status of the gateway to troubleshoot.
  • On successful configuration, the gateway will appear as shown below.
    • Navigate to Settings on the Gateway.
    • Ensure that the following fields are checked.

Remove Authentication for the Egnyte Domain

Go under Power BI Desktop: File | Options, and settings | Data Source Settings | Clear permissions.

Additional factors and Power BI Knowledgebase

Per Microsoft documentation, the user can install up to two gateways on a single computer: one running in personal mode and the other running in standard mode. They can’t have more than one gateway running in the same mode on the same computer.

Personal Gateway:

Personal Gateway allows one user to connect to sources and can’t be shared with others. An on-premises data gateway (personal mode) can be used only with Power BI.

This gateway is well-suited in scenarios where the organization may have one admin user responsible for creating reports. The admin user in this case would not be required to share any data sources with the others. Standard Gateway: Standard Gateway allows multiple users to connect to multiple on-premises data sources. The user can use an on-premises data gateway with all supported services, with a single gateway installation.

This gateway is well-suited to complex scenarios, such as an organization with multiple admins responsible for creation of reports. All these admins will be required to have access to multiple data sources.

  • Authentication to PowerBI Desktop via Chrome is currently not supported.

  • The user can use a Windows server or Windows machine that works all the time so that gateway is always online.

  • During tests, if multiple developers are working on the same MS accounts, it is essential to be sure whose personal gateway is used. For example, if a developer creates a new version of the connector but it points to a different computer with a different version of the connector, then there will be connection error. Ensure that the gateway is pointing to their own machine.

  • A similar issue is with a standard connector. If a developer wants to use it with their source, ensure that it is using the same connector version. It is recommended to use the right naming conventions in settings and ensure it is online.

  • If the VM machine is in use, the location of the .pqx file may be different. It depends on the setup to locate and load the file for a user on the Power BI Desktop.

Limitations

  • Enabling the use of default browser is currently not supported. Power BI must use the built-in browser.

Multi-Domain Co-Editing for Desktop

Overview

Egnyte offers the capability to set up Multi-Domain Co-Editing on Desktop. Users can add multiple domains at the time of setting up Microsoft 365 applications. Once the setup is complete, users can open files from any of the added domains using either the Egnyte Desktop App or the Web UI in co-editing mode. During co-editing, the file automatically saves back to that same domain.

Standard Enablement

Users can set up multi-domain co-editing by importing all associated credentials that are connected in a respective Egnyte Desktop App to their Microsoft 365 application. This is accessible when the user tries to connect to Egnyte from Microsoft.

  • Choose Import to start the process.
  • More information about importing credentials can be found here.
  • Select the primary domain to be displayed in the MS apps from the list of imported domains and click Next
  • Click on Allow Access to provide authorization
  • Multiple domains will be successfully added.

Manual Enablement

If the end users do not have Desktop App and would like to configure their primary domain, users will still be able to manually enable multi-domain.

For this enablement, admins will need to fill out the provided form by entering their Egnyte domains to enable this feature.

​​​​For the optimal user experience, Egnyte recommends importing credentials via the ​​Desktop App​​. Manual enablement is reserved for rare scenarios where users require multi-domain co-editing but are restricted from using the Desktop App, such as Standard Users or those specifically blocked by the admins.​​​​​

Once whitelisted, users will need to re-authenticate to those domains through the Microsoft Application by signing out and signing back into Egnyte. This only needs to be done once for Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, or Word. Afterwards, select Add Manually.

After adding the first domain, there will be a confirmation for the successful addition, and users can continue to add other domains.

To re-setup this integration and add more domains in the future, sign out of Egnyte from the Microsoft apps.

Launching Co-Editing Sessions from Different Domains

Now that the Microsoft Application has all the domains linked in the configuration, users can initiate a co-editing session on desktop using those domains from either the Web UI or the Desktop App.

The Primary Domain in Microsoft

The first domain that a user signs in to will be their primary domain. That means these actions in Microsoft listed below are only available for the primary domain. To re-setup the primary domain, log out from Egnyte on the Microsoft app and sign in first with the domain that will be the primary domain. The primary domain can do the following:

  • Traverse the Domain in Microsoft Apps and Open
  • Access the Recent
  • Save new files to in the Cloud

Desktop Applications

In order to launch a co-editing from the Desktop App, users will need to be on the latest version of the Desktop App.

Limitations

  • Only one device can be logged into multi-domain at a time (If users have multiple device setups for co-editing signing into one domain, then it will invalidate the token of the other device)
  • Desktop App for Mac (Legacy) is not supported

Opening Microsoft 365 Files in Egnyte Mobile Apps

This article explains how to open Microsoft 365 files directly from the Egnyte mobile app.

Opening Microsoft 365 Files From Egnyte iOS Mobile App

Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) files can be opened for viewing only from the Egnyte iOS app in the following ways:

  • Direct Preview in Egnyte: Tap on the file in the listing view to open it in the Egnyte app’s built-in preview.

  • Open with Another App: From the file preview screen, tap the Share button and select an app (example: Microsoft 365) to open the document. This will allow viewing only, not editing. Microsoft 365 documents can also be opened for editing and co-editing (provided that the user has an active Microsoft 365 license in place and the co-editing feature is enabled by Egnyte admin for the domain) in the following ways:

  • By clicking on the 3-dot menu in the listing view and selecting the Co-edit in Microsoft Word/Excel/Power Point option.

  • By tapping on the Co-edit button on the document preview screen. Selecting the Co-edit option redirects the user to the relevant Microsoft 365 App where the document can be edited.

  • Once editing is complete, the Done button can be tapped to exit the editing mode.

  • To return to Egnyte, the Back to Egnyte button should be selected. Detailed requirements and instructions related to co-editing of Microsoft 365 documents via the Egnyte mobile apps are available here.

Opening Microsoft 365 Files From Egnyte Android Mobile App

Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Power Point) files can be opened from the Egnyte Android app for viewing in the following ways:

  • Direct Preview in Egnyte: Tap on the file in the listing view to open it in the Egnyte app’s built-in preview.

  • Open with Another App: From the file preview screen, tap the Share button and select an app (Example: Microsoft 365) to open the document. Microsoft 365 documents can also be opened for editing and co-editing (provided that the user has an active Microsoft 365 license in place and the co-editing feature is enabled by Egnyte admin for the domain):

  • By clicking on the 3-dot menu in the listing view and selecting the Co-edit in Microsoft Word/Excel/Power Point option

  • By tapping on the Co-edit button on the document preview screen. Selecting the Co-edit option redirects the user to the relevant Microsoft 365 App where the document can be edited.

  • Once editing is complete, the Done (Tick icon) button can be tapped to exit the editing mode. Detailed requirements and instructions related to co-editing of Microsoft 365 documents via the Egnyte mobile apps are available here.

Preview Egnyte Files Using Microsoft 365 for the Web

Microsoft 365 for the Web Preview for Egnyte gives users an elegantly integrated viewing experience for all their Office documents. This article covers how to add and use the integration, allowing you to preview supported file formats using the native 365 for the Web viewer.

Microsoft 365 license is not required to use this integration. If the customer has the Microsoft 365 subscription, check out the Microsoft 365 on the web integration to enjoy full viewing and editing functionality

Adding the Microsoft 365 for the Web Preview Integration

An admin user on the domain should enter the Egnyte App Store by clicking Apps & Integrations in the Web UI. Then, hover over the Microsoft 365 preview for the web app and click Enable Integration. Choose the best option for the organization as described below.

  • Added for groups: Choose up to 5 different groups that will have this integration enabled automatically. This is the easiest way to add an integration for some users, but not all.
  • Allowed for users: This makes the integration visible to all users on the Apps & Integrations page; but, each user must enable the integration on their own.
  • Added for all users: This is the simplest way to deploy the integration to all users in your organization. This option makes the integration instantly available for all users.

Using the Microsoft 365 Preview for the web Integration

To view files with Microsoft 365 Preview for the web, simply navigate to the Egnyte Web UI and click the Microsoft 365 file link.

After clicking the file link, the document will launch within the Egnyte Web UI using the native Microsoft 365 viewer.

Microsoft 365 Preview for the web has enhanced viewing capabilities for PowerPoint and Excel documents. For Excel, users can easily navigate, sort tables, copy text, and other simple actions without needing to open the file in edit mode.

On PowerPoint, users can navigate slides and present decks within the preview window.

Microsoft 365 Licensing Requirements

This preview-only integration does not require Microsoft 365 license to use. To edit files, users must have a valid Microsoft 365 for Business subscription. More information on Microsoft 365 for Business licensing is available here.

Protected View Message Workaround for Co-Editing with Microsoft Office Desktop

Overview

A workaround to prevent users from getting the Protected View and the blocked macros message when using co-editing via the Microsoft Office Desktop.. This workaround is only applicable to Windows users. When users open MS Office files, that were uploaded into Egnyte, using the co-editing online option, they will go into protected view and can experience the following issue:

  • Preventing autosaving and co-editing as well as it requires the user to navigate to the folder in Egnyte and save their file via Save As. Afterwards, the protected view is disabled, but this is not an ideal scenario.
  • In addition, the security risk macros have been blocked messaging can be removed as well with the same workaround.

Solution

To prevent the protected view message. The user will need to allow Egnyte in the Trusted Sites settings and add the wildcard entries in the Trusted Sites settings. The user will need to manually authorize (per machine).

  • Open the Control Panel
  • Open the Internet Options
  • In the Internet Properties window, click the Security tab.
  • Select the Trusted Sites entry and click Sites.
  • Add the following wildcard entries in the trusted sites. Be sure to uncheck the checkbox, Require server verification (https:) for all sites in this zone, for the site:
    • Desktop App drive (file://egnytedrive)
    • https://*.egnyte.com

Search Egnyte App for MS Copilot Integration

Overview

Search Egnyte app for MS Copilot integration can be used in MS Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot Web interface, users can seamlessly generate concise summaries and accurate answers from Egnyte-stored files directly within the MS Teams environment by simply writing a prompt in the Copilot tab. The prompt also displays the source files where the summaries were generated from for quick file actions such as preview and share, simplifying information retrieval and enhancing productivity.

The data stays within Egnyte’s security controls and won’t be retained outside of it during AI interactions. Additionally, the integration adheres to Egnyte’s permission model, such that a user’s AI will never have access to more data than that user is entitled to.

The Search Egnyte app for MS Copilot has reached End of Life (EOL) on November 30, 2025 and is no longer be supported by Egnyte. To ensure continued service, users should transition to the new Egnyte for M365 integration.

Benefits

  • Ask questions against shared content stored in Egnyte directly within Copilot tab.
  • Get Egnyte-stored file summaries in the Copilot tab with links to relevant documents and quick access to the source files via the Open in Egnyte action.
  • Maintain organizational security with Egnyte permission-based controls to the documents.
  • Displayed content and documents remain secure and protected within Egnyte.

Prerequisites

- Active licenses for MS Teams and MS Copilot.
- Enabled Egnyte for MS Teams integration.
- Users need to be logged in to the Egnyte domain in MS Teams.
- Users need select the Search Egnyte agent on the right side panel with listed agents
- Only for Admins who have installed the sideloaded app “Egnyte for MS Copilot”. [recommended, not required]
    - Technical Requirements to Uninstall Egnyte Integration
        - Egnyte Admin Account
        - Global Admin in Microsoft tenant
    - To Block or delete ‘Egnyte for MS Copilot’ integration go to the Microsoft Teams Admin Center. This action affects all domain users or all users in a selected group using Microsoft Teams and blocked apps can be reversed at any time.
    - Unfold the Teams apps on the sidebar and go to Manage apps.
    - Search and select Egnyte for MS Copilot app.
    - Delete the app from the details view by clicking on the Delete option.
    - Click on Delete to confirm.

Admin setup

Getting Started

Activation should be done in the Microsoft Teams Admin Center. Activation affects all domain users or all users in selected groups using Microsoft Teams.

Configure MS Teams in Microsoft Admin Center
  • To install Egnyte MS Teams application, navigate to Microsoft Teams Admin Center. Unfold the Teams apps on the sidebar and click on Manage apps.
  • Search for Search Egnyte app and check if the status is Unblocked.
  • Click on the app name to confirm the app is available to everyone or selected groups.
  • Click on Edit availability to make changes in the availability.
  • Click on Grant admin consent in the Permissions tab.
  • Provide consent in the pop-up. Click Accept.
  • The changes will then be visible.

For End User

  • Navigate to Copilot in MS Teams.

  • On the right side panel click on Get agents.

  • Search for Search Egnyte App and click on Add.

  • The user can begin interacting with the Search Egnyte app.

  • With the first attempt to use the Search Egnyte app, the user will be asked to provide consent for the access to Egnyte content.

  • The user will get the responses to their queries based on Egnyte-stored files along with the direct file references. It is possible that the user gets logged out due to inactivity and would be required to sign in again after searching for the Egnyte app. In such a scenario,

  • Search for the Egnyte App.

  • If the user is already logged in and they wish to log-in using a different account, they can click on Sign out, search for the app again and follow the steps mentioned ahead.

Securely Share Egnyte Links to Microsoft Teams

Share to Microsoft Teams allows users to integrate the power of file sharing capabilities of Egnyte into Teams. Teams brings all the team communication together in one place, is instantly searchable, and is available on multiple platforms. The integration helps streamline workflows by pushing content to where conversation happens, reducing the need to switch between applications, manual copy-pasting, and integrating smoothly with existing processes.

Multi-domain environments are fully supported by this integration. Enterprise accounts managing several environments can easily distribute content across channels from any connected domain without needing extra configuration.

Deployment options remain completely flexible. Administrators can implement this solution as a complementary feature alongside the broader Microsoft 365 setup, or deploy it independently focused solely on the sharing functionality to best match organizational requirements.

This integration also includes an AI-powered summarization feature. When sharing a file, users can choose to generate an AI summary of the document. This posts a concise overview in the Teams channel alongside the secure direct file link, allowing team members to understand the context immediately without opening the full file.

Sharing through this integration utilizes secure Egnyte Direct URL links, ensuring the organization’s security and governance policies are respected.

The app includes the following features:

  • Context Menu: Share directly from the file options in Egnyte to the desired Teams Channel, including Private Channels, or to specific Teams users.
  • AI Summaries: Generate instant content overviews to post with the files.
  • Channel Selector: Pick the exact Teams channel for the update.
  • Secure Sharing: Maintain permissions with secure file links, ensuring that only users with valid domain credentials and access to the file can view the shared content.
  • Share Direct Links: Safely share Egnyte file and folder links. Only users with valid domain credentials and the required access can view the shared content.

Prerequisites

This integration requires a valid Teams account.

Getting Started

Admin needs to enable Share to Microsoft Teams in Apps & Integrations in Egnyte

Installing ‘Share to Microsoft Teams’ From Egnyte Web UI

  • Navigate to Apps & Integrations page and search for the Share to Microsoft Teams Integration.
  • Hover over and click the Enable Integration button to install integration
  • Select Who can access this integration
  • Click Save Direct links to Egnyte files or folders can now be posted to a Teams channel with a single click directly from Egnyte Web UI.

Sharing Egnyte Links to Teams Channels

  • Select Integrations -> Share in Teams from the context menu in the file and folder listing
  • For the first time, a user will be prompted to authenticate to Microsoft Teams with their Microsoft account. This is a one-time action.
  • Once authenticated, users can select channel(s) to post direct sharing links.
  • The channel names are fetched directly from Teams settings, offering the option to choose any channel for posting an Egnyte direct file link. Similarly, a folder can be selected and its direct link posted to Teams in the same way.
  • Users can Edit the note that is being auto-generated and approve message
  • Click the Next button with the Teams icon to post a message with an Egnyte Direct link.

Setting the Default Co-Editing App in the WebUI

Overview

Egnyte allows users to set a personal default co-editing app so that Microsoft 365 files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) open in their preferred editor automatically (Microsoft Desktop, Microsoft on the Web, Google Editors) — without being prompted every time.

The default co-editing app can be set in two ways:

  • On-the-fly when opening a file
  • Directly from the Egnyte Apps and Integrations page (App Store) Users’ personal preference overrides any domain-wide default their Admin has configured.

Admins can choose whether to allow users to override domain defaults. See Admin Controls below.

Setting Default App When Opening a File

When a Microsoft 365 file is opened in the WebUI using the context menu (right-click → Open With) or the Edit button, and a co-editing app other than the current default is chosen, Egnyte prompts the user to choose from:

  • Just once: Opens the file in that app this time only; the default stays the same
  • Make it default app: Updates the personal default to this app going forward Users can also check Don’t ask again to suppress this prompt in the future.

Setting Default App from the Apps and Integrations page (App Store)

Users can also set or change their default at any time directly from the App Store:

  • In the Egnyte Web UI, go to Apps in the left navigation.
  • Find the preferred co-editing app (for example, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365).
  • Hover over the app tile, a star icon will appear.
  • Click the star to mark it as the default app for editing. The default app is now set. Files will open in that app automatically going forward.

Admin Controls

Admins can control whether end users are allowed to set their own co-editing defaults, from Settings → App Control Center:

  • Allow users to override these defaults: Toggle on to give users personal default controls; toggle off to enforce domain-wide defaults for everyone
  • Admins can also set per-file-type defaults (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for the Egnyte Desktop App, independently of Web UI settings When the override toggle is off, users will not see the option to set a personal default and will always follow the Admin-configured behavior.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a user have different defaults for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint?

Currently, the Web UI default applies across all Microsoft file types. Per-file-type defaults are available in the Egnyte Desktop App and are managed by the Admin.

Will the default carry over from the Desktop App to the Web UI?

No. Web UI and Desktop App defaults are managed separately.

Troubleshooting

Office files open in ‘Microsoft 365 for the Web’ from the Desktop App, and the co-editing preference is grayed out

This is expected behavior. It happens when the Admin has Allow users to override these defaults turned on and the user has set a web-based app (for example, Microsoft Excel for the Web) as their personal default in the Web UI.

The personal default takes precedence over the Admin-configured Desktop App defaults, so files open in the browser and the Desktop App shows the preference as read-only. The dropdown cannot be used to change it.

User resolution

  • In the Web UI, open any Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file in Preview. Click the Edit dropdown and select the Microsoft desktop application.
  • When prompted, select Make it default app. Files will now open in the desktop application and the Desktop App dropdown will reflect the change.

Admin resolution

  • If the user cannot change the setting themselves, go to Apps & Integrations -> App Control Center and turn off Allow users to override these defaults.
  • Click on Yes, turn off to confirm.
  • This will reset the user’s preference to the Admin-configured defaults. Have the user restart the Desktop App, then turn the toggle back on if needed. Turning off the toggle affects all users on the domain, not just the affected user.

Sharing Co-Editable Share Links For Microsoft Files

Co-Editing via Links

Co-editable links allow recipients to co-edit the target files in Microsoft Office Online Integration, regardless of their permissions in the containing folder. It is intended to facilitate collaboration in cases where the sharing user may not want to grant permissions to recipients for the entire folder.

Prerequisites and Limitations

  • Co-Editing via links is available to all the Platform plans. However, Co-editable Share Links for external users are not supported on GxP domains due to regulatory requirements.
  • Co-editing via preview only links is available to Platform Enterprise Lite plans and above. However, it is not available for the specific GxP Plans.
  • Co-Editable links are supported forMicrosoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files. In addition, Microsoft Office Online integration must be enabled for the domain.
  • To generate co-editable preview-only links, it is necessary to have Microsoft Office (Preview) integration enabled.

Administrator Settings

An administrator can control the types of co-editable links allowed. The configuration item can be accessed via the Settings -> Configuration -> General.

  • Use the toggle for Users can share co-editable links to enable or disable the feature

  • Click on Save changes

  • Warning: Enabling this feature for public links will allow anonymous editing access to the files being shared. Consider restricting this feature to only the Private links unless public access is explicitly needed.

  • Sharing co-editable links setting is Disabled by default and an administrator must enable this setting.

Manage Email Domains

Admins can also manage email domains for external collaboration. They can choose to allow or block certain domains for sharing co-editable links.

Creating Co-Editable Links

Users can create a co-editable link while sharing files or folders. Set Co-editing under Link properties to Allowed.

Show recent file versions link property automatically gets enabled and cannot be changed once the option to co-edit is allowed.

When a recipient clicks on the link in the email notification, they will get an option to co-edit the file with the Microsoft Office Online integration.

  • When a link is shared with domain users with Editor permission to the shared file, a new version will be created by the same user.

  • When a link is shared with domain users without Editor permission to the shared file, a new version will be created under the link creator’s username.

Warning: Creating a co-editable link that can be accessed by Anyone will allow anonymous users to edit the file. Consider using People you choose or Existing User(s) settings instead of Anyone.

Co-Edit via Preview-Only Links

Users can allow recipients to co-edit files that are shared via Preview-Only Links, by setting Downloading to Not allowed and enabling Co-editing. When a recipient clicks on a Preview-only link that is co-editable, they can make changes to the file via Microsoft Office Online but can not save the file locally or download the file.

The download option does not appear when the recipient opens the co-editable preview-only links.

Co-Edit via Preview-Only Links is only available in Enterprise Lite and Enterprise plans. Contact your Account Manager or Egnyte Sales team to add this feature

Switching From Microsoft Co-Editing (Legacy) to New Microsoft Office Desktop Co-Editing Integration

This article will go over the step-by-step on how to move from the previous Microsoft Co-Editing (Legacy) integration to the new Microsoft 365 co-editing for Desktop and Mobile integration. The Microsoft 365 files for both the Legacy integration and the new integration rest in Egnyte so we will only need to change the entry points to edit the documents.

Benefits of New Integration

  • Co-Edit files in the same collaboration session while using either Microsoft 365 for the web or Microsoft 365 Desktop Apps (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint).
  • Directly save Microsoft docs on Egnyte through the Microsoft 365 applications. No SharePoint is used.
  • Easy access to co-edit on desktop through your web interface or Egnyte Desktop App.
  • The integration is an official Microsoft-supported program.
  • Increased file size limits for Online and Desktop Co-Editing.
  • More detailed information on the new integration can be found on this helpdesk article.

Setting Up the Change Over

  • Both Integrations can exist; however, the Legacy integration can only co-edit with the Legacy integration and the new Desktop integration will only be able co-edit with either Online or Desktop. This may lead to some confusion to end users using the integration as they may see someone co-editing and they may not enter.
  • For people to successfully use the new integration users will need to connect their Microsoft Apps to their Egnyte domain. To setup the integration here is an Egnyte University video to help with training.
  • To make the transition easier you can change over during the weekend when users are less likely to be using the integration. Turning off the Legacy integration from the App Store does not end any co-editing sessions, all updates will received and saved into Egnyte.

How to Switch Over

  • Find the Microsoft Office (Legacy) tile on the Apps & Integration Page.
  • Hover over the tile and click on Setting.
  • Select the Not enabled for domain and click Save.
  • After this step is complete no one will be able to open a file using the Legacy integration anymore.
  • Find the new Microsoft 365 co-editing for Desktop and Mobile tile on the Apps & Integration page.
  • Hover over the tile and click on Enable Integration.
  • Ensure that the pre-requisites listed in the pop-up are fulfilled and click on Continue to setup
  • Complete the app setup:
    • Select the default behavior for each of the three Microsoft Apps from the respective dropdowns. By default, Start co-editing automatically is selected for all three apps. Alternatively, the user can select Ask the user or Open file without starting co-editing.
    • The user can Allow users to overwrite these defaults by clicking on the checkbox.
    • Click Next.
  • Complete the Collaborate setup:
    • The user can make Microsoft 365 Desktop as a default co-editing option in Egnyte Collaborate by turning the toggle on.
    • Click Next.
  • As an optional step, Egnyte can be added as a Trusted Place. Click ‘Learn more’ link in the pop-up for additional details. Click Next.
  • Ensure the requirements for individual device setup are met. Reference to the Mass Deployment – Egnyte Co-Edit Configuration guide can be accessed from the pop-up. Click on the Finish and Enable Integration button.

Use MS Copilot while Co-editing Egnyte Files

Egnyte enables users to access and use Microsoft Copilot while co-editing Microsoft 365 files stored in Egnyte. To make this functionality available, administrators must establish the connection between the Microsoft tenant and the Egnyte storage provider tenant.

This article outlines the requirements, guidelines, and steps for the admins to enable the connection, helping users seamlessly use Microsoft Copilot with files stored in Egnyte during collaboration.

Prerequisites

  • Microsoft 365 subscription that supports the Cloud Policy Service (Microsoft 365 Apps for Business or Enterprise)
  • Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or 365 Apps Administrator role in the Microsoft 365 admin center is required
  • Microsoft 365 Desktop and Mobile integration enabled on Egnyte domain
  • Users should have Egnyte storage added within Microsoft 365 Desktop

Identify the Domain’s Workgroup ID

  • On any browser and access the url your-domain-here.egnyte.com.
  • Search using CTRL + F and find the value for workgroupId.
  • The value will be a UUID, such as 429ee5ef-460a-4366-a5fa-dbdb02650851.
  • Copy this, and save for the next step.

Set Up the Policy in Microsoft

  • Open the Admin Policies exposed through Cloud Policy Service.
  • Commercial and US Government customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center directly in the Microsoft Intune admin center, under Apps > Policies for Microsoft 365 apps.
  • Click + Create to create a new policy.
  • Enter a name for the policy and click on Next.
  • Choose the scope: This policy configuration applies to all users OR This policy configuration applies to users in the specified groups. Click on Next.
  • Click on Enable Third Party Storage Provider Connections to configure it.
  • Enter the configuration settings and click on Save.
    • Configuration setting: Enabled
    • Name: TP_EGNYTE_PLUS
    • Value: Workgroup ID from previous step
  • Review the details and click on Create.
    • Policy changes may take up to 48 hours to propagate. To force an immediate policy refresh, sign out of the Microsoft 365 account and sign back in.
    • If Copilot still does not appear, remove Egnyte as a connected storage location from the Microsoft 365 apps and then add it again. This refreshes the connection and allows Copilot to appear.
    • Copilot only has context for the file currently open for co-editing and the SharePoint files. It cannot access or search other files stored in Egnyte unless those files are actively open for co-editing.
  • Once enabled and available, the users will be able to access and use Copilot while co-editing Microsoft files in Egnyte.

Limitations

When co-editing Microsoft files stored in Egnyte, Copilot is supported only in the Microsoft 365 Desktop and Mobile experience. Due to Microsoft limitations, Microsoft 365 for the Web does not allow Copilot to be used with files stored outside native Microsoft storage, such as OneDrive and SharePoint.

Why Autosave Can Turn Off During Microsoft Co-Editing

Egnyte provides the ability to its users to co-edit Microsoft Office files directly within the Egnyte platform. The integrations support real-time collaboration with features like Autosave, which helps preserve changes without requiring manual saves.

However, there are scenarios where Microsoft’s Autosave feature may turn off automatically during a co-editing session. This can affect users working within Egnyte, particularly when relying on Autosave to retain updates in real time.

In order to avoid any potential data loss, the changes made to the files prior to the error message should be saved locally. Once saved, the file version can be re-uploaded to Egnyte, and the co-editing session can be restarted.

Below are the most common reasons why Autosave may be disabled:

Embedded Fonts

Autosave can be turned off when a document includes embedded fonts. Removing the embedded fonts from the file allows Autosave to be re-enabled. The user will have to manually enable auto-save for it to function.

Server Throttling

In situations where Microsoft servers are under heavy load, Autosave may be temporarily turned off due to throttling. During such times, users are prompted to save files manually using File -> Save until Autosave becomes available again.

Protected View

When a file is opened in Protected View—often for security reasons—Autosave will be disabled. Exiting Protected View reactivates Autosave for the session. The user will have to manually enable auto-save then for it to function.

Unsupported Add-ins

Some third-party add-ins may cause excessive background saves, which interferes with Autosave. Disabling or removing these unsupported add-ins resolves the issue.

Privacy Settings

Certain privacy settings within Microsoft Office can block Autosave from working properly. Modifying those settings may be necessary to allow Autosave to function as intended. Users can save files manually using File -> Save option in such a scenario.

Unsupported File Location

This can occur due to an issue with how the file was launched. Reopening the file correctly may help restore Autosave.

Save Error

In some cases, a general save error can disable Autosave. This may result from temporary issues such as network interruptions or internal glitches. Manual saving is recommended until the problem is resolved.

Group Policy Settings (GPO)

Autosave may be turned off by the organization’s administrator through Group Policy. In such cases, users might be restricted from re-enabling Autosave unless the administrator updates the policy settings.

File Encryption

If a file is encrypted, Autosave will be turned off. Removing the encryption from the file is required to enable Autosave. The user will have to manually enable auto-save for it to function.

Shared Workbook Enabled

If the Shared Workbook feature is enabled, it can prevent autosave and co-authoring. The associated Microsoft scripts can impact autosave.

Error Messages

The user will observe error messages displayed if any of the above issues occur.

The following are the error messages that will be displayed:

Issue Type

Error Message

Embedded Fonts

This file includes embedded fonts. Please remove them.

Windowless Mode

You’re currently using windowless mode. Please exit this mode.

Server Throttle

AutoSave isn’t available right now. Please save the file using File > Save.

Protected View

This file is open in Protected View. Please exit Protected View.

Unsupported Add-ins

This app is using unsupported add-ins that are interfering with AutoSave. Please turn off the unsupported add-ins.

Privacy Settings

We couldn’t save your file automatically due to your privacy settings. To avoid losing your changes, please save the file using File > Save.

Unsupported File Location

We couldn’t save your file to this location automatically. To avoid losing your changes, please save the file using File > Save.

Save Error

We couldn’t save your file automatically. To avoid losing your changes, please save the file using File > Save.

Group Policy (GPO)

Your administrator has turned off AutoSave. To avoid losing your changes, please save the file using File > Save.

File Encryption

This file is encrypted. Please remove the encryption.

Shared Workbook Enabled

This workbook contains features that prevent it from using AutoSave. Please save your workbook manually or click the AutoSave toggle button for instructions to turn it back on.

Collaboration between Egnyte Users

Collaboration with other Egnyte users is quick and easy. Anyone with access to a file in Egnyte can easily collaborate with others by adding messages in the Comments option. Users can use “@name” mentions to tag another Egnyte user, ensuring they receive a notification along with the message content and a link to the file. For the Egnyte mobile app on iOS or Android, users will receive instant push notifications when mentioned on a file.

By default, Standard Users cannot tag other Standard Users using @name mentions. However, this functionality can be enabled through a Configuration > User Types & Roles > Standard Users > can search for other Standard Users toggle switch. Once enabled, the standard users can search for other Standard Users in the Workflows Assignee field.

Click here to watch a video demonstrating how users can collaborate in Egnyte.

Use Cases

File Discussions

Collaborators can be notified to provide input on a designated file. When the file is opened in the Web UI or any of the mobile apps, the relevant file and corresponding discussion can be easily referenced.

For WebUI:

For iOS:

For Android:

File Sharing

Quickly share a file with other Egnyte users on the domain who already have permission for the file. Mention them in a comment and the collaborators will receive an email and a push notification on their mobile device(s) (if enabled).

Another way to share a file with Egnyte users who already have permissions is by sending a direct link. This link is available in the details option when previewing the file and works on the Web UI, iOS devices, and Android devices.

  • The direct link is the URL address of the file within the Egnyte domain, ensuring continuous accessibility except in the following scenarios:
    • When the file/folder associated with the direct link is deleted. Note that deleting a version of the file does not impact the direct link.
    • When accessing the direct link, the recipient lacks permission to the source folder.
  • Moving or renaming a file/folder will not alter the direct link. Copying a file will generate a new direct link for the copy.
Request File Edits

Collaborators can be mentioned and instructed to edit a Microsoft 365 file. The file can be opened in 365 on the Web on a desktop or mobile device, and changes will automatically be saved back to Egnyte. Egnyte CLI in Desktop App (Limited Availability)

Egnyte CLI lets AI tools such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor work with Egnyte files directly from Desktop App. Once it is connected, AI assistant can find, read, organize, and share content in Egnyte on user’s behalf, with the same permissions they already have.

  • Egnyte CLI is in Limited Availability and will roll out to all customers in upcoming Desktop App releases. To request this feature, contact the Product team

  • If the option to install Egnyte CLI is not visible in Desktop App, it means the feature is not enabled on the domain.

  • Egnyte CLI in Desktop App does not work alongside an npm installation of Agentic CLI.

  • The Egnyte skill must be installed in the AI tool for the tool to use the Egnyte CLI.

Overview

Egnyte CLI is the integrated version of the open-source Egnyte Agentic CLI. Desktop App installs it and reuses sign-in, so there is no need to install anything with npm or log in separately.

Once Egnyte CLI is installed, a dedicated Egnyte CLI tab appears in Desktop App. The tab explains how to connect an AI tool and gives examples of what it can do.

With Egnyte CLI, AI tools can:

  • Search and read files across Egnyte domains

  • Upload, move, rename, and organize files and folders in bulk. Unlike the Egnyte MCP connector, Egnyte CLI can upload any file type and size, including Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, image, video, and CAD files

  • Apply tags and manage sharing without leaving AI tool

  • Use advanced Egnyte capabilities beyond basic file access, such as AI, permissions, and audit events

  • Actions that change content, such as deleting or moving files, support a preview (–dry-run) so users can review what will happen before it runs.

  • Egnyte CLI in Desktop App does not work if the open-source version of Agentic CLI is already installed through npm (npm install -g @egnyte/agentic-cli). Only one of them can be used at the same time. If the npm version is installed, it needs to be removed first (npm uninstall -g @egnyte/agentic-cli), then Egnyte CLI from Desktop App can be installed.

Install Egnyte CLI

  • In Desktop App, click user profile icon and select Install Egnyte CLI.
  • When the installation is complete, a system notification appears and the Egnyte CLI tab is added to Desktop App.
  • A new tab will for Egnyte CLI will be shown. Egnyte CLI uses the account user is signed in with in the Desktop App. If the user has connected more than one Egnyte domain, the AI tool can work with each of them.
Update or Uninstall Egnyte CLI

Egnyte CLI is a separate application and it updates independently from Desktop App. When a new version is available, it can be updated from the Desktop App. Uninstalling Desktop App does not uninstall Egnyte CLI. To remove it, uninstall Egnyte CLI separately using Add or Remove programs Windows functionality.

Install the Egnyte Skill in the AI Tool

For an AI tool to use Egnyte CLI, the Egnyte Skill must be installed in that tool. Without it, the tool does not know that Egnyte CLI is available or how to use it.

The Egnyte skill covers how to use both the Egnyte MCP connector and Egnyte CLI. It tells AI tool which one to use for each task and how to run commands safely, for example by previewing changes before running them.

  • Download the Egnyte skill.
  • Add it to the AI tool, following that tool’s instructions for installing skills.
  • Ask the AI tool to work with Egnyte files. For example; Search for the Q3 budget in /Shared/Finance.

Available Commands

It is usually not required to use them manually, as AI Agent can easily discover and choose which command to use for a desired outcome. All commands start with egnyte.

  • AI tool can only do what user’s Egnyte permissions allow.

  • The commands available may differ slightly between versions. Run egnyte schema –list to see what is available.

Egnyte Visual Indicators May Not Be Displayed

Description

Some folders and files that are supposed to have an icon overlay show no such visual indicator.

Causes

The number of different visual indicator icons that the system can support is limited by the amount of space available for visual indicators icons in the system image list. There are currently fifteen slots allotted for this function, some of which are reserved by the system. All registered visual indicator icons are visible in the Windows registry under:

  • Computer_LOCAL_MACHINE It would have been best for Egnyte’s visual indicator icons to populate the earlier slots to avoid such a situation. Given this is built for Windows, Microsoft has preemptively assumed the initial slots.

For example, Microsoft’s OneDrive application can place its overlays on the top of this list during installation or update.

Potential Solution(s)

  • Open registry editor with admin permissions
  • Go to the following registry path:
    • Computer_LOCAL_MACHINE
  • Manually remove some icons from the top of this list so that the visual indicator icons from Egnyte are in the TOP TEN
  • Restart computer Keep in mind that OneDrive will again place its icons at the top of this list upon the next update. Given this is the case, it will be necessary to repeat these steps to fix this occurrence. Please bookmark this page for your records.

Enter proxy information in Desktop App

We only support proxies that use basic authentication, we do not support NTLM (Windows Integrated Authentication). Proxy auto-config (PAC) file configurations are not currently supported.

To enter a Network Proxy configuration, do the following:

  1. Click on the Desktop App icon in the Menu bar(Mac) or Taskbar (Windows).

  2. Click on the gear icon and then on the Preferences tab.

  3. Select the checkbox Set up proxy manually

  4. Enter the information regarding your proxy.

  5. Click on Save Changes.

Let’s take the example below:

Proxy Server Name: myproxyserver1

Proxy Port: 8080

If your network proxy requires a username and password, check the Proxy server requires username and password box.

Username: ddavid

Password: **********

Folder Move Confirmation in Desktop App for Windows - Limited Availability

Overview

Folder move confirmation helps prevent accidental drag and drop moves of folders on the Egnyte drive in File Explorer. This feature is available starting with Desktop App for Windows v 4.8.0. In File Explorer, a folder can be moved with a single drag and drop. That makes it easy to move a folder by accident, and the mistake is often not noticed right away. With folder move confirmation turned on, Desktop App asks users to confirm before File Explorer moves a folder on the Egnyte drive. The move starts only after the user confirms. If the user cancels, nothing changes and the folder stays where it was.

  • This feature is currently in Limited Availability for all customers. To request this feature, contact our Products team.

  • This feature is not available in Desktop App for Mac.

Use Case and Benefits

Folder move confirmation is designed to react only to manual actions by a user in File Explorer, such as an accidental drag and drop. It is not meant to interfere with applications that move folders as part of their normal work (see Limitations for exceptions). These moves are made directly through the file system and bypass the Windows shell file operation that File Explorer uses, so they never trigger the confirmation Examples include:

  • Applications that move or save files and folders as part of their own operation, such as CAD and Office applications
  • Command-line tools and scripts, such as PowerShell Move-Item and other third party tools
  • Backup and synchronization software This means the feature is safe to use to prevent manual mistakes. Applications, scheduled tasks and unattended sessions continue to work as before, and the confirmation is never shown in a service, a headless run or an unattended session. There is one limitation to this design that administrators should review before enabling the feature. See the Limitations section below.

What Triggers the Confirmation

The confirmation appears when a user moves a folder inside the Egnyte drive in File Explorer by any of these methods:

  • Dragging and dropping the folder into another folder
  • Cutting the folder and pasting it into another folder
  • Dragging the folder with the right mouse button and choosing Move here If several items are selected and at least one of them is a folder, Desktop App shows one confirmation for the whole selection, not one for each folder.

What User Sees

When a move is started, Desktop App shows a dialog asking whether to proceed. The move waits until the user answers.

  • Move: the folder is moved
  • Cancel: the move is cancelled. Pressing Esc or closing the dialog also cancels the move If the selection also contained files, Cancel stops the whole operation, files included.

When the Confirmation Does not Appear

The confirmation does not pop-up in following cases:

  • Copying and pasting a folder: A copy creates new content and does not change the original folder.
  • Moving files only: If the selection contains no folders, no confirmation is shown.
  • Moving a folder into Egnyte Drive from a local disk: The folder comes from outside Egnyte Drive, so no existing Egnyte folder is moved.
  • Moving a folder out of Egnyte Drive to a different drive: This includes moving to a local disk. Windows treats this as a copy followed by a delete, not as a move.
  • Renaming or deleting a folder: These actions do not move a folder to a new location.
  • Folder names and count are not shown: The confirmation cannot list the names or the number of the folders being moved.
  • A single confirmation for multiple folders:: When several folders are moved to the same destination in one operation, the first confirmation applies to the rest of the selection.
  • Egnyte Drive only: The confirmation applies to Egnyte Drive only. It does not apply to Connected Folders or to moves on local disks.
  • Cancelling does not undo earlier moves: If a move is cancelled while a selection is being processed, items already moved before the first folder was reached are not moved back.

Limitations

Cannot identify who started a move
  • Desktop App cannot yet tell whether a move comes from a user or from an application that uses the same Windows shell file operation as File Explorer.
  • Desktop App shows the confirmation by hooking into that Windows shell file operation (an ICopyHook shell extension). Most applications and scripts do not use it, but some do, and Desktop App cannot currently tell them apart from a user working in File Explorer. As a result, a folder move started by an application or a custom script that uses the Windows shell file operation, for example through the Shell.Application object in a PowerShell or VBScript script, can also trigger the confirmation. In that case:
    • The confirmation appears and the move waits until it is answered.
    • If the move is cancelled or left unanswered, the application or script that started it may report an error or stop.
  • Egnyte is working on recognizing which application started the move, so that only moves made by users in File Explorer are confirmed. Until then, administrators should review the scripts and applications that move folders on the Egnyte drive and check whether they use the Windows shell file operation. If they do, test them with the feature turned on before enabling it widely.

Mobile and Desktop Apps

With Egnyte, you can access your files from a variety of mobile and desktop access points. You can use our mobile applications to access and share content on-the-go. Alternatively, you can access files in the cloud from the convenience of a drive letter using the Desktop App and edit files in the Web UI in their native applications using WebEdit.

Follow one of the links below to learn more:

Mobile

Desktop App

WebEdit

Mobile

With Egnyte’s mobile apps, you can access files on the go, share them easily with co-workers or outside parties, and much more. Apps are available for the iPhone, iPad, Android phones, and tablets.

Egnyte Desktop App

Desktop App provides fast real-time access to the files and folders stored in your Egnyte cloud file server from a familiar Mac Finder or Windows file explorer interface. Desktop App is a great option if you want to view and edit your files without having to first sync them to your computer. Files opened using Desktop App will be locked across various access points (Web UI, WebEdit, and other Desktop clients), effectively preventing version conflicts.

WebEdit

Egnyte’s WebEdit enables you to select a file from our Web UI and automatically open it in its native application. Changes you save will automatically appear in the cloud as new versions. This lightweight product is ideal for users who need to edit files on their desktops, but don’t want to install Desktop App.

Third-Party Apps That Can Be Used With Egnyte

This article contains a list of third-party mobile applications that are certified to work with Egnyte. Most of the apps below either link directly into Egnyte or can connect to the customer’s account using FTP.

The typical workflow for using a third-party mobile app to view or edit files would be the following:

  • Open Egnyte mobile app and select file → Choose Open In option to view or edit file with a different app → Use a Save Back or Open In option from within third-party app to upload file back to the Egnyte mobile app To connect to Egnyte from Windows Explorer or Mac Finder, it is required to install the Desktop App. There are also a variety of third-party integrations that can connect the applications to Egnyte that can be viewed as well.

Set Up

Apps that Connect Directly with Egnyte

For apps connecting directly to Egnyte, credentials should be entered as usual:

  • Egnyte domain name: mycompany
  • Username: <Egnyte username>
  • Password: <Egnyte password>
Apps that Connect via FTP

For FTP clients, use the following structure.

  • FTP Server/Host: ftp-<domain name>.egnyte.com
  • Ex: If the domain name is acme then the URL will be ftp-acme.egnyte.com.
  • Username: <Egnyteusername>$<domain name>
  • Ex: if the username is john and domain name is acme then the username will be john$acme
  • If the FTP Client does not support $ symbol then any of the following symbols can be used: % # | @ &
  • Password: <Egnyte password> Egnyte supports three transfer protocols: FTP, FTPES, and SFTP.

Ensure that the protocol that the app is using is consistent with the Egnyte account’s FTP policy. Otherwise, it will be unable to establish a connection. Admins can access this from the Configuration tab in Settings under the Applications section.

If the account only allows secure FTP connections, make sure the app is using FTPES or SFTP.

Use Egnyte for Adobe Sign

Now that Adobe Sign has been installed on the domain, learn how to send documents for signatures right from the Web UI. The article covers the details on sending a file using an existing template in Adobe Sign and having the signed document automatically added to the appropriate folder.

Send a Document for Signature

After configuring Egnyte for Adobe Sign, a Send with Adobe Sign option will appear under the Integrations option in the file context menu.

Sending with Adobe Sign is currently supported for these file types:

  • Microsoft Word documents (.doc and .docx)

  • Microsoft Excel spreadsheets (.xls and .xlsx)

  • Adobe Portable Document Format documents (.pdf)

  • Text documents (.txt and .rtf)

  • Images (.jpg, .tif, .gif and .png) Clicking this option will open the Adobe Sign interface in a new browser window. Adobe Sign has a rich web interface that gives users many options for managing their signed documents. The article covers a simple case where a user wants to collect a signature from a single person. Detailed documentation on Adobe Sign’s capabilities is available here.

  • Specify a recipient for the document.

  • Indicate where the recipient should sign.

  • Send them an email with a link to where they can review the document online and provide an electronic signature. The counter-party will be asked to provide and confirm their signature.

Once they confirm their signature, the document will be completed in Adobe Sign, and a signed copy of the document (in PDF format) will appear in the Egnyte account in the folder where the original document resides. The signed copy will have a note automatically added to it indicating who signed the document and the time and date of sign-off.

Egnyte periodically checks with Adobe Sign to detect when sign off has been completed, so there may be a slight delay of a few minutes before the signed copy shows up in the account.

Send with a template

In addition to sending a regular file for signature, Egnyte supports sending a template from the three-dots menu -> Integrations. This kicks off a signature flow using the Adobe Sign templates. Once the document is signed, it is returned to the folder from which the send template workflow was launched.

Signing Timeframe

Signed documents are saved back to Egnyte only if the agreement is signed within 30 days of being sent. When a signature request is sent, Egnyte issues an authorization token that is valid for 30 days.

  • If the document is signed after this period, the integration can no longer write the signed copy to the folder. No error is shown in Egnyte or Adobe Sign.

  • To avoid this, set a document expiration deadline of 30 days or less in Adobe Sign when sending the agreement.

  • If an agreement is signed after 30 days, download the signed PDF from the Adobe Sign completion email and upload it to the Egnyte folder manually.

Requirement

In order to work with the Egnyte, the Adobe Sign license must have Integrations and API features currently available only on Acrobat Sign Solutions Enterprise plan.

A User’s Guide to Adding Content

Storing your files and folders securely in Egnyte allows you to access content from anywhere using any device. This article will walk you through the various ways a standard user can upload content to the Egnyte cloud.

Admins looking to undertake a larger data migration project should review our An Admin’s Guide to Choosing a Migration Method for more information.

WebUI

Desktop App

Mobile Device

More Options

WebUI

Drag and Drop

You can drag files and folders from your desktop to Egnyte in just a few steps:

  • Navigate to a folder on Egnyte where you want to add content.
  • Click and hold the file or folder on your desktop that you want to add, then drag to the Egnyte Connect Web UI.
  • ‘Drop’ the content in the destination folder. Larger files may take some time.
Choose Files from your Computer

Add files and folders to Egnyte Connect from your desktop in just a few steps:

  • Navigate to the folder in the Egnyte Connect Web UI where you’ll add new content.

  • Click Upload.

  • Click Choose Files.

  • Select the files or folders you’d like to add.

  • Click Open. Done! Considerations:

  • For migrations of more than 50 GB from on-premises servers, we recommend using Migration App.

  • While Web UI supports drag and drop for up to 100 GB, it isn’t recommended for projects over 50 GB or a few hundred files.

  • If there are errors, you can see them in the UI, but you’ll need to scroll through a long list of files to identify them, and there’s no way to export the list.

  • If your computer goes to sleep in the middle of an upload, the upload will fail.

  • There are file size limitations based on your Egnyte plan (contact your Egnyte account administrator for details).

  • Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge allow you to drag and drop files and folders.

  • Safari allows you to drag and drop files starting with version 6.

  • Internet Explorer allows you to drag and drop files starting with version 10.

  • You can not drag and drop empty folders to Egnyte. Your account Admin has a couple of different options for this, should you need this functionality. Refer to the following knowledge base articles: FTP Overview or Using Migration App to Migrate from On-Premises Sources.

Egnyte Desktop App

You can use Egnyte’s Desktop App to move your content to the Egnyte cloud:

  • From File Explorer on a PC or Finder on a Mac, locate the files or folders you would like to add, highlight your content, then right-click and select Copy.
  • Staying in File Explorer or Finder, navigate to the destination folder on Egnyte Connect.
  • Right-click inside the destination folder, and select Paste. Egnyte also offers the Connected folder feature to connect a local folder with Egnyte folder and upload content.

Considerations:

  • Uploading files creates a temporary storage space on your local machine of 2X the amount of data being copied. So if you want to upload 10 GB of data, you need 20 GB of free space: 10 GB to store the files and 10 GB for the upload cache. Once the upload is finished, the cache is cleared.
  • There is a recommended upload maximum of 40-50 GB of data at once. This isn’t a hard limit, but uploading larger data sets will have various negative implications, such as causing other applications to crash.
  • Larger uploads will take longer, and therefore may be impacted by your local machine’s power save operations. If the machine is set to power down before an upload is finished, you may never be able to fully complete it.
  • If there are errors, you can see them in the UI, but you’ll need to scroll through a long list of files to identify them, and there’s no way to export the list or to generate a log.
  • If your computer goes to sleep in the middle of an upload, the upload will fail.
  • There are file size limitations based on your Egnyte plan (contact your Egnyte account administrator for details).
  • For migrations of more than 50 GB from on-premises servers, we recommend using Migration App.

Mobile Devices

Content can be uploaded either directly from the Egnyte mobile app or shared from a third-party app.

This section of the article outlines the upload process for both iOS and Android. The screenshots below show the interfaces for both iOS (left) and Android (right).

Uploading Content from the Egnyte Mobile App

Photos, videos, PDFs, and other supported file types can be uploaded from a mobile device to an Egnyte account using the steps below.

  • Launch the Egnyte mobile app.
  • Navigate to the folder where the content should be uploaded.
  • Tap the floating + Create or upload button.
  • Select the appropriate content upload option:
  • iOS Options include:
    • New folder - Creates a new folder within the current Egnyte directory for organizing files and subfolders.
    • Upload photo or video – Allows selection of existing photos or videos from the device library for upload to Egnyte.
    • Take photo or video – Captures a new photo or video using the device’s camera and uploads it directly to the selected folder. On supported devices, the full range of zoom levels is supported, including ultra-wide (below 1x).
    • Photos from specific location – Finds photos from a particular location within the device’s Photos library and uploads them to a selected folder.
    • Scan document – Uses the camera to capture a physical document. The scanned file is automatically converted into a high-quality PDF.
    • Extract text – Extracts text from a captured or uploaded image using Optical Character Recognition (OCR). The recognized text can be saved or copied for later use.
    • New text file – Creates a new plain text (.txt) file within the app.
    • New Project Folder - Creates a folder marked as a Project in Egnyte, with project-specific metadata (such as name, ID, and status) automatically applied for easier tracking
    • New URL – Saves a web link (URL) as a shortcut file inside Egnyte. Selecting the shortcut opens the linked webpage in a browser.
    • Import From… – Imports files from other applications or storage locations on the device via the iOS Files app.
    • New file from template – Generates a new file based on a pre-defined company template stored in Egnyte, typically used for standardized documents such as forms or reports.
    • New folder from template – Creates a new folder structure based on a pre-defined company template stored in Egnyte, typically used for standardized project or client setups.
    • New project from template – Creates a new project folder using a designated project template, automatically including predefined folders, permissions, and structure.
  • Android Options include:
    • Create:
      • New Folder - Creates a new folder within the current Egnyte directory for organizing files and subfolders.
      • New Photos – Captures a new photo using the device’s camera and uploads it to Egnyte.
      • New Videos – Records a new video using the device’s camera and uploads it to Egnyte.
      • New Project Folder - Creates a folder marked as a Project in Egnyte, with project-specific metadata (such as name, ID, and status) automatically applied for easier tracking.
      • New URL – Creates a shortcut file containing a web link (URL). Opening the shortcut launches the linked page in a browser.
      • New Text File – Creates a new plain text (.txt) file within the app.
      • From Templates:
        • File Templates - Generates a new file based on a pre-defined company template stored in Egnyte, typically used for standardized documents such as forms or reports.
        • Folder Templates - Creates a new folder structure based on a pre-defined company template stored in Egnyte, typically used for standardized project or client setups
    • Upload:
      • Files – Uploads one or more files stored on the device.
      • Existing Photos & Videos – Uploads photos or videos already stored on the device.
      • Geo-tagged Photos – Finds photos from a particular location within the device’s Photos library and uploads them to a selected folder.
      • Scan Documents – Uses the camera to capture a scan of a physical document, saving the result as a high-quality PDF.
      • Voice Recording – Records audio through the device’s microphone and uploads it as an audio file to the selected folder.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the upload. The next steps will vary based on the selected option - whether uploading an existing file from the device or cloud storage, or creating new content such as a scanned document or a photo taken within the app. On iOS, for example, files can also be selected from other connected cloud drives via the Files app.
Uploading Content from Third-Party Apps
  • Open the third-party app and select the files to upload (for example, from the Gallery or Photos app).
  • Tap the Share button.
  • Select Egnyte from the list of available apps.
  • Navigate to the desired destination folder in Egnyte.
  • Tap Upload to begin the upload process. The Android app includes an Upload Center, a central place to track and manage ongoing and recent uploads.
Uploading Large Batches of Files on Mobile

There is no enforced limit on the number of files that can be uploaded at once in either the iOS or Android app. However, uploading more than 200 files in a single batch may affect performance. To ensure a smoother experience, it is recommended to upload large file sets in smaller batches of fewer than 200 files.

On Android devices, a warning will be displayed if a selected batch exceeds 200 files, advising that smaller batches may help maintain performance.

More Options

Above are just a few ways you can add content to Egnyte.

Learn about more ways to add your files and folders to Egnyte in these knowledge base articles:

Using Egnyte for Slack

Egnyte for Slack allows users to integrate the power of file sharing capabilities of Egnyte into Slack, a messaging app for teams. Slack brings all the team communication together in one place, is instantly searchable, and is available on multiple platforms.
