Prerequisites

This integration requires a Slack team account with the Slack Web or App installed.

Getting Started

Click the button below to add the /egnyte bot to a designated Slack Team.

For more information, visit egnyte.slack.com

Features

  • Post or share a File Link from Egnyte Web UI into the desired Slack Channel
  • Share an Egnyte File in a Slack Channel.
  • Upload a local File to Egnyte from Slack and Share the Link to the Slack Channel Users.
  • Directly Navigate to the Egnyte Web UI from Slack to perform any task (for example, change File Permissions for the Slack Channel team members).
  • Share File Links from Egnyte Web UI to Private Channels or specific Slack users.
  • Share links of type Public and Public with Domain Access (this allows the ability to share links safely even when Public link sharing is disabled at the domain level, a user can share the links, and only people who have valid domain credentials and access to the file can view the file).
  • Share Egnyte folder links to users with Domain Access from Egnyte Web UI into Slack.
  • Share Egnyte folder links to users with Domain Access from Slack into Slack.
  • Unfurl Egnyte Links in the Slack Channel

From Egnyte Web UI

To get started

  • Install Egnyte for Slack as mentioned above.
  • Enable the Slack integration from the Egnyte Apps & Integrations page.
  • 2.1 Search for the Slack Integration and enable it.
  • 2.2 Select who can access this integration and click on save. Files can now be selected and posted to a Slack channel associated with Slack credentials.

The channel names are fetched directly from Slack settings, offering the option to choose any channel for posting an Egnyte file link. Similarly, a folder can be selected and its link posted to Slack in the same way.

From Slack App (Web, Mobile, Desktop, Mac)

Once the Egnyte App is installed, the /egnyte command bot for Slack will be available.

Type /egnyte in any channel and press enter. It will display the actions that can be performed.

These links expire after some time to ensure security.

First time users will be asked to enter their Egnyte domain name and authorize the app to access their Egnyte domain.

Share

This button enables the user to share an Egnyte file into their Slack channel.

  • Click on Share to view the file picker (This will open a page in a new browser window or a new tab if the existing browser is already open).
  • Choose a file to share its link into the Slack channel from which the command was issued. The user can also navigate to the directory and click OK to share the folder link into Slack.
  • Select the Access level of the link (Anyone, Egnyte File Server Users, Egnyte File Server Users with Permissions) and click on continue.
  • Once the file link is posted, the user can close the browser window or tab.
Upload & Share

Upload & Share allows users to upload a file into an Egnyte folder and post a link to that file in the Slack Channel from where the action button was clicked.

  • Go to a Slack channel or chat and enter the /egnyte command. Click on the Upload & Share button.
  • Choose the target folder in Egnyte from the File Picker.
  • Click on the Choose file button and select a local file to upload.
  • Click on Continue after selecting the file.
  • Select the link access level and click on Continue.
  • Once uploaded, an Egnyte link is posted in the Slack channel.
Go to Egnyte

Go to Egnyte opens the Egnyte Web UI for the user to perform any actions not covered by other links. For example, if one of the Slack channel users asks for specific folder level permissions, the user can click on Go to Egnyte to give them permissions.

Unfurl Egnyte Links

Egnyte allows a user to unfurl Egnyte direct and share links in the Slack Channel. You can share links via the Egnyte /egnyte command or by copying a link directly into a chat.

Shared via /egnyte command

Direct Link Example

Limitation
  • The Egnyte integration can only be authorized to one Slack Workspace at a time. To use it in another workspace, the user will need to authorize for that workspace to unfurl the link.

Using Egnyte for Trello Power-Up

The Egnyte for Trello Integration allows users to attach links to Egnyte files or folders to Trello cards.

Adding the Egnyte Power-Up

To add Egnyte for Trello, go to your Trello board, open the side menu, choose Power-Ups, and scroll down to Egnyte Power-Up. Just hit “enable,” and you’re all set.

Sharing Files or Folders

Once you have added the Egnyte Power-Up, open the card, you would like to add an Egnyte link. Click on the “Egnyte” item under “Power-Ups” on the right of the card and choose “Attach files or folders…”

A new pop-up will open. Please specify your Egnyte domain and credentials and allow the Trello app to access your files. You will see the file picker listing your Egnyte domain’s files and folders. Navigate to the folder containing the item you want to share, click “OK,” and select the appropriate accessibility option for those who will be able to access your file or folder - ‘anyone,’ ‘all domain’s users, or ‘domain’s user with sufficient permissions.

Once you submit, the pop-up will close, and you will see that your file or folder is added to the Trello card as an attachment.

It is that easy.

Limitations

Users must be Admin or Power Users.

The mobile app

360 Image Preview

The ability to preview 360-degree images is supported directly within the Egnyte Mobile apps. Users can enjoy an immersive viewing experience, exploring panoramic photos and seamlessly navigating every angle. 360 images can be explored by using standard on-screen gestures and by simply moving the device around.

Opening the 360 Viewer (iOS)

From the file listing in the Egnyte iOS app, a user can select the More […] button to see a list of available actions. The option to Open in 360 Preview will now be available.

If a 360 image is opened in the normal preview window, a user can select the More […] button directly from the Preview window, and then select Open in 360 Preview without needing to navigate back to the file listing.

Opening the 360 Viewer (Android)

From the file listing in the Egnyte Android app, a user can first open the file and on the preview window select the More […] button to see a list of available actions. The option to Open in 360 Preview will now be available.

Selecting Open in 360 Preview will load the file in Egnyte’s Preview window and allow a user to zoom (using touch gestures) and navigate the image (by moving the device around).

Accessing and Using AI Agents on Mobile (iOS)

Using Egnyte AI Agents on Mobile

Egnyte AI Agents automate repetitive, time-consuming tasks by providing intelligent insights and content summaries. These agents are accessible for interaction directly through the Egnyte Android mobile app.

This feature is available for Platform Plans with AI add-on and included in the New Generation Platform plans. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get this feature.

Finding and Selecting an Agent

The AI section of the app serves as the primary hub for agent interaction.

The Appropriate Agent For a Task Can Be Identified Using the Following Methods
  • Search and Filter: Specific agents can be located by name or by utilizing category filters:
    • All: Displays all available agents.
    • Created by Egnyte: Displays system-standard agents.
    • Created by me: Displays agents previously created via the Web UI.
    • Trending Now: Displays the most frequently used agents within the domain.
  • Quick Switch: A dropdown menu at the top of the AI Assistant screen allows for instant switching between different agents.

Interacting with an Agent

Once an agent is selected, interaction begins by providing input to receive insights or automate tasks. The mobile interface supports several input and configuration options:

  • Attaching Content: Typing @ displays a list of recently used files, allowing specific files to be included as context for the agent. Selecting View All Files opens the folder tree, enabling access to and selection of any files available to the user
  • Input Methods: Requests can be submitted via Text, Voice Input, or by selecting from a list of Existing Prompts.
  • Configuration: Depending on the agent’s settings, the Source (Egnyte or Web) and the specific Model can be adjusted before submission.
  • Selection by the agent user may be restricted if disabled by the agent creator.

Managing Agent Responses

After a prompt is submitted, the agent generates a response based on the provided input and attached files.

  • Sources and Citations: If a response includes references to specific documents or websites, the provided links grant direct access to those sources.
  • Response Actions: The Copy button facilitates moving text to other applications, while the Thumbs Up/Down icons allow users to provide feedback on response quality.

Chat History and Session Management

The mobile interface includes tools to manage ongoing and past interactions:

  • New Sessions: A new chat can be initiated from the same three-dot menu, allowing for a fresh start with the selected agent.
  • Accessing History: The three-dot menu provides access to previous chat history.

Known Limitations

Creating and Editing Agents: Agent management, including creation and editing, is not supported on mobile devices. The Egnyte Web UI must be used to modify or create new agents.

Accessing and Using Project Center on Mobile

The Project Center provides a dedicated, project-first view in the Egnyte iOS app, aggregating all folders designated as Projects into a single dashboard. Users can locate and open their active projects without navigating deeply nested folder hierarchies.

This feature is available for all customers that have Projects Hub enabled. Contact your Account Manager or Egnyte Sales team to get this feature.

Accessing Project Center

The Project Center is accessible from the app’s Home screen. The Projects widget displays a preview of the user’s most recent projects; tapping View All opens the full Project Center dashboard, where all projects accessible to the signed-in user are listed in one place, respecting existing access controls and permissions.

Filtering Projects

A filter bar allows users to narrow the project list by one or more of the following criteria:

  • Status: filters projects by their current status (for example, Pending, in Progress)
  • Start Date: filters projects by their configured start date (for example, Last 24 hours)
  • End Date: filters projects by their configured end date (for example, Last 24 hours)
  • Last Accessed: filters projects by the date they were most recently opened (for example, Last 90 days) Filters can be combined to narrow results further.

Opening a Project

Tapping a project in the Project Center opens it directly, providing access to its files, folders, Project Dashboard, and Project Settings.

AI Image Labelling on Mobile

Image Labelling is an AI-powered feature in the Egnyte Mobile Apps that automatically generates a short description and object labels for images uploaded from the device. Analysis is performed entirely on-device using a locally installed AI model — the image is not sent to any external server.

The generated caption and labels are stored as file metadata in Egnyte and fed into the search index, making images discoverable through natural language queries. This is particularly useful for teams in construction and engineering who capture large volumes of job site photos that would otherwise be difficult to organize or retrieve.

Availability

  • Platforms: iOS and Android
  • Minimum app version: iOS 9.11.1 or higher and Android 9.11 or higher
  • Plan availability: AEC Essentials, AEC Elite, AEC Ultimate
  • Processing: On-device (no data sent to external AI services)

How it Works

The AI Image Labelling toggle is available in the Egnyte Mobile Apps under Settings → AI Features → AI Image Labelling. When the toggle is enabled, every image uploaded through the app is automatically analyzed on the device.

The AI model identifies objects, materials, equipment, and site conditions in the photo, and saves a concise description along with individual object labels as file metadata in Egnyte. The description is then indexed, making the image searchable by content.

When a user on a supported domain upgrades to version 9.11.1 or higher on iOS or 9.11 or higher on Android for the first time, the app prompts them to download the on-device AI model.

The model can also be downloaded at any time through the settings path above.

Supported File Types and Behavior

Image Labelling processes standard image files — including JPEG, PNG, HEIC, and HEIF — uploaded through the Egnyte Mobile App. Analysis runs at upload time, on the device. The generated caption is saved as file metadata and is visible in the file details screen in the Tags category.

Image Labelling applies only to images uploaded after the toggle is enabled. Previously uploaded images are not retroactively processed.

Searching by Image Content

Once images have been labelled, their descriptions are included in Egnyte’s search index. Searches for terms such as “caterpillar”, “tractor”,“excavator,” or “rebar” will surface matching images alongside other file types — no manual tagging required.

AI-Driven Document Summarization & Document Q&A in the iOS App

Egnyte’s AI-powered document summarization feature that utilizes cutting-edge large language models (LLMs) to synthesize content is available on the Egnyte iOS app.

Requirements

AI-Driven Document Summarization & Document Q&A is available to users who have version 8.27 (or higher) of the Egnyte iOS App. The most up to date version of the Egnyte app is available in the Apple App Store.

Steps to generate AI-prepared document summary

  • Access the Document - Open the document that needs to be summarized and go to its preview mode.
  • Initiate AI Interaction - Click on the Ask button to begin the process.
  • Generate Summary - On the subsequent screen, choose the Summarize this document button to produce a summary of the document.
  • Ask Questions - Alternatively, interact with the chat bot to inquire about specific details in the document. Users can either select from suggested questions or type their own.
  • The chat also supports voice input. The microphone icon in the chat field allows prompts to be spoken instead of typed. Spoken questions are transcribed in real time and appear in the prompt field for review and optional editing before being submitted. Recording automatically pauses after a brief period of silence and can be manually resumed as needed.
  • Voice input is currently supported in English only.
  • Provide Feedback - After receiving an answer, users can give feedback on its usefulness using the thumbs-up or thumbs-down icons.
  • Copy the summary or the response to a question to clipboard by tapping on the Copy icon. For responses to frequently asked questions refer to the AI-Driven Summarization & Q&A article.

Apple iWorks with the Egnyte Mobile Application

If you prefer working within Apple’s native iWork apps, like Pages, Numbers, and Keynote, you can easily create, open, and save these files directly to Egnyte. You can even open and edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from your Egnyte account in Apple’s iWork apps.

Below, we’ll show you how to get the most out of the iWorks apps with Egnyte.

Create a File in an iWork App and Save it to Egnyte

While the steps below are for creating a new Pages file, the steps should apply to any iWork file you’re creating.

  • Open the Pages app and tap Create Document.
  • Select a blank document or a template to make the new file.
  • When you’re ready to save your new Page document, tap the three dots in the top right corner and tap Share.
  • Tap the Copy to Egnyte option.
  • Select the folder you’d like to save the file. From here, you can change the name of the file or simply tap Upload to add the file to Egnyte.
Open Egnyte file in an iWork App

While the steps below are for opening an existing Egnyte file in Pages, the steps should apply to any iWork file you’re opening.

  • From the Egnyte app, navigate to the file you’d like to open in Pages and tap the file name to open a preview.
  • Tap the Actions/Open In icon and touch the Copy to Pages option.
  • A copy of the file will be downloaded and opened in the Pages app. Once you’re ready to save the file back to Egnyte, continue to the next section to learn more.
Save an iWork file to Egnyte

If you make changes in an iWorks app, you can push it back into your Egnyte account, so you have the latest version of the file.

The steps below are for saving a Pages file to Egnyte, but the steps should work for an iWork file you’re saving.

  • While you have the Pages document open, touch the three dots in the upper right corner of the app and tap Share.
  • Note: If you would like to save the file as a Word document, choose Export and select the Word format instead.
  • Tap the Copy to Egnyte option.
  • Choose where you’d like to save the file, rename the record, and touch Upload.
  • The file will automatically be added to the selected folder in Egnyte as the file type selected Please refer to this Apple Knowledge Base article for more information.

Co-editing with Google Docs on Mobile connects Egnyte Mobile Apps to Google Workspace to allow multiple users to edit a document simultaneously using the GDocs Software.

Requirements

Before collaborative authoring with Google Documents on mobile can be used, certain prerequisites must be met:

  • A device running a supported version of iOS or Android, either on a phone or tablet
  • Latest Egnyte iOS or Android App - check the latest Egnyte installers in the Apple AppStore and Google Play Store for more information
  • Google Workspace License - Users of Egnyte must have a Google Workspace account to change or edit their files.

Starting A Co-Editing Session From Egnyte Mobile App (iOS and Android)

Although the screenshots in this article are from the iOS app, the experience is nearly identical on Android. The layout and functionality of the Co-edit button and menu options work the same way on both platforms.

  • If a document is compatible with collaborative co-editing, and Google Workspace Integration is set up and added for the domain by an admin, a Co-edit button will appear in preview (or in the context (three dot) menu with the option to co-edit in the respective google app).
  • Click Co-edit to open the document and start a collaboration session. After the Co-edit button is clicked users will be redirected to the relevant Google app (Docs, Sheets, or Slides).
  • In the Google app, click on the edit (pencil) icon in the lower right corner of the screen.
  • Use the keyboard that appears to edit the document.

  • To return to the Egnyte app, click the Egnyte button.
  • To exit the Edit mode and remain in the Google app, click the Check Mark icon.

Co-Editing with Microsoft Office on Egnyte Mobile Apps

Co-editing with Microsoft Office on mobile integrates Egnyte Mobile Apps with Microsoft Office applications (such as Copilot 365, Word, Excel, or PowerPoint). This feature enables multiple users to edit the same document simultaneously using the Office software, facilitating seamless collaboration.

Requirements

Starting Co-Editing Session from Egnyte Mobile App (iOS and Android)

During Co-Editing Session and Saving Back to Egnyte

Sharing Co-Editing Session

Limitations and Known Issues

Requirements

The following requirements must be met to enable collaborative authoring with Microsoft Office on mobile devices:

  • Supported Device: A device running a supported version of iOS or Android, either on a phone or tablet.
  • Latest Egnyte Mobile App: The most recent version of the Egnyte iOS or Android app (for additional details, refer to the latest Egnyte installers in the Apple App Store and Google Play Store).
  • Microsoft Office Business License: An Office 365 account with a valid license (Example: Business, Business Premium, E3, E4, or E5) is necessary to edit or modify files.
  • Latest Microsoft Office Apps: The latest version of Microsoft Office apps (such as Copilot 365, Word, Excel, or PowerPoint) must be installed on the device and the user needs to be logged in.
  • Microsoft Office Desktop Enabled: Microsoft Office Desktop and Mobile integration must be enabled in the Egnyte Apps & Integrations page by the Egnyte domain administrator.
Back to Top…

Starting Co-Editing Session from Egnyte Mobile App (iOS and Android)

When a document is compatible with collaborative co-editing and Microsoft Office Integration has been configured for the domain, a Co-edit button will appear in the document preview or within the context menu (three dots) as Co-edit in [Microsoft Word] [Microsoft Excel] [Microsoft PowerPoint].

.

Selecting the Co-edit option initiates document checkout and starts a collaboration session. The user is redirected to the relevant Microsoft application where the document can be edited.

Back to Top…

During Co-Editing Session and Saving Back to Egnyte

If another user opens the document first, a Co-Edit icon (two people) will appear, indicating that the document is already open and being edited by someone else.

If the file is being co-edited by other users, their cursors and names will be visible in the document.

Once editing is complete, the Done (iOS) or Check Mark (Android) button can be tapped to exit the editing mode.

To return to Egnyte on iOS, the Back to Egnyte button should be selected. On Android devices, the native application switcher must be used to return to the Egnyte app.

When a co-editing session is active, the Rename, Delete, and Move options are disabled in both iOS and Android apps to prevent unintended file changes during collaboration.

In addition, an entry point for co-editing has been added in both iOS and Android apps when previewing a shared link to a Microsoft Office file, enabling a seamless transition into a live co-editing session.

Back to Top…

Sharing Co-Editing Session

Other users with correct permissions can also join the collaboration session from the Egnyte App to edit the document simultaneously by using Egnyte direct links.

Copying the direct link allows it to be shared with domain users who have Editor permissions for the folder where the file is located. When accessed, the File Preview will display a blue Co-Edit button, which, when clicked, enables participation in the co-editing session.

Back to Top…

Limitations and Known Issues

  • Multi-domain co-editing is not supported on mobile
  • Co-editing is only available when the device is connected to the Internet
  • Co-editing cannot be launched from Offline Tab files
  • While starting or joining a collaborative session, the Egnyte app will be moved to the background and should not be closed as it may cause some problems with document editing
  • Although all updates made to the document, sheet, or presentation are synced to the cloud, it may take some time before they can be seen in the preview screen in the Egnyte app. The Egnyte app shows a reminder about it in the preview mode.
  • Egnyte storage should add automatically in the relevant Microsoft app (after Microsoft Office Desktop and Mobile integration is enabled by the domain administrator) but in case it fails to appear in the iOS version of the App, users are advised to add it manually as described below:
    • Go to the Device (Example: iPhone) Settings.
    • Find the relevant Microsoft app in the list of apps (Example: Excel/PowerPoint/Word/Microsoft365) and tap on it.
    • Tap Reset at the bottom of the screen.
    • On the next screen, enable all the toggles.
    • Leave device Settings and go to the relevant Microsoft app (Example: Word).
    • The app will be signed out, and the data will be removed.
    • Sign in to the Microsoft app.
    • Tap on the Avatar icon (left upper corner).
    • Select Storage Accounts.
    • Egnyte storage should be visible, activate it.
    • Users need to repeat the above steps for all the Microsoft apps they want to use with Egnyte storage on mobile, for example both Word and Excel.

Conditional Access in the Egnyte for Intune iOS App

Starting with version 9.9 of the Egnyte for Intune iOS app, Conditional Access policies configured in Microsoft Entra ID are enforced both during sign-in and while the app is in active use. This article explains how Conditional Access works in the app, what users may experience, and what IT administrators can do to manage access.

Skip Ahead To…

What is Conditional Access?

When Conditional Access is Evaluated?

What Users See When Conditional Access Blocks Access

Impact Scenarios for IT Administrators

Admin Guidance: Managing Conditional Access Policies

Additional Information

What is Conditional Access?

Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that allows IT administrators to define rules governing when and how users can access organizational applications. These rules, called Conditional Access policies, can require that a user’s device is enrolled and compliant with company policies, that certain authentication apps are installed, or that sign-in comes from a specific network or location. For a full overview, see Microsoft’s Conditional Access documentation.

When Conditional Access is Evaluated?

In version 9.9 and higher for the Egnyte iOS for Intune Mobile App, Conditional Access policies are evaluated at two points:

At Sign-In

When a user signs in to the app for the first time, Microsoft’s authentication component (MSAL) checks whether any Conditional Access policies apply to the user. If a policy is in place and the user or device does not meet its requirements, sign-in is blocked before it completes. The user sees a message from Microsoft explaining what is required.

When Returning to the App from the Background

Each time the app is brought back to the foreground from the background, the app silently verifies that the user’s access is still permitted under current Conditional Access policies. This check happens automatically, with no action required from the user under normal circumstances. If an IT administrator changes a Conditional Access policy after a user has already signed in, for example, by adding a device compliance requirement, the next time that user opens the app from the background, the check will fail and the app will display an alert.

Back to Top ↑

What Users See When Conditional Access Blocks Access

During Sign-In

If a Conditional Access policy blocks a user at sign-in, a message from Microsoft is displayed. The most common messages and their meaning are:

  • Message “Install Microsoft Authenticator”: The organization’s Conditional Access policy requires the Microsoft Authenticator app to be present on the device. The user should install Microsoft Authenticator from the App Store and then attempt to sign in again
  • Message “Secure this device before you can access Egnyte” or “Your device needs to be managed”: The organization’s Conditional Access policy requires the device to be enrolled and managed through Microsoft Intune. The user should install the Microsoft Intune Company Portal app and enroll the device. If the user is unsure how to enroll, they should contact their IT administrator. For reference, Microsoft’s enrollment guidance for iOS devices is available at Microsoft websites. If after taking the appropriate steps the user is still blocked, they should contact their IT administrator, as the policy configuration may require changes.
During Active App Use

If a Conditional Access policy change causes a check to fail when the app is returned from the background, a notification is displayed within the app with two options:

  • Sign In Again: the user is taken through the Microsoft authentication step. If the Conditional Access requirement can be satisfied (for example, by authenticating via Microsoft Authenticator), sign-in completes and the user can continue using the app.
  • Remove Account: the user’s account is removed from the app and they are signed out. The next time the app is opened, the full sign-in flow is required. If the user closes the notification without selecting an option, it will reappear the next time the app is brought to the foreground.

Back to Top ↑

Impact Scenarios for IT Administrators

IT administrators should review their organization’s Conditional Access policies before users update to version 9.9 The following scenarios describe how different users may be affected.

  • Scenario 1: Users with no Conditional Access policies assigned
  • Users who are not subject to any Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID are not affected. They can continue using the app without any change to their experience.
  • Scenario 2: Users already signed in, Conditional Access policies assigned but previously not affecting active sessions
  • Users who are already signed in will not be signed out when they update the app. However, the next time they bring the app to the foreground after updating, the app will check whether current Conditional Access policies permit access. If a policy requires device compliance and the device is not compliant, the in-app alert described above will be displayed.
    • Admin Action: Before the release, administrators should review all Conditional Access policies that apply to Egnyte for Intune iOS app users and ensure that the policies reflect the intended scope. Users who are not intended to be subject to a given policy should be excluded from it before the update reaches them.
  • Scenario 3: Users signing in for the first time after updating, no blocking policies
  • New users or users signing in for the first time are guided through the updated sign-in flow. If no Conditional Access policies block them, the flow completes normally. See Signing in to the Egnyte for Intune iOS App for a step-by-step description.
  • Scenario 4: Users signing in for the first time after updating, blocking policies in place
  • If a Conditional Access policy blocks a user at the point of Microsoft authentication during sign-in, the user sees a Microsoft-generated message and cannot complete sign-in. The messages and recommended user actions are described in the section above.
    • Admin Action: If users are unexpectedly blocked, the administrator should identify which policy is blocking them (visible in the Microsoft Entra admin center under Conditional Access Sign-in logs) and determine whether the policy is correctly scoped.
  • Scenario 5: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) users with Conditional Access policies not intended for unmanaged devices
  • Users with personally-owned devices (BYOD) may be subject to Conditional Access policies that were configured for corporate-owned managed devices. If such a policy requires device enrollment or compliance and the personal device is not enrolled, the user will be blocked.
    • Admin Action: If BYOD users are not intended to be subject to device compliance requirements, they should be excluded from the relevant Conditional Access policy. See the admin guidance section below. Back to Top ↑

Admin Guidance: Managing Conditional Access Policies

Excluding Users or Groups from a Policy

To prevent specific users from being affected by a Conditional Access policy, IT administrators can add them to the exclusion list of that policy. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, navigate to Protection > Conditional Access, open the relevant policy, and under Users > Exclude, add the users or a security group containing them. The exclude setting overrides the included setting, excluded users will not be subject to that policy regardless of other assignments.

Microsoft recommends creating a dedicated security group for exclusions to make ongoing management easier. See Manage users excluded from Conditional Access policies for guidance including a process for regularly reviewing exclusions.

Ensuring a Device is Enrolled and Compliant

If a Conditional Access policy requires device compliance, the user’s device must be enrolled in Microsoft Intune and marked as compliant by Intune’s compliance policies. The user enrolls their iOS device through the Microsoft Intune Company Portal app. Once enrolled, Intune evaluates the device against the organization’s compliance policies and marks it as compliant or non-compliant accordingly.

For administrator guidance on setting up device enrollment and compliance policies, see device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune and iOS or iPadOS device enrollment guide for Microsoft Intune.

Verifying Which Policy is Blocking a User

Blocked sign-in events are visible in the Microsoft Entra admin center under Users > Sign-in logs or Conditional Access > Insights and reporting. Each blocked event shows which policy applied and which condition was not met, making it straightforward to identify and address the root cause.

Configuring Mobile Device Entitlement for Egnyte for Intune on BYOD Devices

The Egnyte for Intune iOS app can receive the Mobile Device Entitlement token through an Intune App Configuration Policy for Managed apps. The token reaches the app through the Intune SDK, so it works on Bring Your Own Devices (BYOD) and managed devices without Company Portal or MDM enrollment of the device.

Requirements

The configuration requires the following:

  • Egnyte for Intune iOS app, version 9.11.1 or later
  • Mobile Device Entitlement enabled for the Egnyte domain, with a Mobile Device Entitlement token generated
  • Access to the Microsoft Intune admin center with permission to create app configuration policies

Creating the App Configuration Policy

The policy is created in the Microsoft Intune admin center under Apps > App configuration policies > Create > Managed apps. A name and description are defined on the first screen, for example, Egnyte for Intune app configuration.

Under Public apps, Egnyte for Intune is selected as the target app. In Settings > General configuration settings, a single name or value pair carries the token:

Name

Value

deviceEntitlementToken

The Mobile Device Entitlement token generated for the domain

The policy is then assigned to the users or groups that should receive it. Intune confirms with the message Configuration saved once the policy is reviewed and saved.

What Users Experience

Once the policy is assigned, no additional steps are required from users. When a user signs in to Egnyte for Intune, the app enrolls the user in Intune as part of the login flow. The Intune SDK passes the token to the app, and the app recognizes the entitlement and completes the setup.

Restricting the Regular Egnyte App

The policy delivers the token only to Egnyte for Intune. The regular Egnyte iOS app does not receive it. With Mobile Device Entitlement enabled and access from unmanaged devices not allowed in the domain settings, administrators can therefore allow Egnyte for Intune on BYOD phones or tablets that are not MDM-enrolled while restricting sign-in from the regular Egnyte app.

Differences Between the Egnyte for Intune iOS App and the Regular Egnyte iOS App

This article describes the differences between the Egnyte iOS app and its counterpart dedicated for use with Microsoft Intune.

Important: With the upgrade to the Intune SDK (Version 21.0.0), a new App Registration requirement has been enforced. This change will eventually cause users who authenticated on previous app versions to be prompted for a mandatory re-authentication (sign-in again):

-Reason for Prompt: When a user’s current valid session expires, the app will be unable to silently refresh the access token, which forces a sign-in. The timing of this is governed by the organization’s Intune policy settings (Offline Grace Period).

-Required User Action: Immediate re-authentication is required when the sign-in prompt appears.

-Consequence of Delay: Failure to sign back in or ignoring the prompt beyond the period defined by the organization’s policy may result in a selective wipe of the Egnyte data within the app.

The Egnyte for Intune app offers enhanced security via app protection policies, ensuring a seamless login experience. There are several limitations to consider when choosing the appropriate version of the Egnyte iOS app for your team, as outlined below.

  • The Egnyte for Intune app is updated quarterly, while the regular Egnyte iOS app receives updates several times each quarter. As a result, new features in the regular app appear in the Intune app after the next scheduled update. Each Intune app release includes all features added to the regular app since the previous update. For detailed functionality differences, please refer to the latest release notes.
  • There are a few permanent differences and limitations in functionality in the Egnyte for Intune app:
    • Unsupported Features:
      • The File Provider extension, which integrates with the iOS Files app, is not supported in the Intune version.
      • Google Docs integration — the ability to open, edit and co-edit Google-native documents — is not supported in the Intune version of the Egnyte app. As a result, Google Docs files stored in Egnyte cannot be directly edited or co-edited from within the Intune app.
    • Conditional Features:
      • Image Markups: Disabled by default but can be enabled if the ‘Send organizational data to other apps’ setting is configured as ‘All apps’ in the Intune app protection policy.
      • Siri and Shortcuts: The availability of Siri voice commands and Shortcuts is determined by the Microsoft Intune administrator.
        • If the admin has permitted Siri and Shortcuts in the App Protection Policy (MAM) or Device Restriction settings, these features will be fully accessible.
        • If these features are restricted by organizational policy, voice-enabled actions and shortcuts will not be available within the app
  • Using both the regular and Intune app concurrently could pose potential challenges due to shared URL schemes and isn’t recommended and supported.

Document Scanner - iOS App

The Egnyte iOS app features a powerful document scanner that provides an efficient and user-friendly scanning experience. This guide provides an overview of using the document scanner and the available controls to help optimize scans.

Getting Started

Accessing the Document Scanner
  • Open the Egnyte iOS App.
  • Tap the +Create or Upload button at the bottom of the screen.
  • Select Scan Document from the available options.

Scanning Your Document

Auto Scanning and Manual Scanning
  • Auto Scanning: The scanner automatically detects and captures the document as soon as it’s in view, ensuring a quick and seamless process.
  • Manual Scanning: If manual control is preferred, the Auto button should be tapped to change the mode to Manual. In the manual mode, clicking the Scan button will capture the document.
Available Controls

The following controls are available to adjust the scanning process:

Flash Settings

  • Auto: The flash is used automatically based on lighting conditions.

  • On: The flash is always on for every scan.

  • Off: The flash is disabled. Color Options

  • Color: Captures the document in full color.

  • Grayscale: Converts the document to shades of gray.

  • Black & White: Provides a high-contrast black-and-white version of the document.

  • Photo: Optimizes the scan for photos, preserving color and detail.

Adjusting the Scan

Once a document is captured, adjustments can be made to the scanned pages by tapping the scanned page thumbnail button in the left lower corner

The following adjustments are available:

  • Dragging Corners: drag the corners to manually adjust the document’s borders, ensuring it’s aligned correctly.
  • Color Settings: select Color, Greyscale, Black & White, or Photo to apply the desired color pattern.
  • Rotate: tap the Rotate icon to set the scanned page to the desired orientation.
  • Delete: tap the Trash icon to delete the scanned page.
Managing Pages
  • Swipe Pages: Swipe left or right to move between pages.
  • Multi-page View: View all scanned pages in a grid layout for easy navigation.
  • Add Page: Tap this option to scan additional pages into the same document.
  • Rotate: Rotate the scanned page to the desired orientation.
  • Delete: Remove the selected page from the document.
Saving A Scan
  • Tap the Save button (which is available both on the Scanning Screen and on the Scanned Document screen).
  • Hitting Save on the Scanning Screen will redirect to the Scanned Document screen, where last minute changes can be made to the file such as:
    • adding a page
    • deleting
    • rotating
  • Selecting Add a Page allows choosing how to add a new page: either by using the Camera or by selecting an image from the Photos app.
  • Enter a name for the scanned document when prompted and hit Save. The scan will be saved as a PDF file.
Extracting Text from a Scanned Document
  • Navigate to the desired folder
  • Tap the +Create or Upload button at the bottom of the screen
  • Select Extract Text from the available options
  • Position the camera in front of a document or image containing text
  • Once the text is recognized and highlighted, tap the capture button to proceed
Saving the Extracted Text to a Document
  • Long-press the extracted text and highlight the desired selection
  • From the context menu, choose Text File
  • When the text file opens, click Save
  • On the next screen, you can:
    • Rename the file by clicking the three-dot menu and then Rename
    • Clicking Change folder to change the destination folder
  • Click Upload to save the file
Additional Options for Extracted Text

Long-press the extracted text to display the context menu with additional actions

Use the arrows or swipe the menu to explore the following options:

  • Copy: Copy the text to the clipboard
  • Select All: Highlight the entire extracted text
  • Look Up: Display a dictionary definition (when a single word is selected), or show Siri-suggested websites and related resources (when multiple words are selected)
  • Translate: Instantly translate the text into selected languages
  • Search Web: Activate the default browser to search for the highlighted text
  • Share: Share the text using native sharing options

Best Practices for Scanning Documents

  • Background: If possible, use a solid, contrasting background for the document to enhance edge detection and clarity..
  • The Document: Ideally, the document should be flat and smooth, with no creases or curled edges.
  • Document Placement: Place the document flat and keep the camera parallel to avoid distortions.
  • Lighting: Bright, even lighting without shadows or glare is recommended for optimal scan quality.

Extend the office through your mobile device and work from anywhere with ease. Collaborate seamlessly with internal and external users and boost your organization’s productivity. The Egnyte mobile app supports iOS and Android platforms for phones and tablets. Access your data, preview files and folders, upload new content, and collaborate through shared folders and file links when you want, wherever you are. Take a deeper look at Egnyte’s mobile application in this summary.

Access Files on the Road

Navigate to folders easily and preview folders and files in a gallery experience. Quickly access files you’ve been working on from anywhere in Your Recent Files. Load any file ranging from large images to Microsoft Office documents onto your device - faster and easier than ever before.

Share Folders

Limitations

File Size Limitations

For the most part, Egnyte mobile apps have the same file size limitations as all other Egnyte cloud storage access points. That being said, mobile devices have significantly less powerful hardware components than laptops and desktops. Depending on the configuration of your mobile device (especially Android devices) and what is running on your mobile device’s background, performance and failure cases will vary.

Watch our quick video at Egnyte University to get a quick overview of how to use the mobile app.

Preview Limitation for Links with ‘Download’ Disabled

Files shared via links with download restrictions or in folders with download disabled cannot currently be previewed in the mobile app. Users can preview these files through the web UI instead. iOS support for these previews is anticipated in January 2025.

Egnyte Sign on Mobile

Egnyte Sign makes it easy to sign documents that have been sent with a Signature Request. This article provides guidance on signing documents using the Egnyte Mobile App. The screens on the left show the iOS app interface and the ones on the right, the Android one.

Egnyte Sign on Mobile - Requirements

Egnyte Sign on mobile is available to users who have version 8.31 (or higher) of the Egnyte iOS App and 8.52 (or higher) of the Egnyte Android App. The Signatures tab is available from version 9.11 (or higher).

The most up to date versions of the Egnyte apps are available in the Apple App Store (iOS) and Google Play Store (Android).

Signing Documents on Mobile

The signing process can be started in two ways: by tapping Review & sign in a signature request email, or by tapping a pending request directly in the Signatures tab. When starting from the Signatures tab, the app opens the document preview screen directly — steps 2 and 3 below apply from that point. When starting from email, all steps apply.

Starting from the Signatures Tab

The Signatures tab (available from the More menu) gives users a central place to view and act on pending signature requests assigned to them.

Tapping any pending request opens the document preview screen directly within the app, at which point the signing flow continues from step 2 below.

The tab displays requests assigned to the user and can be filtered by status: All, In Progress, Completed, Declined, and Canceled. Requests created or sent by the user are not shown in this view.

Starting from Email
  • Click on Review & sign button in the signature request e-mail.
  • When redirected to the Egnyte mobile app, accept the following agreements to continue:
    • Electronic Record and Signature Disclosure.
    • Egnyte’s Privacy Policy.
  • This step is needed to make the signature legally binding.
  • On the document preview screen, find the fields assigned to the designated user by scrolling through the document. Use the arrows to navigate to other fields (for example; signature, name, role).
  • Click each field to enter a value. When multiple signature or initial fields are filled, the app automatically populates subsequent fields with the most recently used entry to reduce repetition.
    • The signature field allows drawing, typing, and uploading signatures from the Photos gallery. The initials can be drawn or typed.
    • Text-based fields allow typing a value, and signature date fields are automatically populated and cannot be edited.
    • Checkboxes allow for individual or multi-select option toggling, while radio buttons ensure that only a single option can be selected within a specific group.
  • The signature and initials input screens are supported in portrait mode only.
  • Once all required fields are filled, click the Submit button in the right upper corner of the screen to complete the signing process.
  • Upon signing the document, a confirmation message will be displayed, and the document will be securely saved.
  • Once all signers have signed the document, the requester of the signature will receive an email with a link to a signed PDF copy of the document. They can click View signed document button to access a page with a preview of the signed document. Egnyte Sign on Mobile currently redirects signature requests requiring enhanced compliance - such as qualified (Part 11-compatible) signatures - or requests containing multiple documents to the mobile browser. On iOS, requests containing multiple documents are also redirected to the mobile browser. This ensures these signatures are completed in the appropriate browser-based workflow.

Multi-Document Signature Requests on Android

Multi-document signature requests are completed within the Android app instead of in a browser. The signing view presents the documents of the request in sequence with a progress indicator. The following field types are supported: signature, initials, date, text, checkbox, and radio button. A single consent confirmation is shown per request.

Completing multi-document signature requests in the Android app requires version 9.12 or higher.

Egnyte’s AI Assistant on Egnyte Mobile iOS App

Egnyte’s AI Assistant on Egnyte iOS mobile app provides an AI-powered conversational interface grounded in a company’s data. It enables employees to ask questions in natural language and receive contextually relevant answers based on the content stored within their organization’s Egnyte environment.

AI Assistant uses Egnyte’s enterprise-grade security and access controls, ensuring that responses remain aligned with permissions, file access, and organizational data safeguards. It is designed to help teams quickly locate information, summarize documents, and understand content while working on the go.

Accessing AI Assistant on Mobile

An Ask Me Anything button has been added to most screens, providing a quick and convenient way to open AI Assistant as needed.

AI Assistant can also be opened from search. When a multi-word query is better suited for the AI Assistant than for a file search, an Ask Assistant suggestion appears in search, and selecting it opens the AI Assistant with the query already filled in. For more information, see Searching in the Egnyte iOS App.

Using AI Assistant

When the AI Assistant interface is open, two conversational modes are available:

AI Assistant (All Company Data)

This mode uses all accessible company content as the foundation for generating responses. It aligns with the user’s permission set, ensuring that results reflect only the data that the user is allowed to see.

On mobile, this is always the default behaviour. Folder-level or file-level source selection is not supported in the current version.

Knowledge Bases

Knowledge Bases (KBs) provide responses based solely on the content stored within a specific KB folder.

Switching to a Knowledge Base allows the conversation to be grounded in a curated set of documents chosen by the organization.

Features Supported in the iOS Mobile App

The initial mobile release includes core conversational functionality:

  • Source and Model Selector
  • Source and Model Selection allows greater control over how responses are generated. In addition to Egnyte content (which is always included), optional web sources can be enabled, and a single large language model can be selected from the supported models to power the conversation. Gemini-2.5 Flash is the model selected by default. The model selector is also available in the Document AI feature for domains with AI Add-on plan.
  • AI Connectors: The AI Connectors source selector allows users to view and manage which external app connectors (example, Slack, Outlook, or Salesforce) AI Assistant draws from when responding to prompts. When multiple connectors are active, AI Assistant combines insights from Egnyte content and all enabled external sources to deliver richer, cross-platform answers.
  • Connectors must first be configured on the Egnyte web app, in the AI Assistant chat, the + button provides access to the connector setup flow. Once a connector has been added on web, it becomes available on mobile. To ensure the mobile app reflects newly added connectors, the app must be sent to the background or fully closed and relaunched.
  • On mobile, individual connectors can be toggled on or off from the AI Connectors selector to control which ones AI Assistant uses in a given conversation.
    • Connector setup and management is available exclusively through the Egnyte web AI Hub.
    • The AI Connector selectors are only visible if the user has at least one connector configured on the Egnyte web app. If no connectors have been set up, the selector does not appear on mobile.
  • Voice input: A microphone icon is available within supported chats. When activated, speech is transcribed in real time, with a waveform visual indicating active recording. If a pause longer than three seconds occurs, recording automatically stops, and transcription remains available for review and optional editing. Recording may be manually resumed as needed (by tapping on the microphone icon), and the prompt can then be submitted through the standard submission control.
  • AI-generated suggestions at the start of each chat.
  • Prompt Library
  • The Prompt Library allows users to access and insert high-quality, pre-defined prompts directly from the AI Assistant input area. Prompts can be filtered by Type, Task Categories, Job Types, and Document Types. Users can also mark specific prompts as favorites for quick access on the go.
  • Web Links in AI Assistant Sources
  • When web links are included as sources, the referenced content can be opened by clicking on them, enabling seamless access to external information in AI Assistant responses.
  • Improve prompt to help refine the questions in the input field for clarity, focus, and effectiveness.
  • New chat to reset the conversation and begin a new thread and Chat history to return to previous conversations.
  • Feedback controls (thumbs up / thumbs down) for rating responses.
  • Copy response to easily share or re-use AI Assistant output.
  • Share Chat to generate a shareable link for any AI Assistant conversation directly from the mobile app. The link can be sent to colleagues via email or any messaging app.
  • Recipients who are authenticated on the same Egnyte domain can open the link in the Egnyte app to view the full conversation transcript. From there, the conversation opens as a new, independent AI Assistant session in the recipient’s own account, allowing them to continue the thread privately, without affecting the original chat.
  • Shared links are accessible only to users authenticated on the same Egnyte domain. Recipients outside the domain cannot open the conversation.

GCC High Tenant Support in the Egnyte for Intune iOS App

Starting with version 9.9 of the Egnyte for Intune iOS app, users whose organizations operate on a Microsoft Government Community Cloud High (GCC High) tenant can access Egnyte through the app. This article explains what GCC High tenant support means and how users and administrators can get started.

What is GCC High?

Microsoft’s Government Community Cloud High (GCC High) is a dedicated cloud environment designed for US government agencies and organizations that handle controlled unclassified information (CUI), International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) data, or Department of Defense (DoD) requirements. GCC High operates on separate Microsoft infrastructure and uses a distinct Microsoft identity platform endpoint compared to the commercial cloud.

For more information on Microsoft GCC High, see Microsoft’s documentation on government cloud environments.

Signing in as a GCC High User

From version 9.9, a GCC High user’s sign-in experience is as follows:

  • Welcome Screen
  • When the app is opened for the first time after installation, the welcome screen presents two options. GCC High users should select GCC High user?. Selecting Continue instead will attempt authentication against the commercial Microsoft tenant and will fail for GCC High accounts.
  • Microsoft Authentication
  • After selecting GCC High user?, the app proceeds to Microsoft authentication using the GCC High tenant configuration. Authentication is handled through the Microsoft Authenticator app (if installed) or through an in-app browser. The user signs in with their GCC High Microsoft account.
  • Intune Enrollment and App Restart
  • After successful Microsoft authentication, the app enrolls with Microsoft Intune using the GCC High tenant configuration. Once enrollment is complete, a notification is displayed prompting a restart. The user taps the button in the notification, which closes the app. The app does not reopen automatically — the user must tap the app icon on the device home screen to reopen it.
  • Egnyte Login
  • After reopening the app, the standard Egnyte login screen is displayed. The user signs in with their Egnyte credentials to complete the process.

Conditional Access for GCC High Users

Conditional Access policies configured in the GCC High Microsoft Entra environment are enforced during sign-in and on every return from the background, consistent with the behavior described for commercial users.

If an organization uses Conditional Access policies in the GCC High Microsoft Entra environment, the admin should ensure that the policies are correctly scoped before users update to version 9.9.1. See Conditional Access in the Egnyte for Intune iOS App for the full impact scenarios and admin guidance.

How to Download Files and Folders Using Egnyte Mobile Apps

Downloading files and folders in the Egnyte mobile apps allows you to access your important content on the go. This article provides a guide on how to download files and folders using the Egnyte mobile apps on iOS and Android devices. It also covers additional features and controls available to domain admins for managing user access to downloads.

Skip Ahead to…

Local Storage Settings

Offline Access

Downloading Files to iOS and Android Apps

Dedicated Download Option in the Android App

Drag and Drop on iPads and iPhones

Admin Controls for Download Access

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Local Storage Settings

When Device Storage is enabled by an administrator at the domain level, users can set up local storage parameters in the mobile application’s settings.

Local storage can be enabled by turning on the storage toggle. An additional option is available to automatically save downloaded files for offline access.

Memory can be allocated for local storage, with options for 2 GB, 10 GB, or unlimited space.

Users can also set a timeframe for when locally saved files will be automatically deleted.

In the File Size Warning section, different alert values can be set for cellular and Wi-Fi networks. Warnings can be configured for files over 100 MB or 500 MB, or the feature can be turned off completely. For wifi networks, warnings can be set for files over 1 GB or 2 GB, or the feature can be turned off.

Offline Access

To ensure access to files even when offline, files or folders can be marked for offline use. When marked, the selected files are downloaded to a device’s storage, making them accessible through the Egnyte app interface. This feature is particularly useful when working with files while offline.

Downloading Files to iOS and Android Apps

In both the iOS and Android apps, files can be saved to various locations supported by a device’s operating system. To do this, open the desired file and tap the Share button. From there, files can be saved to native file systems like the iOS Files App or the Gallery App on Android, as well as other supported locations.

Dedicated Download Option in the Android App

The Egnyte Android app provides a dedicated Download option. This feature allows for the selection and download of specific files and folders to a device’s default storage.

Drag and Drop on iPads and iPhones

iPad users can take advantage of the drag-and-drop functionality to move files between applications and storage by dragging and dropping them in the split screen view.

Admin Controls for Download Access

Domain admins have control over user access to downloads. They can configure download settings to align with security and compliance requirements using the following options:

  • Enable or disable device storage. When device storage is enabled, users can download files for offline access. When device storage is enabled, admins can also set up the time after which files marked for offline use are automatically deleted. They can allow encrypted storage only and decide if folder downloads will be allowed, too.
  • Use the Delete the locally stored data on the mobile device option to remove the marked for offline files from the device storage.
  • Leverage mobile device management (MDM) solutions like Microsoft Intune to enforce device-level policies that restrict or control downloading files on managed devices. By utilizing these administrative controls, admins can tailor the download capabilities within the Egnyte mobile app based on their organization’s requirements and security considerations.

The available functionalities may vary based on the device’s operating system version and app updates.

Additional Resources

How to Download Files and Folders using Egnyte WebUI

How to Download Files and Folders using Egnyte Desktop Apps

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can I Download Multiple Files or Folders at Once in the Egnyte Mobile Apps?

Yes, you can use the dedicated “Download” option to select and download specific files and folders in the Egnyte Android app. In iOS, you can leverage the Files app in which you can select multiple files and folders and copy them to another location including your device storage.

Is There a Limit to the Number or Size of Files I Can Download in the Egnyte Mobile Apps?

The ability to download files and folders in the Egnyte mobile apps may be subject to certain limitations, such as the available storage space on your device or any restrictions imposed by your organization’s policies. Check your device’s storage capacity and consult your organization’s guidelines for any specific limitations.

Can I Choose the Destination Folder on My Device when Downloading Files in the Egnyte Mobile Apps?

The Egnyte mobile apps typically allow you to save files to various locations supported by your device’s operating system. When downloading files, you can choose options such as saving to the iOS Files App or Gallery App on Android. However, the specific destination folder selection may depend on the capabilities of your device.

Is There a Way to Schedule Automatic Downloads of Files or Folders in the Egnyte Mobile Apps?

The Egnyte mobile apps do not have a built-in feature for scheduling automatic downloads.

Can I Customize the Offline Access Settings for Individual Files or Folders?

The offline access settings in the Egnyte mobile apps generally apply to files or folders as a whole. You can mark files or folders for offline use, but you may not have granular control over customizing the offline access settings for individual files or folders.

How to Enable Smart Upload in the iOS Egnyte App

What is Smart Upload?

Smart Upload is a feature available in the Egnyte Mobile Apps that automatically scans the device photo library and finds photographs taken in places matching the ones specified in Projects and, with the user’s permission, uploads the photographs to Egnyte. It saves the users all the manual work they would otherwise need to do copying the pictures from the device photo library into their Egnyte folders.

How to Enable and Start Using Automatic Smart Upload?

Create and Set Up Projects

To use Smart Upload, first create a Project using the Web UI or the mobile app or navigate to an existing Project. Projects are a special kind of folders for which admins can define parameters such as project start and end date, logo, ID, customer name, current status, as well as its address and geolocation.

Add Geolocation for the Project
  • Navigate to the Project
  • Go to Project Settings
    • In the WebUI, Project Settings are available from the More button
    • In the Mobile Apps, Project Settings can be accessed from the three dot menu in the right upper corner of the screen
  • Select the Smart Upload Folder (WebUI) or Smart Upload (Mobile) tab and click the Add Location button
  • Smart Upload only supports a single location per project.
  • On the next screen:
    • Use the interactive map or the Search option to find the location
    • Set the radius using the slider
    • Add the Location Name
    • Change the Upload Folder (if needed)
Set Up the Mobile Device

After a Project and its respective Upload Folder is configured, the mobile devices will need to be prepared. To do so:

  • Allow the camera to access the device location and photo library as pictures are taken in the Settings
  • Go to Settings -> Location Services -> Camera, select While Using the App, and turn on Precise Location
  • Allow the Egnyte App to access the relevant information on his device such as the location and photos library
  • Go to Settings, find Egnyte on the list of apps and select it. Allow Egnyte to access Location (Always), and to access Photos (Full Access) These settings can also be modified when prompted by the app if not enabled already.
Start Taking Photographs

When all the set-up is ready, a user can start leveraging the Smart Upload feature on the mobile device. To start using Smart Upload:

  • Go to one or more locations which match those setup in Projects and take some photographs
  • Launch the Egnyte app and watch for a New Smart Upload suggestion notification at the bottom of the screen
  • Tap on it and it will be redirected to the Smart Upload screen
  • A user can also dismiss the notification and navigate to the Smart Upload icon on the bottom bar later.
Review, Confirm or Reject Smart Upload Suggestions
  • In the Smart Upload screen, upload suggestions can be confirmed to upload the detected images or photos can be reviewed and selected individually for upload. Photos will automatically be uploaded to the relevant Project or Upload folders
  • Each upload is confirmed with a Success notification
  • The Smart Upload icon at the bottom of the Egnyte app screen will always show the number of pending upload suggestions

How to Get Access to Smart Upload?

Smart Upload is available within Enterprise Lite and Enterprise pricing plans, or when purchasing the Project Hub.

Downloads

Customers who want to use Smart Upload are requested to make sure that they have the latest version of the Egnyte mobile apps installed or upgrade to the latest version. The latest version of the app is available in the Apple App Store.

Image Editor in the Egnyte iOS App

The Egnyte iOS mobile app enables users to mark up images and to add text, stickers, hand drawings, and more to JPG, PNG, and HEIC files. Users can add their annotations seamlessly without leaving the Egnyte app. Mark-up changes can be saved by overwriting the existing file or as a new file.

Image Markups (iOS)

Egnyte iOS App users on Platform Pricing Plans can now utilize the capabilities of the Markup Tool, a robust enhancement introduced in version 8.26. This feature empowers users with a range of powerful actions that can be performed on images, including:

  • Adding Text: to enhance documents with textual annotations for clear communication and context.
  • Adding a Sticker: to highlight key points in the files.
  • Adding a Signature: to streamline the approval process and maintain a professional touch.
  • Adding a Shape: to emphasize specific areas or elements in the files by incorporating various shapes.
  • Drawing with Drawing Tools (Pen, Marker): to visually highlight, annotate, and convey ideas using versatile tools like a pen or marker.
  • Drawing Straight Lines with the Ruler: to draw lines and shapes with precision and accuracy.
  • Erasing: to correct and refine annotations by erasing unwanted elements.
  • Moving Freehand Drawings with the Lasso Tool: to arrange freehand drawings by moving them.
  • Changing Colors and Opacity: to further enhance and personalize the drawings. The Image Markups feature can be accessed from the file preview screen by tapping on the blue Edit button and selecting the Markups icon on the next screen.

The drawing tools, the eraser, the ruler and the lasso can be selected by tapping on their icons in the bottom toolbar. The list of additional tools (including adding stickers, text, signature, and shape) can be expanded by tapping on the Plus button in the toolbar.

When a shape, a sticker, or a signature is added, it can be resized and dragged to a different place on the image. Shapes, signatures, and text can also be recoloured.

The screen below shows the tools for editing an inserted object.

Text can be further edited by changing its font type, size, and alignment. It can be bolded, italicized, underlined, and struck through. All the added elements can be cut, copied, duplicated, and deleted.

The eraser comes in two versions: the Pixel Eraser and the Object Eraser. The right type of eraser can be picked by tapping on the eraser icon after it has been selected. The Pixel Eraser is designed to scrub over mistakes made with a finger, and the Object Eraser to remove objects (such as shapes or drawings) by touching them with a finger.

The lasso can be applied to highlight markups or groups of markups in order to drag them to a different position or to cut, copy, delete, or duplicate them.

Undo and redo buttons positioned at the top of the screen can be used to revert or repeat the markup actions.

When the markups are ready, the marked up image can be saved in two ways. On tapping on Done, the user is presented with two options: to save the modified image as a new file (Save As) or to save the existing file with the markups (Save).

Cropping and Rotating

Users can also crop and rotate images. The cropping and rotating mode can be accessed by clicking on the Image adjustment icon in the lower left corner of the screen from within the file preview.

The flip and rotate icons can be accessed from the next screen and the cropping tool can be initiated by touching and holding to any corners of the image.

Image Markups Tool Access Criteria

To access the Image Markups Tool, make sure you are on one of the Platform Pricing Plans and that you use version 8.26 or higher. The latest version of the app is always available in the Apple AppStore.

Intune and Egnyte Mobile Apps

This article describes how Egnyte’s mobile apps and Microsoft Intune can be used together for device entitlement, app deployment, and enhanced security. The FAQs clarify the key building blocks of the Microsoft Intune and Egnyte mobile apps blend. The references include links to detailed setup and configuration guides.

Microsoft Intune and Egnyte Mobile Apps

Microsoft Intune is one of the most powerful Mobile Device Management (MDM) and Mobile Application Management (MAM) solutions, enabling seamless device enrollment, configuration, policy enforcement, and control over applications. It can be used with Egnyte Mobile Apps for

  • Device Entitlement
  • Application Deployment
  • Setting Up and Managing Protection Policies.

Using Microsoft Intune for Device Entitlement

In addition to purchasing the Egnyte Device Control package, a configuration policy for enrolling managed devices can be created in the Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager. Before creating a policy in Intune, an admin must enable the Mobile Device Entitlement feature from WebUI and generate the Mobile Device Entitlement Token.

  • Before creating a policy in Intune, an admin must enable the Mobile Device Entitlement feature from WebUI and generate the Mobile Device Entitlement Token.

  • Once saved, the token will not re-appear. Be sure to securely save this token

Next, create an App Configuration policy in the Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager.

When the Configuration key is requested, set the Configuration key to deviceEntitlementToken and enter the Mobile Device Entitlement Token generated in the Egnyte Web UI Device Control panel as the Configuration value.

On the next screens, users or groups of users will need to be assigned the policy.

Organizations that use Intune for device entitlement only are recommended to consider the regular version of the Egnyte mobile apps.

Using Intune for Application Deployment

The Egnyte mobile apps can be easily deployed on Intune-managed devices so that employees can access their files while sticking to the security rules set by Intune. Organizations that use Intune for application deployment only are recommended to consider the regular version of the Egnyte mobile apps.

For detailed guidelines regarding the deployment process, refer to Microsoft Intune.

Using Intune with Protection Policies

In a more advanced scenario, protection rules including passcode requirements, encryption settings, restrictions on data sharing, and more can be created and assigned using Intune.

Organizations that use Intune with protection policies should choose the Egnyte for Intune version of the app (available for iOS only).

The Egnyte for Intune (iOS) app requires an app protection policy to be both created and assigned to users in Microsoft Intune. A policy that exists but has not been assigned to the relevant users will not take effect, and users without an assigned policy will not be able to log in to the app. Each user who needs access to the Egnyte for Intune app must be included in the assignment of an active app protection policy. The policy must be assigned to a user group — assigning it to a device group will not work, as app protection policies in Microsoft Intune apply to groups of users, not devices.

Detailed guidelines on creating and assigning app protection policies are available on the Microsoft Intune website.

FAQs

What is the Difference Between the Egnyte (Regular) iOS App and the Egnyte for Intune iOS App?

The Egnyte for Intune iOS app is specifically tailored to work in conjunction with Microsoft Intune’s mobile application management capabilities.

  • It includes additional features and integrations that align with Intune’s policies, enhancing security and control over how the app interacts with sensitive data.
  • Egnyte for Intune supports app protection policies enforced by Intune, which can include requirements for passcodes, biometric authentication, data encryption, and restrictions on data sharing between the app and other applications.
  • This version of the app provides a more granular control over app behavior and security settings
Can the Egnyte Android App Be Used with Microsoft Intune?

While Egnyte doesn’t offer an Android app wrapped up in the Intune SDK, you can still use the Egnyte Android app in conjunction with Microsoft Intune to manage device entitlement and application deployment.

Is There a Distinction in Functionality Between the Egnyte for Intune iOS App and Its Regular Counterpart?

While the Intune app introduces enhanced security through app protection policies, which are crucial for seamless login experiences, there are certain aspects to note. Specifically,

  • features like the File Provider extension, which integrates with the iOS Files app, and the Google Docs integration, are not supported in the Egnyte for Intune app
  • using both the regular and Intune app concurrently could pose potential challenges due to shared URL schemes and isn’t recommended and supported
  • the Egnyte for Intune app is updated less frequently than the regular app, which may result in new features being added with a delay of up to a few months in comparison to the regular app. To learn more about differences between the Egnyte for Intune iOS App and the Regular Egnyte iOS App, click here.
What Do I Need in Order to Use Intune as MAM/MDM?

To use Microsoft Intune as Mobile Application Management (MAM) and Mobile Device Management (MDM) tool, you’ll need an active subscription to Microsoft Intune and the compatible devices (such as smartphones and tablets) that you want to manage.

What is Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager?

Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager is Intune admin interface designed to simplify and enhance the management of devices and applications within an organization’s IT infrastructure. It combines mobile device management (MDM), mobile application management (MAM), and PC management capabilities into a single platform. The goal of Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager is to provide a unified approach to managing endpoints, which includes mobile devices, computers, and other devices, regardless of their location.

What is Company Portal in the Context of Intune?

In the context of Microsoft Intune, the “Company Portal” refers to a dedicated app that provides users with a centralized hub for accessing corporate resources, applications, and settings on their managed devices. It’s essentially an application that allows employees to interact with their organization’s IT policies and services from their mobile devices or computers.

What are Protection Policies?

App Protection Policy is a feature within Microsoft Intune that allows you to define a set of rules and restrictions for how apps (especially business apps) should behave on a device. These policies help protect sensitive company data and maintain security while allowing employees to use their devices for work.

Why Do Organizations Create and Implement App Protection Policies?

When you set up an app protection policy, you can control how the Egnyte app interacts with sensitive company data. For instance, you can require the app to prevent data sharing between the app and personal apps or adjust the level of control of the app based on various factors, such as the user’s location, network environment, and device status.

What is Conditional Access and is it supported in the Egnyte for Intune iOS App?

Conditional Access in Microsoft Intune ensures only authorized users on compliant devices, using approved applications, can access the organization’s resources. It evaluates signals like user identity and device compliance to enforce security policies and protect sensitive data. Learn more in Microsoft’s official documentation.

Currently, Conditional Access policies are supported only in the login process for Egnyte for Intune iOS app. Conditional Access is not supported if the device becomes non-compliant during an active session.

Can Microsoft Intune Be Used for Managing the Regular Egnyte Mobile Apps (iOS and Android)?

Intune can be used to a limited extent for managing the regular Egnyte mobile apps (as opposed to the ones wrapped up in Intune SDK), particularly for application deployment or for device entitlement, but not for assigning advanced protection policies.
