iOS Files App Integration (File Provider)

The Egnyte iOS app integrates seamlessly with the iOS Files app, allowing you to manage your Egnyte files alongside files from other cloud providers. This integration enhances organization of and collaboration on documents, images, and more.

To access the Egnyte integration with the File Provider and iOS Files app, ensure the Egnyte iOS app is updated to the latest version from the Apple AppStore. Follow these steps to set it up:

  • Open the Files app on the iOS device.

  • From the Browse screen, tap the three-dot (ellipsis) menu in the top right corner and select Edit.

  • Toggle Egnyte to On and tap Done. To access your Egnyte account in the Files app:

  • Find Egnyte under Locations.

  • Tap on Egnyte to access your files and folders. Once the Egnyte storage is selected in the Files app, the users can perform the following actions on their data (subject to permissions granted within Egnyte Storage):

  • Browsing and Accessing Files: Users can browse and access all their Egnyte files and folders directly within the iOS Files app.

  • Opening Files: Users can open to preview supported file types stored in Egnyte (e.g. PDFs, images, videos).

  • Downloading Files: Users can download files from Egnyte to their iOS device, making them available for offline access.

  • Uploading (Saving) to Files: Users can upload or save files from their iOS device directly to Egnyte storage through the Files app. When multiple files are uploaded, users must use the Upload to Egnyte option in the iOS Share menu.

  • Organizing Files: Users can create new folders, move files between folders, delete and rename files stored in Egnyte using the Files app’s native file management capabilities.

  • Dragging-and-Dropping: Users can use the intuitive drag-and-drop functionality within the Files app to move files between Egnyte and other cloud storage locations, as well as within Egnyte itself.

  • Sharing Files: Users can share Egnyte files with others using the native iOS sharing options available within the Files app. Egnyte Collaborate features not listed above are not available on the Files app. These features include:

  • Accessing Egnyte storage via Files when a passcode lock is set up for the Egnyte app

  • Accessing files in the Egnyte folder via Files while offline

  • Searching to find any file within Egnyte folders

  • Managing folder permissions

  • Syncing tags or colors in the Files app

  • Commenting on files

  • Notifications

  • Reports

  • Account management

  • Egnyte application settings

  • Requesting files from others

  • Opening and previewing unsupported file types (for example; dwg files)

  • Bookmarking folders and adding folders to Favorites

  • File versions

  • File and folder shortcuts

  • Special folder (for example; project folder) indicators

  • Project folder (settings, dashboard, metadata)

  • Smart upload

  • Workflows

Limitations

  • The File Provider extension described in this article is not available in the Egnyte for Intune version of the iOS app.

iOS Mobile FAQs

How Do I Bookmark a Folder?

Folders can be bookmarked for quicker access by selecting the three dots next to the desired folder and choosing Add Bookmark. Once bookmarked, the folder becomes available in the Bookmarks tab located in the bottom bar of the app.

The same steps are followed to remove a bookmark.

How Do I Send Links from the App?

A link to a file or folder can be shared via the Egnyte iOS App by accessing the three-dot menu next to the desired item and selecting the Share option.

Does the App Sync Files to My Mobile Device?

The app does not sync files to mobile devices to avoid excessive data usage. However, individual files or folders can be downloaded directly to the device for offline access.

How Do I Access Files or Folders When I’m Offline?

To make a file or folder available offline, the three vertical dots next to the item need to be tapped, followed by selecting the Mark Offline option. Once marked, the item remains accessible without an internet connection. All folders and files marked for offline access can be viewed in the Offline tab, located in the bottom bar of the app.

How Do I Edit and Save Files Back to Egnyte?

Egnyte partners with many third-party apps which allow users to open and edit a file from Egnyte.

Files can be edited and saved back to Egnyte directly from Microsoft Office apps. Click here to find out how.

I Got an Attachment in an Email. Can I Upload this to Egnyte?

Attachments can be uploaded by opening the iOS native email application and accessing the desired message. The attachment needs to be long-pressed, and from the context menu, Save Image or Save to Files needs to be selected. The Egnyte app is then opened to select the destination folder for the attachment upload.

How Do I Configure Session Timeout in the iOS App to Ensure Users are Signed Out After the Session Expires?

The Session Timeout setting, configured by the domain admin, applies only to the web application and is not supported in the iOS app. Login persistence on iOS is managed through token expiration, allowing users to remain logged in without unexpected interruptions.

What is the Difference Between Deleting a File in Files Tab Vs. Removing a File in the Offline Tab?

Deleting the local version will only remove the file from your device; the file will still exist in the cloud.

What If I Have Multiple Domains?

The Egnyte app now supports the ability to easily switch from one Egnyte domain to another without having to log in each time. To add a new domain, the Menu icon needs to be tapped, followed by selecting Manage Accounts. From there, the Add Account option needs to be selected, and the required login credentials can be entered.

Once a domain has been added, switching between domains is done by tapping the Menu icon and selecting Switch Account and choosing the domain needed.

How Do I Log Out of the App?

First, the 3-dot menu icon (3 horizontal lines) from the bottom bar of the app needs to be selected and the option to Manage Accounts must be tapped. Next, the three dot menu next to the account name must be tapped and the Log out from this account button must be clicked.

Are Egnyte Mobile Applications HIPAA compliant?

Egnyte’s entire platform is HIPAA-ready, which includes the applications developed to access the cloud file server. For more information on HIPAA compliance, click here.

Why Am I Receiving an “Access Forbidden” Error Message?

If there’s an error when updating or installing the mobile app, or Admins have restricted access from certain devices, mobile users may receive the following error message: Access Forbidden, you are not allowed to access your account from this device.

When this happens, there are a few steps you’ll need to take to resolve the error.

  • Log into the Web UI from a browser.
  • Click on your profile picture, then your name, and open the My Devices tab.
  • Locate your mobile device from the list and select it.
  • Click on the device and on the next screen and select Remove Device.
  • Once the device is successfully removed, uninstall the mobile app on your phone and reinstall the latest version from the Apple App Store.

Mobile App - Device Entitlement

Device Entitlement is a mobile security feature that allows administrators to manage which mobile devices are allowed to use the Egnyte mobile app. Device Entitlement works alongside Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) solutions to identify whether users are accessing Egnyte on a managed device. Administrators can control whether access on unmanaged devices is allowed or set up additional restrictions to minimize the risk of data loss.

Requirements

  • Device Entitlement is only available with Egnyte’s Device Control package
  • This feature also requires a compatible MDM/MAM/EMM solution
  • Users’ devices are already enrolled and setup with the MDM
  • Minimum Supported version: iOS 10.0 or Android 6.0

Setup

Step 1: The admin enables and configures Device Entitlement from Egnyte’s Web UI

Step 2: Connect Egnyte to your Mobile Management solution

Optionally, there are some additional steps that you can take to tailor security for unmanaged devices to your company’s preference.

Step 1: Setting up Device Entitlement in Egnyte

  1. If you have purchased the Egnyte Device Control package, you can enable Device Entitlement from our Web UI. Click Settings.

  2. Access the Applications panel by navigating to the Configuration tab, then select the Applications page. Toggle Mobile Device Entitlement on to enable the feature.

  3. Once enabled, generate a Mobile Device Entitlement Token and save this string for the second part of the setup.

Note: If you are managing multiple Egnyte domains (via Multi-Entity Management), please set the Mobile Device Entitlement Token to be the same across all of your Egnyte domains. If an end user tries to authenticate into a domain that is using a different Mobile Device Entitlement token, it will be treated as an unmanaged device and will have restricted access.

Step 2: Linking your MDM to Egnyte

Each MDM is slightly different, so we have created separate guides for the common mobile management solutions that we support.

MobileIron
AirWatch
MobileIron

  1. From your MobileIron admin console, choose Apps from the top menu, then click +Add.

  2. Choose the platform you’d like to add with the app store drop-down menu. Search for Egnyte in the text box and then click Next.

  3. Review that you’ve selected the right app and hit Next again, where you can set your distribution filters for the App Catalog. This is where you can mass deploy the app to your users if you so choose. Anyone who can install the app from the App Catalog will be considered a managed device. Click on Next when you’re done.

  4. In the App Configurations section, tap the + button on the iOS Managed App Configuration row for Apple devices.

For managed Android apps, it’s under the Android for Work row.

  1. Fill in the name as something you can remember and reference later (e.g. Egnyte Device Entitlement Configs). Then click the +Add button to fill in the Device Entitlement token then select Next, and then Done when you have finished.

  • Your key should be deviceEntitlementToken

  • Your Device Entitlement Token should be copy/pasted from Step 1 into the value field. Optional:

  • You can auto-install our app on managed devices so that your end-users don’t even need to search for the app in the app catalog.

Step 3: Restriction Customization (Optional)

Once you have successfully configured Device Entitlement for your domain, you can choose to further customize access restrictions from the Egnyte Web UI.

For managed users, you can set your restrictions under the Mobile section, right above the Device Entitlement section in Egnyte.

For unmanaged users, you can customize restrictions separately for Admin/Power Users and Standard Users. Enable either section to further block local storage, require a passcode lock, and/or block 3rd party app access.

Note: More restrictive settings will always overwrite less restrictive ones.

Step 4: Scalable Authentication Assist (Optional)

To help onboard your managed users faster, you can pre-install and pre-fill some of your end user’s input fields through your MDM. When your users open the app, all they will simply open the app and type in their password.

Note: Single sign-on users will still have to type in both username and password, but no longer need to fill in the domain field.

In the App Policy view, choose to add the following key-value pairs so that these values are injected into your end user’s device for a seamless authentication experience.

Key

Value

Notes

login

<user’s username or email>

This field is ignored when the field useSSO is set to true.

The value should be filled with a MobileIron variable so that each of your end user’s devices will have this field prefilled with their username or email. The available variables that you can select from can be found under the Admin -> Attributes section in your Mobile Iron portal.

This value can’t be read if the company uses SSO login. Username must follow set convention to work.

domain

<domain name>

iOS: <domain name>.egnyte.com Android: <domain name>

deviceEntitlementToken

<String>

This string needs to match what is set in the Web UI Device Control panel.

Airwatch

  2. Choose which platform (iOS or Android) and input Egnyte in the Name field. Hit Next for AirWatch to search the app store for the Egnyte app.

  3. Select Egnyte from the search results and without changing any settings here, choose Save & Assign.

  4. Now, Egnyte should be added to your list view. Select the row’s radio button and choose to Edit Assignment.

  5. Scroll down until you see the Policies’ Application Configuration section. Click on the Add button to add your Device Entitlement Token.

  6. Set the Configuration Key to deviceEntitlementToken then copy and paste the Device Entitlement Token from the Web UI (Step 1) into the Configuration Value field. It should look like the screenshot below when you’re done. Click on Save & Assign, then Publish on the next screen to finish.

  7. The app should now be available in the app catalog for your users to download and install. Any apps installed through the app catalog will receive the Device Entitlement Token that you’ve provided, and these devices will be treated as managed. Any apps installed outside of the MDM will be considered unmanaged, and thus have restricted or limited access.

Optional:

Troubleshooting

Question 1: I’m trying to integrate Device Entitlement with Android for Work. However, my device is not letting me install a work profile. What is wrong?

Answer 1: Your device might be rooted. Android for Work does not support rooted devices.

Offline Mode Auto-update in the Egnyte iOS App

The Offline Mode Auto-update feature keeps designated offline files and folders in sync with the cloud, without requiring manual refresh actions.

Skip Ahead To…

Enabling or Disabling Auto-Update

When do Auto-Updates Occur

Storage Considerations

Offline Mode Behavior

Behavior When Auto-Update Is Disabled

Limitations and Future Improvements

Enabling or Disabling Auto-Update

The auto-update setting can be configured during the process of marking a folder for offline access. A prompt is displayed with the option to enable or skip auto-updates and to include or exclude subfolders.

The setting can also be modified using the More menu (⋯) by selecting the enable or disable auto-update option.

When files or folders are marked for offline access, the download status is displayed in the Dynamic Island at the top of the screen, where the sync can be paused, resumed, or cancelled.

A new auto-update icon will appear in the metadata line for any folder or file with auto-update enabled. When the feature is disabled, the icon is not shown.

If auto-update is disabled for a file or folder, the sync can be triggered manually via the three-dot menu by selecting Update manually.

When do Auto-Updates Occur

Auto-updates are triggered in the following cases:

  • When the application is launched
  • When the app transitions from background to foreground
  • When the folder marked for offline is opened or refreshed from the listing view
  • When the Offline tab is opened Auto-updates apply only to files in the folder marked for auto-update. Subfolder contents are not updated automatically.

Storage Considerations

If a mark offline with auto-update action requires more storage than what is currently allocated for offline files on the device, a warning message is displayed. Three options are provided:

  • Continue: Increases the offline storage allocation to unlimited and proceeds with the update
  • Cancel: Closes the prompt with no changes made

Offline Mode Behavior

When the device is offline, the Offline tab displays a message indicating the time of the last successful sync. The message also recommends reconnecting to the internet to access the latest content.

PDF Viewer In The IOS App

The PDF Viewer allows for the previewing of PDF files within the iOS mobile app. All features of the viewer are available across all Egnyte plans.

Basic Controls

The PDF Viewer facilitates easy scrolling through a document and navigation of pages using swipes or page thumbnails located at the bottom. Additionally, tapping the grid view icon at the bottom enables quick access to a specific page.

At the top of the viewer, the toolbar provides controls for opening the Annotations List, Search within the document, and the native Share button.

The bottom navigation bar provides access to options such as File Sharing, Mark Offline, AI Assistant, Comments, and More. Clicking on More opens additional File Context Menu providing access to Comments, Copy, Move, Rename, Delete, and File Details).

Annotations List

The list displays all annotations, including notes and highlights, that have been added to the document and provides the ability to search through those annotations.

Some annotations may not display correctly when accessing PDF files shared through preview only share links.

Annotations in the preview can be shown or hidden using the toggle, which is turned on by default. To view the document preview without annotations, the toggle switch can be turned off.

Annotations can be searched by clicking on the search input field with the magnifying glass icon on the left and typing the desired word or phrase. Matching results will be listed.

Annotations can be deleted by swiping left and tapping the red Delete button.

Search

Tapping the magnifying glass icon on the document preview screen opens the content Search function.

Typing in a word or phrase will display a list of matches along with surrounding text. Tapping on a match will navigate to that section in the document.

Native Share Button

Tapping the share button in the top-right corner of the document preview screen opens the iOS Native Share menu.

From this location, the document can be easily shared via AirDrop, email, messaging apps, or any other available sharing options. Additionally, the document can be saved to the device or other apps. (Please note that these sharing actions are subject to the permissions granted or denied by the domain administrator).

PDF Editing In The IOS App

PDF Editing is an optional add-on to Egnyte plans that provides the following possibilities within the iOS app: adding annotations, manipulating pages, and filling out interactive PDFs. The changes made in the editing mode are made directly to the PDF and will be visible in 3rd party PDF viewing and editing applications.

Starting The Edit Process

PDF editing is supported when the following criteria are met:

  • The document is a PDF.
  • User has Editor or greater permissions.
  • The file is not locked by another user. The editing mode is enabled by clicking the Edit button located in the lower right corner of the PDF preview screen.

Making And Managing Annotations

Making Annotations

Annotations can be added by selecting Annotation Type Icons from the toolbar (Note: The toolbar can be moved to the left or right side of the screen for easier access):

  • Text Markup: Long pressing the Text icon will present options such as highlight, underline, squiggle, or strikethrough. Running a finger along the desired text will apply the selected markup.

  • Add Note: Tapping the Note icon allows for the addition of a note by tapping the desired location in the document. On the note screen, typing the note and selecting Done will save it.

  • Text: Long pressing the Text icon will present a dropdown menu with options for Text, Callout, or Signature. Selecting one of these options and tapping the desired location in the document will add the chosen element. The text or callout can then be typed, or the signature drawn, with formatting options available for color, fill, opacity, font type, and size.

  • Drawing: Tap the Drawing Tool icon and select either Drawing or Magic Ink from the dropdown menu to draw freehand on the document. Magic Ink will automatically convert freehand drawings into geometric shapes that match the sketch. If needed, use the color button to select options for color, background color, blend mode, opacity, thickness, or color presets for the drawing tool.

  • Freeform Highlight: Tapping the Highlighting tool icon will activate the tool for swiping across the section of the document to highlight it. If needed, the Color button can be used to adjust the color, background color, blend mode, opacity, thickness, or color presets for the highlighting tool.

  • Eraser: Tapping the Eraser icon will enable the tool for removing unwanted annotations by swiping with the finger.

  • Shapes: Tapping the Shape icon will present options for Arrow, Line, Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, or Cloud. Select a shape and draw it with the finger. If needed, use the Color Button to adjust the color, background color, blend mode, opacity, thickness, or color presets for the selected shape.

  • Image: Tapping the Image icon will provide options to add a picture. Select Camera to take a photo or Photo Library to choose an image from the Photos app.

  • More Options: Long pressing the Annotation icon at the bottom of the Toolbar (which dynamically changes based on the last action used) will reveal a context menu. From this menu, select Sound, Link, or Stamp.

    • Pressing the Sound icon will present the option to tap on the desired location in the document for the recording. After selecting the location, click on Record to capture the sound and press the Stop button when finished.
    • Tapping the Link button will provide the option to add a link.
    • Tapping the Stamp button will allow the addition of a stamp.

  • Undo & redo: Tapping the Undo arrow will reverse the last action, while tapping the Redo arrow will restore it.

Formatting annotations

Long pressing on an annotation will display a context menu with options for formatting.

Deleting annotations

Annotations can be deleted by following these steps:

  • Tapping the Edit button to access annotation tools.
  • Selecting the annotation to be removed.
  • Tapping the Trash icon.
Form Filling
  • Tapping the Edit button on the PDF preview screen will highlight PDF form fields in purple.
  • Selecting a form field allows text input using the keyboard.
  • Navigation to the next form field can be done by using the left or right arrow buttons or tapping on the desired field.
  • The active field’s highlight color will change to yellow, and once filled, it will change to green.
  • Tapping on an already filled field will enable modifications.
  • The Clear Field button can be used to erase text from the field.
  • Selecting Done will exit the form-filling mode.
Page Manipulation

PDF Editing also includes the ability to manipulate the pages of a document, including:

  • Adding Pages: Integrate new pages into existing PDF documents.
  • Importing Pages: Import pages from other documents into the PDF.
  • Extracting Pages: Extract pages from PDFs to create separate, independent documents.
  • Page Manipulation: Rotate, rearrange, delete, or duplicate pages. The feature can be accessed by tapping on the Edit button in the right lower corner of the PDF preview screen, followed by selecting the PDF Page Editor icon as shown below

The next screenshot below shows which icons to use for the specific PDF Page Editor actions.

Saving Edits

Once edits have been made to the document, the changes can be saved. Clicking the Save button in the top-right corner provides two options:

  • Save - Creates a new version of the PDF file.
  • Save As – Creates a new file and allows for the selection of a new file name and location.

Personalised Action Recommendations for iOS

The Egnyte mobile app for iOS improves user experience with personalized suggestions and helpful tips, offering potential next steps based on what you’re currently doing. This feature assists in uncovering related functionalities and optimizing your workflow.

For example, if a user opens a PDF file to annotate it, they may receive a suggestion to explore the PDF Page Editor for further editing options.

Another example where personalized suggestions may be helpful is connected with the Project Folders workflow. When a user navigates to a Project Folder for which the location hasn’t been set yet, he will be recommended.

Recommendations may include links to help desk articles or buttons that redirect users to the suggested feature.

Users can dismiss recommendations by clicking the close button or by clicking away. Additionally, users have the option to control whether they receive feature recommendations by toggling this setting on or off in the application’s Settings.

Personalized Action Recommendations on iOS - Requirments

Personalized Action Recommendations are available to users who have version 8.30 (or higher) of the Egnyte Mobile App and whose devices are running iOS version 17 (or higher). The most up to date version of the Egnyte app is always available in the Apple application store.

Record your iOS (iPhone or iPad) screen

Users with iPhone and iPad devices on iOS 11 or later can record their screen. This is useful when trying to capture an issue for your IT department to review. We’ll walk you through how to enable the setting, record with and without sound, and how to view and share the video once it’s completed.

Enable Screen Recording

To use the new screen recording feature in iOS 11, you’ll first need to add the feature’s button to Control Center.

Open Settings, swipe down to Control Center and scroll down to MORE CONTROLS. Then, you’ll need to tap the green plus button next to Screen Recording.

Once its enabled, Swipe down from the top right corner of any screen to open Control Center and look for the Record button.

Record Without Sound

With the shortcut added to Control Center, swipe down from the Top Right corner of your iOS device’s screen and tap the Screen Recording button. The button will begin counting down from 3, giving you time to get to the screen you want to record. The status bar at the top of your phone’s display will turn red when it’s actively recording. Tap the red bar to instantly stop recording.

Narrate as you Record

If you have a 3D Touch-enabled iOS device, hard-press on the Screen Recording shortcut in Control Center. If you lack 3D Touch, a long-press will work.

Press deeply on and tap Microphone to turn Microphone Audio on or off. Tap the button to turn audio recording on, then tap Start Recording. The microphone button will turn red when activated as a reminder that audio will be captured. You’ll be recorded using your device’s microphone along with whatever is on the screen.

View and Share

Once you stop recording, the video is saved to your phone’s Camera Roll on your device. Open the Photos app to find it. You can then view, edit, and share the recording as you would a video you recorded using the Camera app.

Request Files from Others iOS and Android

Upload links are a great way for people outside your Egnyte account to upload content to a specific Shared folder, without being able to see the contents of that folder.

Request Files From Others

iOS App

To create an upload link in the iOS app, follow these steps:

  • Navigate to Shared folders and locate the folder where the uploaded files should be stored.
  • Click the three-dot menu next to the folder name and select Request files from others from the context menu.
  • On the next screen, choose when the link should expire and whether to create a separate folder for each person uploading files through the link. Then click Share link.
  • Click the Share Link option.
  • Choose a method to share the link with collaborators or partners (email, internet communicator, text message, etc.)
Android App

To create the request in the Android application:

  • Click the three-dot menu next to the folder name.
  • Select Request Files from Others from the context menu.
  • The next screen allows for the creation of a separate folder for each person uploading files via the link and offers an option to select the link expiration time.
  • Next, choose a method to share the link with the collaborators. Selecting the Get link option will copy the link to the clipboard and can then be pasted to any message.
  • Selecting Email link enables adding email addresses of collaborators to send the link to, along with an optional message. Clicking the Send button in the upper right corner will dispatch the email.

Reviewing and Approving Workflows and Tasks in the iOS App

To-Do, Review, and Approval Tasks need to be created and assigned using the WebUI (as described in this article) and they can be reviewed, accepted, rejected, and completed also in the Egnyte Mobile Apps.

As soon as a new task is created, the assignee receives an email with a notification and a link to the task. If the email is opened on a mobile device and the link is clicked, the assignee is redirected to the Egnyte Mobile App and the Workflow/Task screen. Within the mobile app, every new task is signaled by a red dot that appears next to the Workflows button on the bottom navigation bar.

On the Workflows screen, the user can see a list of tasks and workflows assigned to him.

The Workflows and Tasks list view can be filtered:

  • to show the tasks assigned to the user or created by the user

  • to show the tasks according to their Type (To-do, Review, Approval) and current status (e.g. In progress, Completed, Approved, Rejected, Canceled) The users can see each workflow and task:

  • current status (e.g. In progress)

  • due date

  • list of assignees Most importantly, users can perform the Workflows and Task actions assigned to them in the mobile apps. For example, they can:

  • review the document associated with the workflow or task (using the file preview mode),

  • accept or reject the workflows and tasks

  • complete them

  • add the reason for approval or rejection (where relevant)

  • Egnyte Sign workflows and tasks with their credentials (if required) To review and approve Workflows on your iOS mobile device, make sure you are using version 8.15 or higher. Some Workflow capabilities described above may be specific to the Life Sciences GxP plan. To find out more about Workflows and Tasks and the Life Sciences GxP plan, go to this helpdesk article.

Searching in the Egnyte iOS App

The Egnyte iOS app offers two ways to search for files and folders: AI-Powered Search that automatically translates natural language queries into structured search parameters, and a manual filter bar for precise, hands-on filtering by file type, date, contributor, location, and more. When a query is better suited for the AI Assistant than for a file search, the app can also suggest asking the AI Assistant directly.

AI-Powered Search

AI-Powered Search allows users to find files using natural language instead of manually configuring filters. A query such as pdf file I recently opened is automatically interpreted and translated into structured search parameters applying the appropriate filters such as: files (not folders), file type, and other filters without requiring users to navigate the filter bar.

AI-Powered Search is available to users on domains with an active AI Add-on. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Ask Assistant Suggestion

When a multi-word query is entered in the search bar, the app detects whether the query is better suited for the AI Assistant than for a file search. If so, an Ask Assistant suggestion appears. Selecting it opens the AI Assistant with the query already filled in.

Single-word queries continue to return standard search results. If detection is unavailable, search works as usual. The suggestion is not shown to users without access to the AI Assistant.

AI-Powered Search is available to users on domains with an active AI Add-on. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Manual Search Filters

The filter bar presents individual filters — Location, Content, Type, Modified, Uploaded, Updated by, and Geolocation — in a horizontally scrollable row. A filter icon on the left side of the bar displays the number of currently active filters. When a filter is active, the color changes to blue and displays the selected value. Filters take effect immediately upon selection; no separate confirmation step is required.

Location

The Location filter controls the scope of the search. Two options are available:

  • Any: searches across the entire Egnyte account
  • Current folder: limits results to the folder currently being browsed (selected by default when navigating into a folder before searching)
Content

The Content filter controls what types of items are returned in results:

  • All Files & Folders: returns both files and folders (default)
  • Files : returns files only
  • Folders : returns folders only
Type

The Type filter allows users to narrow results to a specific file format category. The following types are available: PDF, Document, Spreadsheet, Presentation, Image, Audio / Video, Text / Source Code, Google File, Email, CAD, and Archive. By default, Any is selected, which returns all file types.

Modified

The Modified filter allows users to narrow results to files last modified within a specific time period. The following preset options are available: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Last 180 days, and Last 360 days. A Custom option is also available for defining a specific date range using a calendar date picker. By default, Anytime is selected.

Uploaded

The Uploaded filter works in the same way as the Modified filter, but applies to the date a file was originally uploaded to Egnyte. The same preset time periods and Custom date range option are available.

Updated by

The Updated by filter allows users to narrow results to files last modified by a specific person. A search field within the filter panel queries the organization’s directory as characters are entered, with matching names displayed as selectable results. A Me shortcut is available for quickly filtering to files updated by the currently signed-in user.

Geolocation

The Geolocation filter allows users to find files based on GPS metadata embedded in the file — for example, photos taken on a mobile device. By default, Any location is selected, which applies no location restriction. Selecting Custom opens a map picker where the search area can be defined.

The map picker displays an interactive map with a pin and a blue circle representing the current location and search radius. The location can be set by dragging the map to the desired point, or by using the Search field at the top to find a specific address — suggestions appear as characters are entered. The resolved address is displayed below the map. The Map Radius slider controls the size of the search area, and the active radius is shown numerically alongside the slider. Once the location and radius are set, the Continue button applies the filter.

The Geolocation filter only applies to files that contain GPS metadata. Files without location data will not appear in results regardless of the radius selected.

Share Links in the iOS App

This article describes how to share files and folders via links in the Egnyte iOS Mobile App.

Admin and Power Users can create links to files or folders to quickly share with someone inside or outside of their organization.

To share a link to a single file or folder via the Egnyte iOS App, click on the three dot menu next to the file or folder that needs to be shared and select Share.

To share a link to multiple files or folders, click on the three dot menu in the upper right corner of the screen, choose Select, tap the selection button next to the files or folders that need to be shared and click the Share button.

Next, set up the link sharing options:

  • Who can access the link (Anyone, Anyone with password, Existing user(s), People you choose)
  • Link settings (Allow downloads, Notify when the link is accessed, Add folder/file name to link)
  • Link expiration (On a date, After number of clicks, Never)
  • Choose how to share the link (Email link, Get link)
    • If the Email link option is selected, the system will auto-suggest email addresses based on previous usage, with a prioritization algorithm to help pick the most relevant users.
    • Additionally, clear color indicators differentiate internal (blue) from external (gray) recipients.
    • If domain-based link sharing restrictions feature is enabled, the Egnyte iOS app will notify users if a recipient’s email address belongs to a blocked domain (and will be highlighted in red), ensuring compliance with company policies.
    • The feature is currently available to a limited number of customers who are on select Platform plans - Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Life Sciences, Document Room, GxP and all Next Gen plans. To request this feature, contact our Products team.
    • If the Get link option is selected, the link is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted into a text message or other communication channels. Link Sharing Screen Tour

Click the “?” icon in the upper right corner of the Link Sharing screen for a guided tour of available options and settings.

Signing into the Egnyte for Intune iOS App

The Egnyte for Intune iOS app version 9.9 introduces an updated sign-in experience for new users and users who are signing in for the first time on a device. This article describes each step of the sign-in process.

Users who are already signed in when they update to version 9.9 are not required to sign in again. The updated sign-in flow applies only when signing in for the first time after installing or reinstalling the app.

The Sign-In Steps

Choosing a Tenant on the Welcome Screen

When the app is opened for the first time after installation, a welcome screen is displayed with two options:

  • Continue: for users whose organization uses a standard Microsoft commercial tenant.
  • GCC High user?: for users whose organization uses a Microsoft Government Community Cloud High (GCC High) tenant.
Microsoft Authentication

After selecting an option, the app proceeds to Microsoft authentication. Depending on the device setup, this step uses one of two methods:

  • Microsoft Authenticator app: if the Microsoft Authenticator app is installed on the device, it is used to handle the authentication. The user selects the appropriate account from within the Authenticator app.
  • In-app browser: if the Microsoft Authenticator app is not installed, a browser window opens within the app for the user to sign in with their Microsoft credentials. During this step, any Conditional Access policies assigned to the user by their organization’s IT administrator are evaluated. If a Conditional Access policy blocks the user, for example, because the device is not enrolled or managed, a message from Microsoft is displayed and sign-in is not completed. See the article for details on what these messages mean and what users can do.
Intune Enrollment

Once Microsoft authentication is complete, the app enrolls the device with Microsoft Intune using the authenticated user’s identity. This step is handled automatically.

App Restart

After enrollment, a notification is displayed by the app indicating that a restart is required to apply the Intune policies. The user taps the button in this notification, which closes the app. The app does not reopen automatically — the user must tap the app icon on the home screen to reopen it.

Egnyte Login

After reopening the app, the standard Egnyte login screen is displayed. The user signs in with their Egnyte credentials to complete the process and access the app.

What if Something Goes Wrong During Sign-In?

If the Microsoft authentication step displays a message such as Install Microsoft Authenticator or Secure this device before you can access, these messages are generated by Microsoft and indicate that a Conditional Access policy is preventing access. See the article for a full explanation of these messages and the steps users or admins can take.

Depending on the organization’s Conditional Access or authentication policies, users may be required to use the Microsoft Authenticator app when signing in. If the organization enforces Microsoft Authenticator, ensure that it is installed and up to date on the device.

App Configuration Reference for Administrators

The Egnyte for Intune iOS app uses tenant-specific configurations for Microsoft authentication and Intune enrollment. These configurations are built into the app for version 9.9 and higher and do not require manual entry by administrators in most deployments. However, they may be relevant in the following situation:

Setting

Smart Upload Folders

What is Automatic Smart Upload?

Automatic Smart Upload feature allows users to scan the photo library on their mobile device, and upload photographs taken at specific locations to user-configured folders.

Users can associate a geo-location with a Project folder, and designate an upload folder within the Project Folder. Once an upload folder is configured, Automatic Smart Upload feature can be used to automatically upload all photos taken at that geographic location into the upload folder.

A. Automatic Smart Upload

Automatic smart upload will automatically scan the device photo library and find photographs taken in places that match the ones specified in Project folders and Upload folders created within them. It saves the users all the manual work they would otherwise need to do moving the pictures from the device photo library into their Egnyte folders.

How to enable and start using Automatic Smart Upload?
  • Set up project folders
  • Smart upload works for Project folders, which are a special type of folder for which its admin can define such parameters as project start and end date, current status, as well as its geo-location. In order to enable automatic smart upload, it is necessary to properly set up project folders and Upload folders within them first (which needs to be done through the web browser). In order to find out how to set up project folders go to this link. Once the Project folder is set, its Admin or Power User needs to go to Project Settings and in the Location tab (1) set the geolocation of the project using the Location name, the Interactive map, or the Search option and (2) set the default upload folder for the project.
  • Set up your mobile device
  • Once the project folder and Upload folder is properly set up in your Egnyte domain, you also need to check if your mobile device is set up properly so make sure that:
    • The camera can access your device location when you take pictures. To do it, navigate to
      • Settings > Privacy > Location Services and toggle them to On
      • Settings > Privacy > Camera, and tick ‘While using the app’ and set the ‘Precise Location’ toggle to On
    • The Egnyte App can access the relevant information on your device such as your location and photos library. To do it, navigate to
    • Settings > Egnyte > Allow Egnyte to access > Location (set the toggle to On), and Photos (tick ‘All photos’).
  • Start taking photographs
  • When all the set-up is ready, you can start leveraging the Smart Upload feature on your mobile device (iPhone or iPad). To start using Smart Upload, just go to one or more locations which match those set up in your project folder/s and take some photographs. Next, launch the Egnyte app and watch for a New Smart Upload notification at the bottom of the screen. Tap on it and you will be redirected to the Smart Upload screen. You can also dismiss the notification and navigate to the Smart Upload icon on the bottom bar later.
  • Review, confirm or reject Smart Upload suggestions
  • Once you land on the Smart Upload screen, you can confirm the upload suggestion and upload all the detected pictures or review them and decide which ones you want to include in or exclude from the upload. When you confirm the upload, the pictures will be automatically uploaded to relevant project/upload folders. Each upload is confirmed with a Success notification
Other options available with Smart Upload

From the Smart Upload screen, you can also navigate to

  • The Recent Uploads to check how many photographs were uploaded recently
  • Project Details (the Project folder name and path, the Upload folder name and path, and the project location)
  • Upload folders The Smart Upload icon at the bottom of your Egnyte app screen will always show you the number of pending upload suggestions.

B. Manually Triggered Smart Upload

Manually triggered smart upload allows users to start the photo library scan for photographs taken in an area that they can define using an interactive map.

How to use Manually Triggered Smart Upload?

To launch this option, go to the folder into which you want pictures to be found and uploaded automatically based on their geo-location (it can be any folder you have admin permissions to), tap on the Create and upload button and from the menu choose Photos from a specific area.

On the next screen, use the map to find and set the location and select the time range you want to be included in the picture scan (e.g. the last 7 days) and click on Find Photos. All the photos which fulfill the selected criteria will be listed. You can edit the list if needed and upload the photos to the folder.

How to get access to Smart Upload?

Automatic Smart Upload is available in the Egnyte iOS App within the Project Control add-on only and Manually Triggered Smart Upload is available in the Platform Business Enterprise Lite and Enterprise plans.

How To Enable Smart Upload In Your Egnyte Android App

How To Enable Smart Upload In Your IOS Egnyte App

Downloads

Go to Apple AppStore to download the latest version of the Egnyte iOS Mobile App or upgrade to the latest version on all your devices if you already have it.

Supported Versions of the iOS Operating System

To ensure that customers using the Egnyte iOS App have the best possible user experience and can access their data securely and efficiently, Egnyte normally supports the last two major versions of the iOS operating system as released by Apple.

However, during the period following Apple’s release of a new iOS version, Egnyte may support the newest version plus the previous two for a few months. This temporary extension ensures a smooth transition and provides continued support while users upgrade to the latest iOS version.

After the transition is completed, the standard policy of supporting the two most recent iOS versions is reinstated. By focusing on these versions, Egnyte can allocate resources more efficiently and deliver an enhanced experience for majority of the users.

If the operating system on a device is lower than those supported by Egnyte, the Egnyte App will remain functional but will no longer receive new updates or bug fixes. Users are encouraged to verify the installed version of the iOS operating system. If it is below the supported range, upgrading to a newer device is recommended.

User Homepage on iOS

The new User Homepage in the Egnyte iOS app is designed to provide faster access to essential files, tasks, and tools. Interactive widgets and personalization options make it easier to complete work directly from the homepage, reducing navigation time and improving productivity.

The User Homepage is available only on devices running iOS 18 or a later version.

Skip Ahead To…

Overview

Available Widgets

Customization Options

Overview

The homepage consolidates frequently accessed content and actions in a single view. Files, tasks, recent items, AI Assistant, and Smart Upload suggestions can be accessed without navigating through multiple folders or menus. This creates a more streamlined and efficient mobile experience.

Back to Top…

Available Widgets

The following widgets are available on the homepage:

Files and Folders

Provides quick entry points to commonly accessed folders, such as Shared or personal Private folders.

Quick Access

The Quick Access widget offers streamlined, one-tap entry to commonly used actions. These actions include:

  • Scan document – Enables documents to be scanned and saved as PDF files to Egnyte.
  • Take photo or video – Opens the Egnyte camera to capture photos or videos, which are then saved directly to Egnyte.
  • Upload photo or video – Enables photos or videos from the device’s Photos app to be added to Egnyte.
  • Upload file – Allows files stored on the device to be uploaded to Egnyte.
  • Geotagged photos – Provides access to the feature for locating photos associated with a specific place selected on a map.
Recent Files

Displays documents accessed most recently, allowing fast reopening without searching.

AI Assistant

Provides access to AI-powered Knowledge Bases, which turns selected folders into intelligent information hubs.

Tasks

Shows assigned workflows with details such as due dates and task owners.

Smart Upload

Enables direct uploads of photos, scans, and files into designated locations from the homepage.

Recent Project Folders

Lists projects that were recently opened in the mobile app or in the Egnyte WebUI.

Offline Storage Widget

Provides real-time visibility into offline file readiness and storage limits directly within the app. Users can monitor storage usage against the app’s allocated quota via a visual meter, while a sync status indicator ensures mission-critical files are fully downloaded before connectivity is lost.

The AI Assistant, Recent Projects, and Smart Upload widgets are only visible and available to customers whose current Egnyte plan includes these features.

Back to Top…

Customization Options

The homepage can be customized by selecting the Edit button to better align with individual work needs:

Widget Selection

Widgets can be shown or hidden as needed. In Edit mode, a widget can be hidden by tapping the minus (-) icon in the upper-left corner of the widget.

Additionally widgets can be added by selecting More -> Add widgets and tapping the widget to be included in the pop-up window.

Widget Order

Widgets may be rearranged in Edit mode by dragging and dropping them into the preferred order.

Widget Resizing

Widgets can be resized in Edit mode using the resize icon in the lower-right corner of the widget. Dragging the icon to the right adjusts the widget from small to medium, and dragging it downward adjusts it to large. Dragging upward or to the left reduces the widget size.

Theme Selection

The homepage theme can be adjusted for appearance. In Edit mode, the option is available under More -> Change theme with four theme variations: Neutral, Sunrise, Blue, and Purple. The selected theme is applied immediately, and the preference is saved upon confirming with the Done button.

User Preferences Synced Across Devices

All preferences saved by a user are automatically synced and applied to every device they use, whether on iOS or Android. This ensures the User Homepage remains consistent across all phones and tablets signed in with the same account.

Customizations made on one device - such as homepage layout, widgets, and appearance settings - are automatically shared and reflected on all other devices within the same user’s account.

Viewer Only Permission on iOS

Viewer Only permission is a folder-level permission that allows customers to better protect their content by restricting files to preview only.

  • It prevents downloading, moving and copying of files.
  • Viewer Only permission can be assigned to any user or group, including Standard Users and Power Users. If Viewer Only Permission has been enabled on your domain, no additional configuration is necessary. The Viewer Only permission level will automatically appear when assigning folder permissions.

The assigned folder permissions can be viewed in the folder details.

The folder with Viewer only permission does not have any context menu options.

Voice Shortcuts to Control the Egnyte iOS App

Overview

Voice Shortcuts are supported in the Egnyte iOS mobile app, enabling hands-free access to commonly used actions through Siri. This integration allows tasks to be performed efficiently while on the go by using natural language commands.

Requirements

  • App Version: These features are available starting with Egnyte iOS App V 9.4.
  • Siri Configuration: Siri must be enabled in the iOS device settings for voice commands to function.

Siri and System Shortcuts Integration

Voice Commands

Selected Egnyte actions can be initiated using voice commands through Siri. To ensure the system directs the command to the correct application, the word Egnyte must be included in the phrase (for example, “Hey Siri, open Egnyte AI Assistant”).

The following voice-enabled actions are supported. While primary commands are listed below and are recommended, similar natural language variations can also be recognized by the system:

  • Opening AI Assistant: The AI Assistant interface is launched directly into chat mode.
    • Primary command: “Open AI Assistant”
  • Accessing Recent Files: Immediate access is provided to the most recently viewed or edited files within the platform.
    • Primary command: “Open recent files in Egnyte”
  • Starting a Document Scan: The mobile camera is activated to begin a new document scan directly into the Egnyte environment.
    • Primary command: “Scan a document in Egnyte”
  • Opening Search: The search functionality within the app is launched to help locate specific files or folders.
    • Primary command: “Open Egnyte search”
  • Uploading a Photo: The photo or video upload process is initiated by opening the Photos app view from which images and videos can be selected for upload to the Egnyte cloud.
    • Primary command: “Upload a photo to Egnyte”
  • Uploading Files: The file upload process is initiated by opening the Files app view from which specific files can be selected for upload to the Egnyte cloud.
    • Primary command: “Upload files to Egnyte”
  • Taking a Photo: The app camera is triggered to capture a new image for immediate storage in Egnyte.
    • Primary command: “Take a photo in Egnyte”
  • Uploading Geotagged Photos: The process for uploading photos from specific location is started by opening a screen where the location can be specified on a map. Once it is selected, photos taken at the location are filtered and can be uploaded to the Egnyte cloud.
    • Primary command: “Upload photos from a location in Egnyte”
System-Level Access and Shortcuts

In addition to Siri, these frequently used actions are available within the iOS environment through the Shortcuts app.

Accessing Egnyte via the Shortcuts App and Creating Home Screen Quick Actions

The Egnyte actions are integrated into the iOS Shortcuts app, which facilitates the automation of tasks and provides quick access from the device.

  • App Navigation: Launching the Shortcuts app on the iOS device provides access to all configured automations.
  • Locating Egnyte Actions: Finding the Egnyte section is possible by navigating to the Library tab.
  • Initiating Tasks: Tapping an action such as Open recent files in Egnyte or Scan document triggers the associated action immediately by opening the Egnyte app directly into the requested task.
  • Adding the Shortcut to Home Screen: Long-pressing on any of the action icons opens a context menu with the option to add the shortcut to home screen and creating a new shortcut in the app. The shortcut appears as an icon on the home screen, allowing for the direct launch of the specified Egnyte feature.

Why am I Receiving an “Access Forbidden” Error Message?

If there’s an error when updating or installing the mobile app, or Admins have restricted access from certain devices, mobile users may receive the following error message: Access Forbidden, you are not allowed to access your account from this device.

When this happens, there are a few steps you’ll need to take to resolve the error.

  • Log into the Web UI from a browser.
  • Click on your profile picture, then your name, and open the My Devices tab.
  • Locate your mobile device from the list and select it.
  • Scroll down to the bottom of the page, and click Remove Device.
  • Click Remove Device on the confirmation screen.
  • Once the device is successfully removed, uninstall the mobile app on your phone and reinstall the latest version.
  • If you still receive the error message, please reach out to your Administrator as they may have restricted certain devices from accessing the Egnyte app.

Advanced Procore Integration

Overview

The Advanced Procore Integration is a feature of the Project Hub (FKA Project Control Add-on).. It is a more robust version of the original integration and is automatically activated when the Project Hub is purchased. The integration will sync an Egnyte Folder to a Procore Project Documents section.

Features

Near Real-Time Sync
  • Using webhooks the sync is initiated between Egnyte and Procore on the following events ( Create, Updated)
  • Other actions such as rename, move, and delete will still run on an hourly update
Max Total Projects
  • 1000 Total projects can be synced with this integration
Max Project Size
  • Each project has a max size of 250,000 total objects (Files and Folders)

Limitations

  • Folder and files with unsupported Character Types in Egnyte will not be synced between the two systems
  • Procore projects and Egnyte folders can only be synced to one folder

Autodesk Forma Integration

Egnyte’s native Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) Integration allows users to establish a 1-way or 2-way sync from Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) into Egnyte. The sync will copy files and folders and can also sync project metadata from Autodesk Forma, keeping significant project details like project status, deadlines, and more updated across both platforms.

This integration is available on all AEC plans or plans with the Project Hub add-on except for Platform Business or AFS plans. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Skip Ahead To…

Configuration

Creating a Sync

Editing a Sync

Managing Existing Connections

Limitations

Configuration

The native Autodesk Forma integration relies on customer keys. Before configuring the integration on Egnyte, first set up a Developer Hub. Depending on the needs, choose between a free or paid offering.

Once a Developer Hub is created, sign into an Autodesk Platform Services (APS) account and follow the steps outlined below to create an application.

It is recommended that the application is created by an Autodesk Forma account administrator. Only Autodesk Forma account admins can add the application as a custom integration (step 4 below). This account admin should have access to the Forma Data Management module for any projects that are desired to sync from Autodesk Forma to Egnyte.

To configure the App, follow the steps outlined below:

  • Create an APS account if one has not been created one already and then navigate to the My applications page under the profile icon. If an account already exists, signing in is required before accessing My Applications.
  • Confirm that the correct Developer Hub is selected, and then choose Create application to get started.
  • Provide a name for the application, select a Team Assignment and then select the Traditional Web App type, and click Create.
  • After creating the application, copy the Client ID and Client Secret to be used when configuring the integration from Egnyte.
  • Scroll down to the General Settings and set the Callback URLs. There are 5 Callback URLs that should be added.
    • partner-integrations.egnyte.com
    • euw1.egnyteprotect.com
    • me-partner-integrations.egnyte.com:443
    • us-partner-integrations.egnyte.com
    • usc1.egnyteprotect.com
  • Please ensure the Callback URLs are copied exactly as shown above. The final Callback URL includes port number 443, which many browsers automatically remove when copied.
  • After setting the Callback URLs, select Save changes.
  • Now that the application is created, associate the application with an Autodesk Forma account.
    • To do this, login to Autodesk Forma and go to the Hub Admin page and select Custom integrations
    • Select the Add custom integration option
    • Populate the respective fields in the ensuing modal and select Add
    • Now that the application is created and ready for use, follow the steps below to configure the Autodesk Forma integration directly from Egnyte.
  • Select the Apps & Integrations page directly from the Egnyte Web UI.
  • Only Egnyte admins can make configuration changes on this page.
  • Find the Autodesk Forma tile and select Enable Integration.
  • There is a similar looking tile called Forma Construction Connect (Workato). Please be sure to select the tile called Autodesk Forma.
  • Select Start configuration and populate the Client ID and Client Secret from step 3 above, and then select Save credentials.
  • Update the Status option by enabling the integration for All users, for groups, or for (specific) users.
  • The Status only controls which users will see the option to configure Autodesk Project sync in the Web UI. Even if a user is granted this permission, they still require Full permissions on the Egnyte folder(s) to establish a sync.
  • The final step before creating a sync is to validate that the Egnyte source from Secure & Govern > Settings > Content Sources is in a healthy Monitoring status.
  • If this Egnyte source is in an Error state, the integration will not work properly. For more information on managing this source, click here.
  • An Autodesk source will not be shown in the UI under Cloud Content Sources as a result of this sync integration.
Back to Top…

Creating a Sync

Once the integration is configured on the domain, users with permissions to configure a sync will be able to see the Autodesk Project Sync option after selecting the More button within the Integrations sub-menu.

Selecting this option will open a modal where the user will need to authorize access to the previously created application. Select Allow to proceed.

From the ensuing modal, a user will need to populate the following:

  • Connection Name - A string field to help differentiate between other syncs
  • Sync Type - Select 1 or 2-way sync between Egnyte and Autodesk
  • Select an Autodesk company - A dropdown field that will present Autodesk companies (accounts) in which the custom application has been added.
  • Select an Autodesk project - A dropdown field of projects available for sync in the previously selected Autodesk company.
  • Some projects may be disabled in this list because they are already syncing to Egnyte.
  • Select content to sync from the project above - A radio button to sync the Full project (all files and folders within the selected Autodesk Docs instance) or Selected folders where a user can selectively choose which folders they want to sync to Egnyte. Once the above fields are populated, select Next to continue.

Step 2 of the configuration asks the user to select the respective root Project folder on Egnyte to be marked as a Project. It is likely that the target folder on Egnyte (indicated by the Connection initiated here label) is a subfolder of a larger project. In configuring this integration, Egnyte will also synchronize the Project metadata available in Autodesk Forma to an Egnyte folder. Best practice is to point the metadata sync to the root project folder. Users can select the root Project folder in the folder tree and select Next to continue.

The last step of the configuration is to review and confirm the settings. Once verified, select Create connection to start the data synchronization process.

If the user creating the sync does not have access to Secure & Govern (S&G) and the Allow any power user in linked Egnyte domains to get access to Secure & Govern option is disabled, they will be auto-provisioned a seat in S&G with the Connections Read Only role. To learn more about this access level, click here.

Back to Top…

Editing a Sync

Once a project sync is established between Autodesk Forma and Egnyte, the connection can be modified without first having to stop and remove it.

To edit the sync, navigate to the target Egnyte folder of the existing sync, click on the three-dots options -> Integrations -> Autodesk Project Sync.

While this is the same workflow as creating a new sync, Egnyte will intelligently understand that a connection already exists on the Egnyte folder. The Edit flow will open after authorizing access to the application in your Autodesk developer hub.

Only the Connection Name and the Content to sync can be modified from this modal. Changing the Sync Type, connected Autodesk company or Autodesk project is not supported.

Step 2 of the sync configuration, Egnyte Project, will automatically be skipped after selecting Next because changing the Egnyte Project is also not supported as part of this flow.

To save the changes made to the existing sync, select the Edit connection button on the Review screen.

Back to Top…

Managing Existing Connections

To view the status of existing connections, users can select the More button (3 vertical dots) and then List of Synced Autodesk projects.

This will redirect the user to the Forma Connections page within their Secure & Govern (S&G) instance. Alternatively, users can navigate here manually by opening their S&G instance from the app switcher, selecting Secure & Govern, and then Settings -> Connections -> Forma.

By default, existing connections will be sorted by Connection Name, however users can sort by any of the columns by selecting the column header.

Selecting the More button adjacent to a specific connection will open a menu with a number of actions that a user can take on the respective connection.

  • View details - This will open a modal where users can find additional details about their connection such as which Forma folders were selected for sync, or details on any skipped files.
  • Download skipped files list - Download an Excel file of all files that have been skipped for synchronization and their details.
  • Rename connection - Users can provide a new Connection Name
  • Pause connection - This will pause the sync and prevent any updates from syncing from Forma to Egnyte. The connection will remain paused until a user selects the Resume connection option.
  • Remove connection - This will sever the sync, and any future changes in Forma will not sync to Egnyte. The connection will also be removed from this dashboard.
  • Resume connection - This option will only show on connections that are in Paused status. This will restart the sync and updates made in Forma will begin syncing to Egnyte.
Back to Top…

Limitations

  • The integration is subject to API and data management rates and limits as defined by Autodesk in the following links:
    • aps.autodesk.com
    • aps.autodesk.com
  • Folder and files with unsupported Character Types in Egnyte will not be synced between the two systems.
  • Autodesk projects can only be synced to one Egnyte folder.
  • Subfolders of a Folder that are synced can’t be synced to another Project.
  • Syncs are restricted on /Inactive folders.
  • Currently sync between Autodesk Forma and Egnyte happens every hour.
  • The Egnyte Collaborate instance must be in a Connected status from Secure & Govern. Click here to learn more.
  • Files or folders that exist in the mapped Egnyte folder but outside of a recognized Autodesk root (like /Project Files) are skipped during sync with an RFS_SERVICE_ERROR, because the connector attempts to push them to the invalid Autodesk root / instead of a valid path.
  • If one or more linked Revit models have not yet been published with their latest (synced) version while the host file is published, the host and linked files’ current (synced) versions are published to Forma Data Management as a zipped data “*.zip.rvt” file. Renaming the extension to .zip allows the user to extract all the .rvt files successfully. Click here to Learn more.

Configure Egnyte for DocuSign

Admins will learn the steps to enable and configure the DocuSign app in Egnyte, connect the DocuSign app to Egnyte, and change the configuration in the future. Learn more about DocuSign here.

Enable DocuSign in Egnyte

Connect the Integration

Enable DocuSign in Egnyte

Administrators will need to enable Egnyte for DocuSign for the appropriate users on their account.

  • Navigate to Apps & Integrations -> DocuSign. Use the Esignature category filter on the left side to quickly narrow your search
  • Hover over the tile and click Enable Integration
  • Administrators can choose to add the app for all users, certain groups (up to 5), or allow users to add the app themselves. Click Save after selection
  • Once the app’s enabled, users will be able to add it from the Apps & Integrations page or will automatically have it installed (depending on the option selected).

Connect the Integration

To connect Egnyte and DocuSign, each user will need to allow the integration service to connect to both the Egnyte account and DocuSign account.

Connect
  • Navigate to the Apps & Integrations page
  • Power Users can skip this step.
  • The user may need to turn off the admin mode to get to the Configure DocuSign window
  • Hover over the app’s tile and click the gear icon
  • Click Continue
  • A window will appear to connect the DocuSign account to the Egnyte account. Click Allow Access so Egnyte for DocuSign can access the Egnyte account.

  • Log in with DocuSign credentials and click Continue

  • If the user closes the browser tab/window before logging in or clicking the Cancel button, the app will still show as Added. In this case, they can either change their account to log in or log in when prompted in the next attempt to send a document with DocuSign.
  • The maximum allowed size from DocuSign is 25MB.

Verify the Installation

After entering an email address and password, the DocuSign app will be added on the Apps & Integrations page.

Egnyte Collaborate Webhook UI Configuration Guide

Webhooks in Egnyte Collaborate enable real-time event notifications from the Egnyte environment to external systems. Instead of polling for changes, webhooks allow applications to automatically receive updates when specific actions occur (for example; file uploads, deletions, or modifications).

Use Cases

  • Build event-driven integrations
  • Improve automation and reduce manual monitoring
  • Enable near real-time workflows across systems like CRM, ERP, or custom applications

Access Webhooks UI

To access the Webhooks configuration interface in Collaborate:

  • Navigate to Settings.
  • Click on Configuration.
  • Locate the Webhooks option. This centralized location ensures admins can easily manage all webhook configurations without needing external help.

Webhook Dashboard

The Webhooks dashboard provides a consolidated view of all configured webhooks along with key metadata for monitoring and management. This dashboard helps admins quickly audit, monitor, and check webhook configurations.

The dashboard includes the following fields:

  • Webhook Name: Identifier for the webhook
  • Configured Endpoint: Destination URL where events are sent
  • Connection Modified: Last time connection settings were updated
  • Created Date: When the webhook was created
  • Created By: Admin who created the webhook
  • Updated By: Last admin who modified the webhook
  • Status: Indicates whether the webhook is:
    • Active: Events are being delivered
    • Paused: Event delivery is temporarily stopped

Register a New Webhook

To create a new webhook follow the steps below.

  • Click on Register New.
  • The configuration screen will be displayed.
  • Provide the required configuration details:
  • Field
  • Description
  • Name
  • A descriptive name for easy identification
  • Endpoint URL
  • The external system endpoint that will receive events
  • Folder Path
  • The specific folder scope for event tracking
  • Auth Header
  • Optional authentication header for secure communication
  • Event Types
  • Choose the events to subscribe to. Click here for more details.
  • Click Register to complete the registration.
  • Once registered, the webhook will be active by default.

Webhook Actions

Each webhook provides a set of management actions accessible via the three-dot menu.

Available actions include:

  • View Details: Inspect full configuration and metadata. The view details tab provides the option to update the webhook name and event types
  • Rename: Update webhook name for better clarity
  • Deactivate: Pause event delivery without deleting configuration
  • Delete: Permanently remove the webhook These actions provide flexibility for ongoing management without requiring reconfiguration.

Access Control and Permissions

  • Admins
    • Full access to create, edit, and manage webhooks
  • Standard & Power Users
    • Can view webhook configurations
    • Cannot perform any actions (create, edit, delete, or deactivate) This ensures governance and prevents unintended changes to integration workflows.

Webhook Disabling Automation

The retry mechanism tries to send the request 4 times to the client-server (A total of five requests are made including the original request). If there is no proper acknowledgment for these attempts from the client-server, the client webhook is paused.

Webhook Retries and Wait Time

Attempt

Wait time

1st

immediate

2nd

1 minute

3rd

10 minute

4th

1 hour

Best Practices

  • Use meaningful naming conventions (for example; Salesforce_File_Updates)
  • Scope webhooks to specific folders to reduce noise
  • Ensure endpoint reliability and proper authentication handling
  • Subscribe only to required event types to optimize performance Webhook configuration in Egnyte Collaborate is designed to balance ease of use with enterprise-grade control. By leveraging webhooks effectively, customers can unlock scalable, event-driven integrations while maintaining strong governance and visibility.

Egnyte Collaborate Webhook UI Overview

The Webhook UI in Egnyte Collaborate provides a centralized, user-friendly interface for customers to create, manage, and check webhooks without relying on APIs or backend configurations.

Webhooks enable real-time event-driven integrations by allowing external systems to receive notifications whenever specific actions occur within Egnyte (for example; file uploads, deletions, creation, and more).

With the Webhook UI, admins can:

  • Easily configure webhooks through a guided interface
  • Select and subscribe to specific event types
  • Manage webhook lifecycle (create, update, delete)
  • Improve integration speed without engineering dependency This UI removes the complexity of manual API-based setup and empowers both technical and semi-technical users to integrate Egnyte with external systems efficiently.

Key Capabilities

Webhook Creation
  • Define endpoint URLs where events should be delivered
  • Select event types (for example; file actions, permission changes)
  • Configure authentication
  • Enable or disable webhooks at creation time
Webhook Management
  • View a list of all configured webhooks
  • Edit webhook configurations (events types and webhook name)
  • Enable, disable or delete webhooks
  • Maintain governance over active integrations
Event Subscription
  • Subscribe to granular events such as:
    • File upload, update, or delete
    • Folder creation or deletion
    • Reduce noise by subscribing only to relevant triggers The Egnyte Collaborate Webhook UI simplifies how customers build event-driven integrations by providing an intuitive and centralized experience for webhook management.

It empowers organizations to:

  • Automate workflows
  • Enhance management
  • Integrate seamlessly with external systems using webhooks from Egnyte

Limitations

  • Currently, there is a limit of 10 webhooks for Collaborate.
