Egnyte for Salesforce Multidomain Configuration Guide

A single Salesforce org can connect to more than one Egnyte domain with the latest Salesforce version. Each Salesforce record syncs to exactly one domain, chosen automatically from the record’s data. This guide explains how to connect additional domains, configure record routing, manage per-domain settings, and remove domains.

Multidomain is useful when different business units, subsidiaries, or regions use separate Egnyte domains but share one Salesforce org. For example, after a merger or acquisition, or where content must stay separated by entity.

Some of the key terms and concepts associated with the Salesforce integration include:

  • Default Domain: The org’s original (first) Egnyte domain. Records that do not match any routing rule sync here.
  • Discriminator Field: A field on the record whose value determines which domain the record syncs to.
  • Division Routing: An alternative to the discriminator field for orgs using Salesforce Divisions: records route by division name.
  • Setting Name: The identifier given to a connected domain when configuration is created. The configuration cannot be renamed afterwards, so choose it deliberately.
  • One Record, One Domain: Every record maps to exactly one domain. A record cannot sync to two domains at once.

Prerequisites

  • Egnyte for Salesforce version 3.11 or later installed in the org.
  • Egnyte Administrator Permission Set OR Full Salesforce Org Administrative Rights as of 3.11, as one of these is required to edit Egnyte settings.
  • Egnyte admin credentials for each domain that needs to be connected.
  • Salesforce Integration licenses must be provisioned for each individual Egnyte domain.

Connecting an Additional Domain

  • Login to Salesforce as Administrator.
  • Open the Egnyte Settings page in the Salesforce org.
  • Click on Add Another Domain and enter the domain details, including a Setting Name.
  • -Setting Name cannot be renamed.
  • -The setting name is case insensitive and must be unique.
  • Click on Save after entering the details
  • Authenticate with an Egnyte admin account for additional domain to complete the OAuth connection. Finally click Continue
    • Multidomain mode is enabled automatically when the first additional domain is connected.
    • Invalid multidomain configurations are rejected at save time with a clear message. If a save is rejected, correct the associated issue and save again.

Configuring Record Routing

Egnyte Sync Configuration is used to determine the routing of records to each individual domain. For each object per domain, a separate Sync Configuration record is maintained that defines the settings specific to each domain. This routing determines which domain each record syncs to. There are two options

Option A: Discriminator Field
  • Create a Custom Text Field on the object (For example - EgnyteDomain__c) to hold the Setting Name per record or use an existing field, this is the Discriminator Field. For more information on creating a custom text field, refer here
  • Go to New Egnyte Sync Configuration.
  • Fill in the Object + Folder Details. Since multidomain is on, two extra columns would appear:
    • Setting Name (Multidomain): pick the domain (default, acme, …).
    • Setting Name Field (Multidomain): pick the discriminator field chosen (same field for every domain of this object).
  • Enter all the details and Save.
  • Setting Name and Name Field can be adjusted on Egnyte Sync Configuration Edit screen.
Option B: Routing by Division

Orgs using Salesforce Divisions can route by division name instead of a custom field. Each additional domain setting has to be named exactly the same as the corresponding Divisions (For example- for Division EMEA please name the setting for mapped domain EMEA and select Division matched by division name) as Setting Name Field on the Sync Config.

Fallback Behavior

Any record whose discriminator or division value does not match a configured domain safely falls back to the default domain. Unmatched records never produce an error.

Per-Domain Sync Configurations

In multidomain mode, sync configurations are defined per object per domain. Each configuration has its own folder templates and metadata structures, fully independent of other domains. Create and edit sync configurations from the Egnyte Sync Configurations as described earlier by selecting the domain configuration is applicable to.

Per-Domain Settings

The following are held separately for each connected domain:

  • Credentials / OAuth connection
  • Default permission and community permission settings
  • Metadata namespace and scope
  • Display options

Working Across Domains

My Egnyte Tab

A domain picker on the My Egnyte tab lets users browse the file system of any connected domain. On record pages no picker is shown and the domain always comes from the record itself.

Egnyte Users Tab

Each domain has its own user base and seat counts. A domain picker on the Egnyte Users tab controls which domain the user list, seat totals, and Remove mapping action apply to.

Canvas App and Embedded View

The Egnyte Canvas app and embedded view are domain-aware: opening files or folders from a record always targets that record’s domain.

Bulk Synchronize

The bulk Synchronize backfill follows each record’s own domain, as do folders, files, notes, attachments, enhanced notes, metadata, and mapping deletion.

A sync run processes one domain at a time. Records for other domains in the same batch are picked up on the next run. When mixed domain batches are processed users can expect a small delay, not an error.

Deleting a Connected Domain

  • Open the Egnyte Domain Configuration page and select the domain to remove.
  • Click Edit, then click Delete Domain. A confirmation screen lists exactly what will be deleted - the domain and all of its configuration including related templates and metadata configurations.
  • Check the confirmation checkbox and click the Delete Domain button when ready. If this was the last additional domain, the org reverts to single-domain operation.
  • Deleting a domain does not automatically remove generated Apex triggers for custom objects that no other domain uses. The confirmation screen flags these so the users can remove them manually.

Known Limitations

  • One record maps to one domain; a single record cannot sync to more than one domain at a time.
  • Sync runs process one domain at a time; records for other domains are picked up on the next run.
  • A domain’s Setting Name cannot be renamed once created.
  • Flow action invocables (folder creation/move/delete, permissions, file upload, link creation, metadata) act on the default domain only.
  • Deleting a domain does not auto-remove generated Apex triggers for custom objects no other domain uses.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do the Users Need to Do Anything After Upgrading to Version 3.11 if They Use One Domain?

No. Single-domain orgs behave exactly as before and it is not required to migrate or reconfigure.

How is Multidomain Enabled?

Automatically, when the first additional domain is connected.

What Happens to Records That Do Not Match Any Routing Rule?

They sync to the default domain.

Who Can Edit Egnyte Settings?

Users with the Egnyte Administrator permission set or full org admin rights.

Can the Domain’s Setting Name Be Renamed?

No. Domain settings cannot be renamed once created

Folder Structure and Custom Paths

How does the integration decide where a record’s folder is created in Egnyte?

When the Default Folder Path option is checked (the default), record folders are created under /Shared/Salesforce.com/<Object Name>/<2-letter hash>/<Record Name>. The two-letter hash is the first two characters of the record name (after spaces and periods are stripped), converted to uppercase (for example, J. Smith Co becomes JS). The hash exists for performance: Egnyte has a limit of 50,000 subfolders per folder, and the hash spreads records across subfolders so that large organizations do not reach it. If a Custom Folder Path is selected instead, the integration follows that path exactly, and no hash folder is added.

If an object has a Parent Object set in its Egnyte Sync Configuration, its folder is created inside the parent record’s folder instead. Parenting is supported up to three levels deep (for example, /Shared/Salesforce.com/Accounts/AC/Acme/Contacts/Jane Doe/Custom Object/…), and one object can be the parent of several child objects.

If the parent lookup on a record is empty (for example, a Contact with no Account), the folder is created at the object’s own path instead: the Custom Folder Path if one is configured, otherwise the default path. When a record does have a parent, the parent’s folder takes precedence, and any Custom Folder Path on the child object is ignored.

Can the integration use an existing folder structure in Egnyte instead of creating folders under /Shared/Salesforce.com?

Yes. Use Custom Folder Path and Custom Folder Name on the object’s Egnyte Sync Configuration. Create a formula field on the Salesforce object that resolves to the desired path (everything after /Shared/), then select that field as the Custom Folder Path. See Customizing Salesforce Integration with Custom Paths for the walkthrough.

  • The path and folder name must resolve to the exact name of the existing folder. Any difference (an extra space, TX vs. Texas, or a different dash) causes the integration to create a new folder rather than link to the existing one. If the source data is inconsistent, normalize it in the formula (for example, by trimming whitespace).

  • The integration always prepends the /Shared/ root, so it should not be included in the formula.

Is it possible to rename or move the Salesforce.com root folder?

Not directly. The /Shared/Salesforce.com root is fixed for default paths. To place record folders anywhere else, use Custom Folder Paths.

Can records of the same object go to different locations based on a field value (for example, active vs. inactive clients)?

Yes. Build a formula field that returns a different path depending on the field value, for example IF(Active__c = “No”, “Clients/Ex-Clients”, “Clients/Active”) and select it as the Custom Folder Path. When the field changes, the integration moves the folder to the new location.

Formula fields are part of the Salesforce configuration. Egnyte Support can confirm how the integration reads the field but does not write or debug Salesforce formulas. For formula design, work with the Salesforce administrator or contact an Egnyte account manager to engage Egnyte Professional Services.

What happens to the Egnyte folder when a record’s name (or a field used in its path) changes?

The integration renames or moves the existing folder to match. A new folder is created only when more than one record was mapped to the same folder (multimapping). In that case the renamed record gets its own new folder and the original folder stays with the remaining records.

How can the new folder be created for existing records after it is added to the folder template?

Adding a path to an object’s Egnyte Folder Template only applies to records created afterwards. To create it for existing records, run the Create Template Folders bulk action for that object from Egnyte Domain Configuration → Bulk Actions. Folders are created asynchronously through the sync queue, so they may take time to appear. Monitor progress in the Egnyte Sync Queue tab.

Why did existing folders not move after the Sync Configuration (parent object, custom path) was changed?

Sync Configuration changes only affect records created or updated after the change. To restructure existing folders, run the Update Folder Locations bulk action for the object.

A “blank” record update (saving without changing any field used in the path, folder name, or metadata) does not trigger a folder update. The trigger only creates a sync queue item when one of those fields actually changes.

Back to Top…

Folder Creation Behavior

Is it possible to create folders for only some records (for example, only active accounts or only open matters)?

The Create Root Folder setting on a Sync Configuration is all-or-nothing: when checked, a folder is created for every record of that object. The integration has no built-in record filter. Three options are available:

  • Uncheck Create Root Folder: Folders are then created only when a user first opens a record page that contains the Egnyte component.
  • Use a custom path to segregate records: Route unneeded records to a separate, restricted folder via a formula-based Custom Folder Path.
  • Use Salesforce Flow (package 3.8+ or above): Enable Flow Only on the Sync Configuration and build a record-triggered flow with a Decision element (or entry criteria) so only qualifying records reach the Mapped Folder Creation action. See Salesforce Flows with Egnyte Actions. All Sync Configuration settings (paths, names, templates) still apply to folders created this way. When option 3 is used, the Create Template Folders bulk action still creates folders for all records of the object, regardless of the flow’s conditions. Update Folder Locations only affects folders that already exist. Bulk actions continue to work when a Sync Configuration is in Flow Only mode.
Does the Mapped Folder Creation flow action return the Egnyte folder ID?

No. Mapped Folder Creation runs in the trigger context and does not call Egnyte directly. It only creates a sync queue item that is processed later in a separate transaction, so no folder ID exists at that point.

If the folder ID is needed on the record, call the Unmapped Folder Move/Rename action with the same origin and target path. This does not move the folder but returns its folderId. Because it makes a callout, it must run in an asynchronous (scheduled) path of a record-triggered flow or in a non-triggered flow.

What happens in Egnyte when a Salesforce record is deleted?

The folder and its contents remain in Egnyte. The integration never deletes folders or files. If the content is no longer needed, delete the folder in Egnyte manually, or via a flow using the Unmapped Folder/File Delete action. Note that the Mapped Folder Deletion flow action removes only the mapping between a record and its folder, it does not delete the folder itself.

Record-to-folder mapping behavior

From package 3.11 onwards, deleting a record also removes the record-to-folder mapping. If a record is later re-created with the same name and path, it reuses the existing folder.

In the following cases, the mapping is left in place when a record is deleted:

  • Packages before 3.11

  • Flow Only setups with no delete flow calling Mapped Folder Deletion

  • Custom objects whose Egnyte triggers were generated before 3.11 (those triggers have no after-delete handler and are not regenerated on upgrade) When the old mapping remains and a record is re-created, the behavior differs by path type:

  • Default path: the re-created record collides with the old mapping and a new folder is created with ~1 appended to the name. The original folder is not reused.

  • Custom path: no new folder is created, but both the deleted record and the new one are mapped to the same folder. Renaming or re-pathing the new record creates a new folder rather than moving the existing one. To clear stale mappings at scale, contact Egnyte Support with the original record IDs.

The integration created thousands of empty folders. Can it clean them up?

No. The integration does not remove empty or orphaned folders. Cleanup is done manually in Egnyte or through an Egnyte Professional Services engagement.

What should be checked when the sync queue has a backlog and folders are not being created?

Open Egnyte Domain Configuration and click Start Processing Sync Queue. This restarts the scheduled job if it has stopped. Check queue status in the Egnyte Sync Queue tab. If the queue does not drain after restarting, contact Egnyte Support.

Back to Top…

Notes, Files & Attachments

How to stop the “Notes, Files & Attachments” folder from being created in every record folder?

Uncheck Upload Files & Attachments (and Upload Notes, if enabled) on the object’s Egnyte Sync Configuration. In package 3.6 and later these settings are per object, not domain-wide.

The Create Root Folder and Is Default Folder Name settings are unrelated and do not control this folder.

If Upload Files & Attachments is disabled, will it affect files in Salesforce?

No. Disabling the setting only stops the integration from copying new Salesforce Files, Attachments, and Notes to Egnyte. The integration does not create or modify Salesforce Content Documents, so other Salesforce processes that depend on them (for example, document generation tools) are unaffected.

When Upload Files & Attachments is enabled, do the uploaded files appear in Salesforce’s Files related list?

No. Files and attachments are copied to the Notes, Files & Attachments subfolder inside the record’s Egnyte folder. Nothing changes on the Salesforce Files related list unless Delete Files & Attachments is also enabled, in which case the Salesforce copy is removed after a successful upload. Uploads are limited to 12 MB per file due to Salesforce callout limits.

Back to Top…

Permissions

Users have no permissions on folders the integration creates. Why, and how to fix it?

The integration assigns Egnyte folder permissions only when a user opens a record page that contains the Egnyte component (canvas app, Lightning component, or Visualforce page). At that moment the visiting user is granted the level set in Default Permission on the Egnyte Domain Configuration, or the level set on the component itself.

Folders created any other way (by trigger on record creation, bulk actions, or flows) receive no explicit permissions. They inherit from their parent folder in Egnyte, the same as any other Egnyte folder.

To grant permissions to groups or specific users automatically at folder-creation time, use the Assign Folder Permissions action in a Salesforce Flow (package 3.8+), or set permissions on the parent folder in Egnyte so new record folders inherit them.

Why do users still receive Owner permission after the Default Permission was changed from Owner to Viewer?

Two settings determine the permission granted on visit:

  • Default Permission on the Egnyte Domain Configuration tab.
  • The permission parameter on the Egnyte component itself, set when the component was added to the Lightning record page (App Builder) or in the Visualforce markup (permission=“Owner”). This overrides the domain default. Check the component configuration on each record page. If it has an explicit permission set, that value takes precedence.
Does lowering Default Permission reduce permissions users already have?

No. The integration only adds a permission entry when the visiting user has no permission or a lower level than the configured default. It never downgrades or removes existing permissions. To reduce permissions, change them in Egnyte directly or use the Assign Folder Permissions flow action.

The Salesforce record owner doesn’t automatically appear in the Egnyte folder’s permissions. Is that expected?

Yes. Permissions are granted to users who visit the record with the Egnyte component present, not based on record ownership. If the owner has not visited the record, they will not have an explicit entry. Use a flow with the Assign Folder Permissions action if owner-based permissions are required.

Back to Top…

Lightning Experience

Is there a Lightning component that allows dynamic page layouts to be used instead of the Visualforce page?

Yes. The package includes EgnyteComponent, an Aura component compatible with Lightning App Builder and dynamic page layouts. Look for it under Custom – Managed in the App Builder component list. The Visualforce approach in the Administration article remains supported for orgs that prefer it.

My Sync Configuration doesn’t show Folder Templates in Lightning.

In Lightning, related lists (including Egnyte Folder Templates) appear under the Related tab at the top of the Sync Configuration record, rather than inline as in Classic.

Back to Top…

Upgrades and Compatibility

What should be expected when upgrading the package? Is there downtime? Will the configuration be wiped?

Under normal circumstances there is no downtime, no user-visible interruption, and no configuration change. Upgrades are backward compatible; the Domain Configuration, Sync Configurations, folder templates, and custom paths are retained.

After upgrading:

  • Review new settings introduced since the previous version. There may be many if upgrading from an older release.
  • The Egnyte Sync Configurations page layout is not updated automatically. Add new fields to the layout manually (see Add Egnyte Sync Configurations Layout in the Administration article).
  • If the Egnyte permission sets are used, users receive access to new fields automatically. If custom profiles were built instead, read access to new package fields (for example, efs__EgnyteFolderPath__c) may need to be granted manually. Egnyte recommends the provided permission sets for this reason. Because every Salesforce org has different customizations, always test the upgrade first in a sandbox connected to a trial Egnyte domain before upgrading production.
Is there a rollback or downgrade option if something goes wrong after upgrading?

No. Salesforce does not support downgrading managed packages. This is why Egnyte strongly recommends validating the upgrade in a sandbox first.

Is the package compatible with Salesforce’s ICU locale format update (API version 45.0 or higher)?

Yes. Package 3.7.7 updated all Apex classes to API version 45, and package 3.8 updated all remaining components. Upgrade to the latest version to be fully compliant.

If custom Sync Configurations were created on older versions, the integration generated Apex triggers and test classes in the org. These are not part of the managed package and are not updated automatically. To update them:

  • In a sandbox, go to Setup → Apex Triggers (and Apex Classes), open each Egnyte-generated trigger and test class, click Edit → Version Settings, and set the Salesforce.com API version to 45.0 or higher.
  • Save, run tests, and deploy to production using a change set. There is no need to delete or recreate the triggers. Alternatively, package 3.8 introduced Flow Only mode, which removes the need for generated Apex triggers entirely.
Is it possible to use an Egnyte Service Account for the integration connection instead of a regular user?

Yes, and this is the recommended setup. The existing integration user can be converted to a Service Account, and the connection continues to work. If the integration needs to be re-authenticated (for example, after a password change), the account must be temporarily converted back to a regular user, because Service Accounts cannot log in interactively.

Is it possible to map a new custom object, or re-point an existing custom path to a different object?

Yes. A new Egnyte Sync Configuration can be created for the object, with its parent, templates, and custom path configured as described in the Administration article. If the original implementation was done by Egnyte Professional Services with custom formulas or Apex, changes to that customization are handled through a Professional Services engagement arranged via the Egnyte Account Manager.

Back to Top…

Egnyte for ServiceNow

Egnyte provides its users the ability to enhance their ServiceNow workflows by automating incident creation from Egnyte Secure & Govern. This integration simplifies the process by fetching identified incidents in Egnyte and creating corresponding records in ServiceNow. These incidents can then be assigned to teams such as ITSM or security groups for resolution.

The integration offers configurable options to specify Severity and Issue Type, ensuring precise incident tracking and prioritization in ServiceNow. Leveraging Role-Based Access Control, only ServiceNow administrators can manage settings and access application logs, ensuring secure and streamlined operations.

Configuration Steps

Before configuring the application, the user must be an administrator on Egnyte and ServiceNow side or assign themselves the Egnyte role x_snc_egnyte_prote.egnyte_user within ServiceNow. For more information, click here.

  • Log in to the ServiceNow App and search for Application Registry under System OAuth.
  • Select the appropriate OAuth Provider: Tick the checkbox to select either Egnyte Secure & Govern EU or Egnyte Secure & Govern US based on the region, and then click on the option selected.
  • Enter the Client ID and Client Secret of Secure and Govern obtained from the Egnyte Developer Portal. For more information, click here.
  • In the Egnyte Developer Portal, the Registered OAuth Redirect URI will either be empty or follow this format:

  • Click Update to save the information.

  • After configuring the Egnyte Secure & Govern app details, click on Authenticate.
  • The user will be redirected to another tab; enter the Egnyte account email and click Continue and enter the account password. Note that the user account needs to be an S&G administrator account (Preferrably a service account).
  • Click Execute Now to pull the issues based on configuration.
  • Search for Incidents and click on All to view the incident dashboard.

  • Search for the Egnyte App: Click All in the left-hand top panel of ServiceNow. Type Egnyte Secure & Govern in the search bar to find the app. Click on the Application Logs option under its menu.
  • Access Application Logs: The Application Logs section provides detailed logs of the polling activities (schedule jobs), including timestamps, status, and any potential errors encountered.
  • Use the information below to read the logs.
  • Log Type and Details:
    • INFO: These contain the basic operation details like data sync started.
    • DEBUG: Debug logs provide details about configuration changes. Whenever a configuration is modified, a debug log is generated.
    • ERROR: The Error logs are triggered when the authentication fails, for example:
  • This streamlined process ensures efficient debugging and helps maintain seamless integration between Egnyte Secure & Govern and ServiceNow.

Egnyte ServiceNow Integration FAQs

Egnyte Procore Sync Limitations

Two-way sync of files between one folder in Egnyte to one Project in Procore does not break the sync if the root folder is moved or renamed in Egnyte. In order to rename a root folder user can follow these steps:

  • In Egnyte, open List of Synced Procore Projects
  • Find Sync with desired Folder rename change
  • Rename the desired Folder However, If a folder is already synced with Procore, any subfolders within that folder cannot be synced separately. For example, if /Shared/Procore/Projects/Project_A is synced, syncing /Shared/Procore/Projects/Project_A/Project_B will not be possible.The attempt to do so will break the sync.

Egnyte ServiceNow Integration FAQs

1. What does the Egnyte for ServiceNow integration do?

It automatically creates ServiceNow incidents from issues detected in Egnyte Secure & Govern, enabling centralized tracking and resolution.

2. Does this integration work in real time?

No. The integration uses scheduled polling. Hourly execution is recommended for near-real-time visibility.

3. Who can configure the integration?

Only users with:

  • Egnyte administrator access
  • ServiceNow administrator access (or the assigned Egnyte ServiceNow role)

4. Can I control which issues create ServiceNow incidents?

Yes. You can configure:

  • Severity thresholds
  • Issue types
  • Incident table (IT Service Management or Security)

5. Which ServiceNow tables are supported?

  • Incident table for ITSM workflows
  • Security Incident table for SOC workflows (requires plugin)

6. What happens if authentication fails?

Incident creation stops. Administrators must re-authenticate using the Configuration option in the Egnyte Secure and Govern app within Servicenow.

7. Where can I troubleshoot errors?

Use Application Logs within the Egnyte Secure & Govern app in ServiceNow to view errors, execution status, and polling activity.

8. Can I manually trigger incident creation?

Yes. Administrators can use Execute Now in the Egnyte Secure and Govern app within Servicenow to immediately pull issues based on the current configuration.

9. What ServiceNow release versions are supported?

ServiceNow currently supports:

  • Washington DC
  • Vancouver
  • Xanadu

10. Will end users need access to Egnyte or ServiceNow?

No. End users typically interact only with ServiceNow incidents. Egnyte access is required only for administrators configuring the integration.

Egnyte Webhooks Integration

Overview

Egnyte has made it easier for its users to stay updated with important changes in their files and data through webhooks. Webhooks integration enables sending notifications automatically when certain events happen.

Egnyte has two main products that use these webhooks:

  • Collaborate (Known as Connect in the webhooks repository)
  • Secure & Govern (Known as Protect in the webhooks repository) Whenever an event occurs in either of these products, a webhook sends a notification accordingly. For instance, webhooks can be set up when a particular file is copied or deleted. The endpoint added in the URL field will receive the events from the Webhook.

Prerequisites

  • Only admins can register a webhook
  • The customer’s server should always be in the active state during the entire Webhooks lifecycle.
  • For Collaborate, authorization token must be generated using the associated OAuth scopes in advance.

Event Types

Collaborate (Connect)
  • fs (File System):
    • This is the most commonly used event type for Connect.
    • Events related to changes in the file system, such as adding, updating, deleting, moving, copying, and renaming files and folders.
    • For example - fs:add_file event will generate notifications for the user(s) whenever a new file is added in the given URL.
  • Comment:
    • Events related to comments on files or folders, such as setting or removing comments.
    • Example - comment:set_comment event will generate notifications for the user(s) whenever a comment is added on the provided file link.
  • Link:
    • Events related to shared links, such as creating or deleting shared links.
    • Example - link:create_download_link event will generate a notification whenever a new download link is created for the users.
  • meta (Metadata):
    • Events related to metadata on files or folders, such as adding, updating, and deleting metadata keys.
    • Example - meta:add_metadata_key event will trigger notification when metadata key is added to the provided URL.
  • Permissions:
    • Events related to folder permissions, such as when permissions are changed.
    • Example - permission:permission_change is the event that will trigger a notification when the permission on the specified folder is changed.
Secure & Govern Issues (Protect)
  • Create:
    • This event type can be used when a new issue is created.
  • Modify:
    • These are the events which can be used in scenarios when an existing issue is modified.
  • Resolve:
    • This event type can be used when an issue is marked as resolved. A webhook can be configured to include one or multiple events in a single webhook.

Sample Collaborate Webhook

Steps to Create Webhooks via POST
  • Complete the authentication steps before creating the webhook.
  • Create a webhook via POST by registering webhook.
  • The response will appear as shown below.
  • Following is the payload of the webhook to the receiver
  • The webhook returns the data of the file that was added to the directory. It lists the GroupID which is the unique ID of the file that the receiver can use in order to move the file. The following command shows the GroupID to move the file into another location:

Register S&G Webhook

S&G provides the users with the ability to register a webhook from the UI.

  • Navigate to S&G -> Webhooks to register a new webhook.

Webhook Disabling Automation

  • The retry mechanism tries to send the request 4 times to the client-server (A total of five requests are made including the original request). If there is no proper acknowledgment for these attempts from the client-server, the client webhook is disabled.
  • Conditions for a proper acknowledgment-
    • The response should have a code less than 400.
    • There is a timeout of 3 secs and the response is expected within this time frame.

Limitations

  • Currently, there is a limit of 10 webhooks for Connect and 2 for Protect per domain.

Overview articles

  • Co-Edit Using the Microsoft 365 for the web
  • Egnyte for Google Workspace

FAQ’s

What type of license does one need to use the Microsoft 365 for the web integration?

To use the Microsoft 365 for the web Integration, it is recommended to have the following subscriptions by Microsoft:

  • Microsoft 365 Apps for business
  • Microsoft 365 Business Standard Keep in mind that the subscription compatibility is subject to change by Microsoft and the compatible subscriptions can be referenced here.
Which web browsers are supported for Microsoft 365 for the web integration?

It is recommended to use the supported browsers listed here to use the Microsoft 365 for the web Integration.

Which Egnyte clients are supported?

These changes are available in the Web UI and Egnyte Desktop App for Windows and Mac now. Co-editing in Egnyte Desktop App is not supported with a Smart Cache connection at this time.

Why does the Co-edit button not show up in Web UI?

The Co-edit button is shown so users can have one-click access to their favorite or default co-editing app.

Ensure that the following pre-requisites have been completed:

  • The user must have either Microsoft 365 for the web and/or Google Workspace enabled by the admin and added to the Egnyte account.
  • If both co-editing applications added to the Egnyte account (Microsoft 365 for the web AND Google WorkSpace), the admin will need to set a default app. To do so, the admin needs to go to the App Control Center and and set the default app from the Settings of the respective app. If the user only has one co-editing application (Microsoft 365 for the web OR Google Workspace), the enabled or added application is automatically marked as the default co-editing app.
Are there any size limits?

Microsoft 365 for the web Online has the following limits applied. Google Workspace has its own limitations, for details refer here.

MS Word

100 MB

MS PowerPoint

2 GB

MS Excel

100 MB

Google Docs

50 MB

Google Slides

100 MB

Google Sheets

20 MB

Web UI preview sizes might be different from the above (see Which Types of Files Work with the File Previewer for more details and from the Microsoft site here)

Do these changes work with older versions of the Google Workspace App?

These usability improvements for the Google Workspace App are not compatible with the older versions of Egnyte for Google Workspace. Contact support@egnyte.com if for any questions about compatibility.

Does this integration work with the older Microsoft 365 for the web Online file formats?

For Microsoft, only modern formats including .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, and .xlsb file formats are supported. Users can’t co-author with Office 2007 or earlier format, .rtf, or other formats. In most cases, the user can save the unsupported file format in the supported format first within current versions of Word, Excel, or PowerPoint. For Excel, if the file isn’t in this format, open the file and then click File > Save As > Browse > Save as type. Change the format to Excel Workbook (*.xlsx). Co-Authoring does not support the Strict Open XML Spreadsheet format. For more details on this, see this article Troubleshoot co-authoring.

How can one be sure that the latest changes are saved?

Microsoft 365 for web applications sends edits from the browser to the server as often as possible. However, this process is not instantaneous and can be influenced by many factors, including network latency and performance.

Hence, Microsoft 365 for the web displays the save status indicated in the status bar. If the status bar reads Saved or Saved to <HOST NAME>, then the edits have successfully made it to the server. However, if the status bar reads Saving…or Working…, then the edits have not yet been sent to the server and may be lost if the browser is closed or if the user navigates away from the Microsoft 365 for the web application immediately. Do not close the laptop lid, log out, shut down, or put the machine to sleep during a Saving or Working status to ensure that the changes are saved.

Intermediate (or not the latest) versions of the same file created from the same device by the same user within a short period of time (about 10 min) can be pruned by the version pruning algorithm - see more details on this helpdesk guide Version Pruning.

What are the scenarios where autosave can turn off during Microsoft Co-editing?

There are multiple scenarios where autosave can turn off during Microsoft Co-editing. Refer here for details.

Why does Google Workspace appear as a co-editing option when a user opens a Microsoft Office file?

When Google Workspace integration is enabled for an Egnyte domain, Google Workspace is available as a co-editing provider for both Google-native files and Microsoft Office files.

If the co-editing policy is set to Ask, Egnyte prompts to select a co-editing provider when the user opens a supported file.

If Google Workspace should not be used as a co-editing provider, the administrator can disable the Google Workspace integration entirely.

Sharing Co-Editable Share Links For Google Files

Co-Editing via Links

Co-editable links enable recipients to directly edit files with the Google integration, without requiring access to or permissions for the entire folder. This allows users to securely collaborate on individual documents while maintaining strict control over broader folder-level access.

This approach facilitates cross-team collaboration by eliminating the need to modify folder permissions, reducing administrative overhead, and minimizing the risk of unintended data exposure. It ensures that only the intended files are accessible for editing, improving governance, simplifying access management, and enabling faster, more focused collaboration.

Prerequisites and Limitations

  • Co-Editing via links is available to all the Platform plans. However, Co-editable Share Links for external users are not supported on GxP domains due to regulatory requirements.
  • Co-editable links are supported for Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
  • Egnyte for Google Workspace integration must be enabled for the domain.
  • Co-editable share links are not supported with Anyone or Anyone with password options, for Google workspace integration. In these scenarios, the recipients will not be able to co-edit the files as the co-editing option is disabled while sharing links.
  • When using the People you choose option, it will be required to explicitly grant access to the shared drive.
  • Co-editable preview-only links cannot be shared for Google files. If the users set Downloading to Not Allowed, the Co-editing option will automatically be disabled. There is a message that is displayed to let the users know about the behavior.

Administrator Settings

An administrator can control the types of co-editable links allowed. The configuration item can be accessed via the Settings -> Configuration -> General.

  • Use the toggle for Users can share co-editable links to enable or disable the feature
  • Click on Save changes ​​​​Sharing co-editable links setting is Disabled by default and an administrator must enable this setting.

Admins can also manage email domains for external collaboration. They can choose to Allow or Block certain domains for sharing co-editable links.

Creating Co-Editable Links

Users can create a co-editable link while sharing files or folders. Set Co-editing under Link properties to Allowed.

Show recent file versions link property automatically gets enabled and cannot be changed once the option to co-edit is allowed.

When a recipient clicks on the link in the email notification, they will get an option to co-edit the file with Google Workspace integration.

  • When a link is shared with domain users with Editor permission to the shared file, a new version will be created by the same user.

  • When a link is shared with domain users without Editor permission to the shared file, a new version will be created under the link creator’s username.

Supported Webhook Event Types

Webhooks in Egnyte Collaborate allow users to subscribe to specific system events and receive real-time notifications when those events occur. Events are organized into categories to help configure webhooks based on the integration needs.

File System Events (fs:*)

These events capture file and folder activity within Egnyte.

Supported events (14):

  • fs:add_file: File is uploaded or created
  • fs:add_folder: Folder is created
  • fs:copy_file: File is copied
  • fs:copy_folder: Folder is copied
  • fs:delete_file: File is deleted
  • fs:delete_folder: Folder is deleted
  • fs:delete_from_trash: Item is permanently deleted from trash
  • fs:move_file: File is moved
  • fs:move_folder: Folder is moved
  • fs:restore_from_trash: Item is restored from trash
  • fs:lock_file: File is locked
  • fs:unlock_file: File is unlocked
  • fs:upload_link: File is uploaded via link
  • fs:folder_project_activity: Folder project activity If “fs:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Comment Events (comment:*)

These events track comment activity on files.

Supported events (2):

  • comment:set_comment: Comment is added or updated
  • comment:remove_comment: Comment is removed If “comment:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Link Events (link:*)

These events track creation and deletion of file and upload links.

Supported events (4):

  • link:create_download_link: Download link is created
  • link:create_upload_link: Upload link is created
  • link:delete_download_link: Download link is deleted
  • link:delete_upload_link: Upload link is deleted If “link:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Metadata Events (meta:*)

These events capture metadata changes applied to files.

Supported events (2):

  • meta:add_metadata_key: Metadata key is added
  • meta:delete_metadata_key: Metadata key is removed If “meta:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Permission Events (permission:*)

Supported event (1):

  • permission:permission_change: Permissions modified on a folder If “permission:*” is selected, the above event will be automatically subscribed.

Workflow Events (workflow:*)

These events track workflow lifecycle and approval actions.

Supported events (4):

  • workflow:created: Workflow is created
  • workflow:completed: Workflow is completed
  • workflow:approvaltask_approved: Approval task is approved
  • workflow:approvaltask_rejected: Approval task is rejected If “workflow:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Group Events (group:*)

These events track group lifecycle and membership changes.

Supported events (7):

  • group:create: Group is created
  • group:delete: Group is deleted
  • group:rename: Group is renamed
  • group:add_members: Members are added
  • group:remove_members: Members are removed
  • group:add_owner: Owner is added
  • group:remove_owner: Owner is removed If “group:*” is selected, all the above events are automatically subscribed.

Use Egnyte for DocuSign

Once the DocuSign app is configured, a user start sending Egnyte files for eSignature from the WebUI or the Desktop App. The article covers the steps to send a DocuSign template from Egnyte and more.

Sending with DocuSign is currently supported for these file types:

  • Microsoft Word documents (.doc and .docx)
  • Microsoft Excel spreadsheets (.xls and .xlsx)
  • Adobe Portable Document Format documents (.pdf)
  • Text documents (.txt and .rtf)
  • Images (.jpg, .tif, .gif and .png) The maximum allowed size from DocuSign is 25 MB.

Send a Document for eSignature - Web UI

Send a Document for eSignature - Desktop App

Additional Options

Send a Document for eSignature

DocuSign has a rich web interface that gives users many options for managing their signed documents. This article focuses on a simple use case where a user wants to collect a signature from a single person. Detailed documentation on DocuSign’s capabilities is available here.

WebUI
  • Navigate to the file to send for eSignature.
  • Open the action menu, hover over Share, and select the Send with DocuSign option.
  • A user can send files within any folder for which they have Editor permissions or higher.
  • Users can select the location to store the signed document by clicking on the location field and selecting the folder location. There is also an option to keep/remove the original file. If the Keep original file checkbox is checked, the original file will be kept, otherwise the original file will not be available.
  • This feature to keep original file is currently in Limited Availability. To request this feature, contact our Products team.
  • The DocuSign interface will open in a new browser window.
  • Click on Add Recipients at the top left corner of the screen.
  • Specify the recipient(s) for the document and click Done.
  • Drag the Signature field from the left menu and drop where the recipient shall add the signature. Similarly, add other fields as needed.
  • Click on Send.
  • The recipient(s) will receive an email requesting them to review and sign the document.
  • Once the recipients confirm their signature, the document will be “completed” in DocuSign, and a signed copy of the document (in PDF format) will appear in the Egnyte account in the folder where the original document resides. The signed copy will have a note automatically added to it indicating date of sign-off. Egnyte periodically checks with DocuSign to detect when sign-off has been completed, so there may be a slight delay of a few minutes before the signed copy shows up in the account.
Desktop App
  • Open Window’s File Explorer or Mac’s Finder and navigate to the file to send for eSignature.
  • Right-click on the file, hover over Share and select the Send with DocuSign option.
  • The same steps can be taken as mentioned earlier for WebUI within the DocuSign interface. The user can send files within any folder for which they have Editor permissions or higher.

Additional Options

Send with a Template.

In addition to sending a regular file for signature, Egnyte now supports sending a template from the More menu. This kicks off a signature flow using the DocuSign templates. Once the document is signed, it is returned to the folder from which the “send template” workflow was launched.

DocuSign Status Page

The More menu also has a DocuSign status page which shows the current status of recent DocuSign activity. This includes signature requests in a draft state, in process, and completed in the last week. From here, the user can take some additional actions on the signature request like re-sending the reminder, voiding a contract, reopening a draft, and showing a signed document.

Import Bulk List Feature

The user can send a DocuSign template using the IMPORT BULK LIST feature in DocuSign. All the signed documents from individual users will be saved back to the original Egnyte folder location as separate PDFs.

  • Choose recipients on the DocuSign document.
  • Click IMPORT BULK LIST and upload a .csv file with the recipient list.
  • Proceed with the rest of the usual process and send out the document for eSignature.

The web app

3rd-Party Recipient-Specific File and Folder Links

When files and folders need to be shared with 3rd party individuals only, the newly enhanced specific recipient link security option can be utilized.

Previously the recipient-specific link security choice only allowed domain users to be included as recipients. Now 3rd parties can be added to the recipient list via email address.

This feature is available for Platform Enterprise and Enterprise Lite customers only. Contact your Sales Rep or Egnyte Sales team for more details.

Enabling The 3rd-Party Recipient Option

To enable this ability, an administrator needs to change the following settings for the Egnyte domain. Go to Settings->General, then to the Sharing section and set the value of the Specific Recipients include parameter to “Any email recipient”:

Enabling Send links in user’s default mail client automatically disables Private (recipients only) option in the link types.

Creating a 3rd-Party Recipient-Specific Link

To create a file link that only named recipients can access, choose the People you choose option and add email addresses to the list of recipients.

Recipients will receive an email containing the link. Internal users can click on the link to access the shared file.

​​External users, however, ​will need a​n access​ code to open the file. ​They can click on the link to open a secure access page in their browser. ​

​​The recipient ​will immediately receive a separate ​email with the ​unique ​access code​. ​They can also click on a direct file​ or ​folder link in the mail to access the shared file​ or ​folder.​

​​Alternatively, they​​​​ can enter the access code after opening the original link​​​.​​​​

Revoking Access To Links To Recipient-Specific File Or Folder Links

Active links visual indicator in Web UI

Active links visual indicator in Web UI Sharing links is an integral part of content collaboration. While navigating through the content, it becomes essential for the users to easily know if there are any active links present for a file or folder.

Egnyte provides visibility into the presence of active links while navigating through the file and folder listing, search results and recent files.

This feature is available to all platform customers.

Active links indicator locations

The active link visual indicator is available in the following three places within Web UI. The indicator indicates the presence of active links and the number of active links present as shown below.

  • File & Folder Listing
  • Search Results
  • Recent Files

Active links Details

The user can click on the indicator to get more details about each of the active links for a file or folder. The details like who has shared the link, what type of link it is along with the link properties, and when was the last time the link accessed will be displayed in a pop-up as shown below.

Domain administrators will have an additional option to go to the links dashboard to manage all the links in case they need to.

Standard Users will not have visibility into who shared the link and hence the name of the link owner will be masked on the link details pop-up.

Ad Blocking

For customers who use adblocking extensions (i.e., Adblock Plus and uBlock), please allow the Egnyte domain or pause your adblocking while using Egnyte. If ad blocking is enabled while using Egnyte, some shared functionality may be blocked by the 3rd party application.

Adding Metadata to a File Using Workflows

The Add metadata to a file action, available within the Automated Action step in workflow templates, allows users to automatically apply metadata to files as part of the workflow process. This helps organizations to ensure files are properly categorized and searchable without manual intervention.

This article provides step-by-step instructions on configuring the Add Metadata to File action in a workflow.

How to Add Metadata to File action step to a Workflow

Users can set up Add metadata to a file action within the Template Steps Setup section of a Workflow Template.

Workflow Templates can be accessed in the Workflows -> Configuration Settings. This article specifically covers instructions for configuring a Move file to a folder step only. Refer to Workflow Templates Overview for the complete setup of a Workflow Template.

Follow these steps to add the Add metadata to a file step within a Workflow Template.

  • Click on the + icon in the graphic builder.
  • Select Metadata Tag under Automated Actions as the step.
  • Enter the Step name with up to 128 characters. The Step name can be set to editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.
  • Enter a Description with up to 512 characters. The description can be set to editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.
  • Select an existing Metadata section from the dropdown list. Refer to Create Metadata to create required Metadata sections.
  • Select Property and Value to be applied as a part of this workflow step. When executed, the metadata value will be automatically assigned to the file as part of the workflow process.
  • For metadata properties that require dates, users have two options for defining the metadata value:
    • Add specific date as a metadata value: Users can manually select specific date to be applied for the metadata value.
    • Add step completion date as metadata value: Users can select this option to assign the step completion date as the metadata value. Additionally, they can adjust the date by adding or subtracting days from the completion date using the switch. This provides flexibility to modify the metadata date relative to the step completion date.
  • Set the workflow condition by choosing one of the following options from If this step fails, then dropdown list:
  • Mark step as “Failed” and cancel workflow - This selection will mark the Add Metadata step as “Failed” and cancel the workflow when the Metadata value is not applied to the file within 24 hours.
  • Mark step as “Failed” and continue workflow execution - This selection will mark the Add Metadata step as “Failed” and workflow execution will continue to the next step or workflow will be marked completed if this is the last step of the workflow when the Metadata value is not applied to the file within 24 hours. When the system initially fails to add metadata, such as when metadata value or scope is changed after the workflow creation, the system will automatically retry to add metadata at regular intervals for up to 24 hours. Additionally, users have the option to manually push the Retry Request button in the workflow pane every 2 hours.

Example Use Case

Add Verified tag to a file once reviewed

Create a workflow with a review step first and then add an Automated Action step to update the verified metadata field to Yes.

Additional Details on Folder Sharing

This article outlines how examples of how folder sharing works in Egnyte. To learn how to share folders and the privileges associated with different access levels, please read this article.

Sharing Folders

In Egnyte, a folder and all files within are visible only when the folder is shared with a user (power user or standard user) or a group containing that user. If the folder is not shared, then that folder and all files within it are not visible. The only exception to this case is the administrator of the account. All files are folders are visible to the administrator by default.

A group is any logical grouping of users that satisfies your business needs, such as a department or project team. A user can belong to more than one group.

Folder Sharing Passes to Sub-Folders from a Parent Folder (Inheritance)

By default, folder permissions are inherited by all sub-folders. For example, if you define a folder and share that folder with users A and B when you create a sub-folder within this folder, users A and B will automatically have access to this sub-folder. There is no need for you to explicitly share the sub-folder with users A and B.

Learn more about disabling folder inheritance for a folder

Folders can be Shared at Any Level

Consider a folder Sales under the Shared folder on your file server. The Sales folder has been shared with users A and B. You now define two sub-folders Accounts and Collateral directly under the Sales folder. By the rules of inheritance described earlier, users A and B will have access to Accounts and Collateral. You can optionally share the Collateral sub-folder with user C. In this case, when user C logs in, C will have navigational access to the Sales folder (i.e., the Sales folder will appear in grey). If the Sales folder has files in it, those files won’t be visible to C, since the Sales folder is not shared with user C, and user C will see only the Collateral sub-folder of Sales. Further, user C will not see the Accounts sub-folder since Accounts has not been shared with user C.

Users A and B, however, will see Sales, Accounting, and Collateral folders.

Folder Sharing can be Removed at Any Level (Exclusion)

Consider a folder Sales under the Shared folder of your file server. The Sales folder has been shared with users A and B. You now create two sub-folders Accounts and Collateral directly under the Sales folder. By the rules of inheritance, users A and B will have access to Accounts and Collateral.

Let’s assume you do not want user B to have access to the Accounts sub-folder. You can remove user B from having access to the Accounts sub-folder. We refer to this as Exclusion. In the Folder Permissions Report, there will be a None record for the Exclusion.

When user B logs in, B will see Sales and Collateral folders but not Accounting. However, user A will see all three folders Sales, Collateral, and Accounting.

Alternatively, if the Accounts folder is a very sensitive folder and you want to make sure that when a new user is added to the Sales folder that they don’t automatically get access to the Accounts folder, then you can disable folder inheritance for the Accounts folder.

User and Group Sharing on the Same Folder

You may share a folder with both a user and a group. If the group also happens to contain the same user, the user’s folder sharing access will override the group-based access for that user.

For example, the Sales folder has been shared with both User A and Group X. Group X also contains User A in addition to other users. Group X has been provided Read-Only access to the Sales folder; hence User A derives Read-Only access from Group X. However, User A has been provided Read and Write access directly to the Sales folder. Hence, when User A logs in, A will have Read and Write access to the Sales folder.

Administrator Notification Settings

It’s important to stay up to date with all of Egnyte’s notifications to ensure that important updates or account changes are never missed. Learn how to customize all Admin notification settings to meet organizational requirements and user preferences.

Users can learn how to customize their folder notifications here.

Folder Notifications

First Time User Login Notifications

Password and Email Change Notifications

Sync Notifications

Storage Consumption Notifications

Trash Purge Notifications

Folder Notifications

When an employee or business partner edits or uploads a file to a shared folder, Egnyte can notify all users with access to that folder of the changes. However, Egnyte offers highly granular controls for modifying how often one receive these types of notifications. For details on Administrator settings, visit Folder Notifications for Administrators.

The person that changed the file will not receive a notification.

First Time User Login Notifications

When a new user logs in for the first time, Egnyte can send an email notification to all admins. This notification acts as a confirmation for new user onboarding. The notification setting can be turned off from Settings > Configuration > General.

Password and Email Change Notifications

If the Advanced Authentication feature is enabled on the domain then admins can configure Egnyte to send notification emails to users whenever their passwords are changed. Admins can also receive notifications when users reset their passwords. These alerts can serve as useful red flags for suspicious activity. These notifications can be found by going under Settings > Configuration > Security & Authentication > Password Controls section (shown below).

Sync Notifications

Sync Inactivity

With Sync Inactivity Notifications, Admins can receive email alerts when sync applications don’t successfully sync within a designated time period. This helps in monitoring sync failures across the various Storage Sync products. To set up notifications, go to Settings, select the Configuration tab, choose Applications, and scroll down to the Sync section.

To receive email notifications, set the Notify me… switch to Enabled. A set of options will appear.

  • Use the drop-downs to specify a time interval for inactivity after which an email notification will be sent.
  • Use the check boxes to specify whether inactivity notifications should be sent for Storage Sync Virtual Machines and Storage Sync for NETGEAR. Sync inactivity notification emails will contain a list of sync failures that occurred in a certain period. It will also contain IP addresses and device names to help diagnose sync failures.

Egnyte ended support for NETGEAR on September 30th, 2021. For more information, please see this article: Future of Storage Sync for NETGEAR.

Storage Sync Alerts

Enabling Storage Sync alerts allows Admins to receive an alert when there are possible performance or storage issues with the Storage Sync device(s). It’s highly recommended that admins enable these notifications so they can take immediate action to resolve the issue.

Storage Consumption Notifications

Admins have several notification settings to help them better manage the trash contents and storage capacity on their file server.

Overall storage consumption can be monitored by configuring a notification email to be sent when a specified percentage of the account’s storage has been used. By default, this alert will trigger when the account crosses 85% of the purchased storage. This setting can be found in Settings > Configuration > General.

Admins and users with Can manage billing power user role can also monitor storage consumption from the counter in Settings > Subscriptions > Current Plan page. Hovering the mouse over the storage counter will show what portion of the consumed storage is being used by files, trash, and back-up versions of files.

Private Folder Quota

Administrators can set up a notification for users that exceed a storage size limit within their Private Folder. When this setting is enabled, Admins will receive a weekly summary report with the top 15 users that have exceeded the quota. If a user exceeds the size limit, they will receive a daily notification in their browser until the issue is resolved.

Check out this article to learn more!

Trash Purge Notifications

Deleted files go to the trash can. After a certain number of days (30 is the default), files in the trash will be purged. To receive an email before files are purged, enable the option depicted below.

Administrators, Power Users, and Standard Users

An Egnyte account has three different types of users. A person’s user type governs whether they have access to a broad array of Egnyte features including audit reports, user management, FTP upload capabilities, and private folders.

User types are different from folder permissions, which determine the set of actions that a user can perform on a particular folder (downloading or deleting files, moving the folder, etc.). User Groups are a convenient way to cluster users for assigning common permissions to folders.

Skip Ahead to…

Administrators

Power Users

Standard Users

Additional Resources

Administrators

By default, the person who registers for an Egnyte account is the Administrator of that account. Additional Administrator accounts can be created or deleted as necessary. Administrators can perform the following actions.

  • Create Power Users, Standard Users, and Groups from the Users & Groups menu: This is essential to provide other users with access to Egnyte.
  • Create root-level folders under the Shared Folder: This is the first step in creating a folder scheme that is customized for your business needs.
  • Control license & subscription settings: The Administrator can purchase more Power User licenses and provide credit card information for managing the subscription to the Egnyte service.
  • Run reports to see the status of active file links from your account, how folder permissions have changed, and more.
  • Mandate security controls like two-step log-in verification, password rotation requirements, and minimum password length.
  • Delegate permissions like Plan Details page access or Standard User management using Role-based Administration. Administrators cannot be restricted from accessing specific folders.

Power Users (Employees)

Assign the Power User permission level to your company’s employees. Power Users are given full use of Egnyte’s access methods and advanced features. Depending on your plan, Power Users can access files using the web browser, FTP, Desktop App, mobile apps, and can invite Standard Users. Power Users also receive a personal sub-folder, /Private/username (e.g., /Private/jsmith), that is accessible only to them (and the account Admins).

Admins can assign some administrative rights to Power Users using the Role-based Administration feature. Plan Details page access, standard user management, and top-level folder creation are a few of the functions that can be delegated to Power Users.

Standard Users (Business Partners)

Assign the Standard User permission level to your company’s customers, vendors, and other outside partners. Standard Users can be given access to shared folders (but do not have their own private folders) and can log into Egnyte through a web browser or mobile app. Standard Users have limited access to advanced Egnyte features and cannot share folder or file links.

Standard Users are also not granted access to Egnyte Desktop App, Storage Sync, or STP/FTP. In addition, Standard Users cannot be authenticated using an external Active Directory or SSO identity provider.
