Advanced Folder Copy and Folder Templates

If users recreate the same folder structure each time a new project starts or a new sales opportunity is discovered, folder templates make the process easier with the Advanced Folder Copy feature. In just a few clicks, Advanced Folder Copy lets users copy an entire folder hierarchy, including sample files, to another destination within Egnyte.

How To

Create a Template

First, set up the basic folder structure that can reused as a template. This folder can have the desired sub-folders and sample files (for example, budget template or project plan templates) already populated within the folders.

It is recommended to include Template in the name to avoid having another user accidentally make changes to the structure.

Apply a Template

  • When it’s time to create a new project, click the box for the top-level template folder in the Web UI and select Move or Copy from the menu.

  • Select Copy, and choose the target folder. Click on the Advanced copy properties dropdown located in the footer of the dialog.

  • From here, the user can choose the desired settings:

    • Folder name: Enter the new folder name, as needed
    • Description: Add a description for the folder
    • Permissions: Users can choose to keep source folder permissions, apply destination folder permissions, or setup new permissions after copying

  • If the user chooses the third option Setup new permission after copying, they will be redirected to the target location to set up new permissions after they click on the Copy button.

  • The following permissions pop-up will appear and the users can set up the folder permissions as needed.

  • Options: Users can choose to keep the source folder options or apply destination folder options. The default option is as per the configured folder options setting.

  • Click on Copy after making the desired selections.

  • To understand the difference between inherited permissions and non-inherited permissions, refer to this article.

  • When a folder is created using a template, any metadata values set on the template folder are also copied to the new folder. Refer here for details on managing metadata.

Additional Details

Consider the following points when using Advanced Folder Copy:

  • Advanced Folder Copy is only available when copying an individual parent folder.
  • Any files within the folder will also be copied. This is useful if users want to include base files in a template structure (for example, an empty budget sheet).
  • A folder description can only be set if users have Full or Owner permissions to the destination folder.
  • Similarly, the option to reset permissions is only available if users have Owner permissions to the destination folder.

Advanced Video Playback

Overview

Video files are increasingly becoming one of the most common file types uploaded and shared with Egnyte. With the current Egnyte’s WebUI preview capabilities, users can only preview video formats natively supported for preview in the standard web browser such as MP4 files with H.264 encoding as well as AAC or MP3 encoded audio stream. Video file sizes are often limited to 500MB or less.

Egnyte’s Advanced Video Playback feature supports:

  • Additional video formats.
  • Previews of video files up to 2GB or 90 minutes replay duration. If the original video exceeds 90 minutes, a banner notifies users when a shortened version of the video is being viewed.
  • Video streaming to reduce bandwidth and allow easier content buffering within a video file.
  • Video preview on Preview-Only file and Folder links.

Features

Video Streaming

Videos will be available to the user via HLS (HTTP Live Streaming), providing just enough of the video for viewing. The user can click on a different section of the video and the player will skip to the selection as well as buffer the remaining content.

In order to enable video streaming retroactively (for files uploaded before activation of Advance Video Playback), transcoding of video files is triggered at the first preview request for each given file. After transcoding completion, the transcoded video remains immediately available for all subsequent preview requests.

Supported Video Formats

The following video formats are currently supported:

  • mov
  • avi
  • wmv
  • mp4
  • mpeg
  • m4v
Video Resolution

Transcoded videos will be generated at a 720p resolution. Higher-resolution videos will be downscaled, while smaller videos will be kept at their original size.

Maximum Video Size/Length

The maximum size for videos that will be transcoded is 2GB or 90 minutes of video. Files larger than 2GB will not be transcoded.

If the original video exceeds 90 minutes, a banner notifies users when they are viewing a shortened version of the video. Users can choose to download the full video onto their device for uninterrupted viewing.

Video Preview on Preview-Only File and Folder Links

With Advanced Video Playback, video preview is also available for Preview-Only file and folder links (files and folders shared via links with the ‘Allow downloads?’ settings option set to ‘No’).

Known Limitations

  • Transcoding Speed
  • The transcoding speed of videos can vary based on factors such as file size and resolution, sometimes taking several minutes. While Egnyte is constantly enhancing transcoding performance, certain video files may temporarily be delivered directly (as full file downloads) to the browser cache, utilizing the browser’s built-in video player. This approach aims to enable quicker preview initiation for users, specifically for videos undergoing transcoding.
  • If the transcoded video is not yet accessible and a native preview is not available, an error message will be displayed.
  • Preview Delay
  • Transcoding videos to another format may take some time to complete and the preview may not be available immediately for video files. Typically, videos can be previewed a few minutes after uploading; however, larger or longer videos will take more time to transcode.
  • WebUI Only and Android App
  • Support for Advanced Video Preview is currently limited to the WebUI. The support of this feature has been added to the Android App (Egnyte 8.12 or higher). iOS support is not available yet.

Agent Step in Workflow Templates

The Agent Step allows users to run the existing Egnyte agents as part of a workflow execution. The agent reads the document and understands its content and can automate time-consuming repetitive tasks for users.

AI Actions are available to the customers with the AI add-on enabled. AI Agent step is available to the customers on Elite or Ultimate plans. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Add AI Agent in Workflow Template Step

  • Select the AI Agent from the Add Step pop up.
  • The system adds the Agent step in a workflow and opens the step configuration panel on the right side of the workflow builder.
    • Under the General section, enter a title in the Step name field and add an optional summary in the Description field. Check the Allow edits box under either field to let users modify the step name or description during workflow creation.
    • Select the file(s) to be used as a Source for the Agent.
    • If any of the selected files are unavailable during the agent step execution, then the step will be marked as failed, and workflow execution will continue based on the Failure Logic configuration for the step.
    • Click Select agent to use on this step field under the Details section then type and search for the specific AI agent to add.
    • Provide custom instructions in the Additional prompt for the Agent field which will be appended directly to the base agent instructions during execution.
    • Click the Test AI Agent Execution button to launch the interactive AI Agent execution testing window.
    • Select the file to run the test on.
    • Confirm the testing document under the Selected file section of the pop-up, or click Select different file to select an alternative sample document. Review or refine the instructions in the Additional prompt for the Agent field’s text area, then click the Execute button at the bottom left. Evaluate the generated output on the right side of the screen and click Use prompt to save the verified configuration back to the workflow step.
    • Navigate to the Save the output of the prompt execution as a dropdown menu located below the testing button. Users can save the output of agent execution as a Workflow step comment, File comment, File metadata or save it in a New file (.docx).
    • If the File metadata option is selected, then users can select any predefined Metadata section. The metadata properties from the selected section are displayed below the Metadata section field.
    • If the New file (.docx) option is selected then users can click the Edit button on the blue informational banner to customize the dynamic naming convention (for example, {Document Name}_{Workflow ID}).
    • The system opens up a File Saving rules dialog box. Type a custom title in the File name field, or press the opening curly bracket key { to insert dynamic tokens such as {Document Name} or {Workflow ID}.
    • Navigate to the Specify the location to save the file section to configure where the generated files will live.
      • Select the Same as the original file location radio button for the output to be stored alongside the original source document.
      • Select the Specific folder radio button to direct all generated files to a designated directory, making sure the template users have appropriate access permissions to that location.
    • Click the Save button in the bottom right corner to finalize the naming conventions and file storage rules.
    • Navigate to the Failure Logic section at the bottom of the side panel to configure how the system handles errors during execution of this step.
      • Click the dropdown menu underneath the label If this step fails, then to view error-handling options.
        • Select Mark step as “Failed” and cancel workflow to mark the Agent step as Failed and cancel the workflow when the agent is not executed successfully within 24 hours.
        • Select Mark step as “Failed” and continue workflow execution (default) to mark the step as Failed and workflow execution will continue to the next step or workflow will be marked completed if this is the last step of the workflow when the agent step is not executed successfully within 24 hours.

Delete the Agent Step

To delete the step, click on the three-dots icon -> Delete either from the right side panel or from the graphic builder.

Connector Authorization

Some AI agents in Egnyte workflows use MCP connectors, such as Gmail, Slack, or Jira. For the successful completion of the agent step execution, the workflow creator must authorize each required connector. The steps mentioned below walks through how authorization works when creating a workflow manually and when created from an automated trigger.

  • When creating a workflow manually from a template that includes an agent step requiring connector authorization, the system will display a warning before the workflow is created.
  • Click any connector name in the list to open its authorization page in a new browser tab.
  • Complete the authorization flow for each connector. Users can authorize all connectors before proceeding, or skip this step and authorize later.
  • Click Create workflow to proceed. The workflow will be created regardless of whether authorization has been completed.
  • When a created workflow (manually or automated) reaches the agent step, the workflow creator receives an email notification.
  • Click Authenticate in the email to open the workflow and view the agent step.
  • In the agent step, review the list of connectors requiring authentication.
  • Click any connector name in the list to open its authorization page in a new browser tab.
  • Click each connector link in the error message to complete authorization.
  • Once all connectors are authorized, click Retry to execute the agent step. The step is marked as failed if connectors are not authenticated within 24 hours of the step starting. If any tool within a connector requires user permissions, those specific tools are blocked in the workflow.

AI Prompts in Workflow Templates

Egnyte enables users to integrate AI prompts directly into workflow steps. While creating workflow templates, users can add AI prompt execution as part of an Automated Action step.

During the template setup, users can run and test these prompts in real-time, with the option to store the AI-generated output as a workflow step comment, a file comment, or as custom metadata.

These AI-powered workflow steps can be leveraged to automate tasks such as document review, summary generation, and custom metadata extraction.

The feature is available only through the Egnyte AI Add-on. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get it enabled.

Add AI Prompt in Workflow Templates Step

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> Workflows.
  • Navigate to Templates and click on Add template -> File Workflow Template.
  • Create the template referring to the steps here.
  • Click on the + icon in the graphic builder.
  • Select AI Prompt under AI Actions as the step.
  • Fill the details as Step name and Description. Click on Allow edits checkbox for Step name and/or Description to allow edits.
  • Provide the desired AI prompt.
    • The user can save the prompt result as a workflow step comment, file comment, or file metadata.
    • They can also choose the action that shall be taken if the step fails.

Test AI Prompt Execution

  • After providing the AI prompt, click on Test AI Prompt Execution.
  • Click on Select File and select the file that can be used to test the AI prompt. Click on Continue after file selection.
  • Click on Execute to test the prompt. The user can also modify the prompt and select a different file for testing, if needed. Click on Apply after the desired modifications are done.
  • The user can then continue to create and save the template.

AI-Driven Document Type Metadata Tags

Egnyte uses AI to automatically apply Document Type metadata tags to the files. When a document is previewed or used with AI features like Egnyte’s AI Assistant, the system analyzes the content and assigns an appropriate type such as Contract, Engineering Report, RFI, or Specification.

How Classification Works

The classifier is built on language models and analyzes document content to determine the most appropriate type from Egnyte’s supported document categories.

For most documents, this works seamlessly. However, for complex or highly specialized documents, the classifier may sometimes choose a related type instead of the best fit. For instance, tagging a geotechnical report as an Engineering Report rather than a more specific category.

Classification Improvement Based on User Feedback

Egnyte offers users the ability to modify the document type tags as required. When a user updates a Document Type tag, the change is recorded as feedback and used to improve classification accuracy over time. For complex or specialized document types, the system looks for consistent correction patterns before applying improvements.

Accuracy improves when similar corrections are made across multiple files, especially when they come from multiple users. Corrections made by Admins and Power Users are given greater weight, and the system applies the pattern only after observing enough consistent corrections.

As Document Type tags are refined across the document library, the classifier gradually adapts and becomes more aligned with the organization’s specific document landscape.

When AI auto-classification applies a document type tag, the event is recorded in the audit log as ADD_METADATA_KEY and attributed to the user who opened the file while the AI Assistant pane was open. This is expected behavior and does not indicate that the user manually changed the metadata.

Updating Document Type Tags

Users with read or write permissions on a document can update Document Type tags in multiple ways:

From File Listing in Web UI
  • Hover over the document in the Web UI and click on the Edit icon in the Document Type column.
  • Add or remove the tag(s) and click on Save.
From File Preview
  • Open the file in preview and navigate to Tags.
  • Find the Egnyte Document Tags and click on the three-dots option -> Edit tags.
  • Add or remove the tag(s) and click on Save.
From Egnyte’s AI Assistant in File Preview
  • Open the file in preview. In the Egnyte’s AI Assistant option, Click on Modify to change the document type.
  • Add or remove the tag(s) and click on Save. AI Assistant is only available for customers having Platform Plans with AI Add-on and included in the New Generation Platform plans. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

AI-Powered Summary of the Share Links

Egnyte provides its users with the ability to generate the summary of the link being shared via email and include it as a message for the recipient(s).

When the users share file and folder links in the Web UI, they get an option to email the link after setting the link properties.

Click on Generate Summary option to get the AI-generated summary of the file or folder being shared.

The summary will be generated and it will appear in the message box.

Users can continue to share the link while the summary is being generated. In this case, the email will be sent without the summary included as an optional message.

If the user has already typed a message and then clicks on the Generate Summary option, the summary will be generated and added after their message.

The summary will be generated only when a single file or folder is selected for being shared via email.

Am I Subject to Any Restrictions?

There are certain limits that an account may be subject to depending on if it is a trial account or a paid account, so be sure to review the information below for more details.

Trial Account Limits

Trial accounts have a limit on certain file types including .zip, .exe, .bat, etc. Likewise, trial and newly created domains are not allowed to send share links via email. These are precautionary measures to help prevent spammers from utilizing Egnyte to send malware and phishing links. These limits are only applied to trials and newly paid domains and are lifted by contacting support.

Furthermore, trial users on all plans are restricted to uploading 1GB of data via FTP and are limited to 20GB of total storage on their trial domain. These restrictions are lifted immediately upon subscription.

Trial domains are restricted from using the Create URL functionality under the Create button due to security concerns.

Paid Account Limits

Plan File Size Limits

Different plans are subject to different file size limits.

  • Platform Business: 100GB
  • Platform Enterprise Lite: 150GB
  • Platform Elite: 150GB
  • Platform Ultimate: 150GB
Uploading Files

Egnyte offers many different ways to upload the content into the cloud. Please note that the overall plan file size limits apply regardless of the upload mechanism in use.

  1. Dragging and Dropping files into the web interface works as per the plan’s file size limits.

  2. Browsing for Files from the web interface upload screen works as per the plan’s file size limits.

  3. Accessing files through the Desktop App is only subject to plan file size limits.

  4. Server synchronization using Storage Sync is only subject to plan file size limits.

  5. FTP uploading is only subject to plan file size limits.

FTP is NOT recommended as a migration tool. For 50GB data total to migrate, consider using Egnyte’s Migration App or some other third-party tool designed to handle larger data migrations.

Downloading

The user can download up to 10,000 files at a time from the Web UI for folder downloads or multi-file downloads, which create a zip. The total download size is restricted to 10GB, in addition to the 10,000 file limit or the 50,000 folder count limit in both Web UI and Mobile Apps. This restriction is different from the limits that apply when users download from Shared File Links For the single file download limit - the plan file size limit applies, as well as the information below:

  1. Downloading single files from the web interface works for files up to 100GB in size.

  2. Accessing files through the Desktop App is only subject to plan file size limits.

  3. Server synchronization using Storage Sync is only subject to plan file size limits.

  4. FTP downloading is only subject to plan file size limits.

Also, keep in mind that browsers impose their own set of limitations on downloading, which the user can change.

Downloading from Shared File Links

Customers on certain Platform and Legacy plans are subject to limits on the quantity of data that can be downloaded from Shared Links.

  • Team plan: 5GB per hour or 30GB per month.

  • Office and Business plans: 5GB per hour or 60GB per month. Partner-Exclusive plans:

  • Cloud File Server plan: 5GB per hour or 30GB per month.

  • Advanced File System plans: 5GB per hour or 60GB per month. For example, if the user is on the Office plan, and they sent five people a file link to a 2GB video, and they all downloaded the video within an hour, this would result in the violation of the shared file link data limit. Users will start seeing the message “Bandwidth Limit Exceeded - sender’s monthly download quota has been reached.”

  • The monthly limit is reset at the beginning of every month. Admins can run File Audit Report to check the downloaded files via Share Links

  • Other than the plan max file size limit, single files up to 100GB in size can be downloaded via shared links

  • Contact your Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team to learn about the newest Plans.

  • A limit of 10GB is applied for folder downloads or multi-file downloads which creates a zip file.

File and Folder Size Limitations
  • Maximum number of files in a folder (immediate children): 50,000
  • Maximum number of sub-folders in a folder (immediate children): 50,000
  • Maximum path length: 5,000 bytes
Upload Links
  • Maximum of 500 files per session
  • File Size: 25GB (or plan limit, whichever is smaller)
  • Total Upload Quota per lifetime of a single link: 10% (or less) of the plan limit To modify the limit of individual file size or total upload size allowed through Upload Links, contact the Egnyte Representative.
Sending Attachments

When sending a file attachment from the Web UI, it is limited to attachments that are 5MB or less.

For any questions about the account’s file link limits, contact Egnyte representative.

Printing from Preview

If a file is over 20MB or more than 100 pages, the user will not be able to print directly from the Preview pane.

Search

Refer to this article for detailed information about the search and its parameters or limits.

Public API

Refer to this article for detailed information about Public API limits.

Sharing Links via Email

​​​​As a spam prevention measure, email limits are applicable to both Trial and Paid accounts when sharing links via email. ​​​​​​ These limits are applicable to both trials and paid domains and can only be lifted only for paid domains by contacting support.​​​

Autoplace Fields with Structured Inline Tags

Egnyte Sign supports Structured Inline Tags — short codes users can embed directly in a document before uploading it to Egnyte. When the document is opened for signing, Egnyte Sign automatically detects these tags and converts them into signature fields at the exact positions where the tags appear. This eliminates the need to manually drag and place fields during the signature request workflow.

Inline tags are well-suited for teams that generate documents programmatically (for example, from templates or document generation tools) and want signature fields to appear consistently in the right place every time.

Structured inline tags are not supported for 21 CFR Part 11 (GxP) signature workflows. For Part 11-compliant signature requests, fields must be placed manually.

Key Capabilities

  • Automatically place signature, initials, date, text, name, title, and company fields
  • Assign each field to a specific recipient by number
  • Mark fields as required or optional
  • Customize labels, text styles, date formats, and name formats per field
  • Combine inline tags with the Egnyte Sign Public API to automate end-to-end signature workflows

Tag Syntax

Each inline tag follows this format:

{{es:fieldType:recipientNumber|param:value|param:value}}

Component

Description

es

Required prefix identifying this as an Egnyte Sign tag

fieldType

The type of field to place (see Field Types below)

recipientNumber

Which recipient the field belongs to (e.g., 1 for the first signer)

param:value

Optional parameters to configure the field (see Parameters below)

Example:

This places a signature field for recipient 1 at the tag’s location.

{{es:s:1}}

Spaces within a tag — between the components or around the separators — will invalidate it. Only trailing spaces before the closing }} are valid, as they control field width. For example, {{ es:s:1 }} will not be recognised, but {{es:s:1 }} is valid.

Abbreviation

Field Type

Description

Example Tag

s

Signature

Captures a drawn or typed signature

{{es:s:1}}

i

Initials

Captures initials

{{es:i:2}}

d

Date

Auto-fills the signing date

{{es:d:1}}

t

Text

Free-form text input

{{es:t:1}}

n

Name

Auto-fills the signer’s full name

{{es:n:1}}

tl

Title

Auto-fills the signer’s title

{{es:tl:1}}

c

Company

Auto-fills the signer’s company name

{{es:c:1}}

Parameters

Parameters are appended after the recipient number using a pipe (|) separator. Multiple parameters can be chained together.

Abbreviation

Parameter

Applicable Fields

Description

r

Required

All field types

Whether the field must be completed. Values: t (true), f (false). Default: t

lbl

Label

All field types

A label displayed above the field (e.g., lbl:JobTitle)

sty

Style

t (text) only

Text weight. Values: l (light), r (regular), b (bold), i (italic)

nf

Name format

n (name) only

How the name is displayed. Values: f (full name), fn (first name), ln (last name). Default: f

df

Date format

d (date) only

How the date is displayed. Values: mmddyyyy, ddmmyyyy, yyyymmdd. Default: mmddyyyy

  • The r (required) parameter defaults to t (true) if omitted.

  • The lbl value is a free-text string. Avoid special characters and spaces.

Field Sizing

The size of each auto-placed field is determined by the tag text itself — no separate configuration is needed.

Width

Field width is controlled by the number of trailing spaces added before the closing }}. The more spaces you add, the wider the field will be.

{{es:t:1|lbl:FullName               }}   ← wider field
{{es:s:1}}                               ← narrower field
Height (Signature and Initials Fields)

Field height is determined by the size of the terminal curly brackets ({{ and }}) of the tag. A larger font size for the tag text produces taller brackets and therefore a taller field. Egnyte Sign applies a minimum and maximum height limit — if the bracket size falls below the minimum or exceeds the maximum supported size, the field height will be capped at the respective limit.

Height sizing based on terminal brackets applies to signature (s) and initials (i) fields. Non-signature fields such as text, date, name, title, and company follow a different sizing approach.

Making Tags Invisible — Tags should be formatted with a white font color (or a color matching the document background) so they are not visible to signers. The fields will still be placed correctly at the tag’s location.

If a user needs a narrow field but the tag text itself is long, reduce the font size of the tag to keep the field width compact while maintaining the desired height independently.

Examples

Basic Signature and Date Fields for One Recipient

Places a signature field and a date field for recipient 1.

{{es:s:1}}
{{es:d:1}}

Two Recipients Signing Sequentially

{{es:s:1}}   ← Recipient 1's signature
{{es:d:1}}   ← Recipient 1's date

{{es:s:2}}   ← Recipient 2's signature
{{es:i:2}}   ← Recipient 2's initials

Text Field with a Label and Bold Style

Adds a bold text field labeled “JobTitle” for recipient 1.

{{es:t:1|lbl:JobTitle|sty:b}}

Date Field with a Custom Format

Displays the signing date in DD/MM/YYYY format

{{es:d:1|df:ddmmyyyy}}

Name Field Showing First Name Only

Auto-fills only the first name of recipient 1.

{{es:n:1|nf:fn}}

Optional Text Field

An optional comments text field for recipient 2.

{{es:t:2|r:f|lbl:Comments}}

Full Example — Contract with Two Signers

Client Name:      {{es:n:1|nf:f}}
Client Company:   {{es:c:1}}
Client Title:     {{es:tl:1}}
Client Signature: {{es:s:1}}
Date:             {{es:d:1|df:mmddyyyy}}

Witness Initials: {{es:i:2}}
Witness Signature:{{es:s:2}}
Date:             {{es:d:2|df:mmddyyyy}}

Limitations

Item

Detail

Supported file types

Tags are detected in PDF, DOCX, DOC, PPTX, PPT, XLSX, XLS, RTF, and image files supported by Egnyte Sign

Tag detection

Tags must appear as plain text in the document. Tags inside images, headers/footers, or text boxes may not be detected

Recipient numbering

Recipient numbers must be consecutive starting from 1. Gaps (for example; :1, :3 with no :2) will result in field assignment errors

Apply Template

When a template is applied to a document using Apply Template, the template’s fields are applied as-is (including both auto-placed and manually placed fields). The document’s own inline tags are not processed, and tag scanning is disabled for any subsequent documents added to the envelope

Rotated pages

Tags on rotated pages will not be detected or applied. Ensure pages are in standard orientation before embedding tags

Field size limits

Egnyte Sign applies a minimum and maximum size for all fields. If the tag sizing results in a field smaller than the minimum or larger than the maximum supported size, it will be capped at the respective limit

Manual field placement

If no inline tags are present, fields can still be placed manually during the signature request workflow

Maximum recipients

Up to 20 recipients (signers + CC) per signature request

21 CFR Part 11 (GxP) domains

Inline tags are not supported in Part 11 signature workflows. Fields must be placed manually

  • Signing a Signature Request

Best Practices for Creating an Egnyte Folder Structure

Egnyte has the flexibility to create a custom folder structure that best fits the company’s organization and use-cases. This custom folder structure will make it easy to organize and find data and apply permissions. Sign in to Egnyte University to watch this video on creating folder templates in Egnyte to learn more.

Use Cases

The optimal folder structure depends on the company structure and use cases for Egnyte. This article includes a few suggestions to jump-start the process.

Construction

Construction companies have many projects in various locations. We recommend creating a folder structure in the form Region > Job Site > Project. There can also be a folder for past jobs that is treated as an archive.

High Tech

Technology companies have multiple departments that each collaborate frequently. We recommend having a top-level folder for every department. For example, Accounting, Customer Success, Customer Support, Engineering, Human Resources, Sales & Marketing.

Retail

Retail companies have many offices scattered around the world. The headquarters can be in one place, but there are many more satellite offices. If there are multiple offices, Egnyte recommends creating a folder structure by location where each office location has its own top-level folder.

Apply Folder Permissions

The folder structure is greatly influenced by how to simplify permissions. Think about how the company treats data. Do users in one location have similar permissions? Do users with one job role have similar permissions? Then it makes sense to create a group, add the users to the group and give permissions to the group (not to the individual users). Refer to Sharing with Folder Permissions article to learn about setting folder permissions.

File and Folder Size Limitations

  • Maximum number of files in a folder (immediate children): 50,000
  • Maximum number of sub-folders in a folder (immediate children): 50,000
  • Maximum path length: 5,000 bytes
  • Note that it is not possible to browse a folder in the Desktop App if it has more than 25,000 files and/or folders as immediate children

Bookmark Folders in the Web UI

Quickly access the content that matters most to you by Bookmarking folders in Egnyte.

Rather than navigating through the entire folder structure in the Web UI, enable fast access to your content by creating a bookmark.

  • To bookmark a folder, simply navigate to that folder and click the star icon to the right of the folder name.
  • The folder will be available in your personal Bookmarks section.
  • Removing a bookmark is as easy as de-selecting the star.

Browse by Metadata Tags

Egnyte provides powerful built-in metadata capabilities that allow the users to efficiently set metadata properties on a large number of files and folders, and enable quick searching of content based on metadata.

Browse by Metadata Tags brings a new and unique way to navigate through the content using metadata tags. It enables the users to navigate to the files and folders of interest regardless of the overall folder structure or where each individual file may be located in the folder tree. Users can navigate the collection of tagged documents by simply clicking on Tag values and automatically filtering the files and folders to the matching results.

This feature is not available for customers on Document Room Plans.

Browse By Tags View

Click on the Browse by Tags icon near the top-right of a folder list view.

This changes the display mode to Browse by Tag. A new pane opens up that shows all the metadata properties (tags) that have any value applied to any of the files in the current folder tree.

The tags are divided in two separate sections

  • Egnyte Tags: Egnyte tags are system tags created and applied by the system, such as Secure and Govern Policy Tags, and Document Tags.
  • Your Tags: These are the custom tags that are user-defined metadata. Learn more about Metadata in Egnyte.

Egnyte Tags section may or may not include some of the Tags depending upon the specific Egnyte plan enabled for the customer.

Choose one or more values from the dropdown menus to filter the results based on the tags selected.

For Example: select Document Type as Employee Handbook to view the matching results. Additionally, users can use the column-level dropdowns for custom attributes to filter the results. The values in the multi-level attributes appear as per the matching results in the associated file or folder listing.

Users can sort the results based on Egnyte as well as Your (custom) metadata tags.

Sorting on Multi-Value String and Multi-Value Enum is not supported.

Users can mix and match values from different properties to narrow down their search. As Tag values are selected, the list of chosen values appear on top. The user can click on the x symbol to remove any given filter.

As the user chooses one or more Tag values to filter their view, some of the Tags in the left pane become disabled and are displayed as greyed out.

In the example below, after selecting the Training Manual as the Document Type, the options Project Tags and Smart Tags are greyed out as these do not have any tag values set.

Back to Top ↑

Search Tags

Users can search for the tags using the search option in the left pane.

Back to Top ↑

Hide Disabled Tags

Some of the tags may be disabled as there may not be any content matching with the current filter. The user can click on the Hide disabled tags checkbox to hide any disabled tags.

Back to Top ↑

Edit Tags

Users can edit the tags associated with a particular document by hovering over the document and clicking on the Edit icon.

They can choose to add or remove the tag(s) as needed. Click on Save to save the changes.

Back to Top ↑

Enumerated vs Freeform Tags

Fundamentally, there are two types of metadata properties.

Enumerated properties: These are the properties that can only contain a finite set of values.

  • For Example: Document Type can only contain a handful of distinct values. On the other hand, a Property like Address can contain any of the billions of possible values. All enumerated Tags in the left pane display a drop-down menu when clicked. The drop-down menus contain the values for that Tag based on the associated records in the file or folder listing. The user can choose one or more values in the menu to filter their results.

Freeform Tags do not show a drop-down menu. When a user clicks on a freeform property, the display gets filtered down to show all items that have any value set for that property.

For example, if a user clicks on the Address property, the display shows all items where the Address is set to any value. If the user needs to search for all files with a specific value, they can kick-off advanced metadata search from the bottom of the Tags pane.

Back to Top ↑

Save Views

Users have the option to save views when browsing by tags. They can also rename, share, and remove any of the saved views.

  • Click on Views when browsing by tags and click on +.
  • Provide Saved View name and click on Save. This will save the current view including all the applied filters and displayed column list.
  • The Saved views will be available under My Views.
Rename the Saved View
  • Navigate to Views -> My Views -> Click on the three-dots for a view to rename and click on Rename.
  • Enter the new name and click on Rename.
  • The saved view will be renamed.
Share the Saved View
  • Navigate to Views -> My Views -> Click on the three-dots for a view to share and click on Share.
  • Users can share the saved view with the existing domain users. They can choose to Email link or Get share link and share it with the user(s).
  • When emailing the link, the users can enter the Email addresses of the domain user(s), provide a message (Optional), choose to Send a copy of this email to myself, and click on Send email.
  • Alternatively, they can choose to Get share link and the link will be copied to the clipboard for sharing.
  • When the recipient clicks on the shared link, the shared view will be automatically saved for them, and will be available under the Shared With Me tab.
Remove the Saved View
  • Navigate to Views -> My Views -> Click on the three-dots for a view to remove and click on Remove.
  • Click on Remove to confirm.
  • The saved view will be removed.
Export Tags Report

Select at least one tag and click on the Export icon to export the report.

The icon will be disabled if there are no tags selected.

The report will be exported in the CSV format on the user’s system.

The larger exports may take a while to download and the user will receive a Notification when the file has been processed.

Currently, CSV exports are limited to 100,000 items. If the number of items exceeds this limit, only the first 100,000 items will be exported.

Back to Top ↑

Tag Multiple Files

Tags can be added on multiple files at once. Select the desired file(s) while browning by tags and click on the Tag option in the context menu.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Why Do Some Tags Appear as Active, but When a User Clicks on Them, the Screen Displays “No results found”?

There are a number of reasons why there may be no results found for a Tag that appears active and clickable:

  • The user may not have permissions to see the tagged files
  • The tagged files were recently moved or deleted and the tags have not yet been re-indexed
  • If the tag is an enumerated type, the dropdown menu is marked as active as long as at least one value from the list is assigned to a file. However, not all values in the menu may have files associated with them, so clicking on certain values might show “No results found”
The User Launches the Browse by Tags View From One Folder, But they Wish to go to Another Folder Without Losing the Filters Already Set. Is This Possible?

The folder tree pane gets collapsed in the ‘Browse by Tag’ view. However, the folder tree can be expanded by clicking on the ‘expand’ arrow as shown below. Once the folder tree is visible, the user can navigate to any folder. As long as any files in the new folder tree match the filters, the filters will remain applied.

Back to Top ↑

Browse Images with Gallery View

The gallery, or large icons, view lets the users quickly review a collection of images stored in a folder. This feature is ideal for architects, designers, photographers, or anyone else who keeps a large collection of images in Egnyte and wants to see a preview of the file.

The gallery view can be selected by clicking the View options icon indicated below and choosing Large icons.

After opening the gallery view, hovering over the image reveals some quick options. Users can:

  • Preview a larger version of the image by clicking on it.
  • Inline status actions, such as active links, versions, comments, lock, and insights.
  • Three-dots icon to open the context menu.
  • Checkbox on the top-left corner to select the file and view the context menu. To perform the same action on more than one image, check the box of each image. The context menu will appear on the right side of the screen.

The gallery view is available in WebUI and mobile app for iOS and Android. The file types supported in gallery view include:

  • JPG
  • JPEG
  • PNG
  • GIF
  • BIMP
  • TIF
  • TIFF
  • PSD
  • PCT
  • WebM
  • MP4
  • MOV
  • WMV
  • OGV

Bulk Extraction - Automatically Extract and Apply Tags Across Files

Bulk Extraction automates the process of identifying and applying tags to files stored in Egnyte. After configuration, the feature processes content within designated folders, including both existing files and new uploads, and applies tags automatically. This eliminates the need for manual tagging while improving content organization and searchability.

This article covers how to:

  • Create, Duplicate, Activate, Deactivate, and Manage extraction jobs
  • Manage Bulk Extraction access
  • Select folders by search or wildcard pattern
  • Use smart filters and summary statistics
  • View job details
  • Edit draft configurations Bulk Extraction is available for customers on the Ultimate Plan. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Manage Bulk Extraction Access

Administrators can create new role or update existing ones to delegate access to power users. Administrator needs to enable Can manage Bulk Extraction capability under the Edit Role modal.

Create a New Extraction Job

  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures
  • Click on Extractions -> New extraction
  • Enter the Extraction name and select the Tag Section from the dropdown.
  • Select the desired properties for the Tag section and click on Next.
  • Users can choose to enter additional instructions by clicking on the edit icon and entering the instructions. They can also click on Generate Instruction for AI to generate instructions. Click on Save.
  • Click on Select to select the folder locations for the extraction job
  • Click on Select.
  • Use folder search to find folders by name.
  • Use wildcard or pattern-based criteria to select folders that match a location pattern.
  • To change the selection, click Edit, update the folders or pattern criteria, and click Next.
  • Define the extraction criteria for existing tags. Users can choose to Keep (default) the existing tag value or Override the tag value with extracted ones.
  • Optionally, users can add condition(s) to filter documents by existing tags. Enter the condition by selecting property, relative, and value. Click on the delete icon to delete the entered condition and click on Add conditions to add a new condition. Click on Next.
  • Users can add a maximum of 5 conditions and the Add conditions option will be disabled thereafter. Additionally, if a specific property type is already added once, it cannot be re-added as a condition.
  • Review the details and click on Save as draft If metadata namespaces are configured as folder-scoped, Bulk Extraction can only apply tags to files within those scoped folders. Files outside the namespace scope will return no tags.

Back to Top ↑

Duplicate an Extraction Job

Duplicate an existing extraction job to reuse its configuration.

  • Open the extraction job that you want to reuse.
  • Select Make a copy.
  • It will create a copy of the selected job and present the same creation wizard with pre-filled configurations.
  • Update the folder locations, tag selections, or extraction requirements as needed.
  • Review the configuration and save the new job. The option to create a duplicate job is also available directly from the extraction dashboard.

The duplicated job preserves the original configuration until you change the new job’s settings.

Edit Configuration

Users can edit configuration for jobs in the Draft status. Open the job and click on Edit configuration.

Make the changes and click on Save changes to confirm the edits.

Back to Top ↑

Activate the New Extraction Job

The newly created extraction job is saved as a draft. Users get the option to activate the job once all the files have been calculated. The progress is visible under the Documents column for the job saved as a draft.

Open the extraction job and click on Activate.

Click on Activate to confirm and the job will be activated.

Back to Top ↑

Filters and Sorting Options for Extraction Jobs

Users have the option to filter the extraction jobs to view the desired details.

  • Name: Enter the job name to filter the jobs as per the name
  • Section: Enter the keyword for Tag section
  • Status: Jobs can be filtered by any of the three status options as Draft, Active, or Inactive
  • Created By: Filter the jobs created by a specific user. Anyone is the default selection.
  • Last used: Filter the jobs as per the last used timeframe as Any time (default), Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or a Custom range.
  • Activated on: Filter the jobs as per the activated timeframe as Any time (default), Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or a Custom range. Sorting options are also available for all the fields to sort the view as per preference.

Back to Top ↑

View Extraction Job Details

  • Open any of the extraction jobs to view its details. The File name, Status of the file, and the Tags are displayed for the job.
  • Use smart filters to identify and review extraction jobs that match relevant job activity and status criteria. Smart filters make it faster to find jobs that require review.
  • Users can also manually filter the files as per the File name or the Status as Processed, Skipped, or Error.
  • Click on the Settings button to view the job settings. The settings are view-only and cannot be modified once the job has been activated.
  • Users can deactivate an active job from the job details by clicking on the Deactivate icon.
  • Click on Deactivate to confirm.
  • Click on any of the listed files to open it in preview. Tags tab will display by default listing all the extracted tags.
  • Users can also click on the Tags count on the jobs page to view the tags. Back to Top ↑

Activate or Deactivate a Job

Open an inactivate job and click on the Activate icon or hover over on the job in the Extractions list.

Click on Activate to confirm.

Similarly, click on the Deactivate icon after opening the job details or hover over an active job and click on the Deactivate icon.

Click on Deactivate to confirm.

Users can also activate or deactivate a job from the respective settings option.

Back to Top ↑

Known Limitation

Files added via permission changes are not processed (power user–initiated jobs only)

When an extraction job is created by a designated power user, the job is scoped to only the folders/files that user had access to at the time of job creation. New files or folders added afterwards within that scope are picked up and processed automatically.

However, if the power user is granted access to additional existing sub-folders after the job has already started (for example, a folder owner extends their edit permissions to more sub-folders), those newly accessible items will appear in the job’s file list but will not be processed. They remain in a Pending state indefinitely, and the job’s file or completion counts will not reflect them.

Bulk Extraction - Frequently Asked Questions

Bulk Extraction allows users to automatically extract and apply metadata tags across large volumes of files. This article addresses common questions about configuring and managing extraction jobs, supported file types, processing quotas.

Bulk Extraction is available for customers on the Ultimate Plan. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

When Can an Extraction Job be Activated?

An extraction job can be activated after it has been configured and the file count has been calculated. The file count progress is displayed in the Documents column while the job is in Draft status.

Users can also activate an inactive job.

Can Users Edit the Configuration of An Active Extraction Job?

No. Extraction job configurations can only be edited while the job is in the Draft status. Once a job has been activated, its configuration becomes read-only.

Can users duplicate an existing extraction job?

Yes. Users can duplicate an existing extraction job to reuse its configuration. After duplicating a job, users can update details such as the location, selected tags, or extraction requirements before activating the new job.

Can Users Delete An Extraction Job?

No. Extraction jobs cannot be deleted. However, users can deactivate a job if it is no longer required.

Users can delete the draft jobs by clicking on the delete icon.

They can click on Delete to confirm deletion.

Who can create and manage Bulk Extraction jobs?

Administrators and designated power users with the Can manage Bulk Extraction privilege can create and manage extraction jobs. Power users can view and manage only the extraction jobs they created.

What Happens When New Files Are Added to Folders Monitored by An Active Extraction Job?

Bulk Extraction continues to process newly uploaded files in the selected folders after the job has been activated. Processing progress for newly added files can be viewed from the extraction job details.

Can Bulk Extraction Process Files That Already Contain Tags?

Yes. During configuration, users can choose whether existing tag values should be retained or overridden by the extracted values.

Can Users Limit Extraction to Specific Documents Within the Selected Folders?

Yes. Users can define conditions based on existing metadata properties to determine which documents should be processed.

Can users search for a folder when configuring an extraction job?

Yes. When selecting a location for an extraction job, users can search for folders in the folder picker. This helps users quickly find the required folders in large folder structures.

Can users select folders using a pattern?

Yes. Users can use wildcard or pattern-based criteria when defining an extraction job location. This is useful when an extraction job needs to apply to multiple folders with consistent naming patterns.

How can users monitor extraction jobs and identify whether documents have been processed, skipped, or encountered errors?

Bulk Extraction includes smart filters and an extraction-job summary statistics dashboard to help users quickly identify and review relevant jobs.

The Documents column displays counts for Processed, Skipped, and Error files. Each status is displayed using a distinct color code, making it easy to track processing outcomes.

In the example below, 964 files have been successfully processed, 33 have been skipped, and 51 have encountered an error.

Users can also open the job details and apply column-level status filters.

Additionally, users can open the job details and read the details for the skipped or errored document.

How Can Users View The Tags Extracted For a File?

Users can open a file from the extraction job details page to view the extracted tags. The Tags tab displays the metadata that has been applied to the file.

Users can also click on the Tags count on the jobs page to view the tags.

Which File Types are Supported For Bulk Extraction?

The supported file types, associated file extensions, and file size limits are the same as those supported by Egnyte’s AI Assistant.

Is There a Limit on the Number of Files That Can be Processed Through Bulk Extraction?

Yes. A maximum of 200,000 files can be extracted per month for a domain.

Does the Limit Reset Per Month?

No. The extraction limit does not reset at the start of each month. Instead, the available quota is replenished gradually on an hourly basis throughout the month.

This means that as documents are processed, the available quota decreases and is then incrementally restored over time, rather than being fully reset on a fixed monthly date.

How Quickly is the Extraction Quota Replenished?

The extraction quota is replenished incrementally every hour throughout the month. The hourly refill rate is calculated based on the monthly quota.

For the default limit of 200,000 documents per month, the approximate replenishment rates are:

Time Period

Approximate Documents

Per hour

~278

Per day

~6,667

Per 30 days

200,000

The available quota cannot exceed the configured monthly limit.

What Happens When the Extraction Limit is Reached?

Extraction jobs are not stopped when the available quota is exhausted. Instead, document processing continues at the quota replenishment rate.

For example, with the default limit, processing continues at approximately 6,667 documents per day as quota becomes available. Active extraction jobs remain operational but may take longer to complete.

Will Users Receive a Notification When The Extraction Limit is Reached?

No. There is currently no in-product notification or indicator that shows when processing has slowed due to quota exhaustion.

If extraction jobs appear to be processing more slowly than expected, the available quota may have been depleted. Please contact the Product team for assistance if additional information is required.

Is the Extraction Limit Based on a Monthly Quota or a Daily Processing Rate?

Both measurements describe the same quota model.

The monthly quota represents the maximum amount of extraction capacity that can be accumulated, while the daily processing rate represents the approximate amount of capacity replenished each day.

For the default limit of 200,000 documents per month, the replenishment rate is approximately 6,667 documents per day.

Bulk Extraction - Overview

Egnyte extracts and applies tags at scale across files within folders, automatically, turning unstructured files into structured, searchable data with the Bulk Extraction feature.

Bulk Extraction processes existing files and newly uploaded content in selected folders. After the user configures an extraction job, it monitors the designated locations and automatically extracts and applies tags without manual tagging.

Bulk Extraction is available for customers on the Ultimate Plan. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Manage Extraction Jobs

Use the folder picker to search for folders when defining extraction-job locations. Users can select folders with wildcard or pattern-based criteria to target locations that match the folder structure.

Duplicate an existing extraction job to reuse its configuration, then modify its locations, tag selections, or extraction requirements. Use smart filters and the extraction-job summary statistics dashboard to locate, review, and monitor extraction jobs.

To learn more, please refer to the detailed article.

Access Control

Administrators can grant the Can manage Bulk Extraction privilege to control which users can create and manage extraction jobs.

To learn more, please refer to the detailed article.

Benefits

  • Reduce manual tagging: Bulk Extraction automatically populates tags based on document content, reducing the time spent manually classifying files.
  • Improve tags consistency: The same extraction logic is applied across all files, helping maintain consistency and reducing variations introduced by manual tagging.
  • Apply tags to existing and new content: Tags can be extracted from historical files already stored in Egnyte as well as new files added to monitored folders after activation.
  • Work with existing metadata schemas: Extracted values are written directly to existing Egnyte metadata schemas, allowing organizations to continue using established metadata structures and workflows.
  • Support search, governance, and AI workflows: Consistent tags helps make content easier to find, organize, govern, and use in AI-driven experiences.

Use Cases

Contract Management

Extract information such as contract numbers, effective dates, renewal dates, and customer names from contracts and automatically apply them as tags. This makes it easier to locate contracts based on key attributes, track upcoming renewals, and support contract review and compliance processes.

Financial Documents

Capture key information from invoices, purchase orders, financial statements, and other business documents to improve organization and retrieval. Tagged financial records can be searched, filtered, and grouped more efficiently, helping teams locate relevant documents during audits, reporting activities, and financial reviews.

Human Resources Records

Extract tags such as employee names, employee IDs, departments, and document types from HR documents to support record management. Structured metadata can assist HR teams to quickly retrieve employee records, organize documents consistently, and support retention and compliance requirements.

Project and Construction Documentation

Identify and tag project numbers, locations, document categories, and other project-related information from drawings, submittals, permits, and related files.

This enables project teams to quickly locate documentation associated with specific projects, locations, or document types and improves visibility across large document repositories.

Compliance and Quality Records

Extract tags from policies, audit reports, certifications, procedures, and other compliance documents to improve tracking and governance.

Consistent tagging makes it easier to locate records during audits, monitor compliance documentation, and support governance initiatives across the organization.

Historical Content Classification

Apply tags to existing repositories of untagged files, making previously unstructured content easier to search, organize, and govern.

This helps organizations improve the discoverability of legacy content and enables existing repositories to participate in metadata-driven workflows, governance processes, and AI-powered experiences.

Can Egnyte Host QuickBooks Data?

Although we can store QuickBooks backup data, we currently cannot host the QuickBooks application or database on our servers (e.g. you cannot edit a QuickBooks file directly from Egnyte servers or appliances). This is due to the fact that QuickBooks is built like a client-server application and requires access to multiple underlying system files to edit your records.

If you wish to have multiple users access the QuickBooks file, you can create a portable QuickBooks file and upload that to your Egnyte server. The portable copy allows you to download the file locally on another machine which can then be modified and placed back on the Egnyte server. This provides a way for changes to be made by multiple users and for the file to be transferred.

Note: Do not use a portable file if you need to work on your company file at the same time with other users. You cannot merge changes made by the other person into your company file. Intuit recommends an accountant’s copy if you need to merge the changes to the main company file.

Further instructions for creating a QB portable file can be found here.

Perform a QuickBooks Backup

You may use the Egnyte Sync to backup your QuickBooks data. Since Egnyte Sync data is synchronized to your Egnyte cloud file server, the sync effectively backs up your QB backup files on a regular basis to the cloud.

  • Install Desktop Sync, Storage Sync, or the Desktop App on your local machine.
  • From the QuickBooks File menu, select Backup Company then Create Local Backup.
  • On the Create Backup window, select Local Backup then click the Options button.
  • Click Browse.
  • From the drop-down list in the Save in field, select a location on your Desktop Sync or Desktop App directory where you will be able to find the back up easily later, e.g., Backups.
  • Click OK.
  • The next sync will upload the QB backup file to your Egnyte Cloud file server. The number of versions to keep can be set to your preference. For detailed instructions on scheduling a QuickBooks backup, click here.

Collaborative File Editing

Egnyte enables users to collaborate on files to easily edit them. These collaborative editing sessions can be carried out when an application, such as Microsoft 365 for the web or Google Workspace, allows co-editing. This helps users work on the same file at the same time without creating multiple copies.

Starting or Joining a Collaborative Session

Users can start the session from both Folder Listing, File Preview, and Quick View.

Folder Listing
  • Hover over the three-dots menu on a file and click on the Edit icon. Select the application to edit the file in.
  • Alternatively, select Edit -> Application from the context menu.
  • As soon as the collaborative editing session begins on a file, a UI indicator will be added for the particular file.
File Preview

When previewing a file, users can click on Edit and select the application to collaborate with others in real-time.

As soon as the collaborative session begins, a UI indicator will be added to the file.

Quick View

Egnyte domains on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Starter, Essentials, Elite and Ultimate plans will have access to the Quick View feature. Within Quick View, users can click on Edit dropdown and select the application to collaborate with others in real-time.

Configuring a Default App

When both Microsoft 365 on the web and Google Workspace integrations have been added to the domain, a domain admin can configure one of the integrations to be the default app for editing.

  • Navigate to Apps and Integrations.
  • Click on App Control Center and hover over the preferred app. Click on Settings.
  • Enable Set as default app for editing for the preferred app and click on Save.

Desktop App, Mobile App, etc.

In Desktop App, the file will be “locked” - except for the case when the file is being opened by the same user who had started editing the file in Microsoft 365 on the web or Google Workspace (v3 integration) earlier.

Additional Resources

Learn more about co-editing by watching a Quick Tip on Egnyte University: Co-edit Files in the Web UI

JDK version: Java is optional (required for the drag & drop). When used, we recommend always installing the latest version of Java to protect against security vulnerabilities.

Configure Folder Details and Options

Folder options allow specific users to add descriptions to make the right folders easier to find, limit what other users can do with the folders, and set up notifications when specific actions are taken. This article outlines various options available for making the most of Egnyte’s flexible folder structure.

Skip Ahead to…

Access Folder Options

Folder Descriptions

Delete and Move Permissions

Settings for Folder Options

Access Folder Options

Folder Details & Options can be accessed from the three-dots menu -> More actions -> Details and Options.

Users can also find them by selecting a folder and choosing Details & Options from the context menu in the Web UI.

Folder Descriptions

If a user has Full or Owner permissions to a folder, they can write a folder description. This is a great way to differentiate folders with similar names or provide information about the contents of the folder. The folder description will be visible to all users with access to the folder.

To add a folder description, open Details & Options and scroll down to the Description section. Click the Edit icon, type in a description, and click Save. Descriptions can be seen from the Web UI and mobile apps.

Allow Upload Link Creation

Allow upload link creation for this folder is enabled by default. If the option is disabled, all the users will be restricted from creating new upload links for the specific folders. The existing links will continue to remain operational.

  • Disable the toggle and click on Save.
  • The option to create upload links will not be available for the folder.

Delete and Move Permissions

Admins and users with Owner permissions can choose to grant or revoke delete and move permission for a folder. The fixed folder setting allows Admins and folder owners to prevent users with full permissions from moving, deleting, or renaming the folder.

These folder settings can be found under the Options tab of the Details & Options dialog box.

Turning this setting on enables Admins to empower their users while simultaneously protecting against accidental deletions of valuable content.

Keep these details in mind when using this setting:

  • Egnyte supports four different levels of folder access: Owner (Download/Edit/Upload/Delete + Permissions Management), Full (Download/Edit/Upload/Delete), Editor (Download/Edit/Upload), and Viewer (Preview/Download). In addition, Viewer-Only permissions are also available for certain customers. Click the link to learn more about folder access levels.
  • This setting is not enabled by default; Admins or folder owners must allow this setting on a per-folder basis. Unlike some other folder options settings, this setting is not inherited by sub-folders.
  • Marking a folder as fixed does not prevent a user with Full permissions from deleting files or sub-folders within that folder.
  • Top-level folders are always fixed, meaning only Admins and users with Owner permissions can move, delete, or rename them.
  • Users with at least Viewer permissions can copy top-level folders.

Folder Notifications

Users can configure folder notifications by selecting Details & Options and clicking on the Options tab. The folder notifications set here will apply only to the user setting them. These and other folder notifications are discussed in-depth in a separate article.

Settings for Folder Options

Admins can choose to configure the folder options to be managed only by Admins or by Folder Owners as well.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General.
  • Select Admins Only or Admins and Folder Owners as the choice. By default, it is set to Admins and Folder Owners.
  • Similarly, select the default folder options for folder Copy and Move action:
    • For copy action, the default is set to Apply destination folder options and the checkbox for users to override the default value is checked
    • For move actions, the default is set to Keep source folder options. The checkbox to override the settings does not appear in this case.
    • Admins can choose to modify the settings, as needed. They can select the respective checkboxes for users to override the default value if the setting is Apply destination folder options.
  • Click on Save Changes.
  • The folder options will be disabled for the Folder Owners if manage folder options is set to Admins only.
  • Similarly, folder options will be set as per the configured setting while copying or moving the folder.

Inherit Folder Options to Sub-Folders (Limited Availability)

When the user makes changes to the folder options, they can choose if the changes are inherited to the sub-folders.

  • Make changes to the folder options and click on Save.
  • Select the option for application of the changes and click on Apply.
    • This folder only: The settings will be applicable only to the selected folder and the sub-folders will not be affected.
    • This folder and the subfolders (respect overrides): This is the default selection where the settings are applicable to the selected folder and its subfolders. Any of the overridden custom settings will be respected in this case. The future subfolders will automatically inherit the settings; however, users can manually change the setting, as needed.
    • This folder and all subfolders (override everything): The settings will be applicable to the selected folder and all of its subfolders including the ones with custom settings. The future subfolders will automatically inherit the settings; however, users can manually change the setting, as needed. The feature is currently available to a limited number of customers that are not using any of the hybrid devices (Storage Sync and/or Smart Cache). To request this feature, contact our Products team.

Folder-Level Controls for Admins Only (Limited Availability)

The option to delete, move, or rename a particular folder can be set to be managed by Admins only. It enables organizations with strict compliance and security requirements to adhere to their policies.

  • Access folder options and click on Options. Choose Admins as the option for Who can delete, rename, or move this folder and click on Save.
    • The feature is currently available to a limited number of customers that are not using any of the hybrid devices (Storage Sync and/or Smart Cache). To request this feature, contact our Products team.
    • If a user with Full folder permissions sees You do not have permission to perform this action when moving a folder, check whether the folder has Who can delete, rename, or move this folder set to Admins only. This setting overrides Full-level permissions for move, delete, and rename operations.

Conflict Detection

Conflict Detection removes the confusion that can occur when changes seem to be ‘lost’ in the latest version due to multiple users editing a file at the same time.

An example of this would be when a user syncs a folder for offline access and makes changes to a file while offline. If another user makes changes to the file before the original user has synced the changes, a Conflict Copy of the file will be saved separately once the first user re-establishes the internet connection. Before the introduction of conflict detection, users editing a file that was no longer the latest version would overwrite any new changes that were made by other users.

Conflict Detection is available on the Desktop App, Storage Sync, and Egnyte’s mobile apps.

Conflict Detection Flow

Here’s what will happen when a conflict is detected on the Desktop App:

  1. The user will see a notification saying that a conflict was detected with the name of the file.

  2. The user’s changes (and any subsequent changes as long as the file remains open) are written to a new file with the text (conflict copy from <user’s email address>) appended to the end of the name.

  3. The user will also receive an email specifying the name of the original file, whose changes are conflicting with theirs, and the conflict copy.

  4. Upon closing the document, the original document is updated so the user sees two documents - the original document and the conflict copy. They will need to go through and apply their changes to the original file before deleting the conflict copy. This will result in the resolution of the conflict and the user can ensure that the latest version is retained.

Users can run an audit report to get further insights on the conflict.

Disable Conflict Detection

While Conflict Detection can be enabled or disabled from the Web UI, Egnyte recommends leaving it enabled to avoid unnecessary data loss.

Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General. Enable or disable the toggle for Conflict Detection and Save Changes.

If conflict detection is disabled, any changes made are uploaded to the cloud as new versions of the same file. Versions of a file are ordered based on the ‘last modified time’ of the file.

Unsupported File Extensions

Conflict detection is not supported or triggered on the following file extensions:

  • .backup
  • .bak
  • .bpn
  • .cache
  • .dat
  • .db
  • .db-journal
  • .dll
  • .dsn
  • .dwg
  • .dwl
  • .dwl1
  • .dwl2
  • .eml
  • .exe
  • .ffs_lock
  • .gz
  • .ini
  • .itm
  • .log
  • .mdb
  • .nd
  • .nwc
  • .old
  • .ost
  • .pdb
  • .pkgx
  • .pst
  • .qbb
  • .qbw
  • .sldasm
  • .snap
  • .xls

Self Conflicts

Self Conflicts can occur due to a caching issue in the Smart Cache application that the user’s Desktop App is connected to.

Contact Egnyte support in case of self conflict.

Convert File to PDF Step in Workflow Templates

Egnyte provides users with the ability to directly convert files to PDF as part of a workflow template step. With the Convert file to PDF automated action step, users can configure workflows that automatically convert selected files during workflow execution—removing the need for manual conversion.

This helps reduce repetitive tasks and supports consistent file formats across teams. Users can choose to store the converted PDF in the same folder as the source file or specify a different destination folder based on their needs. The feature is useful for processes that require standardized document formats for sharing, record-keeping, or compliance.

By including this step in a workflow, users can simplify routine operations and maintain better control over how files are processed and stored.

The Convert File to PDF step in Workflow Template is part of the PDF File Handler Add-On. Please contact an Egnyte account manager or the Egnyte Sales team to add this feature.

Add Convert File to PDF Step in Workflow Template

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> Workflows.
  • Navigate to Templates and click on Add template -> File Workflow Template.
  • Create the template referring to the steps here.
  • Click on the + icon in the graphic builder.
  • Select PDF Conversion under Automated Actions as the step.
  • Fill the details as Step name and Description. Click on Allow edits checkbox for Step name and/or Description to allow edits.
  • Specify the folder to save converted file.
    • By default, the same folder as the source file’s location is selected.
    • To choose a specific folder, click on a Specific folder, select the desired folder location and click on Select.
  • Choose the action that shall be taken if the step fails.

Create a New Service Account

A Service Account is an account for an application. For example for Storage Sync, Smart Cache, Egnyte Secure and Govern, or apps built with the Egnyte API.

Service Account Features

  • Password never expires
  • Two-factor authentication is disabled
  • Cannot access interactive applications (like Web UI, mobile apps, or desktop apps)

Creating a New Service Account

After determining the type of user to be added, log in to the Egnyte Web User Interface with an Admin account.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Users & Groups -> Users.
  • Click the Add New Account button, hover over Service Account in the dropdown menu that appears, and select the desired type of Service Account - either Administrator or Power User.
  • Enter the relevant information for the user and click Save.
  • The new Service Account will then be created and automatically set to Active. No confirmation email will be sent at your admin email nor the email address associated with the existing Egnyte admin accounts. Service Accounts do not need to have a unique email address. A Service Account can use the same email address as another user in your Egnyte account. The email address for a Service Account is used purely for email notifications and not for authentication.

Create a New User

When Admins or Power Users are ready to give a new employee access to Egnyte, a new user account can be created right from the Web UI. Some accounts may have different settings to restrict Power Users from creating new user accounts, so please check with your Administrator if you don’t have access to add a new account.

Egnyte has three user types:

  • Standard Users: A limited role suitable for external collaborators.
  • Power Users: The role you will assign to users who are employees of your company.
  • Administrators: Like Power Users, but with a wide range of administrative capabilities, like running reports. Learn more about the different types of users in our Administrators, Power Users, and Standard Users article.
