Create a Shared Folder

Folders contained within the Shared folder will house content that other users in the company need to access and share with customers. As new projects are started and more teams are formed, creating additional folders under Shared will be critical to maintaining organization within your Egnyte account. The article covers details on who can create folders and how to add a new folder. Additional resources are also provided to help assign permissions and add content to the newly created folder.

Who Can Create Shared Folders

  • Administrators and Power Users with can create top-level folders role can create new folders directly under the Shared folder.
  • Administrators, Power Users, and Standard Users that have been granted Editor, Full, or Owner permissions to a folder can create new sub-folders within it.

Create a New Shared Folder

  • Navigate to the folder where the new folder has to be created.
  • Click + Create and select Folder from the drop-down. Alternatively, to create a folder from a template, click on Folder -> From Template -> Select the specific template.
  • Enter a name for the new folder and click Create.
  • The user can then add content to the folder and assign permissions so other users can access it.

Rename a Folder

  • To rename an existing folder, select the folder and select Rename from the context menu.
  • Enter the new name and click on Rename. Alternatively, hover over on the folder to rename and click on the Rename icon.

Enter the new name and click on Save.

Create Bulk Signature Requests

Egnyte Sign templates can be used to send across signature requests in bulk, that is, sending across multiple requests through a single click.

This makes it easier for a user to get signatures on the same documents, such as NDAs, waivers, and others to different signers through separate requests.

Users can create bulk signature requests from the preconfigured templates. It is essential that the Admin has already created the signature templates beforehand for use.

This feature is not available for trial accounts. To get this feature, please contact Egnyte Sales team.

Create Bulk Signature Request from a Template

  • Navigate to Workflows and Signatures -> Signatures ->Templates
  • Hover over on an active template and click on Use template -> Send Bulk Request
  • A preconfigured signature request screen will open where users can rename the bulk signature request. Click on Upload CSV to upload the .csv file, which contains the details of all the signers. Provide an optional message and click on Send.
  • For bulk signature requests to initiate successfully, the .csv file should contain the first row as roles (column header) corresponding to the template. The subsequent rows should have signer or cc email. Each row will be considered as a unique signature request. Users can download the sample .csv file by clicking on Download sample CSV.
  • The following is a sample .csv file, which can be uploaded to send signature requests in bulk. In this example, there are two roles, Employee and Manager. Each row contains emails of signers and 10 individual requests will be sent though this .csv file.
  • If the uploaded CSV file has errors, the user will be notified and bulk request will fail entirely and no request will be sent. In this case, users can click on Upload CSV again to upload the correct file.
  • If there are no errors, the user will be notified that the request is initiated successfully.
  • Once the bulk request is initiated successfully, the user can navigate to the Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests tab and manage all the requests. The Bulk ID column helps them identify the requests corresponding to a specific bulk request.

Actions on Bulk Signature Requests

Replace Signers
  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests. Hover over any of the bulk signature requests and click on the three-dots -> Replace signer option.
  • Enter the existing and new signer IDs and click on Replace.
  • The signature request will be updated and the new signer will be notified.
Send Reminder
  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests. Hover over any of the bulk signature requests and click on the three-dots -> Send reminder option.
  • Click on Remind.
  • The reminder will be sent to the signer.
Cancel Request
  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests. Hover over any of the bulk signature requests and click on the three-dots -> Cancel request option.
  • Enter the optional message and click on Cancel Signature Request.
  • The signature request will be cancelled.

Create Signature Requests Using Self-Service Links

Egnyte Sign templates can be used to send across signature requests using Self-Service Links, that is, creating multiple requests through a link which can be shared on any platform like websites, forums, channels and more.

This makes it easier for a user to get signatures on the same documents, such as NDAs, waivers, and others from different signers whose email address are unknown.

Admins can create Self-Service Links from the pre-configured templates. It is essential that the Admin has already created the links beforehand for any other signature creator to use.

  • The following features are not available for trial accounts: creation of self-service links, bulk-signature requests, adding external users, and forwarding signatures to external users..

  • Egnyte Sign is available as part of the PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales Team team to get access to this feature.

  • Navigate to Workflows and Signatures -> Signatures -> Templates.
  • Hover over on an active template and click on the three-dots icon -> Create Self-Service Link.
  • Enter the details and click on Create:
    • Signature Request name: By default, it is the template name. Users can make changes, if required.
    • Signature Request initiator: The requestor name who will act as creator of all requests created through Self-Service Link
    • Signers Instructions: The description which will be shown after the user accesses the link. Self-Service links can be created for the templates with a single role only. For templates with multiple roles, the option to create a self-service link will be disabled.

Create Signature Requests using Templates

Users can quickly create signature requests from the pre-configured templates. Ensure that the admin has already created the signature templates beforehand for use. To learn more about the steps to create and manage signature templates, click here.

To Create a Signature Request from a Template

  • To create a signature request from a template:
    • Navigate to Workflows and Signatures -> Signatures -> Templates
    • Hover over on an Active template and click on Use template -> Send for Signature
    • Power users will see active templates for which they have at least Editor access on all the associated document folder(s).
    • For templates that have a single role and already have ​​​self-service links created, users can share those links for signature requests.​ ​​
  • A pre-configured signature request will open to fill and send the signature requests.
    • Edit the Signature request name, if required, and enter the recipient(s) email address or name. Click on Send Signature Request
    • Alternatively, click on Skip to edit the template. Click on Send Signature Request after making the necessary changes.
    • Modify the Signature request name and enter the Message, as needed. Click on Send.

Send for Signature – Steps to Create Signature Request from Template

The user also gets the option to choose a template while choosing to send a document for e-signature.

  • Choose Egnyte Sign Icon -> Send for signature
  • Click on Apply Template.
  • Choose any of the templates listed or search for a template. The option to override signed document location with the one from the template is checked by default. Uncheck the box as needed and Click on Apply after making the desired choice.
  • If the user selects the Override option, the signed document will be saved in the location specified in the chosen template. If the user does not select this option, the signed document will be saved in the location selected by the user when creating the signature request. The selected location can also be viewed in the Settings tab of the signature request. The user can repeat the steps in the pre-configured signature request as mentioned in step 2 of the previous section.

Custom Upload Link Disclaimer

How Do I Customize the Upload Disclaimer Displayed to the User While Uploading Documents Using the Upload Link?

Most organizations have their own disclaimer text approved by their legal department to be reviewed and accepted by the external/internal parties invited to upload documents via upload links within their Egnyte cloud storage.

Egnyte helps customers to easily customize the disclaimer text such that they can use their own legal language approved by their legal department. The admin gets the option to override the Egnyte default disclaimer text from within branding settings.

The Egnyte default disclaimer text will be pre-configured by default; hence, there won’t be any impact on existing behavior unless you customize the disclaimer text.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who Can Configure the Custom Upload Link Disclaimer?

Only the users with administrative privileges will be able to configure the upload disclaimer text.

Can I Continue to Use the Out-of-the-Box Default Disclaimer Text?

Yes, the existing Egnyte default disclaimer text will be pre-configured as the default upload disclaimer text.

Can I disable the Upload Link Disclaimer Text Completely?

Deactivating vs Deleting Users

There are a few key differences between deleting and deactivating a user: the ability to reactivate the user, private folder retention, and how shared links and tasks are handled. The article covers how deactivating or deleting a user impacts each of these options for improved assistance.

Skip Ahead to…

Reactivate User

File Content

Links

Groups & Roles

Permissions

Tasks

Billing

Comment Notifications

Reactivate User

The primary difference between deactivating a user and deleting user is that deactivating a user means they can still be reactivated in the user menu. When a user is deleted, their data is permanently removed and there is no way to restore that user.

If 3rd party contractors are given access to Egnyte and their current contract has ended, there may be a possibility to hire them for a different project in the near future. In this scenario, deactivating the users will be the preferred option.

File Content

All content that is in Shared folders remains, whether the user is deleted or deactivated.

Private folders and their content remain for deactivated users, but deleted users have their Private folders sent to Trash. Egnyte recommends deactivating a user until there is a chance to review their Private folder for any content that should be moved to a Shared folder.

If a user is deleted and it is later realized something from their Private folder was required, the content can be restored from the trash.

Private folders of the deleted users will be restored to Shared/Files from Deleted Users.

Links

When a user is Deleted:
  • the Admins will receive a User Deprovisioning Report email to show how many active links were created by the user.
  • Share links will still be accessible and active until the admin delete them. However, the share link will be shown as a deleted link for other users under Links I’ve Received
  • Upload links will be accessible and can still be used to upload file(s)
When a user is Deactivated:
  • Share Links will still be accessible and viewable. However, share links will be disabled if the Folder Permissions are removed
  • Upload links accessible; however, link recipients will not be able to upload the file(s) The detailed rules for deactivating or deleting a user with regard to links is explained in the Share Links FAQ.

Groups and Roles

Deactivated users remain as members or owners of the groups that they are assigned to.

There is currently no indication that the user is deactivated in the menu. Those users can still be removed from the group but cannot be re-added.

Deleted users are permanently removed, and therefore are removed from the groups as owners or members.

Permissions

Deactivated users still show under folder permissions but the user will be shown as Deactivated.

The deactivated user may be removed from folders where they exist, but they may not be re-added with permissions until they are reactivated. The users that are deactivated will not appear in any search boxes. Share links will be disabled if a user is removed from Folder Permissions.

If a user is deleted they are completely removed from permissions.

Tasks

If an assignor user is deactivated and then subsequently re-activated, all the same notifications and emails that would be sent at the time or for a due date will be sent. Since there is no way to currently restore a deleted user, no subsequent task notifications are sent. In Tasks & Workflows, for any workflows where the assignor is deleted/deactivated, the user will still see the assignor name but will have Deleted or Deactivated next to the name.

If the assignee user is deleted or deactivated, the assignor will get an email notification indicating that the assignee for the task has been deleted. Until the assignee is replaced, none of the other notifications will be sent because the task is dead if there is no assignee. Under My Tasks, the task will be available for viewing but the assignee will now be listed as Deleted or Deactivated. In addition, in the file preview, the task widget will show the user as being Deleted or Deactivated.

Billing

When the first Admin user of the workgroup is deleted, deactivated, downgraded, or changed, the primary contact of the domain will be automatically updated to the next Admin user.

Comment Notifications

Deactivated users will continue to receive notifications about comments added by other users on files the deactivated user uploaded or owns.

Decision Step (Conditional Logic) in Workflow Templates

The Decision step adds conditional branching to the workflow, automatically routing documents down different paths based on rules defined by the user.

Each Decision step contains one or more named routes (the condition-based paths) and an Else branch (the fallback path when no route condition is met).

This enables the users to create flexible, condition-based routes that adapt workflow execution based on document attributes and metadata.

Decision (Conditional Logic) is available to the customers on Elite or Ultimate plans. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Add Decision Step in Workflow Template

  • Select Decision from the Add Step pop up.
  • The system automatically creates a framework consisting of Route 1 as the first conditional branch and a mandatory Else branch. It opens the Decision panel on the right side of the workflow builder. By default the user will see two items already created as Route 1 and the Else branch.
  • Enter the Step name and Description (Optional). Click on Allow edits checkboxes to allow edits.
  • To set up the specific routing rules, click either Route 1 of the workflow builder or the Route 1 card on the side panel to set up the routing rules and define conditions using standard file metadata or existing document metadata.
  • The dialog opens with a Route name field and a Route setup section where the users can define the conditions.
    • Enter a unique and descriptive title in the Route name field to easily identify this path on the workflow builder.
    • Navigate to the Route setup section and use the first dropdown menu to select the desired metadata or file attribute, such as File size.
      • Select the appropriate option in the next dropdown as per the attribute selected. For instance, if File Size is the attribute selected, select the comparison operator as Equal, Greater than, Greater than or equal, Less than, or Less than or equal from the required relational dropdown menu next to the selected attribute
      • Enter the target criteria value in the open text field and select a corresponding unit, such as MB, from the final dropdown menu if applicable.
      • Click the + Add AND condition button to continue adding more conditions
      • Click the trash can icon located at the far right of the condition line to delete any unwanted rule.
      • Click the Save button in the bottom right corner to save the routing rules and return to the main workflow builder.
  • Click + Add route button on the side panel to add additional routes.
  • To set up the Else branch, locate the Else configuration section in the side panel. Click the dropdown menu underneath the label If none of the conditions above met, then to view your fallback options:
    • Choose Execute another step (default) for the workflow to continue down an alternative path where users can add any type of the step.
    • Choose Finish workflow execution for the workflow to complete the execution when no custom route rules are satisfied.

Delete the Decision Step

To delete the step, click on the three-dots icon -> Delete either on the right side panel or within the decision step in the graphic builder.

This article covers these default settings in detail to help users understand the available options and use them in line with their organization’s security and governance policies. It also provides a clear view of how these settings compare across the Web UI and Desktop, Mobile apps, or other clients.

Additional Resources

Available Settings and Default Options

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General.
  • Choose the settings for default folder options for copy action and default folder options for move action
    • For copy action, the default is set to Apply destination folder options and the checkbox for users to override the default value is checked
    • For move actions, the default is set to Keep source folder options. Please note that when the setting is set to Keep source folder options, it will always be overridable at the time of copying or moving the folder
  • Modify the settings, as needed to Keep source folder options or Apply destination folder options for copy and move actions. Check the respective checkboxes to enable the users to override the default value.

Back to Top…

Copy a Folder (Web UI)

Apply destination folder options (user override enabled)
  • The default is set to Apply destination folder options
  • Users can change this selection to Keep source folder options by selecting it from the Options dropdown. This is independent of their usual permission to manage folder options
  • If Apply destination folder options is used, the new folder inherits the destination folder’s settings
  • If changed to Keep source folder options, the new folder retains the source folder’s settings
Apply destination folder options (user override disabled)

The new folder always inherits the destination folder’s settings. Options will be disabled in the Copy dialog with a tooltip available for users.

Keep source folder options

The Copy dialog has Keep source folder options as the default in Options dropdown. Users can change this selection to Apply destination folder options.

Back to Top…

Copy a Folder (Desktop, Mobile, and Other Clients)

By default, the setting configured in the Web UI for the copy action will apply. The new folder will inherit the destination folder settings or retain the source folder’s settings accordingly.

Back to Top…

Create a Folder from Template

When creating a folder from a template, the configured defaults do not affect this action. Folder options always follow Keep source folder options, meaning the new folder retains the settings from the template.

Back to Top…

Create a Project from Template

When creating a project from a template, the configured defaults do not apply. Folder options always follow Keep source folder options, so the resulting project retains the settings from the template.

Back to Top…

Move a Folder (Web UI)

Apply destination folder options (user override enabled)
  • The Move dialog defaults to Apply destination folder options
  • Users can change this selection to Keep source folder options, independent of their usual permission to manage folder options for move actions The selected option determines whether the moved folder follows source or destination folder settings
Apply destination folder options (user override disabled)

The Move dialog is set to Apply destination folder options and the users cannot change this setting. Options will be disabled in the Move dialog with a tooltip available for users.

The move action always follows destination folder settings

Keep source folder options
  • The Move dialog defaults to Keep source folder options
  • Users can change this selection to Apply destination folder options, independent of their usual permission to manage folder options for move actions The selected option determines whether the moved folder follows source or destination folder settings
Back to Top…

Move a Folder (Desktop, Mobile, and Other Clients)

By default, the setting configured in the Web UI for the move action applies. The moved folder will either inherit destination folder settings or retain the source folder’s settings accordingly.

Delete Files and Folders

In Egnyte, when files or folders are deleted, they go into a Trash folder. Users may be allowed to restore items from their Trash folder to reverse accidental deletions. After items have been in the Trash folder for the designated period, they are emptied from the Trash and completely removed from Egnyte’s system.

Users can learn more about the trash and retention policy settings here.

Only users with Full or Owner permissions to a folder can delete items.

How to Delete

To delete folders or files:

  • Select the item(s) to remove.
  • Choose Delete from the menu.
  • Click Delete in the confirmation pop-up.

Do I Need a Specific Version of Storage Sync or Other Egnyte Applications to Use Non-Inherited Permissions?

No, non-inherited permissions work with all the existing versions of Egnyte applications, including Storage Sync.

Document Comparison

Egnyte offers a file comparison feature, allowing users to compare a file with its previous versions or with a different file altogether. This functionality highlights the differences between the two documents, making it easier for users to track changes, ensure accuracy, and maintain consistency across document versions.

  • The feature is available with Egnyte’s PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact your Sales Rep or Egnyte Sales team for more details.

  • Document Comparison is currently supported on Desktop Web browsers only.

To carry out file comparison, Open the file in preview and select the Compare document option.

Alternatively, open context menu in WebUI and select More actions -> Compare document.

The user will get the option to select a document for comparison. If the file has earlier versions, a list of the previous versions will appear to choose from.

  • Select A different document to compare with a different file OR click An older version and select the previous version of the file for comparison.
  • Click on Compare.

Text-based Comparison

The comparison will show the two documents side-by-side with an additional panel that shows the list of differences between the documents. Clicking on a difference in the panel will automatically scroll the documents to show where the difference was detected. This allows the user to quickly navigate the document focusing on the differences.

There are 3 toggles while comparing the document:

  • Sync zoom and scroll behavior: If enabled, syncs zoom and scroll of both documents together
  • Show differences: If enabled, it will highlight differences between the two documents
  • View list of differences: If enabled, shows differences in panel at the right.

Overlay-based Comparison

The user can also select overlay-based comparison when comparing the two documents.

The overlay-based comparison displays the two documents overlaid on top of one another in a single panel which is ideal for comparing documents containing drawings.

  • Click on Overlay for overlay-based comparison. The common elements in the document are shown in their regular color, while the unique elements in the primary document are highlighted in green.

Unique elements in the secondary document are highlighted in red.

User has the options for the secondary document to:

  • Rotate clockwise / anti-clockwise
  • Move left / right/ up / down
  • Zoom-in / Zoom -out The primary document is the document that the user wants to compare and the secondary document is the one selected for comparison.

Change Document or Version to Compare

After selecting a document or version for comparison, the users can click on Change and select a new document or version for comparison.

Supported File Types And Limitations

  • PDF (.pdf) - 25 MB
  • Microsoft Word (.docx, .doc) - 50 MB
  • Microsoft Excel (.xlsx, .xls) - 5 MB
  • Microsoft Powerpoint (.pptx, .ppt) - 50 MB
  • Google Docs (.gdoc) - 50 MB
  • Google Sheets (.gsheet) - 5 MB
  • Google Slides (.gslides) - 50 MB

Does the Non-Inherited State Get Inherited to Sub-Folders?

No, folder inheritance has to be set on each folder. Usually, when you turn off inheritance for a folder and give that folder permissions, you want the users with access to also have access to the sub-folders.

For example, when you turn off inheritance to a folder /Shared/Finance/budget its sub-folder /Shared/Finance/budget/Q2 will inherit permissions from the budget folder. If you want to, you could disable inheritance for the Q2 folder as well.

Drag and Drop in the WebUI

Drag and drop is a feature that allows users to organize files and folders in a quicker and seamless manner. There are multiple places within Egnyte where a user can perform drag and drop.

  • Drag & drop on Desktop App
  • Drag & drop on Storage Sync/mapped drive
  • Drag & drop when uploading files and dragging files from the desktop into a folder in Web UI
  • Finally, the drag & drop in WebUI, described in this article. It is an improvement to existing functions behind Move or Copy options from the select menu

Skip Ahead To…

Moving Files With Drag and Drop (and Holding SHIFT)

Copying Files With Drag and Drop (and Holding ALT/OPTION)

Drag and Drop Without Holding SHIFT or ALT / OPTION key

Additional Drag and Drop Destinations

Why SHIFT and ALT / OPTION key?

We require users to hold SHIFT or ALT / OPTION keys to prevent accidental moves of files and folders.

Moving Files With Drag and Drop (and Holding SHIFT)

If a user wants to move files in WebUI, they can achieve that by using the SHIFT button during operation.

  • Select one or multiple files or folders to move.
  • Drag the file(s) or folder(s) to the desired place.
  • Press and hold the SHIFT key.
  • Release the mouse or touchpad; the files or folders are moved.
  • Release the SHIFT key.

Copying Files With Drag and Drop (and Holding ALT/OPTION)

If a user wants to copy files without a confirmation window, they can achieve that by using the ALT/OPTION button during the operation.

  • Select one or multiple files or folders to copy.
  • Drag the file(s) or folder(s) to the desired place.
  • Press and hold the ALT / OPTION button.
  • Release the mouse or touchpad, files will be copied.
  • Release the ALT/OPTION button.

Drag and Drop Without Holding SHIFT or ALT / OPTION key

When users drag any file or folder and drop it in any other place both in the folder listing and the folder tree on the left, a move or copy confirmation popup is displayed.

  • Select the required file(s) or folder(s).
  • Drag the file(s) or folder(s) to the desired place.
  • When the user releases a mouse or touchpad, the confirmation box is presented.
  • Select Move, Copy, or cancel the action.

Additional Drag and Drop Destinations

Users can also drag a file or folder within the folder tree on the left.

They can even drag files or folders from one view to another.

Easily Switch Between Accounts With Multiple Entity Management (MEM)

Many companies maintain multiple Egnyte accounts, enabling disparate business units to collaborate in controlled environments. Some examples include:

  • A financial services firm that maintains two different accounts: one for their analyst unit and one for their retail brokerage unit
  • A manufacturer with an account for each of its two subsidiaries, and another for the parent holding company
  • A multinational engineering firm that has divided its users geographically: Europe and Africa, Asia, and the Americas However, certain users (high-ranking executives, cross-projects team members, IT administrators, etc.) may need access to more than one account. Having to enter multiple login credentials for each account can be cumbersome.

Domain Switching

Multiple Entity Management (MEM) enables authorized users to switch between Egnyte accounts without having to re-enter account credentials on the Web UI. Once this feature has been enabled, a list of linked accounts will appear at the top of the user’s screen. Switching between accounts is simple: just select an account from the drop-down menu, and go.

Domain switching is also available through the Egnyte mobile app without having to enable MEM. Log in to all Egnyte accounts with authorization; tap between accounts in the left panel under the hamburger icon.

Multi-Entity Management (MEM) is also supported in the Desktop App. When a user authenticates to a domain that is interlinked with other Egnyte domains, the Desktop App detects the associated domains and automatically authenticates the user without requiring a separate manual login per domain. This simplifies the authentication process for users that operate across multiple linked Egnyte tenants.

Requirements

  • The Multiple Entity Management feature is only available to customers on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Elite, and Ultimate plans
  • Users must have an account with the same Egnyte-validated email address in all the linked domains
  • Egnyte must link the accounts behind the scenes for the feature to work

Searching Across Linked Domains

When MEM is enabled, searching for files on one domain automatically checks all linked domains for matching results.

After performing a search, a dropdown labeled X results in N other domains appears in the search results filter bar. Clicking this dropdown shows each linked domain by name and URL, along with the number of matching results found in that domain.

Clicking a domain entry opens that domain’s search results in a new browser tab, with the same search query and filters applied. From the new domain, the cross-domain indicator updates to reflect results available in the other linked domains, so users can navigate between all of them.

Cross-domain search works with all search types, including keyword search, filtered search, and Metadata Search. Results from other domains respect the permissions on those domains.

Limitations

  • Domain configuration and settings for each domain are not shared across linked domains and each linked domain must be configured and maintained separately
  • Remove Device option on a single domain may not remove the drive from the Desktop App if other MEM-linked domains remain authenticated on the same device. In this scenario, the Desktop App detects that another MEM-linked domain is still authenticated and automatically re-authenticates the affected drive using the existing authentication context. As a result, the drive may reconnect automatically, and the Remove Device action may not have the expected effect This feature is the first in a powerful suite that will allow the users to manage multiple Egnyte accounts. To enable and benefit from Multiple Entity Management contact us.

Edit a Signature Request

Egnyte provides the senders with the ability to edit an in-progress signature request. The senders can edit the general details, such as the request name and message. They can also edit the options available under Settings, such as expiration date, reminders, signature forwarding, and signed document location.

This enables senders to update request details as requirements change without having to cancel and recreate the signature request.

  • Egnyte Sign is available as part of the PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more details on how to get access to this feature.

  • Currently, options under General and Settings can be edited for an in-progress signature request.

  • Only the senders can edit a signature request. Other users, such as other admins or power users cannot edit the requests.

Edit an In Progress Signature Request

  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests
  • Click on the three-dots menu -> Edit
  • Edit the desired details under General and Settings tabs. Click on Save changes
  • Users will be notified if they try editing any other details apart from the ones under General and Settings.
  • The signature request will be updated and the email notification with the updated details will also be sent.

Audit Logs

The edits made in the signature request are captured in the audit logs and can be accessed from Signature Audit Reports.

Egnyte Policy for Browser and OS Support

Egnyte supports the latest major releases of the following web browsers and desktop/mobile operating systems (OS). Update to the latest version if you experience any issues.

Web Browsers

  • Microsoft Edge - The two latest, major released versions
  • Safari - The two latest, major released versions
  • Firefox - The two latest, major released versions
  • Chrome - The two latest, major released versions Egnyte ends support for Internet Explorer (IE) - 11 effective March 31, 2021

Operating Systems (OS)

  • Windows 10 and Windows 11
  • Android - Last 4 major versions
  • macOS - These three major released versions:
    • macOS 26.x - Tahoe
    • macOS 15.x - Sequoia
    • macOS 14.x - Sonoma Desktop App Core can support Mac devices that utilize Apple Silicon chips
  • iOS - The last 2 major versions will be supported

Additional Information

  • Each time a new OS version is released for general availability (GA), Egnyte begins supporting the most recent version.
  • Egnyte does not support Beta OS versions.
  • Egnyte reserves the right to make exceptions to this policy at any time.
  • We recommend keeping all Egnyte applications (Mobile, Desktop App, WebEdit, etc.) on the most recent, generally available version at all times. Egnyte will make reasonable efforts to troubleshoot issues, provided all web browsers, OS’, and applications are up to date. If they are not up to date, this will be the first step our Support team will suggest to fix any issues.
  • Egnyte software is only supported for physical machines, not any specific virtual desktop environment.

Egnyte Sign Overview and Administration

Egnyte Sign allows users to send electronic signature requests for a set of documents stored in Egnyte. Recipients sign in their browser and a legally binding signed copy is saved back to Egnyte as a digitally signed PDF.

Key Capabilities of Egnyte Sign include:

  • Legally binding electronic signature process
  • Sending requests to anyone with an email address
  • Parallel or sequential signature workflows
  • Add signature, initial, text, and date fields
  • PDF digital signatures with an Adobe Approved Trust List (AATL) certificate with Long Term Validation (LTV) to ensure data integrity
  • A signature dashboard to track sent and received signature requests Learn how to send a signature request

Learn how to sign a signature request

  • Egnyte Sign complies with the ESIGN Act and other electronic signature laws like UETA (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act), providing a secure and legally recognized way to manage electronic signatures.

  • Egnyte Sign is available as part of the PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get access to this feature.

Administration

Egnyte Sign offers several configuration options for administrators. Navigate to Settings > Configuration > Signatures to access these options.

The following settings are available:

Setting

Description

Permission

By default, any Administrator or Power User in the domain can send signature requests. To limit who can send requests, choose the Specific Groups option and add up to 10 Egnyte groups. Any Admin or Power User in those groups will be allowed to send a signature request.

Note: Standard Users cannot send signature requests

Custom Consent

Egnyte provides a default Electronic Record and Signature Disclosure. This option allows the user to customize that disclosure. The user can enter up to 8000 characters in their custom disclosure.

Reasons for Signing (Applicable only to the Egnyte Sign GxP enabled domains)

This includes a link to the workflows configuration. Signing reasons can be managed in the Reasons for approval section in Workflows Configuration.

Add Certificate of completion to the signed document

Once enabled, when users download the signed document, the certificate of completion will be appended to the same file.

Validate external signers

If enabled, external signers will be required to authenticate themselves before starting the signing session. This setting is not applicable for Egnyte Sign GxP enabled domains.

Reasons for signing setting is available only for GxP domains.

Add Certificate of Completion to the Signed Document

Admins can choose to configure the settings to add the certificate of completion to the signed document.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> Signatures
  • Enable the preference to Add Certificate of completion to the signed document.
  • Click on Save Changes. Once enabled, when users download the signed document, the certificate of completion will be appended to the same file. They will continue to have the option to download the certificate of completion as a separate document.

Advanced Configuration

Although WebEdit doesn’t have any user interface, advanced configuration options can still be configured. Purposes

Common Issues and Troubleshooting

  • With an outdated version of Egnyte WebEdit, users might see an error message “unknown error opening file to edit”.
  • If WebEdit is installed, but an error shows up about needing to install it, check the following:
    • Users can run WebEdit on Windows by choosing Egnyte WebEdit from the start menu. On Mac, choose Egnyte WebEdit from the applications folder.
    • Microsoft Edge users on the latest Windows 10 updates may see errors about WebEdit not being installed if they have added their Egnyte domain to the trusted sites or intranet zone in Internet Options.
    • Internet Explorer’s Enhanced Protection Mode blocks access to WebEdit and other applications running on localhost.
    • If the user is sure that WebEdit is running, access to it may be blocked by security software on their computer. Try accessing webedit.egnyte.com:9404 and verify that it shows the version of WebEdit. If it doesn’t show the version, contact support for options.
  • Mac users may see an error message when attempting to download and install WebEdit. Follow these instructions from Apple to successfully install WebEdit for Mac.
  • WebEdit does not work with Windows 8 Metro Mode.
  • WebEdit will not automatically lock .txt files when they are opened. This is because text editors typically load files in memory and do not lock the file on disk.
  • On-screen notifications will not appear for OS X users running 10.7 or lower.
  • Mac users may see a slight delay (up to 5 seconds) between when they save a file and when the new version of the file appears in the web UI.
  • WebEdit is not compatible with remote desktop solutions.
  • Office 2010 users may notice an issue where they open an Excel workbook with WebEdit, make a change without saving, and they are unable to open additional Excel workbooks. To open additional workbooks, simply select another cell in the first workbook.
  • Microsoft 365 - Microsoft Store version will not work correctly with WebEdit. Re-install Microsoft 365 with Click-to-Run version will resolve the issue.
  • WebEdit is only available to users with at least Editor-level folder permissions on the folder containing the file.
  • Having the Power User domain role does not grant Editor-level access to all folders. Folder-level permissions must be checked separately.
  • If WebEdit does not appear for a user, admins should verify the user’s folder permission level on the specific folder.
  • Any files failing to upload can be found in Egnyte WebEdit Failed Uploads folder on the Desktop for both Windows and Mac.

FAQs - Manage Email Domains for External Collaboration

How can a user manage external collaborations from their domain?

Can a user allow certain email domains while keeping some of the email domains blocked?

What happens if users switch from allow to block and vice versa?

If email domain restrictions are disabled and then re-enabled, is the previous email domain list retained?

When email domain restriction is enabled, when are links validated?

What happens to the existing shared links if an email domain is blocked?

How many email domains can be allowed or blocked?

Is there a provision to add exceptions to the allowed or blocked email domains?

What happens to pending Standard User invitations sent before an email domain was blocked?

Can an external user from a blocked email domain be converted into a Standard User?

What happens if the admin tries to activate a deactivated user belonging to a blocked email domain?

What happens if a Standard User’s email domain becomes blocked after they are added?

Can a user from a blocked email domain be converted back to a Standard User after being changed to another user type?

Can different restrictions be applied to sharing, co-editing, and invitations simultaneously?

How can a user manage external collaborations from their domain?

Egnyte allows domain administrators to manage emails domains for external collaboration by applying restrictions across three key areas:

  • Sharing Link Restrictions – Controls email domains to be allowed or blocked for link sharing
  • Co-editing Link Restrictions– Restricts which email domains can be allowed or blocked to collaborate via co-editing links
  • Standard User Restrictions – Controls whether users from specific email domains can be invited as Standard Users by allowing or blocking those domains
Can a user allow certain email domains while keeping some of the email domains blocked?

Users can either choose to allow email domains or block domains for Sharing Link Restrictions, Co-Editing Link Restrictions, and Standard User Invitations. They cannot apply both the rules of allowing and blocking the email domains at the same time.

What happens if users switch from allow to block and vice versa?

When switching modes:

  • Email domains added under a specific mode will be removed
  • Administrators would need to redefine the domains based on the new restriction type
If email domain restrictions are disabled and then re-enabled, is the previous email domain list retained?

Yes, when the setting is disabled and then re-enabled, Egnyte retains the previously configured email domain list. Administrators can choose to continue with the same setup or start afresh.

When email domain restriction is enabled, when are links validated?

Validation depends on whether Public Links Verification is turned on:

  • Public Links Verification OFF: Validation only occurs when sending emails directly through Egnyte. Links copied and shared manually (or existing public links) are not validated upon access, so compliance is not guaranteed.
  • Public Links Verification ON: Links are validated both when shared AND accessed. This ensures real-time compliance whenever a recipient clicks a public link.
What happens to the existing shared links if an email domain is blocked?

For customers with Public Links Verification NOT enabled, the existing links will continue to work for the link recipients. However, if the users attempt to share new links to the restricted email domains, they will receive an error message.

For customers with Public Links Verification enabled, existing public links set to verify the link recipient will be blocked when recipients with restricted email domains access the Share Link.

How many email domains can be allowed or blocked?

There are a maximum of 2000 email domains that can be configured to the allowed or blocked list for a specific restriction.

Is there a provision to add exceptions to the allowed or blocked email domains?

Yes, Egnyte provides the ability to add exceptions to the allowed or blocked email domains. Users can hover over an email domain added and use the edit icon to add user(s) as exceptions for the allowed or blocked email domains. They can always edit these exceptions as needed.

What happens to pending Standard User invitations sent before an email domain was blocked?

If there is a pending invitation for a Standard User from a now-blocked email domain:

  • The invitation cannot be accepted
  • The invitation cannot be resent
Can an external user from a blocked email domain be converted into a Standard User?

No. Users from blocked email domains cannot be invited or converted into Standard Users.

What happens if the admin tries to activate a deactivated user belonging to a blocked email domain?

Admins will not be able to activate such users as the Activate user option is disabled for users belonging to the blocked email domains. There is also an indicator informing the admins.

What happens if a Standard User’s email domain becomes blocked after they are added?
  • The user will continue to exist in the system. There is an indicator for such users in Users & Groups and user’s profile for the admins to easily identify the users belonging to the blocked email domains. Admins can then determine if they wish to delete these users to ensure compliance.
  • However, restrictions apply to future actions involving that email domain.
Can a user from a blocked email domain be converted back to a Standard User after being changed to another user type?

No. If a user from a now-blocked email domain is converted to another user type (for example, to a Power User), they cannot be converted back to a Standard User because their email domain is restricted.

Can different restrictions be applied to sharing, co-editing, and invitations simultaneously?

Yes. Each of the three areas can have independent configurations, allowing granular control over external access.

File and Folder Shortcuts

Skip Ahead To…

Overview

Creating Shortcuts Using the WebUI

Creating Shortcuts Using the Desktop App

Creating Shortcuts using the Mobile App

Permissions and Shortcuts

Frequently Asked Questions

Overview

Egnyte provides powerful capabilities to create and manage shortcuts. These shortcuts are native to the Egnyte file system, and are OS independent (unlike Windows or MacOS shortcuts). Users can create the shortcuts using the WebUI or the Desktop App. Once a shortcut is created, the users can use it to navigate to the target file using the Mobile App, Desktop App, or the WebUI.

Using shortcuts, users can centralize & manage their data in one place, but put shortcuts to the content in multiple places as needed, without duplicating data or storage.

Creating Shortcuts Using the WebUI

In order to create a shortcut, right click on the File or the Folder and choose the Create Shortcut option. A new shortcut would be created with the default shortcut name. Once created, a shortcut can be copied, renamed, moved, or deleted just like any other item. Anytime the user clicks on the shortcut, whether the click happens in WebUI, Desktop App, or Mobile App, they would be automatically redirected to the underlying original file or folder.

Creating Shortcuts Using the Desktop App

Prerequisites

To use this feature, users need to have the Desktop App installed and running (minimum version 3.14.12 for Windows, for Mac - Desktop App Core 0.8.1 or higher). Additionally, the drive on which a source file is located must be installed.

How to Use

To create a shortcut:

  • Right-click on the file or folder to create a shortcut to.
  • Go to the Egnyte Actons menu. Select Create Shortcut from the context menu.
  • A new shortcut will be created with the default shortcut name. Once created, a shortcut can be copied, renamed, moved, or deleted just like any other file. The shortcut will have the following icons and extensions: .egnyte_f for files and .egnyte_d for directories (folders).
Windows Icons

Folder shortcut File shortcut

Mac Icons

Folder shortcut File shortcut

Egnyte create shortcut option is not available for legacy Deskop App on Mac.

Creating Shortcuts using the Mobile App

To create a shortcut, click on the three-dot menu next to the file or folder name and select the Create Shortcut button.

.

A shortcut pointing to the file or folder is created with a message stating successful creation of the shortcut.

Creation of file and folder shortcuts is supported only in the iOS mobile app.

Permissions and Shortcuts

In order to successfully follow a shortcut, the user must have appropriate permissions on the target file/folder. For example, suppose there is a shortcut in Folder-A that points to Folder-B, and a user has full permissions in Folder-A, but no permissions in Folder-B. They will be able to see the shortcut in Folder-A, but they will not be able to navigate to Folder-B using that shortcut. Shortcuts do not bypass permission checks.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does a User not see the Option to Create a Shortcut?

This feature is only available on Platform plans. For users who are on a platform plan and not seeing this feature, contact the Support team.

What Happens to Shortcuts if a user Moves or Renames the Underlying File or Folder?

The shortcuts will continue working even if the target is moved or renamed after the shortcut is created.

What Happens to Shortcuts if a user Deletes the Underlying File/Folder?

When someone clicks on the shortcut, they will get an error that the file/folder is deleted.

What Happens to Shortcuts if a user Deletes the Underlying File/Folder, and then Restore it Back from Trash?

After the file or folder is restored, the shortcuts will continue to work as normal.

Can a user Share a Shortcut via a Link?

No. Shortcuts can’t be shared via links. Users will need to share the underlying file.

Can a user Create a Shortcut to a Shortcut?

No, Shortcuts can’t be nested.

If a user has Some Shortcuts in their Folder, but when they Share it via a Link, the Recipients Can’t See the Shortcuts.

When a folder link is shared, the recipients can not see the shortcuts for security reasons.

Do Shortcuts Work on Desktop App when it is Offline?

Shortcut creation and opening won’t work if the Desktop App is offline.

Do Shortcuts Work in Connected Folders on the Desktop App?

No. Creating shortcuts won’t work for Connected folders.

Does a user Have Any Egnyte Custom Actions Available for Shortcuts from the Context Menu in the Desktop App?

No. Currently, no Egnyte custom actions are available through the context menu on shortcuts. In the next iterations, View in cloud option will be provided.

Can a User Create a Shortcut for a File that is Being Uploaded in My Desktop App?

Shortcut cannot be created for a file which is still being uploaded.

File and Folder Templates

Overview

Many Egnyte customers often use the same file or folder structure in their processes. Here are a few examples to illustrate this:

  • Company A has a default presentation template that should be used by all employees to keep the branding and messaging consistent externally.

  • Company B works on several projects. Any project should include the same static list of folders due to public regulations. In both these cases, the users would need to copy files and/or folders from one location to another. Egnyte improves this process and allows easier management and access to the templates using the File and Folder Templates feature.

  • To create any folder or file based on a template, there must be at least one template in the Folder Templates or File Templates folder.

• File templates are created in the /Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates folder by creating a new file or uploading a file there.

• To create a folder template, the user has to create a folder within the /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates folder.

File and Folder Templates

File and Folder template capability allows having “template files” and “template folders” in one place so that it is easier to manage them and provide access to end-users.

  • The system creates the following three folders:
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates
  • File Templates should be uploaded to “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates” while Folder Templates should be uploaded to “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates”: File Templates

Folder Templates

Permission Requirements
  • By giving Viewer permissions to “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates” and “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates”, users will be able to easily create a file or folder from a template by using the Create button in the folder view.
  • By giving Editor permissions to “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates” and “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates”, users will be able to control and edit templates that are available under the Create button in the folder view.
File Creation from Template Examples

  1. If the user wants to create a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file and if Microsoft Office Online Integration is also enabled then the option to create from the template will be listed under the respective file creation menu as shown below.

  2. For all other file types OR if Microsoft 365 for the Web Integration is not enabled then the option to create a file from template will be listed under Other file templates.

Folder Creation from Template Example

When a folder is created using a template, any metadata values set on the template folder are also copied to the new folder. Refer here for details on managing metadata.

Editing Templates

To edit a File or Folder template, the user needs to go to the folder “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates” (for File Templates) and to “/Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates” (for Folder Templates) and edit the templates there as they would do for regular files or folders.

Editing a File or Folder Template will not change files or folders that have been created earlier using the File or Folder Templates.

Limitations and Known Issues

See below for some existing limitations:

  • If a user has permission to File Templates but not to Folder Templates, the user will not see any folder templates in the Create menu.
  • Egnyte requires using the specified names listed below for template folders. Ensure these names are not altered, as any changes will prevent users from accessing and utilizing the templates.
  • Folder structure for templates:
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates/File Templates
    • /Shared/Egnyte Templates/Folder Templates
  • Egnyte supports only a flat structure for file templates for now. Any folder or files in sub-folders will not be taken into account.
  • Egnyte supports only a flat structure for folder templates for now. Only folders directly under the Folder Templates folder can be used from the Create menu.
  • When creating a folder from folder template, it will take into account all sub-folders.
  • File and Folder template capability is available in Web UI and Egnyte Android applications only.
  • If a user (or admin) deletes the “/Shared/Egnyte Templates” directory, either it needs to be restored from trash, or the folder structure needs to be manually recreated. Refer to point 2 for the folder structure.

File Conversion

Egnyte provides a file conversion feature that lets users seamlessly convert files between Microsoft Office and PDF formats, enhancing workflow efficiency and accessibility. This feature enables easy sharing of documents in universally compatible PDF format and streamlines collaboration by allowing quick format changes. The users can also convert the PDF files to Microsoft Office format, such as Microsoft Word, Powerpoint, and Excel.

This feature is available with Egnyte’s PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact the Sales Representative or the Egnyte Sales team for more details.

Microsoft Office to PDF Conversion

To carry out file conversion from a Microsoft Office format to PDF

  • Open the context menu on the file, click on More actions and select Convert to PDF.
  • Enter the File name (default name will be source file) and Location (default location will be same as the source file) in which the file will be saved. Click on Convert.
  • The conversion process will begin and the user will get a UI notification.

PDF to Microsoft Office Conversion

To carry out file conversion from PDF to a Microsoft Office format

  • Open the Context menu on the file -> More actions.
  • Select the desired format from the Convert to menu.
  • Enter the File name (default name will be source file) and Location (default location will be same as the source file) in which the file will be saved. Click on Convert.
  • After clicking on Convert, the process will start and the user will get a notification.

Supported File Types And Limitations

  • Formats supported to convert a file from PDF format: .xlsx, .docx, .pptx
  • Formats supported for PDF conversion: All Microsoft Word, Powerpoint, and Excel formats
  • PDF file size limit: 25 MB
  • Microsoft Word file size limit: 50 MB
  • Microsoft Powerpoint file size limit: 50 MB
  • Microsoft Excel file size limit: 5 MB

File Locking

File locking keeps data safe from accidental overwrites when multiple people try to work on a file simultaneously, and the file type does not allow co-editing. The article covers how Egnyte handles file locking, how to see who locked a file, and how Admins and folder owners can manually unlock files.

If Microsoft 365, Microsoft 365 for the web, or Google Workspace integration is being used, the user will still be able to use the co-authoring function if the person opened the file through the integration.

Skip Ahead to…

Lock a File

Unlock a File

Lock Summary Report

Lock a File

There are two ways in which files can be locked within Egnyte. The first is an automatic file lock that occurs whenever one person has opened a file utilizing the Desktop App or WebEdit, Microsoft 365 Office Desktop, Microsoft 365 for the web, or Google Workspace. As long as the file remains open (and the computer is online), the file will remain locked.

The second way to lock a file is to manually lock the file via the web interface, using the file action menu to lock the file.

A locked file will show a lock icon on hover over (except when the file is being co-edited).

Users can also manually lock and unlock the files directly from the Desktop App and Desktop App Core context menu. Lock/Unlock options let users explicitly prevent concurrent edits when working on a file.

Locked files may be previewed or downloaded, but may not be renamed, moved, or deleted. Users may not upload new versions of a locked file.

These rules do not apply to Admins or users with the “Owner” permission on a folder, who may manually unlock any files in that folder (except files that are under a co-editing session using Microsoft 365, Microsoft 365 for the web, or Google Workspace).

Unlock a File

An open, locked file in the Desktop App, WebEdit, Microsoft 365 Desktop, Microsoft 365 for the web, or Google Workspace will unlock automatically after closing the application (or the users’ computer goes offline). For files being co-edited, it might take up to 35 minutes (usually, much faster - just a few minutes) to automatically unlock upon everyone leaving the co-editing session.

For files that were locked manually through the web interface, the user, an Admin, or a folder owner must unlock the file manually. If a file is not unlocked manually, the lock will be automatically removed in 7 days.

If a file is being co-edited using Microsoft 365 Desktop, Microsoft 365 for the web, or Google Workspace integration, it is impossible to unlock the file until the co-editing session ends. To co-edit the file under the co-editing session, the user can click on the Co-edit button.

Lock Summary Report

Administrators and Power Users that have been provisioned with the can run reports role can use the Lock Summary Report to view all of their domain’s locked files. Learn more about the Lock Summary Report here.

File Versions

Appending file names with indicators like v2.1 and 2013 03 23 is an inconvenient way to track the iterations of a file and dramatically increases the storage needs. By contrast, Egnyte automatically creates a new version of a file each time a change is saved for an existing document. The Administrator has set up version policies to dictate how many versions are collected before the old versions are moved to trash. Read on to learn more about file versions and how to “promote” old versions to replace the existing file.

Skip Ahead to…

Setting Version Policy

View Versions

Restore Old Version

Additional Information

Setting Version Policy

Navigate to Settings > Configurations > General and scroll down to Trash and Version Policy section to set the desired number of Versions to retain and click on Save Changes.

A maximum value of 999 versions can be set. Increasing Version retention will increase the storage utilization. Refer to

View Versions

Users can view the file’s versions in any of the views as List View, Condensed view, or Large Icons (Gallery) view.

The number indicated next to the icon that looks like a clock is the file’s version count.

In the large icons view, users can hover over on a particular file and look at the count of file versions.

For any given file, only a certain number of versions will be retained. By default, this maximum number of versions is 3, but Admins can change this value through a setting in the Egnyte domain if the respective plan allows it. This setting can be found under Trash and Retention Policies.

Only three versions will be kept for the following file types, regardless of the account setting: Microsoft Outlook/Exchange (.pst and .ost), Microsoft Access (.mdb), QuickBooks (.qbb), and email (.eml) files.

Restore Old Version

  • Click the version icon.
  • Locate the old version to promote to the current version and click the icon highlighted below.
  • The selected version is now the current version and will be shown when users preview or access the file through a link. Egnyte employs version pruning to automatically purge some of these versions from the system. Refer to Version Pruning for more details.

Additional Information

Egnyte always orders file versions by their modified date when determining the current version. When restoring an old version (or making a version current) through the WebUI, the timestamp is overwritten with the present time.

If a user is trying to copy and replace a file through the Desktop App or Storage Sync, they’ll need to be aware of some caveats. When users attempt to copy a file in Windows File Explorer or Mac Finder with an older timestamp than the latest version that is available in the Web UI, the file is uploaded but treated as an older version. This means that anyone can still access the file from the version history window in the WebUI. If the newest version needs to be promoted, choose the Make current option from version history in the WebUI. Alternatively, the file can be revised to update it’s modified date to the current date, so it’s regarded as the newest version based on modified time.

Folder Access Request

Direct Link recipients can request access to the folders through the folder access request feature. Folder owners can then review these requests and approve or deny them as needed.

This feature aims to enhance collaboration by ensuring easier access to shared folders and their contents. Instead of requesting new links, the option to request access to the shared folder simplifies the process for teams, enabling them to access the required information and work more effectively.

There are various scenarios where direct links may be shared with recipients who do not have access to the shared folder. For instance, new employees in an organization may request access to shared folders containing company policies and documents. Similarly, the feature can be useful in cross-departmental collaboration, training activities, new resources joining project teams, client and vendor interactions.

Here’s how it works:

  • Open a direct link to a folder which is currently inaccessible.
  • Provide a brief reason for the access request (optional but helpful for folder administrators).
  • Click on the Request access button located within the folder.
  • Submit the request. Once the access request is submitted, the folder owner will receive a notification and can promptly review and approve the access.
How does the email notification look like

Email title: [Action needed] You have received folder permissions requests

On clicking View the request, the user will be re-directed to the permission pop-up to approve or deny the request.

Once the request is approved, the requesting user will receive a notification that they have been granted permission to the folder.

If the request is denied, the requesting user will receive the notification informing them about the denial.

Who will receive an email notification about the folder access request?

Notification is sent either to the user with owner permissions or to admin user (which has owner permission to every folder). Notification is sent to 5 folder owners (or admins) based on the activity stream in the folder in question, most active owners will receive the email notification about the request. If there are less than 5 active owners in a given folder, then the notification recipients will be selected based on overall activity.

How many requests can a user send?

User can have 5 pending folder access requests.

Folder Notifications

Egnyte recognizes the need of the customers to keep track of the file/folder changes accessible to them within their company’s Egnyte domain. Email notifications can assist in monitoring these changes; however, receiving excessive notifications for every action may be overwhelming.

Egnyte addresses these challenges with folder notification features enabling customization of these alerts. Users can choose to receive notifications for specific actions like uploads, file updates, deletions, moves, copies, downloads, and previews.

We classify notifications into two types:

  • File additions, updates, and removals
  • File downloads and previews

Notifications

All Folders

Users can modify their folder notification email settings from My Profile -> My Preferences if enabled by the Admin.

Users can configure whether notifications are enabled for all folders, only for chosen folders, or disabled entirely. Notification criteria and email frequency can also be customized in this section.

Select “for chosen folders” to receive folder notifications for specific folders. The section below provides details on how to set it up.

It is important to note that users need to select folders manually to receive email notifications; otherwise, they won’t receive any.

The frequency option determines how often the user will receive shared folder notifications. If the user sets the interval to every day, they will receive a single email each day with all of their shared folder notifications for that day. If they set the interval to every hour, they could receive up to 24 shared folder notification emails in a day.

Folder-Specific Notifications

To enable notifications for a specific folder, click More Actions > Details & Options from the three-dots drop-down at the top of the screen.

From here, select the Preferences tab to access the settings. The notification criteria for the current folder can be selected. Click on Save.

These settings need to be applied for each folder to receive notification emails. Also, to enable folder-specific notifications, select the “for chosen folders” option in the My Preferences section.

Sub-folders will inherit the notification policies of their parent folder, but these can be overridden.

Shared Folder Notifications

For shared folders, notifications are sent based on the selected actions and frequency, but only for actions performed by users other than the recipient. This setup is designed to prevent excessive notification emails in the user’s inbox.

Folder Permissions

Folder permissions in Egnyte allow admins and folder owners to control access to files and folders within the Egnyte domain. By setting up appropriate permissions, one can ensure that the data remains secure while facilitating collaboration among team members. In this article, we’ll explore how to manage folder permissions effectively in Egnyte.

For further questions on how permissions work in Egnyte, please refer to the Permissions FAQs article.

Learn more by watching a short video about Granting Access with Folder Permissions.

Add A Domain User or Group to Access a Folder

After creating a new folder, a user can share the folder using the Permissions menu icon at the top.

  • Navigate to the folder -> Select Permissions icon from the list of top menu icons.
  • Only Admins and folder owners can grant access to shared folders.
  • The Folder Permissions window shows all users that have access to the current folder. To share files with colleagues who already have an Egnyte user account, enter their username or group name in the search bar.
  • Enter username or group name in the search bar and select from the results.
  • Click on the permissions dropdown and select the permission for the user or group. Click on Add
    • The default permission is set to Viewer when adding a new user.
    • A visual indicator will appear after adding the user or group. ↑ Back to Top

Add a User to Existing Group

A user can be assigned to an existing group within permissions to a given folder. This will eliminate any need to provide folder permissions specifically for the user and additional steps to add the same individual to the appropriate groups. Here are the steps to add users from the pop-up:

  • Enter the username and select the user from the results in the dropdown.
  • The default permission while adding a new user is Viewer.
  • Change the permission if required.
  • Click Add to existing group.
  • Select the group name and click Add.
  • A visual indicator appears after the addition of the user.
  • The new user added will have permissions to all the folders that the group is associated with. Alternatively, a user can also be added to an existing group from the Groups page. Refer Manage Groups article for the details. ↑ Back to Top

Invite New User(s)

  • Click on Invite new user(s) button at the bottom or while searching for a user to add.

  • Enter the user details such as Email address and Username (both are mandatory). Select the User type (default is Power User) and Permission Type (default is Viewer). Click here to learn more about the different user types.

  • Click on Add more to invite multiple users in bulk

  • Click Invite new users.

  • The new user will be added to the list with the visual indicator as Added.

  • Adding multiple users is currently available only for Document Room and Enterprise Lite plans. Please contact your Egnyte representative to inquire about this feature.

  • The new user will have immediate access to all files in the current folder as well as all the files contained in its subfolders (if permissions are inherited from the parent folder).

Owner Permission - Access Blocked for Subfolders

Even if a user has owner permission on a folder and permission inheritance is enabled for all its subfolders, it is possible that the permission assignment can be blocked for some individual subfolders. For example, consider the scenario below -

  • A user, Jane, is the owner of the folder /Shared/finance
  • /Shared/finance has two subfolders - /Shared/finance/invoices and /Shared/finance/reports
  • Jane is the owner of /Shared/finance/invoices but is not the owner of /Shared/finance/reports.
  • Permission inheritance is enabled for the entire folder subtree.
  • Another user, John, has no permissions on any folders in that folder subtree.
  • Jane assigns ‘Editor’ permissions to John on folder /Shared/finance
  • One would expect permissions inheritance to cascade the permissions so that John gets Editor permission on /Shared/finance/Invoices and /Shared/finance/reports
  • However, note that Jane is not the owner of /Shared/finance/reports and hence, should not be able to grant any permissions on this folder.
  • Therefore, John would only get the permissions for /Shared/finance and /Shared/finance/invoices folders. Permissions for /Shared/finance/reports will remain unchanged. One can imagine even more complex scenarios with deep folder trees, where a user is the owner of a top-level folder and also owns some of the bottom-level folders, but not the folders in the middle of the tree. The permissions would actually change only till the topmost subfolders where the grantor loses owner permission. The permissions for all other subfolders shall remain unchanged.

As a best practice, Egnyte recommends starting with minimal access at the top-level folders, and assigning permissions/ownership to users as needed at the lower-level folders

↑ Back to Top

Remove a User or Group from a Folder

As users’ duties and responsibilities change, it may be necessary to remove the permission they no longer need.

To remove a user or group from a folder:

  • Navigate into the folder where the permission needs to be removed.

  • Select Permissions icon from the list of top menu icons.

  • Locate the user or group that needs to be removed and click the delete icon next to its name.

  • Click on Remove in the confirmation pop-up.

  • Only Admins and folder owners can change access to shared folders.

  • Removing user permissions from a folder would lead to deletion of Share links created by that user.

  • Removing a user from a group would cause the user to lose folder permissions leading to Share Links deletion.

↑ Back to Top

Whenever access to a folder is either granted, altered, or revoked for a specific user by the admin or the folder owner, a permission change email notification is sent to the user whose permission has been updated. This notification will let the users know the specific changes affecting them.

The feature is in limited availability for all customers. To request this feature contact the Products team.

The email notification appears as follows.

Case 1: Permission is Granted

Case 2: Permission is Altered

Case 3: Permission is Revoked

The permission change email notification is sent only when the permissions are changed explicitly for the specific user, and for each change, a separate notification is sent.

For non-explicit permission changes made through user group permissions, inheritance, and folder movement will not trigger such notifications.

Sharing from a Mobile Device

Egnyte offers the ability to manage permissions from Android, iPhone, and iPad using Egnyte’s mobile apps.

Here are the steps to manage permissions.

Folder Sharing with Storage Sync

Egnyte allows centrally managing all folder access from the WebUI, so anyone with access to folders in Egnyte WebUI will be able to access those same folders on Storage Sync. When a user make changes to folder access in the Egnyte account, the modifications are automatically applied to the local folder structure on Storage Sync.

During the initial data migration to an Egnyte account, NTFS local file server permissions are replaced with folder access levels configured in the cloud.

Forgot Password

If you forget your password, use the steps below to reset it from the WebUI:

  • Open the WebUI login page, enter a valid username or email address, and click Continue. If your username or email address is already entered, skip to step 2.
  • Select the Forgot password? option on the login page.
  • Click Continue to proceed.
  • Once you receive the email, click the Change Password button. This button can only be pressed once and will only be active for two hours. You’ll be directed to a page where you can enter a new password.
  • If you receive an email stating “your account is configured to log in using your company’s directory service or identity provider” it means your company uses Active Directory or a Single Sign-on provider for authentication.
