Retain Original Permissions on Restore from Trash, Move, and Copy Operations

Egnyte provides the ability to preserve a folder’s original permissions when restoring it from the trash, moving it, or copying it. Retaining the source folder’s permissions is typically straightforward, but some nuances prevent non-admin users from gaining access to sub-folders to which they don’t have permission.

For example, imagine that Steve, a Power User in the account, copied the Finance parent folder that they only have partial access to into a different folder where they have Owner-level permissions. To prevent an escalation of privileges in cases like this, Power Users do not have the option of inheriting a destination parent folder’s permissions for some move or copy operations; instead, the source folder’s permissions are automatically applied.

This article covers the details and special scenarios (like the one above) when opting to preserve a folder’s original permissions.

Restoring a Folder from the Trash

When restoring a folder from the trash, account administrators have two options:

  • Retain the folder’s original permissions (this is the default option).
  • Ignore the original permissions and instead apply the inherited permissions from the parent folder.
  • This option is not presented when restoring a top-level folder (i.e., directly under Shared), a private folder, or a folder where no permissions were set. Select Yes, restore original permissions, and click Restore to reuse the folder’s original permissions.

Here are some details to keep in mind when restoring a folder from the trash:

  • Keep in mind that only Admins and Power Users who have been given trash management privileges through Egnyte’s role-based administration feature can access all Trash in the Web UI.
  • Users without this role will be able to access and restore Trash they’ve deleted by default. Admins can disable this feature in the General settings under the Trash and Retention Policies section.
  • Role-based Admins will not see the option to inherit the parent folder’s permissions. Instead, the original folder’s permissions will be applied automatically.
  • Role-based Admins will be prevented from restoring a folder if doing so would result in a conflict with an existing same-named folder on the same path. In these cases, only Admins can restore the folder.
  • In cases where restoring a given folder results in merging with a same-named folder on the same path, the restored folder’s original permissions will be ignored at each point where there is a conflict. Instead, the existing and more recent folder permissions will be maintained.
  • When restoring a mixture of top-level and non-top-level folders, the option to inherit the parent folder’s permissions will be shown. However, top-level folders will still automatically reuse their original permissions.

Moving or Copying a Folder

Admins will be presented with the same two options when moving or copying a folder:

  • Retain the folder’s original permissions (this is the default option, but users can change the default on the Security & Authentication section of the Configuration settings page).
  • Ignore the original permissions and instead apply the inherited permissions from the target parent folder. Stick with the default option of Keep source folder permissions to retain the folder’s original permissions.

Alternately, select Apply destination folder permissions for the moved or copied folder to inherit permissions from the target parent folder.

Select Move or Copy after making the desired selections.

  • This option is not presented for top-level folders (i.e., directly under Shared, like a Finance or HR folder).

  • Non-admin users will not see this option when moving or copying a folder. Instead, the folder’s original permissions will automatically be applied.

Keep these details in mind when moving or copying a folder:

  • In situations where the client cannot present a choice (for example, while using the public APIs), admins will not see a choice. The source folder’s permissions will automatically be retained in these cases.
  • Non-admin users will not be able to move or copy a folder in cases that would result in a folder merge. In these cases, the same rules described above for restoring a folder from the trash will apply, and only Admins will be able to move or copy the folder.
  • When moving or copying a folder to the top-level (directly under Shared), the folder’s original permissions will always apply.
  • Non-admin users will be prevented from moving or copying a folder from the Shared area to their private folder if they do not have at least Viewer access to all of its sub-folders.

Additional Information and Resources

The copy modal presents an additional option called Setup new permission after copying. Users can use this option to set up new permissions. This clear the current permissions for that folder.

Review and Approval Workflows

Need a document reviewed and approved, or assigned to team members to add content, publish, or validate data? Egnyte’s Review and Approval workflows let you automate these processes in a structured, repeatable way, complete with detailed audit reporting at every step. Beyond manual task assignment, advanced capabilities allow you to integrate AI actions, set up dynamic branching logic, and run automated file actions like updating metadata, moving files, executing webhooks, and converting documents to PDF.

A number of the capabilities described below are specific to the Life Sciences GxP plan - those features are indicated with a Life Sciences GxP badge.

Access to these features depends on your Egnyte plan. Platform Team and Business plans are limited to single-step workflows, whereas Platform Enterprise Lite and Enterprise plans support multi-step workflows with templates. Advanced features like the AI Agent and conditional logic steps are available exclusively on Elite and Ultimate plans.

Creating a Workflow

To create a new workflow on a file, follow the steps below:

  • Open the file preview and select the Workflows tab in the sidebar.
  • Click New Workflow. If an Egnyte plan with multi-step workflow is enabled, click New Workflow and then Custom Workflow.
  • Life Sciences GxP Users can optionally add a reason for change. This field allows an explaination to all the workflow assignees why a new document is being created or an existing document is being updated.
  • Choose one of the following step types:
  • Step Type
  • Description
  • To Do
  • Creates tasks for assignees asking them to do something, e.g., add content to the document, add metadata, submit the document, etc. After assignees are done, they mark the task as complete.
  • Review
  • Creates tasks for assignees asking them to review the document and provide feedback. Once an assignee is comfortable with the content, they mark the task as reviewed.
  • Approval
  • Creates tasks for assignees asking them to either approve or reject the document.
  • Life Sciences GxP Life Sciences plans with 21 CFR Part 11 compliant workflows provide an additional option to require a digital signature from approvers.
  • Rejection logic can also be configured for every approval step in the workflow. The feature is available to the customers on Elite or Ultimate plans. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.
  • After choosing the step workflow type, add the properties for the step.
  • Enter the Step name and optionally a description.
  • Choose the assignees. Users can pick up to twenty assignees. They can also search and select user group(s) in the Assignee(s) field. If a user group is selected, all its members will be added. By default, all assignees will need to perform the step before the workflow is completed or before it moves to the next step (in case of multistep workflows).
  • On adding two or more assignees to a workflow step, the system provides the following two options. Choose one of the two options to define the number of assignees required to complete a task.
    • All the assignees need to take action: This is a default selection that requires all the assignees to take action on their tasks.
    • Option to specify the number of assignees needed to take action: This option allows defining a specific number of user(s) required to complete the task.
  • Choose a due date. The due date can be any time from the current day until 180 days in the future. The maximum length for any workflow is 180 days.
  • Depending on the Egnyte plan, the user has the option of adding more steps by clicking on the + icon in the Graphic Builder. The user will again get an option to choose the user task. The user can create up to 25 steps in a workflow.
  • Click on the Create Workflow button at the top right.
  • Modify the General workflow details, if needed. Navigate to Notifications & Reminders.
  • Change the default selections and frequency of task reminders. Skip this step to use the default selection. Task reminders are email notifications sent to assignees to remind them of pending or overdue tasks. Click on Create Workflow.
  • Click Create to start the workflow.
  • Assignees will get an email notification telling them they have a new assignment.

Editing A Workflow

Users can edit an in-progress workflow by clicking Edit from the three-dot menu located on the right side of the workflow pane.

Users can change any workflow parameters for the step that has not started yet. They can make the following changes for in-progress steps:

  • Add or remove the assignees who haven’t completed their task
  • Change the task due date of incomplete task(s)
  • Update task reminders for incomplete task(s)
  • Modify the number of assignees required to complete the step Users can optionally add a reason for the workflow edit, which is available in the Workflow audit report along with all the changes made to the workflow.

View Flow

  • Click on the three-dots icon -> View Flow
  • Alternatively, click on the workflow to open the details and click on View flow.
  • The flow will be displayed.

Completing Workflow Tasks

Assignees will be notified of new task assignments via email and can also see all of their assignments in Tasks Assigned to Me. They can also access a task by navigating to a file and opening the Workflows tab in the upper-right.

Assignees can complete their workflow tasks on Egnyte Mobile apps. To learn about how to complete the workflow task on Egnyte IOS app, refer to this article, and for Android app, refer to this article.

A user can complete a task on a workflow if they are one of the assignees and if their step is listed as In Progress. Depending on the step type, the way that you complete the task is slightly different:

Jira Link

Completing the Task

To Do

Click the purple Complete button and confirm it in the dialog.

Review

Click the purple Mark Reviewed button and confirm it in the dialog.

Approval

Approval tasks have two options to complete their step, clicking Approve or clicking Reject. Then, confirm the action in the dialog.

Rejecting the task will cancel the entire workflow, so be careful in choosing this option.

Life Sciences GxP If a digital signature is required for approval, a signature screen will be shown asking the user to enter their username, password, and a reason for approving the document. If the user logs into to Egnyte via an SSO provider, they will need to set up a Non-SSO Password on the My Preferences screen.

The system will automatically lock files while they are in an Approval step. All assignees of Approval steps for a workflow must approve the same version of the document.

The required number of assignees must complete their tasks for a step before the step is considered complete. When the required number of assignees have finished the step, the workflow will transition to the next step. If there are no additional steps, the workflow will be marked as Completed.

Assignees can also choose to add comments while completing the workflows. The maximum length of workflow comments is 2000 characters.

If a completed workflow has an approval step, the user will have the option to download the approved version of the document.

Life Sciences GxP For documents with a signature, the download will be a PDF rendition that includes a signature page at the end.

View Tasks and Created Workflows

Users can access a list of all the tasks assigned to them or the workflows they have created by opening the Workflows & Signatures in the left navigation bar.

Tasks Assigned To Me

The Tasks assigned to me tab shows a list of tasks assigned to you, the current user. By default, it displays in-progress tasks but you can filter the tasks list based on the following filters:

  • Assigned by, the user who assigned the task
  • The task status
  • The task type
  • Completion date Clicking the file’s name in the Task column will open the file preview and bring the user to the appropriate workflow in the Workflows tab.

Users can view the reason for a task cancellation by hovering over to the task with a canceled status.

Workflows I Created

The Workflows I created tab shows workflows created by the current user. By default, it displays in-progress workflows but users can filter them based on the following filter:

  • The workflow status
  • Template name
  • Assigned to
  • Assigned date
  • Completion date
  • Due date Workflow creators can expand a workflow by clicking the caret to the left of the file type icon. Expanded workflows show the workflow steps, assignees, and status.

Clicking the file’s name in the File column will open the file’s preview and bring you to the appropriate workflow in the Workflows tab.

Workflow creators can edit or cancel an ongoing workflow by hovering over the specific workflow.

Users can view the reason for a task cancellation by hovering over an individual assignee’s task with a canceled status.

All Domain Workflows

Admins have the option to view all the domain workflows created by all the domain users. They can expand the specific workflows to view the associated steps.

Admins can edit an in-progress workflow by clicking on Edit Option. They can also click on the Cancel option to cancel the workflow.

To cancel a workflow, click on Cancel workflow in the confirmation pop-up.

Export CSV

Users can export the Workflows listing for the document workflows under Tasks Assigned to Me, Workflows I Created, and All Workflows. Click on Export CSV and the CSV of the workflows’ list will be downloaded to the user’s system.

Users can export up to 10,000 workflow entries per export.

Audit

For plans supporting Audit Reporting, a Workflow Audit report is available, which captures all details about workflow, including user actions (e.g., creating a workflow, editing a workflow, completing a task) and automated system actions (e.g., completing a step, starting a new step).

Life Sciences 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance

Life Sciences GxP Life Sciences GxP plans with Workflows contain the following functionality that provides compliance with 21 CFR Part 11:

Capability

Description

Digital Signature

Approvals support digital signatures which capture the user’s username, password, and a reason for approval. The system stores a cryptographic digital signature to validate the integrity of the signature.

Human Readable Rendition

The system can generate a rendition of approved documents that include a signature page with a list of signors with their first and last name, signature date and time, and approval reason.

Approved Document Retention

Approved documents are retained forever, preventing users from purging the data from the system. Workflows and digital signature records are also permanently retained and cannot be deleted.

Reviewer and Approver Authorization

Reviewers and Approvers must belong to specified groups. This ensures that only authorized users can approve regulated documents. The default groups for authorization are WorkflowReviewers and WorkflowApprovers.

Full Audit Coverage

All actions taken as part of a workflow are tracked in the Workflow audit report.

Limitations

The following is a summary of the limitations of Review & Workflow:

  • Maximum steps per workflow: 25
  • Maximum assignees per step: 20
  • Maximum workflow duration: 180 days. The system will automatically cancel workflows exceeding 180 days. Any workflows that remain open for more than 180 days will be automatically canceled. However, these canceled workflows will still remain available and continue to appear in the list.

Learn more about Review and Approval Workflows by watching a Quick Tip on Egnyte University: Review and Approval Workflows

Rule-Based Metadata Tags

Overview

Egnyte provides powerful capabilities to create and manage metadata. The metadata can then be used to search, sort, and filter the files and folders. Rule-based metadata provides a new way to apply metadata tags at scale using simple prescriptive rules.

This feature allows Power Users and Administrators to define simple rules that are used to apply a user-defined tag to all files and folders that match the rule. Any Power User that has Editor permissions on a folder can create a new rule and apply the rule to any folders that they have Editor permissions on.

Every rule has a user-defined tag associated with it. Once a rule has been created and applied to a folder (or a set of folders), all files/folders that match the rule get the tag automatically applied to them. In addition, any new files or folders that are added in the future, will be compared against the rules and the tags will be automatically applied to any items that match. Multiple rules can be created and applied to the same folder if needed.

A user can also see the list of all rules already created (including rules created by other users), and can apply any existing rule to their folders (provided they have editor permissions on those folders).

Skip Ahead to…
Creating Rules
Editing Rules
Adding Existing Rules to a Folder
Removing Rules from a Folder
Deleting a Rule
Searching for Tagged Files

Creating Rules

A Power User or an admin can navigate to the Settings -> Metadata Tags-> Rules Tags menu and click on Add New Rule

On the New Metadata Rule screen, the user can specify the rule name, tag (label), description, associated folders, and rule conditions. In order to associate folders with the rule, click on the Select Folder(s) button and choose folders. Note that a user can only choose folders where they have editor permissions or higher.

The example below creates a rule that will apply a tag ‘fin-reports’ to all spreadsheets in the chosen folders.

The conditions can include a number of system properties such as item type, pathname, creator, date, and more. In addition, a user can also choose any custom metadata value that they have previously defined. This provides an extremely powerful mechanism to tag files based on previously applied metadata, including tags previously applied by other rules.

The comparison operator in the middle can take on a variety of values depending on the property type.

Note that when a rule has multiple conditions, it will apply the tag to files that match all of the conditions. In order to apply the tag to files that match any of the conditions, one can create multiple rules, each with just one condition; and apply all those rules to the same set of folders.

When a rule-based metadata policy is applied to a file or folder, the resulting Rule Tags can be found under the metadata namespace System Tags -> Rule Tags.

Editing Rules

Only the user that created the rule, or an admin, can edit a rule.

In order to edit an existing rule, a user can click on the Edit icon in the metadata rules list. Once the edit view opens, the user can edit the rule.

Editing a rule only takes affect for new files/folders being uploaded, and new versions of existing files being created. An edited rule does not retag existing files that were already tagged via an older version of that rule.

Adding Existing Rules to a Folder

If a user has Editor permissions on a folder, they can apply any of the existing rules (including rules created by other users) to their own folder. In order to add rules to a folder, click on More actions -> Details & Options in the three-dots menu.

In the dialog box, choose the Metadata Rules tab and click Apply Rules.

Choose the rules you would like to apply to this folder and save.

When a rule is applied to a folder for the first time, it will scan through all files/subfolders and tag the ones that match the criteria. From that point on, the rule will scan and tag new files/folders being uploaded, and new versions of files being created.

Removing Rules from a Folder

If a user has Editor permissions on a folder, they can remove any of the rules applied on that folder. In order to remove rules, navigate to the Metadata Rules tab as described above.

Note that if a rule is applied to a parent folder, all its subfolders automatically inherit that rule. The rule cannot be removed from the subfolders. It would need to be removed from the parent folder itself.

Deleting a Rule

A rule can be deleted by clicking the Delete icon in the rules list.

Deleting a rule does not delete any of the tags that have already been applied by that rule. It would only stop any new files/folders from being tagged.

Searching for Tagged Files

Once files are tagged, they can be searched using the normal Egnyte search functionality (see this article for more information).

Additionally, if a file is opened in the preview pane, the user can also see & edit all tags assigned to the file in the Tags section.

Saved Search Queries

Users can save the queries that they run often (such as - find all spreadsheets with the word ‘expense’ in the title that have been uploaded within the last week). When a search query is saved, all search keywords as well as all associated search filters are saved.

In order to save a query, first execute the search, and then click ‘Save Search’ on the Search results screen.

At that point, you would be prompted to provide a name for the saved query.

To execute a previously-saved search, click on the saved searches dropdown and select the query you would like to execute.

You can also click on the menu within the dropdown to delete queries.

If no searches have been saved yet, the saved searches dropdown box will display a message indicating that no searches have been saved yet.

Search for Files and Folders in the WebUI

Egnyte offers AI powered Smart Search experience to help users quickly find the files and folders they need. Users can type their query in plain language and also tag specific users to get the matching search results. From basic keyword search with auto-suggestions to advanced filters, metadata-based search, image similarity and geolocation search, the system is built to handle a wide range of use cases. Users can further refine the search results using the filter controls.

AI-generated overviews enable the users to explore results more efficiently and saved searches let users quickly revisit frequent queries.

This article goes into the details of each capability included when searching in Egnyte.

Comments and Tasks are not included in searches.

Search Details

Cross-Domain Search (Multiple Entity Management)

Default Search

Entering a term, like Employee Policy, will return results that contain that term, like Employee, Policy, Employee Property Policy, and so on.

  • Words are automatically split at case transitions. For instance, ‘PowerShot’ is broken into ‘Power’ and ‘Shot’ so it will not match with words like ‘Powershot’.

  • Egnyte search returns up to 10,000 results per query. Results show the latest version of each file, file versions are not counted as separate results. If a search query matches more than 10,000 files, only the first 10,000 are shown. To ensure accurate results are obtained in large repositories:

Use a more specific search term - More precise query would result in fewer total matches for relevant results

Scope to a folder - Use the folder filter or navigate into a folder before searching to limit results to the specific location

Combine filters - Use Item Name, file type, or date modified filters together with the search query to narrow the search results

AI Powered Search

Users can type their query in plain language and they will get the matching search results.

Users can also search by tagging specific users in their queries. By typing @username, they can include a particular user in the search, and results matching that user and the entered query will be displayed.

Based on the user’s query, Egnyte automatically executes the keyword-based search for non-complex queries. For more complex queries, the users can continue their interaction with Egnyte’s AI Assistant to get the response(s).

AI Powered Search is only available to customers with the AI add-on. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Auto-Suggestions

When a user begins typing a search term, Egnyte automatically suggests files and folders based on their recent activity and bookmarks. This is useful in quickly locating frequently accessed items without needing to fully type out the query or sift through longer lists of results.

AI Search Overview

Users can view the AI overview generated based on their search results. This overview is a quick, AI-generated summary based on the user’s query and the top hits in the search results. The source files analyzed to generate the AI-powered overview are also listed by its side.

Users can click on any of the source files listed under AI Overview to open its preview and ask Egnyte’s AI assistant questions about that file.

They can also use the icons below the AI overview to copy the content generated and provide their feedback on the response.

This feature also supports natural language queries such as:

  • “List all the 2026 company holidays”
  • “What is my insurance policy number?” AI Search Overview is accessible to users with an active AI add-on. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Quick Search Filters

Search Current Folder Or Entire Account

The user can search only the items contained in their current folder, or can search their entire account. By default, only the items contained in the current folder are searched. User can search the entire account by changing the location setting to All Folders.

Search For Items Containing Any Or All Words

Users can search for items that contain any of the search words entered, or search for items that include all of the search words entered. By default, the search will return results that contain any of the words entered. Users can restrict the results to items that contain all of the search words by choosing All search words in the dropdown menu.

Search Through Folders Or Files

Egnyte account might contain tens of thousands of folders and files; finding a single one of those could be tough. Egnyte has a folder or file search option for this use case. Select Folders, and it will return folders that match the search criteria; select Files and only files matching the search will appear.

Filter Search Results By Modified Time

Users can narrow down search results so that they include only files modified within a certain time period. Modified Time filter can be used in such scenarios. Users can choose only to see files modified within the last 24 hours, week, month, 3 months, 6 months, the last year or define a specific time period.

Advanced Filter Options

Users can click on the Filters dropdown to view and apply filters. They can click on x to remove the applied filter and view the updated search results. Users can also click on Reset all to reset the filters.

Filter Search by Folder

The user can choose to search in the current (default) or any folder in the domain.

Filter Search Results by Content

The user can choose to keep the search limited to both files and folders, only files, or only folders.

Filter Search Results By File Type

The user can limit the search results to only show certain types of file formats. For instance, if the user is looking for an image file, they can select Image from the list so all other file types will be excluded from the results.

Filter Search Results by Modified Time

If the user knows the file they are looking for was modified within a specific time frame, they can use the Modified Time filter to narrow the results. They can choose only to find files modified any time (default), within the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, 360 days, or within a specific time period.

Filter Search Results By Uploaded Time

If the user knows the file they are looking for was modified within a specific time frame, they can use the Modified Time filter to narrow the results. They can choose only to find files modified any time (default), within the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, 360 days, or within a specific time period.

Filter Results Based on Updated by

The users can filter the search results based on the content being updated by Anyone (default), Me, and by specific user(s).

Search for specific user(s) to view the results updated by them.

Wildcard Search

Users can insert an asterisk to act as a wildcard in their search; this will pick up any extra letters or suffixes that might be attached to the search term. For instance, a user is looking for any files and folders that contain the word “image” in the name. Searching for “image” alone would miss results like “images” or “image-new,” but adding an asterisk ensures those results are fetched.

Search for at Least One Term (“OR”)

If the user uses AND, OR, NOT keywords in the search query, the ‘Any Search Words/All Search Words’ setting in the quick filters will be ignored.

Entering multiple terms will return folders and files that pertain to any of those search terms. For example, a search for “image capture” would return any items where either “image” or “capture” is relevant. In this case, the “Capture” file name pertains to the term “capture,” but has nothing to do with the search term “image.” Spaces between search terms are interpreted as “OR.”

Search for All Terms (“AND”)

If the user uses AND, OR, NOT keywords in the search query, the ‘Any Search Words/All Search Words’ setting in the quick filters will be ignored.

The user can narrow the search by inserting the word “AND” in all capital letters between each term. This will limit results to files that contain both terms. Searching “image and capture” yields only results where both terms are relevant.

Search for a Specific Phrase

If the user is looking for a specific phrase, they can also search using quotation marks. This will only yield files that contain that exact phrase. In the example below, searching “create folder templates” will only return items that match that string.

Boolean Search

If the user uses AND, OR, NOT keywords in the search query, the ‘Any Search Words/All Search Words’ setting in the quick filters will be ignored.

Certain Boolean operations (AND, OR, NOT) are supported in Egnyte search. Egnyte supports grouping to allow adjusting how multiple Boolean operators work together using parentheses to group words.

  • For instance, the filename is “marketing plan 22072024 powershot a 123”, then a valid search criteria to fetch the file will be “marketing plan” AND “powershot a”.
  • Similarly, if the filename is “marketing plan 22072024 powerShot a 123”, then a valid search criteria to fetch the file will be “marketing plan” AND “power shot a”.
  • Similarly, if the filename is “marketing plan 22072024 a 123” (and it does not contain the word “powershot”), then a valid search criteria to fetch the file will be “marketing plan” NOT “powershot”

Metadata Search

If the user has Metadata set up in Egnyte’s Web UI or with API, they can add metadata search criteria to their search options by selecting the three dots next to the search bar, and clicking metadata search criteria.

Users can click on the dropdown to select the metadata section and apply it to the search criteria by clicking Apply.

They can click on Add another metadata tags section to continue to add other metadata tags sections to the search criteria. Users can reset the metadata search criteria by clicking on Clear all.

If there are two or more metadata tags sections added to the search criteria, the users can click on the respective remove icon to remove the criteria from the search.

Users can sort the search results for the system as well as the custom metadata.

Sorting on Multi-Value String & Multi-Value Enum is not supported.

Egnyte’s file search engine will also consider a folder or file’s metadata (i.e. the folder where it lives, notes added to the file, etc.) when determining how relevant a result is. Although, a file’s name is weighted more heavily than metadata. Learn about using Egnyte’s Metadata API on the domain.

Image Similarity Search

Image Similarity Search can locate images that are visually similar. This feature provides an efficient way to find related images based on the image being viewed in a folder list or search result.

Users can search for similar images by:

  • Clicking the More like this row action, which is shown below.
  • -OR-
  • Selecting More like this within the context menu via normal selecting or right-clicking the image file. The system will then use the selected image as a reference to find and display other images in the folder structure that share visual similarities.

This feature is accessible to users with an active Project Hub. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Geolocation Search

This feature is accessible to users with an active AEC package. It enables users to locate images taken in specific places. By harnessing the EXIF data within image files, this feature accurately identifies the geolocation of photos, providing the user with the ability to conveniently search and organize their image collection.

How to Leverage Geolocation Search
  • Select the Geolocation filter from the filters dropdown.
  • The defaults to the current location.
    • If the location is incorrect, make sure the location has been granted for the given device. Check the browser’s site settings and ensure location access is allowed for the Egnyte domain.
  • Alternatively, manually enter the desired address or geo-coordinates.
  • Adjust the radius slider to fine-tune the search area according to the preference.
  • Click Apply to locate all images taken within the specified vicinity.

Save Search

The user can save the queries that they run often (such as finding all spreadsheets with the word ‘expense’ in the title that have been uploaded within the last week). When a search query is saved, all search keywords as well as all associated search filters are saved.

In order to save a query, first execute the search, and then click Save Search on the Search results screen.

Users would be prompted to provide a name for the saved query.

To execute a previously-saved search, click on the saved searches dropdown and select the query to execute.

Column-Level Filters

Users can search for specific items using the column-level search filters.

  • Item name: Enter the search keyword and the results will filter to show the item names matching with the entered keyword
  • Date Modified: Users can filter the items using the date filters as Any time (default), Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or choose a custom range
  • Updated By: Users can search for items updated by a specific user
  • Document Type: Select the document type(s) and click on Apply to view only the selected document type(s)

Inline Insights

Users can also preview basic viewing insights directly from the content listing and search result pages by clicking the Insights button under the Status column.

  • This feature is currently limited to PDF files.

  • This feature is currently available on the Elite and Ultimate plans only. Contact your account manager or Egnyte Sales team to get this feature.

Search Details

Search Trash

Egnyte’s search results do not include files in the trash. To learn more about searching in the Trash, refer to this article.

Search Weights

Filenames have a higher weight in scoring results. The number of matches within a file also plays a role in ranking the search results. In addition to that, files modified relatively recently will have a higher weight.

Tokenized Search of File and Folder Names

When searching for a file or folder name, Egnyte tokenizes the search into groups of 3 letters called trigrams. For example, searching for “brexit” would create four tokens (“bre,” “rex,” “exi,” and “xit”) and any file/folder name which matches at least 50% of search tokens would be considered a match. A folder named “Existing Breaks” would be displayed in the search results since it matches two out of the four tokens (“bre” and “exi”) but a folder named “Breaks” would not be displayed since it only matches one token (“bre”).

Searching Document Content

Text from the following file types are searchable: doc, docx, docm, xls, xlsx, xlsm, ppt, pptx, pptm, pdf, htm, html, txt, rtf, xml, pages, numbers, key, msg, zip, tar, tgz, odp, ods, odt, tsv, xhtml, csv, dot, wbk, dotm, docb, xlt, xlm, xlsm, xltx, xltm, xlsb, xla, xlam, xll, xlw, ppt, pot, pps, potx, potm, ppam, ppsx, ppsm, sldx, sldm, ps, epub, mbox, m, md.

  • Text content is indexed for search for files smaller than 20MB.

  • Egnyte also limits the indexed text to no more than 50KB of extracted text and 10,000 tokens (words).

Cross-Domain Search (Multiple Entity Management)

For organizations using Multiple Entity Management (MEM), search results include a cross-domain results dropdown in the filter bar. This dropdown shows how many matching results were found across other linked MEM domains.

Self-Serve 14-Day Trials for Add-Ons

Plan Details are available under Settings > Subscription and renamed to Current Plan for better clarity.

Additionally, a new Trial Add-Ons tab is available under Subscription, allowing customers to explore and activate free trials for add-ons.

The functionality makes it easier for the customers to explore the new features without making financial commitments. Trials before the purchase provides the customers with an opportunity to evaluate the add-ons in their own environment and make more informed upgrade decisions.

The following are available as trial add-ons:

  • AI Add-On
  • Specialized File Handler Add-On
  • PDF File Handler Add-On
  • Project Hub
  • Document Portal Add-On Customers will be able to self-serve the trial add-ons if they are optional on their plan.

How It Works

  • Start a Trial: Customers can enable a 14-day free trial for eligible add-ons from the Trial Add-Ons page.
  • Immediate Access: The add-on is enabled for all users on the domain as soon as the trial starts.
  • User Notifications: If the domain has “Show announcements about new features to users” enabled, users will receive a notification about the trial.
  • Manage Trials: Customers can start, cancel, or purchase a trial at any time.
  • Trial Extensions: Customers can contact Sales if they need the trial extended beyond the initial 14 days.
  • Automatic Expiration: If not purchased or extended, the trial will automatically expire after 14 days.

Start a Trial

  • Navigate to Settings -> Subscriptions -> Trial add-ons
  • Click on Start free trial for a specific add-on available to start the 14-days free trial.

Purchase a Trial Add-on

  • Navigate to Settings -> Subscriptions -> Trial add-ons
  • Click on the three-dots menu for the add-on to purchase.
  • Click on Purchase Now.
  • Click on Go to Plan Details. The user will be re-directed to the Settings -> Subscription -> Current Plan page to complete the purchase.

View the Current Plan Details

To view the current plan details, navigate to Settings -> Subscription -> Current Plan.

Self-Service for Enabling or Disabling Private Folders

Admins have the ability to enable or disable Private folders from the Collaborate settings. This feature provides more control and flexibility to manage data access with just a click.

For instance, admins can enable private folders across their domain to maintain data privacy for sensitive information. Similarly, they can disable private folders to ensure broader visibility and support compliance requirements.

Skip Ahead To…

Enable or Disable Private Folders

What Happens to the Data in Private Folders?

How Long Does it Take To Disable Private Folders?

How to Check Which User Disabled the Private Folders?

Additional Resources

Enable or Disable Private Folders

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General.
  • Use the toggle to Enable or Disable the private folders. By default, the private folders are enabled.
  • To disable the private folders, set the toggle to Disable, type DISABLE in the input box, and click on Confirm. Click on Save changes.
  • Private folders will then be disabled and removed from all users’ views like WebUI and Desktop App.

What Happens to the Data in Private Folders?

When Private folders are disabled, all the existing data in those folders is immediately moved to Trash and can be easily recovered, manually deleted or automatically purged from Trash based on the retention policies. It is highly recommended to take a backup of all the data in private folders before disabling.

How Long Does it Take To Disable Private Folders?

Depending on the amount of data, it can take some time to finish moving all the data to trash. Users can still access the data in Private folders during that time. For domains with large amounts of data we recommended disabling the Private folders during off hours to minimize user impact. Admins can check for existing data using the Private Folder Size Report.

How to Check Which User Disabled the Private Folders?

Admins can run Configuration Settings Audit Report and look for generalSettings.privateFolderEnabled under the Settings Path column.

Sending and Managing Signature Requests

Egnyte Sign makes it easy to send a set of documents for electronic signature and automatically save back the signed document to your Egnyte account. Follow the steps in this guide to send and manage signature requests.

Egnyte Sign is available as part of the PDF File Handler Add-On. Contact the account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more details on how to get access to this feature.

Sending Signature Requests

Users with permission to send signature requests can send a request by following these steps:

  • Select the file or right-click on any supported file.
  • Click Egnyte Sign -> Send for signature in the context menu.
  • Users can also open the file and click on the Send for signature button to get redirected to the document preparation interface.
  • Alternatively, signature requests can be sent from Quick View. Users can click on the Egnyte Sign icon and select Send for Signature from the dropdown menu.
  • This feature is only available to customers on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Starter, Essentials, Elite and Ultimate plans with PDF File Handler Add-on.
  • Users can add more documents by clicking on Add document which will open the Egnyte file explorer and supported file can be selected. Documents can be deleted and re-ordered. Maximum 10 documents can be added in a signature request.
  • The user can create a new signature request or choose from the templates available:
    • Click on New Signature Request to create a signature request from scratch as described in the steps ahead.
    • Choose a template from a pre-determined list or search for one to create signature request using templates by clicking on Apply Template.
      • Select the template and check or uncheck the box to Override the signed document location with the one from the template and then click on Apply.
      • Power users will see active templates for which they have at least Editor access on all the associated document folder(s).
  • If New Signature Request is selected, click Continue to Add signer(s), choose the formatting, and select the desired fields. If a template was selected, click Apply and skip to step 11.
  • Add one or more signers. User can send requests to both domain users and anyone else with an email address. When adding multiple signers, choose whether they should sign in parallel (the default) or sequentially. To sign sequentially, enable the Sequential Signing toggle and then drag and drop the signers in the desired order.
  • Senders can also send signature requests to the groups or CC the groups. A Signer Group is a set of people where any one member can fulfill the signing requirement.
  • A CC Group is a distribution list that automatically receives the final signed document once all signing is complete. These groups are defined at the Egnyte’s domain-level.
  • Click on the Group to select it as a Signer (default) or CC the group.
    • Unverified internal email addresses cannot be added as recipients of signature requests.
    • The maximum size of a Signer Group is 50 active members at the time of sending the request.
    • The same Egnyte group cannot be added more than once to the same document.
    • A recipient may appear in more than one Signer Group, or as both an individual signer and a group member, on the same document. Each signing slot is treated independently; fulfilling one does not auto-fulfill the other.
    • When the sender enables forwarding on a document that contains a Signer Group, a disclaimer is shown as group signers cannot forward the request.
    • An individual signer can be replaced with a Signer Group, and vice versa.
  • Click on Formatting to choose one of the following signature styles and its size:
    • Light
    • Regular
    • Bold
    • Italic
  • Add fields for each of the signers: Select the signer’s name from the dropdown menu and then Drag and drop fields to the document at the desired location. Users can Drag and drop the field on a particular page and then move it to any other page within the document as required. Double-click a field to edit the signer or to mark it as optional.
    • The user has the option to add fields such as Signature, Initials, Name, Company, Date Signed, Title, Dropdown, Text field, Checkbox, and Radio Button to the document.
    • Once selected, each field is displayed at the chosen location, and there are Edit and Delete options available for each field added. For instance, on adding Signature, Name, Title, Company, and Date signed, the fields will appear as shown in the screenshot below. The users can easily adjust the size of these fields.
    • Adding the Dropdown field additionally shows the Edit Dropdown field option. It enables the requester to add a Field label and Dropdown options. The user can choose a default option by selecting Show this as selected radio button.
    • Requestors can add one or multiple checkboxes to the signature request and they can click on the Edit icon to provide a label to the checkbox or to mark the field as mandatory or optional. They can click on the Delete icon to delete the checkbox.
    • Click on Save after entering the label and marking the field as optional or mandatory.
    • The label will appear when the requestor hovers over the checkbox.
    • Egnyte also allows requestors to add radio button groups to a signature request. Recipients can select only one option within each group. Requestors can add multiple radio button groups to a document as needed. They can use the Edit icon to assign a label to each of the radio buttons in the group and to mark the field as mandatory or optional. The Delete icon can be used to remove a radio button group.
    • Click on Add radio button to continue adding more radio buttons to a particular group. Users can click on the delete icon to delete a radio button from the group. Enter the label(s) and click on Save.
    • The delete icon will be disabled when there are only two buttons present as it is required to have at least 2 radio buttons in a group.
  • Align and distribute fields: Click on the Select tool at the top and select the desired fields to align, distribute, and/or delete.
    • Click on the Align option on the fields.
    • Align the fields left, vertical center, right, top, horizontal center, or bottom. Users can also Distribute the fields vertically or horizontally.
    • Click on the Delete icon to delete all the signature fields if required.
  • Add one or more CC’s. User can add CC for both domain users and anyone else with an email address. When adding CC’s, add them like any other signer, go to their settings and change them to CC. A CC user gets the final signed copy after the request is completed.
  • Click Send Signature Request in the top-right corner of the screen.
  • The user will be able to verify all the details filled in the signature request through the request verification screen. Click on Send to create the request and send it to all signers. All signers will receive an email with a link to sign the document and all CC’s will get the final signed copy after the request is completed. By default, the request name is the first document selected for request creation or the name of the template. User can change the request name on verification screen.
Optional Steps

  • Add a customized Message for the email notification sent to signers.

  • Change the Expiration date (defaulted to 30 days) and the destination folder for the signed document (defaulted to the current folder).

  • Requesters can choose to turn on Signature forwarding the ability to forward the signature requests. By default, the option is turned off.

  • Requesters can turn on reminders by going to Settings tab. The reminders can be configured based on a timetable, with two specific configurations:

    1. First reminder after - The initial reminder will be sent out ‘x’ days following the submission of the request.

  • b. Subsequent reminder frequency – This determines the interval between subsequent reminders after the initial one has been issued. Signature requests are automatically canceled in the following scenarios:

  • The document you sent for signature has been deleted

  • The sender of the request no longer has permission to access any of the documents.

  • The sender of the request is either deactivated or deleted.

Manage Signature Requests

The Signatures dashboard allows you to track the status of your active and completed signature requests.

Viewing Sent Requests
  • Click Workflows & Signatures in the left navigation.
  • Click the Signatures tab.
  • Click Sent Requests section to see the signatures requests sent. By default, Sent Requests shows In Progress requests. To see already completed or canceled requests, change the Status filter.

Users can also filter the sent requests using the other column-level filters.

By default, requests Assigned to Anyone are displayed. These can be filtered to display the requests assigned to a particular user.

Similarly, users can filter the requests based on Templates used. The options are All (default), No template used (custom), Any template used, or a Specific template.

Requests can also be filtered as per the Bulk ID to display All (default), All Non-bulk Requests, or All Bulk Requests.

Details of each signer and their status can be seen by expanding each row.

Edit a Request

Senders can edit a signature request by clicking on the three-dots menu -> Edit option.

Currently, the options under General and Settings can be edited.

Replace Signer(s)
  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> Sent Requests and click on the Three-dot menu for requests in-progress. Click on Replace a Signer.
  • Enter the username or email address of the existing and new signers. Click on Replace.
  • A UI notification will appear confirming the replacement of the signer. The existing signer who has been replaced with a new signer will receive an email notification informing them about the reassignment.

Similarly, the new signer will also receive an email notification.

  • For signature requests sent using templates with ‘Recipients and Fields’ section locked, the Replace signer option will be disabled.

  • For sequential signing, if the signer is replaced before their turn to sign is due, they will not receive any email notification informing them about the reassignment.

Forward a Request

If the requestor turned on the Signature Forwarding option at the time of the request, the signer can forward the request to another signer.

To forward a request,

  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> My requests and hover over on the request to forward. Click on Forward.
  • Alternatively, the user can click on Review & Sign from the email notification or Sign it on a particular signature request listed under Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures -> My requests and click on Forward.
  • They can also view the signature document and click on the Forward option at the top. In either of the above scenarios, the user will get the option to forward the document. Enter the email and an optional message for the new signer and click on Forward.

Once forwarded, the previous signer cannot access the request again as the signing rights are taken from them and passed on to the new signer. Also, the requester gets notification that the request is forwarded by the signer to another person.

The same option is applicable if a signature request is created using a template.

Cancelling a Request

If a signature request is no longer needed, the user can also cancel the request. To cancel the request, click on the three-dots menu of an In Progress request and click the Cancel Request option.

In the cancel dialog, you can add a message for the signers and then click the Cancel Signature Request button. All signers will receive an email notifying them of the cancellation.

Viewing All Requests

The All Requests dashboard allows administrators to view and manage all signature requests created in the account, regardless of who sent them. From this view, admins can track request status, open individual requests, and perform the same actions available to the original requestor, such as sending reminders, canceling requests, replacing signers, and downloading documents.

  • Navigate to Workflows & Signatures -> Signatures tab.
  • Click All Requests section to see all signatures requests sent.
  • By default, All Requests show the In Progress requests. To see completed or canceled requests, change the Status filter.
  • Admins can click on the Three-dots menu on any of the requests and take actions such as Edit, Replace Signer, Send Reminder, and Cancel Request.

Setting a Non-SSO Password

If you sign in to Egnyte via an SSO provider (for example, Okta, Azure AD, Google, etc) and you need to log into a tool that does not support SSO login, you can set up a separate non-SSO password to log in.

Non-SSO passwords are valid for the following protocols and functions:

  • FTP and SFTP
  • Public API
  • 21 CFR Part 11 digital signatures in Review & Approval Workflows Non-SSO passwords cannot be used to log into the Egnyte Web UI, desktop, mobile, or other Egnyte applications.

Delegated Authentication

Whenever a “delegated auth” is configured (currently supported for Okta and OneLogin), by providing an API key token in Egnyte SSO setup, users can log in to the given service (for example, FTP or SFTP, etc) using their IdP (Okta or OneLogin) password and Egnyte username. Note that when delegated authentication is enabled, the option to set non-SSO passwords is not available.

Setting a Non-SSO Password

To set or update your non-SSO password, follow the steps below:

  • Log in to the Egnyte Web UI
  • Click your profile picture or initials in the top-right of the screen and then click your name
  • Click My Preferences
  • Under the Security section, click the Set non-SSO password link
  • Egnyte will send you an email with the subject line Set a non-SSO password for your Egnyte account. Click the Set Password button.
  • You’ll be asked to enter a password and confirm it If you’re an admin, you can send a non-SSO password setup link to a user by clicking the Set non-SSO password link on the right of the user’s profile in Users & Groups.

SHA-1 Setting Change

Overview

A key part of every SAML communication between Egnyte and IdP is the signature used to sign requests between the two entities. Due to recent security update, the SHA-1 algorithm will no longer be supported as it is considered unsafe. It is recommended to update the chosen algorithm in any IdP setup that use old and unsupported ones to SHA-256.

Instructions for Common IdP Setups

OneLogin

  1. Log in to the OneLogin console as an admin and access “Administration” panel on the top right.

  2. Go to Applications List and select Egnyte application that the customer is using.

  3. In “SSO” panel select SHA-256 from the “SAML Signature Algorithm” dropdown and click “Save” in top right.

Azure

For customers that have not created a new SHA-256 cert previously on Azure SSO:

  1. Login to “portal.azure.com” as an admin and access “Azure Active Directory.

  2. Go to “Enterprise applications” and select Egnyte application that the customer uses.

  3. In “Single sign-on” locate “SAML Signing Certificate” and click Edit.

  4. Create new cert by clicking ‘ + New Certificate’ (make sure to select SHA-256).

  5. Once cert is saved on the list above, ACTIVATE IT and download it.

  6. Go to Egnyte, replace existing cert with downloaded one, save.

  7. Navigate back to Edit the SAML signing certificate tab on Azure.

  8. Change the ‘Signing Option’ from ‘Sign SAML assertion’ to ‘Sign SAML response’ and click Save.

  9. Wait for few seconds for the change to apply.

  10. Change the ‘Signing Option’ back to ‘Sign SAML assertion’ and click Save.

For customers that have created a SHA-256 cert but still sending SHA-1 on Azure SSO:

  1. Navigate to the Single sign-on on the Azure portal.

  2. Edit the SAML signing certificate tab.

  3. Change the ‘Signing Option’ to ‘Sign SAML response’ and save.

  4. Allow a few seconds for the change to apply.

  5. Change the ‘Signing Option’ back to ‘Sign SAML assertion’ and save.

Okta

Okta uses predefined Egnyte app that has a hardcoded SHA-256 certificate, so no change is required.

Other Providers

As Egnyte supports every provider that is SAML-compliant, it’s hard to provide detailed instructions on each of them separately. However, general rules on how to locate the signing algorithm setting are the following:

  1. Log in to IdP as an admin.

  2. Go to list of Applications (may also be called connectors/entities/etc) and find one used for Egnyte authentication.

  3. In Single Sign-On settings find value that uses “SHA-1” - it may be called “Signature Algorithm”, “SAML Signature Value”, etc, etc.

  4. Update algorithm to SHA-256 and save.

Allow couple minutes for change propagation on IdP side and test login.

Instructions presented in this article are subject to change based on the IdP service provider. Refer to your IdP service provider’s own documentation for more accurate information.

Share Links - Email Auto-Suggestions

Egnyte offers its users with the email auto-suggestions while sharing links. The feature is introduced to improve link sharing experience for the end-users. The platform automatically suggests email addresses of the recipients during link sharing based on the link access type.

The feature is available to all platform customers.

Auto-Suggested Email Addresses

Link Access Type - Anyone or Anyone with Password or People you Choose
  • Hover over on a file or select a file and click on Share.
  • Select link access type as Anyone, Anyone with Password (default), or People you choose and click on Email Link.
  • Quick suggestions will show up below the Email addresses field based on the user’s engagement in the past.
  • Select from the suggested email recipients or type in the name or email address of the recipients to share the link with. Frequently used email addresses will show up before the rest of the matching results based on the user’s input. Click on Send Email.
  • An alert will show up confirming that the email has been sent. For People you choose (Specific Recipients), internal users will be able to access the link directly. External users will need to include the code included in the email.
Link Access Type - Existing User(s) (Domain Users)

  • Hover over on a file or select a file and click on Share.

  • Select link access type as Existing User(s) and click on Email Link.

  • Select the recipients from the quick suggestions displayed below the email addresses field or enter the email addresses of the recipient(s) to share the link with. Frequently used email addresses will show up before the rest of the matching results based on the user’s input. Click on Send Email.

  • Users will not be able to enter the email addresses for any of the external users (non-domain users).

  • An alert will show up confirming that the email has been sent. Considerations:

  • Non-domain users added in the past will show up with the External tag.

  • Non-domain users not added previously will show up with the Unknown tag.

  • Selected email addresses will be removed from quick suggestions for that instance.

Share Settings

To ensure complete control over the sharing of your company’s data, Egnyte provides a number of sharing settings for Administrators to customize.

Skip Ahead To…

File and Folder Link Sharing Options

Link Expiration and Timezone Behavior

Individual Folder Sharing Options

Inheritance of Folder Sharing Options

File and Folder Link Sharing Options

To manage how users share files via links, Admins can navigate to the Configuration tab of Settings, and in the General section, scroll down to the Sharing options section.

To enable or disable file or folder sharing, simply choose the default type and select one or more link type options:

  • Public (no password): Accessible by anyone with the link
  • Public (password-protected): Accessible by anyone with the link and the password
  • Private (all account users): Accessible only by users with an active account on the domain.
  • Private (recipients-only): Accessible only by the recipients of the link shared using the Email Link option.
  • Specific Recipients include: Specify the choice of recipients to send the links to.
    • Any email recipient: This option enables users to send links to any specified email address.
    • Only <client> File Server Users: Choosing this option allows sending links to the client’s Egnyte domain users. For more details on the Specific Recipients feature click here.
  • Users can share upload links to folders: Enabling this option will allow users to create share upload links to folders. Using upload links, recipients can upload files to the specific folder without signing in.
  • Public File and Folder Link Expiration: Users can enable or disable the public file and folder link expiration. The link can be set to expire after the selected days/weeks/months or number of clicks. Users can also choose to mention the maximum expiration for time-based links and click-based links.
  • Private File and Folder Link Expiration: Link expiration options are available for private file and folder links as well. User can enable or disable the expiration policies for private links and choose the links to expire after selected days/weeks/months or number of clicks. They can also enable the maximum expiration for time-based links and click-based links.
  • Expiration policies for public and private links is available only on the Platform Enterprise Lite plans and above excluding Trial domains. If the above settings are not visible, contact your Sales Rep or Egnyte Sales team for assistance.
  • Default file and folder link expiration: Set the expiration parameters for file and folder links. Links can be set to expire after a set amount of time e.g. days, weeks, or months, or after a number of times the link is accessed. Once expired, links become inaccessible.
  • Click here to learn how to make files and folders more secure.
  • Maximum file and folder link expiration: Set the maximum file and folder link expiration values users can select during link creation. This applies to both time-based and click-based expiration parameters.
  • Send links in the user’s default mail client: Enabling this feature allows users to send share link using their own email client like Outlook instead of being sent through Egnyte.
  • Enabling Send links in user’s default mail client automatically disables Private (recipients only) option in the link types.
  • Users can share co-editable links: Enabling this setting allows users to send file share links that will allow the recipient to co-edit the file without requiring any permissions to modify the file.
  • For more details on the Sharing co-editable links feature click here.
    • Co-Editing via links is available to all the Platform plans
    • Co-editing via preview only links is available to Platform Enterprise Lite plans and above

Link Expiration and Timezone Behavior

When a link is created with an expiration date, the exact expiration time is determined based on the link creator’s local timezone settings.

How Expiration Works

The expiration time is set to 11:59 PM on the selected expiration date in the creator’s local timezone.

Example:

Creator’s timezone: GMT +2:00

Expiration date: 2nd April

  • The link will expire at 11:59 PM on 2nd April in GMT +2:00, which corresponds to 9:59 PM GMT.
  • This means if someone checks the link from a different timezone, the expiration time will be adjusted accordingly.
Behavior After Expiration
  • User Access: Once the expiration time has passed (as per the creator’s timezone), the link becomes invalid. Any attempt to access it afterward will result in failure to open the content.
  • Automated Expiry Checks: A system process runs daily to identify and mark links as expired.
  • This check uses the link creator’s timezone to determine whether the expiration time has passed.
Timezone Difference Considerations

Significant differences in timezone between the creator and the recipient can result in scenarios where the link is marked expired even though the expiration date has not yet ended for the recipient.

Example:

A link set to expire on 2nd April by a user in Australia (GMT +10) will become invalid at 11:59 PM AEST. A recipient in the USA (for example, GMT -7) will find the link expired while it is still the morning or afternoon of 2nd April in their local time.

Individual Folder Sharing Options

On top of the domain-level sharing options, it is possible to restrict sharing using folder-level link controls on certain folders that may contain sensitive documents.

The folder level link controls can be accessed by selecting the three-dots menu, choosing Details & Options from the drop-down, and opening the Options tab. Only folder owners or admins can modify the folder options.

Content sharing can be enabled or disabled to allow or restrict users from sharing the content in the folder (Enabled by default).

There is an option to Allow sharing public links for:

  • File and folders (default)
  • Files only
  • Folders only If Allow sharing public links for toggle is disabled, users will be prohibited from sharing any public folder or file links from this folder.

Disabling the Allow content sharing in this folder toggle will automatically disable the Allow sharing public links for toggle.

Inheritance of Folder Sharing Options

Changes to folder-sharing options are inherited (propagated) to subfolders when the user making the adjustments has the necessary permissions on those subfolders, and no manual changes have been made to the sharing options of the subfolders before.

Share with File and Folder Links in the WebUI

Egnyte makes it easy to share content inside and outside of your organization through Share links. Follow one of the links below to learn how to effortlessly collaborate with Egnyte.

Only Administrators and Power Users can create share links.

Share File Links

Share Folder Links

Direct Links

Share File Links

To share a file with a user without requiring a login, a link to the specific file can be sent. When the user clicks on the link, Egnyte will generate a preview of the file. The user can review it there or download the file.

  • There are four easy ways to share files from Web UI.
    • The first option is to hover on the three-dots icon for a file and select the Share button.
    • Alternatively, hover over the file, click on the three-dots option and click on the Share option from the context menu. Users can also right-click on the file and select the Share option from the context menu.
    • The example below displays the context menu when the user right-clicks on the file.
    • Another way is to select the checkbox next to the file and then click on the Share option in the Context menu.
    • Additionally, customers on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Starter, Essentials, Elite and Ultimate plans can also create Share links from the Quick View window.
  • When the dialog opens, the user will see the share options and link properties.
  • If the Get share link is chosen, the link will be copied with the access settings and link properties as selected.
  • Choosing Email Link option will enable the user to specify the email recipients and share the link with them.
Access Settings

To adjust the access settings before sharing the link, choose any of the following options.

  • Anyone: Public link accessible to anyone with the link

  • Anyone with a password: Password protected public link accessible to anyone with the link and the password

  • Existing user(s): Private link accessible only by users with an active account on the domain

  • People you choose: Accessible only by the recipients of the link shared using the Email Link option Public Share links to files posted in messaging apps such as Slack, Microsoft Teams, and iMessage display a visual thumbnail preview of the linked file.

  • Thumbnail previews are available for PDFs, images, videos, and other supported file formats and are shown for files up to 100 MB in size.

  • Links that are password-protected, have recipient email verification enabled, are restricted, expired, watermarked, click-expiring, or are folder links are not supported.

Links Properties

The user can set the link properties using the options available.

  • Co-Editing: Choose to allow co-editing on the file. The option enables the link recipients, regardless of the permissions, to co-edit the file in online editor and save changes back to the original location of the file. When co-editing is allowed, the option to show recent file version is auto-enabled and cannot be changed.

  • Downloading: Choose to allow downloading the file

  • Link expiry: Make links more secure by setting the link expiry for a specific date or number of clicks on the link.

  • Notify when link accessed: Request an email notification whenever the link is clicked

  • Include file name: Choose to include file name in the link

  • Watermark file: Choose to watermark a file. Watermarking a downloadable file will convert it into a non-editable PDF

  • Show recent file version: Set whether the link always points to the most recent version of the file or whether it references the current version only. When co-editing is allowed, the option to show recent file version is auto-enabled and cannot be changed.

  • The user cannot watermark a co-editable file and vice versa.

  • Co-edit via normal links is available to all the platform plans whereas co-edit via Preview Only Link is only available to the Platform Enterprise Lite, Platform Enterprise, and both the Document Room plans.

Share Folder Links

To share the contents of an entire folder with a user who doesn’t have permission to a folder or with an outside business partner, browse to the folder and then select the Share option at the top.

Users can also select a specific folder and click on the Share option in the context menu.

The folder link dialog looks very similar to the file link dialog. Users can adjust the link’s options to decide who will have access to the folder, set an expiration for the link, and more.

When the recipient opens a folder link, they’ll see a display of all its contents. They can preview the contents there, download all of it at once, or pick individual files. If the public folder link is password-protected then they’ll be asked to enter the password before they can proceed.

Users can also share preview-only folder links. The recipients will be able to preview the content in the Web UI using these links but will not be able to download it.

Preview-only folder links are available to Platform Enterprise, Egnyte Gov Enterprise, Life Sciences Professional, Document Room, Document Room Professional and GxP with Governance customers.

Direct Links

A Direct Link is the URL address of the file or folder within the Egnyte domain, and it takes the recipient directly to that item in the Web UI. It applies each recipient’s existing permissions, so only users who already have access can open it, and they see the content according to those permissions.

A Direct Link remains accessible unless:

  • The file or folder associated with the link is deleted. Deleting a version of a file does not affect the Direct Link.
  • The recipient does not have permission to the source folder. Moving or renaming a file or folder does not change its URL, so existing Direct Links remain active. Making a copy creates a new URL for the copied item, so the original link does not point to the copy.

A Share Link created for existing users can be opened by any authenticated user on the domain, and every recipient sees the full contents of the shared folder regardless of their own folder permissions. A Direct Link, by contrast, respects each recipient’s existing permissions.

To copy a Direct Link, select a file or folder and click Copy direct URL from the context menu.

Alternatively, for folders, navigate to the folder that is to be shared, click the three-dots icon and select Copy direct URL OR choose More actions -> Details & Options.

From there, just copy the Direct link on the Details tab and start sharing.

Additionally, for files, Direct Links can be copied from the Details pane in full File Preview.

Direct links can also be copied from the Quick View window. This option is only available to customers on Business, Enterprise Lite, Enterprise, Starter, Essentials, Elite and Ultimate plans. Contact your Egnyte account manager or the Sales team for more information.

Learn more about Share Links vs Direct Links by watching a Quick Tip on Egnyte University: Share Links vs. Direct Links

Shared and Private Folders

With Egnyte, files are stored in one of two main directories: your domain’s Shared folder or your Private folder.

Shared Folder

The Shared Folder is the main directory for organization’s files. When an Egnyte domain is first created, the Shared Folder will only contain sample folders. Administrators (or a Power User belonging to a role with access to create top-level folders) can create a sub-folder directly beneath the main Shared folder, like Sales, Engineering, Finance, etc. Power or Standard Users with the appropriate permission level can create sub-folders beneath these new folders.

Limitations
  • Files cannot be saved directly to the Shared Folder; the user must save them in a subfolder.
  • The Shared folder name, description, and permissions cannot change.
  • The Shared folder cannot be deleted.

Private Folder

Administrators and Power Users may each have a Private sub-folder, which is ideal for personal documents like pay statements, performance assessments, and other documents that wouldn’t be shared with other employees. Each sub-folder is named after the user to whom it belongs. Within their private sub-folder, each Power User can create as many additional sub-folders as they please.

In certain situations, Administrators might prefer to disable Private folders to prevent users from saving documents privately. They can navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General and set the private folders toggle to enabled or disabled.

If the admins disable the private folders, the existing private folders for all users will be moved to Trash and will be available to restore until it is purged. It is highly recommended to take a backup of all the data in private folders before disabling.

Administrators can access (and edit data) within all the Private folders in their domain. An Administrator’s private folder will appear with their name, while those of the other users in their account will appear in the All Private Folders section.

The table below covers the difference between Shared and Private folders.

Action/Permission

Shared Folders

Private Folders

Folder Name

The top-level folder name is Shared

The folder name is the username of the folder owner

Draft Mode

Users can create files in draft mode within a shared folder, but the draft is saved in the user’s private folder. Once finalized, the file can be moved to the shared folder.

Files can be created in draft mode within the Private folder.

File Creation

Only Admins or Power Users/Standard users with access can create files or subfolders in the top-level folder.

Admins and Owners of the private folders can create files.

Uploading a File

Must be uploaded in a sub-folder.

Can be uploaded in the topmost folder.

Ownership

Typically owned by Admins or groups.

Typically owned by an individual user.

Folder Access Levels

Users can have access levels as Viewer-only, Viewer, Editor, Full, or Owner.

Only the folder owner and admins have complete access.

Visibility

Visible to users or groups with the appropriate permissions.

Visible to the user. Only the admin can view all private folders.

Collaboration

Designed for collaboration among multiple users; changes and updates are visible to all with access.

Limited collaboration; primarily used for individual work.

Still have questions about Shared links or the Links section in the Web UI? Find answers to frequently asked questions below.
