Using Metadata in the WebUI

Egnyte provides powerful built-in metadata capabilities that allow the users to efficiently set metadata properties on a large number of files and folders and enable quick searching of content based on metadata. See this article for an overview of metadata features.

Administrators can create sections for metadata to allow their users to add and edit metadata for files and folders within the WebUI. The metadata properties are displayed in the file details and the folder details pane. It can be used to simplify the search process, making it easier to locate related folders and files. This article covers how to create new metadata using the WebUI, how to edit and delete existing metadata, and how users can add metadata to files and folders.

Skip Ahead to…

Create Metadata

Add Metadata Sections to Folders

Remove Metadata Sections from Folders

Edit or Delete Metadata

Add Metadata to File

Auto Tag a File
Tag Manually

Edit Metadata for a File

Edit Metadata Section from File Preview

Purview Labels as Metadata

Configure Custom Project Metadata

Create Metadata

Admins can use the following steps to create new Metadata sections:

  • Navigate to Settings -> Metadata Tags -> Configuration. Click on Add New Section.
  • Enter the section name.
  • Choose a scope for the section. The scope can be one of the three values below.
    • Global: This metadata section is applicable to all files and folder
    • Folder scoped: This metadata section is only applicable to items in the specific folders (and their subfolders).
    • If Folder scoped is chosen, then the admin can optionally select one or more folders to associate with this section.
    • Filetype scoped: This metadata section is only applicable to specified filetype(s).
    • If Filetype scoped is chosen, the admin must choose at least one filetype from the dropdown list.
  • Use the toggle to choose whether inheritance should be enabled on this section.
  • Inheritance can only be enabled at creation time. This property cannot be changed after the section has been created. See this article for a description of Metadata inheritance.
  • Enter the following property values for the new section. Up to twenty properties can be added to any given section.
    • Property name: Create a name for the property (required).
    • Description: Provide additional details about the property (required). Users can enter a minimum of 20 and a maximum of 200 characters.
    • If the users try saving with the description less than 20 characters, they will get an error message.
    • Type: Select a type for the property (required). See descriptions of the types below:
      • Integer: A whole number
      • Decimal: Integer and non-integer numbers
      • String: A string of arbitrary characters
      • Date: Past, present, or future date
      • Dropdown with options: Provide predetermined options for users to select from
      • For Date, there is an option to adjust for the viewer’s time zone (disabled by default). When enabled, dates are automatically adjusted as per user’s time zone.
      • Timezone-Aware attributes can also be converted to Fixed Date; however, converting Fixed Date back to Timezone-Aware is not supported. When the user tries to convert an existing timezone-aware date attribute to a fixed date attribute, the user will be prompted with a warning as shown below.
  • Once all of the needed information has been entered, click Save Changes.

Add Metadata Sections to Folders

After a folder scoped Metadata Section has been created, an admin or a folder owner can associate the section with a folder by following these steps:

  • Go to the folder listing view.
  • Click on the three-dots menu and choose More actions -> Details and Options.
  • On the resulting pop-up dialog, click on the Associate metadata sections menu and choose the section to associate with this folder.

Remove Metadata Sections from Folders

An admin or a folder owner can dissociate a section from a folder using the same dialog box as above. In order to remove the association between a Metadata Section and a folder, perform the following steps:

  • Go to the folder listing view.
  • Click on the three-dots menu and choose More actions -> Details and Options.
  • Click on the Remove option next to the section that is to be removed.
  • Note that if a value has been set for a property in a section, and that section is removed from the folder, the value of that property is not automatically deleted. Instead, the property is moved to Unassociated metadata sections.
  • The unassociated properties can be used for searching and filtering, just like any other metadata.

Edit or Delete Metadata Sections

Admins can use the following steps to edit or delete existing Metadata sections.

  • Navigate to Settings -> Metadata Tags -> Configuration. Hover over any of the metadata tags to see the respective Edit and Delete options.
  • Clicking on the Edit icon allows making the necessary changes to the metadata section name or properties, including deleting a specific property. Click on the Save Changes button after making the changes.
  • Section scope or inheritance cannot be changed after the section has been created.
  • To delete a section, click on the Delete icon. Confirm that you want to remove this section by typing in a confirmation message and clicking Remove section.

Add Metadata to File

Admins and users can use the following steps to add Metadata in files.

  • Open the file in preview and navigate to the Tags option.

  • Users can choose to Auto tag the file or add the tags manually using the dropdown options.

  • Auto tag functionality is only available to customers with the AI add-on. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

  • Domains without the AI add-on will only see the option to manually add tags.

Tags can also be added on multiple files at once. Select the desired file(s) and click on the Tag option in the context menu.

Auto Tag a File
  • To tag the file automatically, choose Auto tag from the dropdown and select a specific section. The sections will be listed as per the configured metadata in the domain.
  • The system will extract the metadata tags. Users can review and click on Save after making the necessary changes.
  • The tags will then be displayed for the file.
Tag Manually
  • Choose Tag Manually from the dropdown.
  • Select the desired section to create the tag.
  • Enter the associated values and click on Save.
  • The tag created will then be displayed for the file.

Edit Metadata for a File

  • Open the file in preview, navigate to Tags and click on the three-dots option for the tag added. Click on Edit tags.
  • Make the necessary changes and click on Save.

Edit Metadata Section from File Preview

Open the file in preview, navigate to Tags and click on the three-dots option for the tag added. Click on Edit section.

The user will be redirected to the Metadata configuration page in Settings to edit the metadata section.

Edit section option will be disabled for the metadata sections that are restricted or cannot be modified.

Purview Labels as Metadata

Egnyte provides the ability to automatically detect and read the Microsoft Purview sensitivity label applied to a file whenever that file is uploaded, created, or edited in Egnyte. When a file containing a Purview label is added to Egnyte, the label information is captured and stored as Egnyte metadata on that file. This allows the sensitivity classification to remain visible and searchable within Egnyte, even if the file was labeled outside of Egnyte or prior to being stored in Egnyte.

Refer to this article for more details about the functionality.

Configure Custom Project Metadata

Egnyte provides the option to configure custom project metadata tags for the projects. It enables the teams to capture the custom project details and makes it easier to search, filter, sort, and review projects based on specific metadata.

Important Notes
  • The terms Section, and Property map to the terms Namespace and Attribute as mentioned in the API documentation.
  • A maximum of 50 project tags (including both default and custom tags) can be added to a project.
  • The following limits are applicable on the metadata attributes:
    • Max number of attributes per namespace - 35 (Hardcoded)
    • Max number of attributes that can be applied on a document - 65 (Configurable)
    • Max number of values for a labels/multi-value enum type attribute - 1000 (Configurable)
    • Max length of values for metadata attributes - 4000 chars (Hardcoded) The configurable items can be modified by submitting a request to the Products team.
  • Projects are available in the Platform Enterprise Lite, Platform Enterprise, Life Science, and GxP plans as well as plans with the Project Hub enabled. Contact the Egnyte account manager or the Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Fix

Turning off browser extensions or Add-ons and restarting the browser should resolve the issues. Use the links below for instructions to turn off or uninstall browser extensions.

Verification for Public Links

Egnyte offers a domain-level setting to enable or disable recipient verification for public links. Admins can also configure whether link owners can override this setting when sharing links.

When enabled, recipient verification replaces anonymous entries in audit reports with the recipient’s verified email address, providing better visibility into who accessed shared content and improving auditability.

This feature is available for the New Generation Platform plans only. Contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Configure Email Verification Process

  • Navigate to Settings -> Configuration -> General
  • Enable or disable the toggle for Activate email verification process for shared links’ recipients. Additionally, if enabled, admins can choose to allow override this setting when creating a share link.

Share Public Links with Email Verification Enabled

Users can share public links with Verify link recipients set to Yes.

  • Public Link Email Verification is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by a domain administrator in Domain Settings.

  • Verification applies only to public links created after the feature is enabled; existing public links are not affected.

  • Recipients who are already signed in to the same Egnyte domain can access public links directly, without completing email verification.

If the setting to allow overriding when creating a shared link is enabled, the link creator can choose to keep the attribute as Yes or No.

Accessing Links Requiring Verification

  • When users access a public link requiring verification, they are asked to enter their Email address.

  • The Verification code is sent to the provided address.

  • Once verified, the user will be able to access the public link. The session is active for about 15 minutes ensuring that the users get seamless access to the link without having to re-verify. The activity will be captured in the audit report with the Email address, location, and IP address of the user.

  • If External access rules are enabled for share links, only recipients with an allowed email domain can access the content after successfully verifying their email address.

  • For Watermarked file links, when dynamic watermarking is configured to include user details, the verified recipient’s email address is automatically added to the watermark.

Version Pruning

Many accounts limit how many versions are kept before they’re moved to trash. If multiple versions were created by the same person on the same device (for example, clicking Save after every edit) within a short amount of time, these versions would quickly pile up and push relevant versions to the trash prematurely. Even if there are a higher number of versions available to users or infinite trash enabled on the domain, the storage is used up by keeping too many (almost identical) versions of the same file. Finding the correct version when researching changes would become tedious, if not impossible, due to the sheer number of similar versions to sift through.

To help keep the version count down, Egnyte employs version pruning to automatically purge some of these versions from the system.

How Does It Work?

Purging Versions without Moving those to Trash

When the same person from the same device saves a file multiple times within a 10-minute window, all of the versions are initially saved as a version in Egnyte. Every so often, Egnyte will prune (remove) the intermediary versions created within the window and only keep the last version and those created outside the 10-minute window. The pruning process does the same for other older versions of the file.

If another edit to the file is made later (outside the 10-minute window), a new version will be created.

Deleting Versions to Trash

This is applicable when the version limit is enforced. Admins can choose how many versions of a file shall be retained from Settings -> Configuration -> General -> File version policy.

Any of the file versions that exceed the applicable version count are automatically moved to trash.

Version pruning is applicable for domains with retention policies from Secure & Govern.

  • The algorithm will not delete any new file versions uploaded with a timestamp set in the past.

  • If there are multiple consecutive versions of a file with identical content, only the latest consecutive version will be kept even if the versions were uploaded outside the 10-minute window.

  • Although these intermediary versions aren’t kept as a version in Egnyte, they are still tracked for reporting and auditing purposes.

Viewer Only Permission and Partner Integrations FAQ

Viewer Only permission is a fundamental platform feature introduced by Egnyte, that if enabled on a given domain is also visible in Egnyte’s Public API used by partners in their Egnyte integrations.

This FAQ is intended for partners maintaining existing or developing new third-party integrations with Egnyte. Read more about Viewer Only permission in general here.

Why Should I Approve or Re-Test My Egnyte Integration?

By approving compatibility of their integrations, partners enable their and Egnyte’s customers to benefit from the latest functionality provided by Egnyte.

What Changes Did Egnyte Introduce to the Public API?

Egnyte’s Public API consists of more than 20 endpoints falling into the following categories:

  • File/Folder endpoints: Folders for which the API user has Viewer Only permissions continue to be visible on these endpoints and the user can navigate through the entire folder tree, however, files will not be shown in the endpoint responses. Copy and move operations containing subfolders with Viewer Only permissions are entirely blocked.
  • Permission endpoints: Viewer Only permissions are fully visible to API users having sufficient permissions to view or manage permissions.
  • Audit endpoints: Viewer Only permissions are fully visible to API users having sufficient permissions to view or manage permissions.
  • Streaming / Event endpoints: Viewer Only permissions are fully visible to API users having sufficient permissions to retrieve events.
  • Webhooks: Viewer Only permissions are fully visible to webhook users.

Is Testing Always Needed?

Egnyte cannot advise whether full testing is required for your integration or a static code analysis is sufficient to approve compatibility for your integration. Partners should review their code and integration based on the documentation provided by Egnyte to decide on the required testing scope.

Do I Need to Test For All of Egnyte’s API Endpoints?

Use cases only using the following endpoints can safely be excluded from testing for Viewer Only Permission:

  • User management API (/pubapi/v2/users)
  • Group Management API (/pubapi/v2/groups)
  • Trash Management API (/pubapi/v1/fs/trash)
  • Embed UI API (/pubapi/v2/navigate)
  • Project Folders API (/pubapi/v1/project-folders)
  • Bookmarks API (/pubapi/v1/bookmarks) For an overview of all endpoints, refer to Egnyte for Developer API Documentation

Which Test Cases Should Be Tested?

The particular test cases and acceptance criteria depend on the use case of your integration and cannot be generally stated by Egnyte. However, the following scenarios may help partners identify test scenarios:

  • Ensure permission responses containing Viewer Only permission are correctly handled and understood by your integration including proper exception handling
  • Ensure best security principles following latest OWASP recommendations
  • Prevent permission elevation scenarios when assigning permissions through your integration
  • Aligned user experience, respecting that in Egnyte WebUI files with Viewer Only permission are visible, listed and able to preview but not in the Public API

Which Additional Help Does Egnyte Offer to Test or Approve My Application to Work with Viewer Only Permission?

Egnyte provides test domains, documentation about the changes introduced and ensures support in case of issues found during your testing.

Test domains can be created using Egnyte’s trial sign up on Egnyte website and raising a support ticket to activate Viewer Only permission on that domain.

I Have Tested My Integration and Approve It is Compatible - What Should I Do?

Reach out to Egnyte Support and approve that your integration works with Viewer Only Permission.

Viewer Only Permission Limited Availability

Viewer Only Permission (Limited Availability)

Viewer Only permission is a new folder permission level offered to Platform Enterprise, GxP with Governance and Life Science Professional plans that meet the technical domain qualification criteria set out further below.

  • Viewer Only permission allows customers to better protect their content by restricting files to preview only.
  • It prevents downloading, printing and copying of files.
  • Viewer Only permission can be assigned to any user or group, including Standard Users and Power Users. If Viewer Only Permission has been enabled on the domain, no additional configuration is necessary. The Viewer Only permission level will automatically appear when assigning folder permissions by selecting Share from the list of options and clicking Manage Folder Permissions.

More details about managing Folder Permissions can be found here.

  • Viewer-Only permission is under limited availability and is only offered to Platform Enterprise, Elite, Ultimate, GxP with Governance and Life Science Professional plans that meet the technical domain qualification criteria. To request this feature, contact our Products team.

  • Egnyte will not activate Viewer Only permission on domains that show Public API usage without prior consent from the customer.

Watermarking for Viewer Only Permissions
  • Watermarking for Viewer Only Permissions is currently offered as part of the dedicated Document Room domains (beta) plan and is configurable per Document Room.
  • Watermarking is only supported for documents, video and audio content is previewable with Viewer Only permission without watermark.
Viewer Only Permission on Mobile, Desktop App, and Other Clients

  • On the Desktop App, Viewer Only permission is not supported. The Desktop App syncs a local copy of the file to the user’s device, and once a file exists on local disk it can be copied, moved, or opened outside Egnyte with no way to enforce restrictions, so rather than expose files without real protection, Egnyte does not make Viewer Only-permissioned files visible or accessible on the Desktop App. Users in folders where they have Viewer Only permission will not be able to see or otherwise access those files from this client.

  • On the Mobile App, if the viewer-only permissions are enabled on the domain, users with viewer-only permissions can access folder contents and preview files. This applies to both iOS and Android platforms. Click on the links in the previous sentence for more information.

  • Additionally, in the iOS mobile app, users will receive the following prompt when attempting to open a direct link to a file or folder in that folder: ‘Your access is restricted to viewer-only permissions. Please use the Web UI to view this folder.’

  • Other clients, including FTP, will experience the same behavior.

  • Regarding Public API support, please read the details in this separate article.

Supported File Types

All files that can be previewed in the WebUI previewer are supported. More information can be found here.

All previews will occur exclusively through Egnyte’s native previewer, even for file types supported by Microsoft Office’s previewer (available through the Microsoft Office integrations). This ensures consistent security measures across all previews, effectively preventing content exfiltration.

Link Sharing and Viewer Only Permissions
  • Users who have Viewer Only Permission to a file cannot create share links for it.
  • Folders with Viewer and higher permissions that contain sub-folders for which the user has Viewer Only permission can be shared by the user. In this case, link recipients will not be able to see and preview files through the shared folder link for which the link creator has Viewer Only permission.
Commenting, Workflows, Metadata, File Versions & Download History

Users with Viewer Only Permission are allowed to

  • Read and create comments.
  • View, approve and comment workflow tasks (but not create or cancel).
  • View but not modify metadata.
  • View the list of file versions, but not download, delete, or revert to previous versions.
  • View the download history of a file.
Previewing Video Files

Users with viewer-only permission can preview video files only if advanced video playback is enabled.

Without advanced video playback, the video would need to be previewed in the browser’s native previewer, which cannot enforce preview-only.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Will Viewer Only Permission Be Available on My Domain?

Egnyte is activating Viewer Only permission on a rolling basis to eligible plans as soon as the domains fulfill the technical requirements.

What are the Technical Requirements that Need to be Fulfilled Before Activation?

Viewer Only permission is a fundamental platform feature that requires certain client devices to upgrade to a new software version or to be migrated:

  • All admins and power users must use Egnyte Mobile app version 8.12.2 for iOS (available since October 2022) and 8.32 for Android (available since September 2022), or higher.
  • Desktop Sync devices are not supported with Viewer Only Permission and must first be synchronized and thereafter migrated to the Desktop App.
  • Smart Cache devices must be upgraded to version 3.10.0(available since November 2022) or higher.
  • Storage Sync devices must be upgraded to version 12.14.0(available since November 2022) or higher. This applies to public cloud connectors as well.
  • NETGEAR devices are not supported with Viewer Only Permission and must first be synchronized and thereafter migrated to Smart Cache. Further information can be found here.
  • 3rd party integrations (not developed by Egnyte) are currently not supported.
  • Customers’ own integrations with Egnyte’s Public API need to be tested by the customer on their own test domains first. Egnyte will not activate Viewer Only permission if the above technical requirements have not been met.
How Can Users Upgrade Their Egnyte Mobile Apps?

Users who have activated automatic updates for Egnyte’s mobile app will automatically get the latest version.

For users that have deactivated automatic upgrades, a list of users/devices with their currently used Egnyte App version is available in domain Settings -> Devices. Admins may reach out to these users directly requesting to manually upgrade to the latest Egnyte App version.

How Can a user Upgrade their Smart Cache and Storage Sync/Public Cloud Connector Devices?

Smart Cache Devices will automatically be updated in the chosen maintenance window. For more information about Smart Cache update windows see here.

If automatic updates for Storage Sync and Public Cloud connector are disabled, updates need to be manually performed by the admin. Please refer to Storage Sync and Public Cloud Connector pages for more details.

The Domain Uses Egnyte’s Public API - What does an admin Need To Do?

Since Egnyte has no control over customers’ own integrations using the Public API, customers are required to test their integrations on a test domain before activation of Viewer Only permission. To request a test domain, contact your Egnyte representative.

Once activated on a domain, Viewer Only permission is also activated on the domain’s Public API and the API fully supports it.

To test the integration with Egnyte’s Public API, the same requirements and instructions apply as 3rd party integrations. Please refer to the Viewer Only Permission and Partner Integrations FAQ for more information.

Are There Any Limitations After Viewer Only Permission has been Activated on the Domain?

Yes. After Viewer Only permission has been activated on a domain, the following general limitations apply:

  • Registration of mobile devices with Egnyte app Versions not supporting Viewer Only permission is no longer possible (applies to all user types).
  • Registration of Desktop Sync devices is no longer possible (applies to all user types).
  • Registration of Smart Cache, Storage Sync and Public Cloud Connector devices with versions not supporting Viewer Only permission is no longer possible
  • Registration of NETGEAR devices is no longer possible.
  • 3rd Party applications not developed by Egnyte must NOT be activated or integrated by admins.
What If a customer wants to Downgrade to a plan not including viewer only permission?

As long as there are active permission assignments using Viewer Only Permission, a plan downgrade is not possible. Before downgrading, customers must re-assign Viewer Only permissions to another (higher) appropriate permission level or revoke permissions entirely for users with current Viewer Only permission assignments.

Admins can use Folder Permission Reports in Collaboration or Permission Explorer in Secure & Govern to list users/folders with assigned Viewer Only permissions.

Watermarking

In Egnyte, you can easily apply Watermarks to files viewed through a shared link within a regular Egnyte domain and even to files previewed and/or downloaded from within the Document Room domain by the user with viewer and viewer-only permissions. Watermarks can be set at any time and will apply to every link, regardless of when it was created (so it will apply to both links created before enabling this feature and newly created ones).

Egnyte offers two levels of watermarking – basic watermarking is available with the Document Room plan and advanced watermarking is available with Platform Enterprise and Document Room Enterprise plan.

Enable and Configure Watermarks (Basic Watermarking)

To enable the Watermarking feature on your domain, go to Settings > Configuration > General section and enable the Watermark files option.

Once enabled, the Admin will have to provide the static watermark text for the whole domain. Admin can optionally choose to include the viewer’s IP Address in the watermark which will be dynamically added to the watermark along with the static text

Enable and Configure Watermarks (Advanced Watermarking)

To enable the Watermarking feature on your domain, go to Settings > Configuration > General section and enable the Watermark files option.

Once enabled, the Admin can select the Customise watermark button to open the watermark editor and configure the watermark.

In the watermark editor, the Admin can provide the main text for the watermark and then select additional dynamic items to be added on top of the main text. The admin will have the option to choose the Recipient’s IP address, User full name and User email address as dynamic items. The admin can also choose to add a line break after each component to structure the watermark better.

To assist the administrator in ensuring accurate watermark configuration, a sample preview will be displayed as they select the configurations.

When the domain admin enables the watermarking for the very first time for the domain, the text Confidential will be set as the default value of the watermark.

The user’s full name will be applicable only when the logged-in user is viewing the files. For users accessing files anonymously via shared links, the user’s full name will not be included in the watermark, irrespective of the configuration.

The user’s email address will be included in the watermark only when the logged-in user is viewing the file or a specific recipient is viewing the file via a shared link.

If the checkbox Add a line break after each component is not checked, all the selected components within the watermark will appear one after another in one single line.

Preview

When watermarks are enabled and configured for the domain, then the watermark text and additional dynamic components as per the configuration will be displayed diagonally in the preview for all files viewed via shared links within the regular Egnyte domain or previewed and downloaded within the Document Room domain. The text will be automatically scaled to the preview size.

Ways to Upload Files

Egnyte provides multiple ways to upload content to the Cloud to ensure the user always has convenient access to all their files wherever they go .

Users can sync content from their desktop, quickly transfer large files, and access files on the go from mobile devices. This article outlines the various methods available.

Most of the suggested methods preserve timestamps; however, there are some exceptions. If the user is downloading a single file, the browser will cause the timestamp to be set as the time of download. Unfortunately, this browser behavior cannot be changed. Also, when downloading a ZIP file, the modified timestamp may or may not be preserved depending on the ZIP client.

Admins looking to perform a large scale data migration should refer to An Admin’s Guide to Adding Content to Egnyte. Standard and Power Users can reference the article A User’s Guide to Adding Content to Egnyte.

Web Browser Access (Web UI)

Desktop App

Storage Sync

Mobile

Migration App

FTP

File Size Upload Limits

Web Browser Access (Web User Interface or Web UI)

To access files from any computer with an internet connection, log in through a web browser. Using the browser, drag and drop files for upload, send file links to outside business partners, share folders, and manage the account settings.

The Web UI is not recommended for larger onboarding or data migration projects. For migrations of 50GB or larger, see Migration App.

Learn more about the Web UI

Desktop App

Egnyte Desktop App provides a way to access all the data from the desktop without requiring local storage space as long as a persistent Internet connection is available. Note that there will be a temporary requirement of up to twice the storage space to upload new files (one copy to actively edit and one copy queued for upload). This local disk space will be cleared as files are successfully uploaded.

Desktop App is not recommended for larger onboarding or data migration projects. For migrations of 50GB or larger, see Migration App.

Learn more about Desktop App

Mobile

Mobile apps provide easy access to the files on the go when a user may only have their mobile phone or tablet with them. Egnyte offers one of the most extensive selections of mobile apps in the industry. The user can access Egnyte through an iOS device, Android device, or Windows Phone.

Egnyte’s mobile apps allow the users to edit and share files, manage folders, invite new users, and even download files for offline access.

Learn more about Mobile

Migration App

Migration App is Egnyte’s self-service data migration tool that enables the users to easily move files, folders, and their associated permissions from an on-premises network share to the cloud. It also offers the ability to sanitize file and folder names on the source, as well as True-Up data from the source to the destination for larger, more complex migration projects. Migration App can copy between 1 and 5 TB per day, depending on a variety of network considerations.

Migration App is limited to use by account Admins and must be requested for each domain.

Learn more about Migration App

FTP / SFTP

FTP/SFTP (File Transfer Protocol/SSH File Transfer Protocol) is a technology that transfers files in a moderately secure and easy-to-configure manner. Egnyte integrates with most FTP and SFTP clients to transfer files and folders. For reliable FTP/SFTP transfer experience, file and folders dataset uploads should not exceed 50 GB of total size and a single file upload should not exceed a file size of 10 GB. It is an ideal tool to use with APIs to upload data from other applications, or if they have a command line script that pushes data on a regular basis.

FTP is NOT recommended as a migration tool. If you have more than 50GB data total to transfer, consider using Egnyte’s Migration App or some other third-party tool designed to handle larger data migrations.

Learn more about FTP

File Size Limits

The file size limits are applicable as per the customer’s plan. See Am I Subject to Any Restrictions? for more details.

Web UI - Unable to Sort Items in Trash

Limitation for Sorting Items in Trash

The sort option is unavailable for performance and scalability reasons when the number of items in the trash exceeds 50,000 items.

If the limit is reached, users won’t be able to sort the data residing in the Trash.

The sorting option (arrows next to the labels) is visible but these will not sort the data if the users click on the arrows.

Webhook Steps

The Outbound Webhook step, available within the Automated Action step in workflow templates, allows users to extend workflows beyond Egnyte. These steps can be added alongside todo, review, and approval steps. When the Outbound Webhook step is reached, it will make an HTTP POST request to the webhook URL to notify the third-party application.

Common use cases for Outbound Webhook steps are:

  • Sending custom notifications via Slack, Microsoft Teams, or email

  • Updating external databases or spreadsheets

  • Converting files

  • Executing AI workflows Users can use Outbound Webhook steps with any application that accepts inbound requests, but the most common webhook receivers are:

  • Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) solutions such as Microsoft Power Automate, Make, or Zapier

  • Public Cloud Serverless Functions from AWS, Azure, or Google

  • Custom applications

How to Add an Outbound Webhook Step to a Workflow

Users can set up an Outbound Webhook step within the Template Steps Setup section of a Workflow Template.

Note: Workflow Templates can be accessed in the Workflows -> Configuration Settings. This article specifically covers instructions for configuring an Outbound Webhook step only. Refer to Workflow Templates Overview for the complete setup of a Workflow Template.

Follow these steps to add an Outbound Webhook step within a Workflow Template.

  • Click on the + icon in the graphic builder.

  • Select Webhook Call under Automated Actions as the step.

  • Enter the Step name with up to 128 characters. The Step name can be set to editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.

  • Enter a Description with up to 512 characters. The description can be set to editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.

  • Enter the endpoint URL of the external system in the Endpoint field. A Webhook endpoint is a URL (https://) that receives webhook event notifications and can trigger an action based on the payload sent in the message.

  • To include an authentication header, enable the Use authentication header option by using a toggle switch. Once enabled, enter the required authentication header in the provided field. By default, Outbound Webhook steps will be marked as complete as soon as the 3rd party app receives the Webhook call. When the Wait for Completion Signal option is enabled, the step will stay in progress until the 3rd party application makes a separate API call to Egnyte to indicate that it is complete. If no completion signal is received within 24 hours, the step will automatically be marked as Failed.

  • Set the workflow condition by choosing one of the following options from If this step fails,, then dropdown list:

  • Mark step as “Failed” and cancel workflow - This selection will mark the Webhook step as “Failed” and cancel the workflow when the webhook request does not pass within 24 hours.

  • Mark step as “Failed” and continue workflow execution - This selection will mark the Webhook step as “Failed” and workflow execution will continue to the next step or workflow will be marked completed if this is the last step of the workflow when the webhook request does not pass within 24 hours. When an initial webhook request is triggered upon step activation and the request fails, the system will automatically resend the request at regular intervals for up to 24 hours. Additionally, the user has the option to manually resend the request every 2 hours by using the Retry request button in the workflow pane.

Technical Notes

  • The provided endpoint must be an HTTPS URL with a valid TLS certificate. Egnyte will make a POST request to this URL when the step is executed.
  • The POST body is a JSON object that includes the details of the workflow, the details of the file associated with the workflow, and the callback URL (if the completion signal is enabled). The request has a Content-Type HTTP request header of application/json.
  • If the endpoint returns a success HTTP response code (e.g., 200, 204, etc.) within 60 seconds, the Webhook will be considered as received
  • If the endpoint returns an error HTTP response code (e.g., 400, 404, 500, etc.), the webhook will be considered as not received
  • If the endpoint is not reachable or takes more than 60 seconds to respond, the webhook will be considered as not received
  • When a Webhook is not received, Egnyte will perform automatic retries using exponential backoff over a 24 hour period
  • The optional Authentication header will be passed as is. Users can provide any value in this field such as an encoded HTTP Basic Authentication, a Bearer Token, or any other value.
  • When using the Completion Signal option, the user must make an HTTP POST call to the callback URL using the Egnyte Public API. Users can get a developer key from developers.egnyte.com. The auth token used for the request must include the Egnyte.filesystem scope.

What Happens When I Copy or Move a Folder That Doesn’t Inherit Permissions?

When you choose to keep source permissions the folder will retain its non-inherited permissions state. When you choose to use destination permissions, then the folder will inherit permissions from the new destination folder.

Preview with Integrations

Certain third-party applications (for example, Microsoft 365 for the web) can generate file previews for their native file types in the Egnyte Web UI. Because such applications are designed specifically for their file types, they may offer a better user experience for previewing these files. Egnyte must pass a copy of the relevant file to the third-party application developer to generate a preview. The preview capability is turned on by default once the user enables an application that supports the preview capability.

To use Egnyte’s preview capability or to avoid passing files to the relevant application providers, domain administrators can turn off the third-party preview capability from the Egnyte Settings page. To do so, open the Settings page, select the General tab, find the Previewing Files option and select it to disable.

Who Can Change the Permission Inheritance Status for a Folder?

Why am I not Receiving Invitation and Password Reset Emails?

Egnyte’s email delivery services send system-generated emails such as new user account invitations, password resets, and folder notifications to end-users using the alias notify@egnyte.com.

If a user is not receiving such email notifications and can not be found in obvious places like ‘Spam’ and ‘Trash’ folders, then the email could be in a bounced suppression state. Generally, emails go into bounce suppression when an email marked for delivery is returned back to Egnyte from the receiving email provider.

To avoid excessive delivery attempts and to protect the reputation of the sending email address, Egnyte’s delivery services stop sending further emails for 24 hours or until the issue on the receiving end has been resolved.

Emails are bounced back to Egnyte for several reasons. Mainly due to strict spam filtering on the receiving email provider or sometimes when a new mailbox is created but not fully functional. Using the list of common errors below related to bounced emails, admins can troubleshoot email delivery issues on their SMTP server or email provider.

Error Code

Description

550

  • Envelope blocked - User Entry

  • Rejected by header-based block

  • Sender blocked - notify@egntye.com 550 - 5.1.1

  • Recipient address rejected: User Unknown

  • The email account that you tried to reach does not exist

  • Email address could not be found, or was misspelled

  • No Such User Here

  • Invalid Recipient 550 - 5.1.10

  • RESOLVER.ADR.RecipientNotFound; Recipient email address not found by SMTP address lookup 550 - 5.2.1

  • The email account that you tried to reach is disabled

  • The user you are trying to contact is receiving mail at a rate that prevents additional messages from being delivered 550 - 5.2.2

  • Delivery failed: mailbox is full (quota exceeded) 550 - 5.4.1

  • Recipient address rejected: Access denied (Microsoft Outlook Protection) 550 - 5.4.14

  • Hop count exceeded - possible mail loop 550 - 5.7.1

  • Recipient address rejected: User email address is marked as invalid 550 - 5.7.133

  • Delivery restriction check failed because the sender was not authenticated when sending to this group

We recommend the steps below to minimize bounced notification emails:

  • Whitelist Egnyte’s mail server IP addresses below and listed in Egnyte-Hostnames-for-Firewall-Rules- on the safe sender or allowed list to ensure an uninterrupted flow of all emails from Egnyte.
  • Location
  • Mail Server IP Addresses
  • Global
  • 168.245.53.124
  • 208.117.56.144
  • 149.72.193.80
  • 149.72.202.3
  • 149.72.133.214
  • Create the new user mailbox and allow some time for activation before creating a user account on Egnyte. This is a very common reason why emails are bounced.
  • Verify all server MX records have been updated successfully and the user is able to send and receive emails successfully from their mailbox.
  • Check for spelling mistakes in the email address or other issues with mailbox configuration.
  • Some users create custom rules and filters to manage their email that could delete or move emails to a different folder. Try searching for emails from notify@egnyte.com.
  • Check Spam filtering in the email provider’s admin console and run an email trace
  • Egnyte sends verification emails to users with unverified email addresses regardless of the user’s account status (Pending or Active). A user can be Active and still have an unverified email. This generally happens when users are provisioned and log in via SSO or Active Directory, which makes their account Active upon login. Since they didn’t go through the standard email invite flow, their email remains unverified until they manually click a verification link from a prompt.
    • If a user is Active and is prompted to verify, it is recommended to check whether verification emails are being blocked by email security tools (spam filters, gateway security, Okta email settings). Additionally, check email delivery logs before reporting the issue.
  • Contact Egnyte support if further assistance is needed.

Why Can’t I See Permissions Inheritance Status for Folders Directly Beneath /Shared?

Folders directly under Shared (e.g., /Shared/Projects) never inherit permissions since permissions cannot be set directly on /Shared. This means that the option is not relevant for these folders.

Why Do Some Users Still Have Access to a Folder After I Disable Permissions Inheritance?

Any permission that was already set directly on the folder (not on the parent folders) will remain. Also, if you choose to keep existing permissions, then a copy of the parent’s permissions will be copied to the folder.

Workflow Templates Overview

Users can create repetitive review and approval workflows efficiently and consistently using reusable Workflow Templates. This feature allows streamlining review and approval processes for the entire organization.

Depending on the Egnyte plan, access to these features may be limited. Workflow templates are available to Egnyte plans with multi-step workflow enabled.

Decision (Conditional Logic) and Agent step are available to the customers on Elite or Ultimate plans. AI Actions are available to the customers with the AI add-on enabled. PDF Conversion is only available when the PDF File handler add-on is enabled. Please contact the Egnyte account manager or Egnyte Sales team for more information.

Workflow Templates have the following configuration options:

  • Settings to control template access by folder location(s), user group(s), and file extension(s).
  • Settings for Workflow Creation Conditions
  • Customize workflow notifications
  • Configuring the step(s) by selecting the preferred action (such as User Tasks, AI Actions, Automated Actions, or Logic and Branching)

Accessing Workflow Templates

Workflow Templates are available in the Workflows section in the Configuration settings. The Templates page allows users to create new templates and view and edit existing templates.

The Templates section is available to:

  • Administrators
  • Users with a role that grants the can manage Workflow Templates capability Templates can have Active or Inactive status. By default, the page shows templates with both Active and Inactive status, but the user can filter only Active or Inactive status templates by using the Status filter. Active templates are available to end users to create workflows. Inactive templates are not available to users to create workflows.

Users can click on the Template name to access and view the template details.

They can use the available filters to refine the templates list. Users can click on Reset filters to reset the templates list to the default view. They can also click on Hide filters to hide the filters from the view.

Creating a Template

Follow these steps to create a template:

  • Navigate to the Configuration | Workflows | Templates page.
  • Click the Add Template button
  • Click Create template.
  • A New Workflow Template page will appear to configure the template using the Graphic Builder. The editor will automatically display the canvas with the Start block selected and following sections on the panel on the right.
    • Template General Setup
    • Workflow Creation Conditions
    • Workflow Notifications
Template General Setup

This section allows defining information about a template such as template name and description. The user can limit the accessibility of the template by using a combination following three parameters:

  • User group(s) - Determine who can initiate the workflows from the template.
  • File extension(s) - Specify which file extensions can be utilized to create workflows from the template.
  • Folder location(s) - Specify folder locations from where the workflows from the template can be initiated. Follow the steps to complete the General Setup section of the template.
  • Enter a unique Template name with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 50 characters.
  • Enter Template description with up to 128 characters.
  • Choose one of the following two options from Who can use this template dropdown list:
    • Anyone - The template will be available to any user
    • Specific Group - The template will be available to specific groups. User can add up to 10 groups.
  • Choose one of the following two options from Types of files that the template can be applied to:
    • Any file type - The template will be available for all the files
    • Specific file type - The template will be available to specified file extensions. User can enter up to 10 file extensions
  • Choose one of the following two options from the Location where the template can be applied to:
    • Any folder-The template will be available to use within all the folders.
    • Specific folder - The template will be available only with the selected folder(s).User can select up to 10 folders. All nested folders contained within the chosen folder are automatically selected.
Workflow Creation Conditions

This section of the Workflow Template allows users to define conditions for the Workflow creation.

Choose one of the following options from the dropdown list for Select the allowed option for the workflow creation

  • Manually - Users can manually create workflows using this template
  • Automatically - Workflows are created automatically when predefined conditions are met
  • Both manually and automatically - Workflows are created automatically when predefined conditions are met and users can also manually create workflows using this template When the Manually option is selected, proceed to the Template Steps Setup section to configure the remaining steps of the workflow template.

However, when the Automatically or Both manually and automatically option is selected, refer to Workflow Triggers to set up a condition for creating automatic workflows.

Workflow Notifications

This section allows for customizing the notifications sent to workflow creators and assignees for a template.

The Notify workflow creator about the workflow status changes option controls whether email notifications will be sent to the workflow creator when steps are completed or the workflow is completed.

The Custom reminders for assignees option allows workflow template authors to override the default task reminder options set for the domain in Workflows General Settings. Task reminders are email notifications sent to assignees to remind them of pending or overdue tasks.

  • Users can customize the reminders for a template by enabling the Set custom reminders value for this template.
  • Users can update the number of days for the reminders sent to assignees before the due date or opt out of the reminders sent to assignees before the due date.
  • Users can update the number of days for the reminders sent to assignees after the due date or opt out of the reminders sent to assignees after the due date.
Adding Steps to Template
  • Click on the (+) button below the Start block in the Graphic Builder to add a new step to the workflow.
  • This opens the Add Step dialog modal, where users can select from the following step types: User Tasks

Use these steps when human action is required to advance the workflow.

  • To Do: Assigns a manual task to a user.
  • Review: Requests a team member to review content.
  • Approval: Requires an explicit approve or reject action. Rejection logic for every approval step can also be configured. AI Actions

Use AI Prompt or AI Agent step to leverage artificial intelligence for automated content generation or intelligent handling. AI Agent allows users to select specific source files for context and choose the optimal AI model for performing the complex task.

Automated Actions

Use the following automated system operation steps to streamline file management:

  • Add metadata to file : Updates file attributes automatically.
  • Move file to a folder : Relocates files to designated directories.
  • Execute a webhook : Connects to external systems or services.
  • Convert file to PDF : Automatically converts documents to PDF format. Logic and Branching steps

Dynamically route documents based on specific conditions and rules.

  • Decision: Evaluates specified conditions to route a document down the correct path automatically. For example, users can route a file based on its size: if it’s under 500MB, it goes to Route 1; if it’s between 500MB and 1000MB, it goes to Route 2; and if it’s over 1000MB, it goes to Route 3. If a file doesn’t fit any of these criteria, it will default to a mandatory “Else” branch. To set up To Do, Review and Approval steps, proceed to the next section of this article. For all other step types, please refer to the corresponding external articles linked above.

  • Enter the Step name with up to 128 characters.

  • Users can keep the Step name editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.

  • Enter a Description with up to 512 characters.

  • Users can keep the Template description editable or non-editable when a workflow is created from a template. Select Allow edits option to make it editable at the workflow instance.

  • Choose one of the following three options for Assignees:

    • Anyone - Any user(s) can be added as task assignees while creating a workflow from the template.
    • Anyone from a specific group(s) - Only the user(s) from the specified group(s) can be added as task assignees while creating a workflow from a template. Users can add up to 10 groups.
    • Specific user(s) and group(s) - Specified user(s) and group(s) cannot be modified while creating a workflow from a template. When a specific group is added to the template, all the users from that group are added as individual assignees at the workflow instance. It is possible to enter up to 20 users in total.

  • When the Anyone or Anyone from specific group(s) option is selected, the user will get an option to define the Minimum number of assignees required. When a workflow is created from a template, the same number of assignees must be added.

  • After selecting any one of the three options for the Assignees field, the user will see an extra option to define the Number of assignees required to complete the step. When a workflow is created from a template, the defined number of assignees will be required to complete the step.

  • Users can define the Step due date using the Step should be completed within _ days field. When a workflow is created, the step due date is calculated automatically based on the step start date and number of days entered in this field for a step.

  • When an Approval step type is selected, the user will get an additional option to Request the digital signature when the assignee approves. By choosing this option, the digital signature option is selected by default when a workflow is created from a template. Once all the parameters are filled out, select the checkbox to Activate and click the Create template button in the top right corner to make it available to domain users.

Selecting the Activate checkbox makes the template available to other users. To restrict users from using the template, do not select the Activate checkbox.

Known Limitations

  • A single branch path supports up to 25 steps.
  • A single workflow template supports up to 50 total steps.
  • Workflows are limited to 1,000 executions per template per day and 10,000 executions across the entire domain per day.

Creating Workflows from a Template

Once the template is defined, the domain users based on the access defined in the template can create workflows from the template. To create a workflow from a template, open a file preview and follow the steps listed below.

  • On the file preview, select the Workflows icon in the sidebar.
  • Click the New Workflow button and select the template to use for creating a workflow.
  • A new workflow dialog modal with the name of the template and pre-populated workflow parameters based on the template.
  • Enter or Modify the parameters, if needed. Please note that the parameters may be non-editable based on the template configuration.
  • Click the Create button.

Editing a Template

The user can edit any of the existing templates. They can hover over a template to edit and then the Edit option will show up. Click on Edit to update the template configuration. After successfully saving the edited template, it is saved with an incremented version. The system automatically keeps templates in version control.

Deactivating a Template

Users can deactivate a template by hovering over a template and clicking on the Deactivate icon.

Click on Deactivate to confirm and the template will be deactivated and marked as inactive.

Reactivating a Template

If a template is marked as Inactive, users can reactivate the template by clicking on the Activate icon.

Click on Activate to confirm.

The template will be marked as Active.

Duplicating a Template

Users can easily create a new template by using the existing templates. On duplicating an existing template, all the parameters except the template name are copied to create a new template. Users can modify any of the template parameters and provide a new unique Template name in order to create a new template.

Audit Trail

For plans supporting Audit Reporting, a new Workflow Templates audit report is available, capturing all the actions related to workflow templates such as template creation, template edition, and template status change. The existing Workflow audit report is updated to track the workflows created from a template.

Automated Email Notifications for Workflow Templates and Conditions

There may be scenarios where errors occur while executing the workflow trigger or automated conditions. In such cases, Egnyte sends automated email notifications to the workflow creators. These notifications include direct links to the workflow, enabling creators to quickly identify and resolve the associated errors.

  • Email alerts for workflow limits: Template creators will be notified when a template reaches its daily automation limit which is default to 1000, and domain administrators will receive alerts for domain-wide limits which is 10000 by default.
  • To request an increase in automation notification limits, contact our Products team.
  • Immediate trigger failure notifications: Template creators will get instant emails if a workflow trigger fails to create workflows automatically due to issues like access permissions, deleted folders, or user/group changes but not limited to those.
  • Automated step failure alerts: Workflow creators will receive immediate notifications for automated step failures that require user intervention (e.g., permission fixes) and after 24 hours if a step completely fails or times out.

Workflow Triggers

Workflow Triggers enable automatic initiation of workflows when a specified condition is met. To save time and maintain process consistency, users can ensure that workflows start on their own by setting up one of the following conditions:

  • File is added to a specific folder
  • Specific metadata is applied to a file
  • Document is signed using Egnyte Sign
  • A workflow from a specific template is completed

How to Set Up a Workflow Trigger

Users can set up a Workflow Trigger within workflow Templates. Workflow Templates now include a new section,“Workflow Creation Conditions”, where users can define the condition for the Workflow Trigger.

Workflow Templates can be accessed in the Workflows -> Configuration Settings. This article specifically covers instructions for configuring automated workflow conditions only. Refer to Workflow Templates Overview for the complete set up of a Workflow Template.

When the Automatic or Both Manual and Automatic option is selected in the Workflow Creation Conditions, follow the steps to set up a condition for creating automatic workflows.

  • When the Automatic or Both Manual and Automatic option is selected for Workflow Creation Condition, the Automatic workflow creation conditions section is displayed.
  • Choose one of the following conditions from the dropdown list:
    • A document is added to a folder
    • A specific metadata is added to a document
    • A specific workflow is completed on a document
    • A document is signed When a document is added to a folder option is selected, the Select Trigger Folder dialog will appear. Users can select up to 20 folders to trigger the workflow. Choose the folder(s) for the system to monitor the changes and click on Select.

Once 20 folders are selected, users will be notified that the maximum limit is reached.

Users can also specify which file operations trigger a workflow. By default, all the options are enabled. Users need to select at least one event from the list. When any of the selected events occur, a new workflow will automatically be created.

If the Workflow Creator lacks minimum edit rights to the file, the trigger will fail, and the workflow creation process will be unsuccessful. Therefore, you should select a user who possesses the necessary file edit permissions to guarantee the workflow trigger functions.

When a specific metadata is added to a document option is selected, users must choose an existing metadata property, an operator, and a value to compare with. When this metadata field is added or updated on a file and it matches the condition, a workflow will automatically be created.

When a specific workflow is completed on a document option is selected, users can choose one of the existing workflow templates. When a workflow of the selected type is completed on a file, a workflow will automatically be created.

When a document is signed option is selected, a workflow from this template will be automatically created once a document is signed using Egnyte Sign.

  • Choose the desired option from the dropdown list of the Workflow Creator.

    • Originating actor - The user performing the action of adding a file to the folder will be assigned as the workflow creator.
    • Specific user - The specific user can be added to act as a workflow creator. The following three parameters available in the Template General Setup section of a Workflow Template can be used to further restrict conditions for the trigger. Each parameter, or any combination of them, can act as an additional filter:

  • Who can use this template.

  • Types of files that the template can be applied to

  • Location where the template can be applied

These filters allow users to set more specific workflow conditions, such as selected folder location and a metadata value being added, allowed file types and document added to a folder or selected folder location and a document being signed.
